title: Lokeśvaraśataka
subject: Bauddhastotra
colophon: iti śrīvajradattajinabhikṣukaviviracitaṃ śrīlokeśvaraśatakaṃ samāptam || || śubham astu || || || || khanayananidhiyuṃkte[[varṣe]] mārgamāse valakṣe ditisutaguruvāre sūryajābhrātṛtithyāṃ || nṛpatigurunimittaṃ śrṭmadāryavaloke śvaraśatakam aleṣīt(!) kopi bauddho ʼmṛtādyaḥ(!) || 1 || || || śubham astu jagatāṃ || || || || (fol.19r4-6 )
purpose: nṛpatigurunimittaṃ — for (the sake of) the king's guru, or for the king and the guru
notes: Chronogram read right to left: kha = 0, nayana = 2, nidhi = 9, giving 920. The era is not named, but in a Nepalese Buddhist context it is most likely NS: NS 920 Mārgaśīrṣa ≈ Nov/Dec 1799 CE. The catalogue's '[VS] 420?' looks like a misreading of nidhi (9) and is implausible. 'valakṣe' = bright fortnight (śukla). 'ditisutaguru' = Śukra, so the weekday is Friday. 'sūryajābhrātṛtithi': Sūryajā = Yamunā; her brother is Yama. Yama is lord of the 10th tithi (daśamī). Yamadvitīyā belongs to Kārttika and does not fit Mārga. The catalogue's 'pratipadā' has no support in the text. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris. 'aleṣīt(!)' = alekhīt. Scribe: 'kopi bauddho ʼmṛtādyaḥ(!)' means 'some Buddhist, Amṛta...'. Possibly read ʼmṛtāhvaḥ 'named Amṛta', which fits the mālinī cadence. Given the date (c. 1799) and the phrase 'nṛpatigurunimittaṃ', an identification with the Buddhist paṇḍita Amṛtānanda of Kathmandu is tempting but unproven. The verse is mālinī.
review: Tithi: 'sūryajābhrātṛtithi' = tithi of Yama (brother of Yamunā, daughter of the Sun). Under the standard tithi-lord scheme Yama governs the 10th tithi, so it is daśamī, not dvitīyā. Yamadvitīyā is a Kārttika festival and does not fit Mārga. Confidence medium.
Scribe name normalized to 'Amṛta' (ʼmṛtādyaḥ(!) probably corrupt for ʼmṛtāhvaḥ 'named Amṛta'); possible identification with the Buddhist paṇḍita Amṛtānanda (fl. c. 1800) noted.
'bauddha' moved from titles to affiliation.
Era: chronogram 920 most plausibly NS; era left as unspecified because the colophon does not state it. ce_approx 1799 kept on the NS assumption.
Purpose clarified: written for the king's guru (or for the king and guru).
Notes expanded: catalogue's 'VS 420?' and 'pratipadā' do not agree with the colophon.

colophon: iti śrī dakṣIṇāmūrtti viracite uddhārakośe sakalāṃgamasāre ṣoḍaśadevī saptakumāra navagraha saptadevī catuṣṭadevī maṃtradhyānakośa nirṇayo nāma saptamakalpaḥ svāṃgarbhūrvī sammite śākalāe jyeṣṭhaye ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śuklapakṣe’kavāre || pṛthvīpālasyālayādo(!) lilekha gaṃgā viṣṇustaṃtram uddhārakośam ❁ ❁ || trivikrama varmaṇo rājñādeḥ pustakaṃ śubhadm astu ❁ (fol.23v2-5)
purpose: book of King Trivikramavarman (copied at the king's palace)
notes: 'śākalāe' is probably a corruption of śākakāle, so the era is Śaka. The chronogram 'svāṃgarbhūrvī' is corrupt. One possible reading is kha (0), aṅga (6), bhū (1), urvī (1). Read right to left, that gives ŚS 1160, about 1238 CE. However, 'sva' is not a standard number-word: it could also be svara (7), giving ŚS 1167. I have left ce_approx blank for that reason. A 13th-century date also seems early for a Devanagari paper manuscript, so this needs checking against the weekday. 'pṛthvīpālasyālayādo(!)' is most likely pṛthvīpālasyālaye, 'in the king's palace'. The 'pṛthvīpāla' there is probably the common noun 'king', meaning Trivikramavarman, not a personal name. 'rājñādeḥ' could be rājñaḥ, or rājñā + ādeḥ/ādeśāt ('by the king's order'). If it is ādeśāt, Trivikramavarman would also be the commissioner. Read 'gaṃgā viṣṇustaṃtram' as Gaṅgāviṣṇus tantram. 'śubhadm' should be śubham.
review: Removed 'Pṛthvīpāla' (p3) as a person: pṛthvīpālasyālaya most likely means 'the residence/palace of the king' (pṛthvīpāla = king, a common noun), probably meaning Trivikramavarman's palace; this is now recorded only under place.

Trivikramavarman: removed 'commissioner' because the colophon only says the book is his (pustakam), with no likhāpita/lekhayāmāsa. Kept 'owner' and added 'king' with medium confidence, since he is called rājan and the copy was made at a king's palace.
Weekday changed to its normal form 'arkavāra' (Sunday); the colophon has ’kavāre.
Place: added a tentative reading of 'king's palace'.
Purpose filled in: the copy was made for the king's own book.
Notes: added a tentative decoding of the chronogram.

title: Kālīkulakramārcana
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Sunday 9 Nov 1698, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti vāśiṣṭhīye, uttarāmnāya,kālīkramasaṃkṣepahomavidhiḥ || || ❁ || samvat 819 kārtikaśuklaṣaṣṭhami utrabhadranakṣetra bṛhaspativāra thva kunhu śrīśrīśrī vimalaprabodhamata śrīśrīśrīguhyakālyāna krama saṃpūrṇṇa yāṅā likhita karmmācāryya cakrasiṃhana || śubham astu sarvvadā kālam || (fol. 61r2-4)
notes: The era is not named, but 'samvat' with Newari text is Nepal Saṃvat (NS), which matches the catalogue. The NS year starts at Kārtika śukla 1, so Kārtika śukla 6 of NS 819 is Oct/Nov 1698 CE. The usual NS+880 rule gives 1699, which is too late for a Kārtika date. The tithi 'ṣaṣṭhami' is corrupt: it could be ṣaṣṭhī or aṣṭamī. On either day the moon is unlikely to be in Uttarabhādrapadā; on Kārtika śukla 6–8 it is usually around Uttarāṣāḍhā to Dhaniṣṭhā. So the date details are internally inconsistent, and the weekday has not been checked. The copy contains the krama of Guhyakālī 'according to Vimalaprabodha's doctrine' (vimalaprabodhamata). I take Vimalaprabodha as the traditional author of the Kālīkulakramārcana, not as someone involved in making this copy. The colophon names the text as 'kālīkramasaṃkṣepahomavidhiḥ' from the Vāśiṣṭhīya, Uttarāmnāya.
review: Added Vimalaprabodha (p2) as author: 'vimalaprabodhamata' is the doctrine of Vimalaprabodha, to whom the Kālīkulakramārcana is attributed. The first reading treated it only as a school name.
ce_approx changed from 1699 to 1698. The Nepal Saṃvat (NS) year begins at Kārtika śukla 1, so Kārtika śukla 6 of NS 819 falls in Oct/Nov 1698.
Normalized the nakṣatra and recorded it as inconsistent with the tithi; marked the corrupt tithi 'ṣaṣṭhami' as doubtful in notes.
Normalized the scribe's title to 'karmācārya'.

notes: The colophon only identifies the author. It gives no scribe, no commissioner and no copy date. The closing verse 'bhīmaseno ranyabhaṅga (= raṇe 'pi bhaṅgaḥ) ... yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā likhitaṃ mama doṣo na dīyate' is a stock scribal apology; Bhīmasena in it is mythological, not a person. The author's name 'Tatkālaṃkāra' is probably corrupt, perhaps for Tattvālaṃkāra or a similar -alaṃkāra name. The epithet 'niravedyāgamavidyāvidyetita' is probably meant as 'niravadyāgamavidyāvidyotita'. Nandana(ācārya) is the author's teacher (antevāsin) and Sanātanaguṇārṇava(ācārya) is the author's father. Neither is connected with this copy.

notes: The colophon gives only 'samvat 963' and does not name the era. I inferred Nepāla Saṃvat (= c. 1843 CE) from the Devanagari script and the 'roja' weekday formula. The first akṣara of the scribe's name is uncertain ('(jñ)ogarasiṃha'). It may stand for Jogarasiṃha or a similar name. The cataloguer also queries it ('Jñogarasiṃha ?').

title: Mantrakoṣa
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Monday 26 Dec 1644, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year + 1 (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: || iti śrīmad āditya tripāṭhīsaṃgṛhīte maṃtrakoṣe mudrādikathanaṃ nāma viṃśatimaḥ (!) paricchedaḥ samāpto yaṃ maṃtrakoṣaḥ ||…………………… || ………………………………………………………………………………………….. śrīśāke 1565 pauṣavadi 13 vidhānurādhāyāṃ likhitaṃ manoharasutaśrīmad anaṃtaśarmaṇo || || śubham astu || (fol. 183v10–11, 184r1–5)
notes: The catalogue gives 'Āśāditya Tripāṭhī' as the scribe. In the colophon he is the compiler of the Mantrakoṣa (saṃgṛhīte), so the role is author. The quoted text reads 'śrīmad āditya'. The catalogue's 'Āśāditya' may come from a misreading of 'śrīmadāditya', or the manuscript may actually read 'śrīmadāśāditya'. The copy was written by Ananta(śarman), son of Manohara. 'vidhānurādhāyāṃ' is taken as vidhau (Monday) + anurādhāyāṃ (nakṣatra). Adding 78 to ŚS 1565 gives 1643/44. Pauṣa kṛṣṇa 13 falls around late December 1643 (pūrṇimānta) or January 1644 (amānta). The weekday has not been checked.

The colophon calls him Kāśīnātha 'bhaṭṭopanāmaka', meaning his surname (upanāma) is Bhaṭṭa, and gives him the epithet 'dakṣiṇāmūrti-śivārādhaka' (worshipper of Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti; 'śīva' is a slip for 'śiva'). The colophon closes the uttarārdha with the stock 'ādarśadoṣā...' and '...kṣamasva' formulas but names no scribe, patron, date or place. 'likhidisva' is corrupt, probably for likhitvā or likhitam.

title: Mantramahodadhi
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Saturday 7 Nov 1767, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīma(5)nmahīdharaviracite maṃtramahodadhau ṣaṭkarmādinirūpaṇaṃ paṃcaviṃśas taraṃgaḥ || || śrīnṛsiṃhāya namaḥ | saṃvat 1824 mīti (!) (6) agahanabadī 1 vārasanīścarake līkhāḥ (!) dasakhataguravakaśakāethaḥ kāsī madheyī arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ (7) śrīkṛṣṇāya namo namaḥ || || śrīrāmāya namo namaḥ || || śrīnaraśīṃghāya (!) namo namḥ (!) ❁ (fol. 136r4-7)
notes: The colophon is in Hindi. 'mīti' is miti and 'līkhāḥ' is likhā. 'dasakhata' is dastkhat, 'handwriting/signature', so the phrase reads 'written in the hand of Guravakaśa (probably Gurbakhś) Kāyastha (kāetha), in Kāśī (kāsī madhye)'. The era is not named: 'saṃvat' with a Hindi date formula (agahana badī) points to Vikrama. Under the North Indian pūrṇimānta reckoning, Agahana badī 1 falls about late October or November 1767 CE. I did not verify the weekday. 'arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ' is unclear. It may name a locality in Kāśī (Haripura?) and a person Cirañjīvī, perhaps the owner or beneficiary. It may also be a corrupt blessing formula (cirañjīvī). Cirañjīvī is therefore recorded with role 'other' and low confidence.
review: p2: 'dasakhata' read as Hindi dastkhat 'handwriting/signature' (not part of the name); name kept as Guravakaśa, probably the Hindi name Gurbakhś (Gurubakhśa); confidence lowered to medium because the reading is not certain
p2: residence given as written (Kāśī) and normalized to Vārāṇasī in place
date: month normalized to Mārgaśīrṣa (agahana); paksa normalized to kṛṣṇa (badī); weekday to Saturday (śanaiścara)
place: normalized spelled Vārāṇasī
notes: expanded on dastkhat, the pūrṇimānta month reckoning, and the unclear 'arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ'

title: Bhūtaḍāmaratantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Wednesday 5 Jan 1859, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti bhūtaḍāmare mahātaṃtre yakṣasiddhisādhanavidhiḥ paṃcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || || śivaproktabhūtaḍāmarataṃtro yaṃ lalitāprarīyaśrīsūryānaṃdenālikhat || (!) śrī 1915 || pauṣe site śukladale viśāṣe (!) tithicaṃdrage || etatprāpte śubhadine sampūrṇam agamat śubham || (fol. 35r4-6)
notes: The colophon gives no era name ('śrī 1915'). It is taken as VS because NS 1915 is impossible and ŚS 1915 lies in the future. Pauṣa of VS 1915 falls in Dec 1858 to Jan 1859. 'tithicaṃdrage' is read as tithi = candra (1), i.e. śukla pratipad. 'viśāṣe (!)' most likely stands for Viśākhā. But the moon is not normally in Viśākhā on Pauṣa śukla 1, so the word may instead be a corruption of 'viśeṣe'. Lalitāprarīya stands for lalitāpurīya, 'of Lalitapur (Patan)'. It describes where the scribe is from, and the place of copying (catalogue: Latitapura, sic) is inferred from it. 'ayaṃ … ālikhat' is ungrammatical, as the cataloguer marked with (!).
review: p1 as_written trimmed to the name itself (sūryānaṃdena); residence given as lalitāprarīya (= lalitāpurīya, Patan)
tithi: 'tithicaṃdrage' read as candra = 1, i.e. pratipad (śukla 1), not just 'caṃdra'
nakshatra: viśāṣe (!) read as Viśākhā, with a note that this is astronomically doubtful
era: the colophon has no era name; VS is inferred, and this is now stated in notes; ce_approx changed to 1858/1859
place: noted that it is inferred from the scribe's residence, not stated as the place of copying

title: Merutantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Tuesday 20 Oct 1812, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti śrīrudrayāmale gāya〈ta〉trītattv[as]āre stavaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || śubham astu || saṃvat || 1869 || aśvini(!)māse śuklapakṣe tithau || 15 || bhaumavāsare || pratiliṣi(!)taṃ ma///veratharīyā || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ kṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || yad aśuddham(!) aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate || 1 || śrīmate rāmacaṃdrāya. (fol. 26r9–11)
notes: The scribe's name is damaged ('ma///veratharīyā'). The opening 'ma' could even be the start of 'mayā', so the personal name may be lost entirely. 'Tharīyā' looks like a family, clan or caste designation (cf. Nep. Tharī), but this is uncertain. The era is not stated explicitly; VS is assumed from the year 1869 and the catalogue. The weekday was not checked against the tithi. The quoted colophon closes a 'Gāyatrītattvasāra stava' attributed to the Rudrayāmala, not the Merutantra of the catalogue title; it may be an appended text, or the title may be wrong. The catalogue's 'King: Upendravikama' is not in the colophon. Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha ruled Nepal in VS 1869, so the catalogue field is doubtful and no reigning king is recorded. 'śrīmate rāmacaṃdrāya' is an invocation of the deity Rāma. 'yad aśuddham(!) aśuddhaṃ vā' is a corruption of the stock verse 'yad (a)śuddham śuddhaṃ vā'.
review: Scribe name: removed the invented capitalised stem 'Ma...veratharīyā'. The name is given as a lacuna-marked fragment '[ma]...vera Tharīyā', and 'tharīyā' may be a family or caste name. Confidence stays low.
Scribe evidence extended to include 'tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā'.
Date fields normalised: month Āśvina (written aśvini), pakṣa śukla, tithi 15 (pūrṇimā), weekday Tuesday (bhaumavāsara). VS 1869 = c. 1812 CE confirmed.

Notes expanded: the colophon names a Rudrayāmala Gāyatrītattvasāra stava, not Merutantra; 'Upendravikama' does not appear in the colophon and is not a known Nepalese ruler for VS 1869 (Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha reigned then), so no king was added.

title: Śāradātilaka
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Tuesday 4 Oct 1558, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīśāradātilake paṃcaviṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ || || śūbhaṃ || uduṃvaragoviṃdenālekhi ||………….. ………..|| saṃ. 1615 | kā. Va. 8 bhaumayuktāyā tithau || (fol. 224r8–10)
notes: 'saṃ. 1615' in a Devanagari manuscript is taken as Vikrama Saṃvat. If the year is Caitrādi, Kārttika kṛṣṇa 8 of VS 1615 falls in Oct/Nov 1558 CE; if it is Kārttikādi, it falls in Oct/Nov 1557 CE. 'kā. Va.' is read as kārttika vadi (dark fortnight), and 'bhaumayuktāyā' gives Tuesday. Uduṃvara (= Audumbara) is probably the scribe's community, lineage or family name (possibly the Audumbara brahmin group) rather than a personal name. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Uduṃvara Śrīgiviṃda', but the colophon reads 'goviṃdena', so Govinda is the right reading. A lacuna (dots) after 'ālekhi' may have held more names or details.
review: date.month: corrected the typo 'kāttika' to 'kārttika'
notes: added that the year could be 1557 or 1558 CE depending on the reckoning, and noted the catalogue's variant scribe name 'Śrīgiviṃda'

title: Śivārcanacandrikā
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Monday 7 Jul 1732, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śṛīsundarācāryyacaraṇāraviṃdadvadvāṃte vā śrīnivāsabhaṭṭeba viracitāyāṃ śrīśivārcanacaṃdrikāyāṣaṭcatvāriṃśaḥ parakāśaḥ || samātā śivārcanacandrikāḥ || yādṛśa (!) pustakaṃ………………………. ……………………………doṣo na dīyate || śrīśāke samvatsare 965 || śrīvikramasamvatsare 578 ? śrīkarisamvatsare 4833 nepālasamvatsare 852 | āṣāḍhaśuklacaturddaśī, mūlanakṣatra (!) aindrayoge caṃdravāsare saṃpūrṇam iti, bhaktapattanasthāna (!) lekhyate | (fol. 292v7–9)
notes: The colophon gives the date in four eras. Nepāla Saṃvat 852 (Āṣāḍha falls in 1732 CE) and Kali 4833 (4833−3101 = 1732) agree. Śaka 965 and Vikrama 578 do not: the expected figures are about ŚS 1654 and VS 1789. These two numbers are corrupt, either in the manuscript or in the cataloguer's transcription (the '?' after 578 may be the cataloguer's). The weekday (Monday) and the nakṣatra have not been checked against an ephemeris. Mūla on śukla 14 of Āṣāḍha is astronomically plausible. The scribe and the commissioner are not named; the passage after 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ' is only the stock scribal verse. Sundarācārya and Śrīnivāsa Bhaṭṭa are connected with the composition of the Śivārcanacandrikā, not with this copy. The author's name, 'śrīnivāsabhaṭṭeba', should read śrīnivāsabhaṭṭena, and 'dvadvāṃte vā' should read dvandvāntevāsinā.

notes: The colophon is in Newari. It reads roughly '[Sumatijaya]jitāmitramalladeva-sana (agentive) dhā(?) pustaka dayakā (had made) Bhagirāma pramāṇa-yā velasa (at the time of)'. 'jayatitāmitra' is a corrupt spelling of jayajitāmitra, and 'malladea' of malladeva. The king is Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1673–1696), whose full style is Sumatijayajitāmitramalla. 'dhā' is unclear: it may be a corruption of thva ('this') or part of a word for the type of text. 'pramaāna' is taken as the office title pramāṇa/pramāna; Bhagirāma's exact office is uncertain. NS 810 is consistent with Jitāmitra's reign. The place is not stated, but Bhaktapur is likely given the king.

title: Śaktisaṅgamatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_raw: śaradi apani paṃcāṅkendge īṣa śūbhre ahi tithi gurū pāre
colophon: iti śrīmadakṣobhyamahogratārāsamvāde tārāsūkte vrahamajātivarṇane daśamaḥ paṭalaḥ śaradi apani paṃcāṅkendge īṣa śūbhre ahi tithi gurū pāre śakti saṃgākhyataṃtraṃ vilikhatya śūbhamaṃ vedvāś dhanāyaṃ suviñair anativipulavudhir ṭōḍarānandasaṃjñaḥ śubham astu śāṃtir astu lekhakapāṭhakayo (!) bhavyaṃ bhūyāstām samāptaḥ (fol. 177r2–4)
notes: The colophon is a corrupt verse. 'apani paṃcāṅkendge' = avani(1) pañca(5) aṅka(9) indu(1); read right to left this gives 1951. The colophon names no era. VS 1951 (= 1894 CE) is the likely reading for a Devanagari manuscript; Śaka 1951 would be impossible. 'ahi' = 8 (serpent), so the date is Āśvina (Iṣa) śukla aṣṭamī, a Thursday, which fits śarad. The name Ṭoḍarānanda (or Ṭoḍara-, depending on how '-ānandasaṃjñaḥ' is parsed) is taken as the scribe, who describes himself modestly as 'anativipulabuddhi'. The name is unusual and the passage around it ('vedvāś dhanāyaṃ suviñair') is garbled. Be careful not to confuse it with the well-known compendium Ṭoḍarānanda. The phrase 'lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ' is a standard blessing formula and does not name anyone.

title: Saṃmohanatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Tuesday 28 Jun 1892, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīmad akṣobhyamahogratārāsamvāde śaṃmohanataṃtradvītīyakhaṇḍe vrahmajātivarṇane ekādaśamaḥ paṭalaḥ || 11 || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā…. ……………. || śrīvikramasamvat 1949 sāla śrīnepālasamvat 1012 miti āṣāḍhaśukla 4 aśleṣā valiyān joga maṃgalavāra. Tasadīna leṣaka. Śahara mṃktāpurai pācheyā śrīharakumārajāra dvijātmaja śrīāśvinīkumārarāja vipraṇa 21 saṃphudayekā || śubham sarvadā śubham || || || (fol. 41r8–11)
notes: The colophon is in Nepali. VS 1949 and NS 1012 agree (both 1892 CE), and Āṣāḍha śukla 4 falls on about Tuesday 28 June 1892, which matches maṃgalavāra. 'mṃktāpurai' is most likely Muktāpura. It could be a misreading of Bhaktāpura (Bhaktapur), since म and भ are easily confused, but this is not certain. 'pācheyā' may name a locality or tole. The father's name 'harakumārajāra' is corrupt: it could be Harakumārarāja (with metathesis, matching the son's '-kumārarāja') or contain 'Jhā'. 'vipraṇa 21 saṃphudayekā' is unclear and may be a garbled 'vipreṇa … sampūrṇa garekā' ('completed by the vipra'). 'Tasadīna leṣaka' = 'tas dina lekhaka' ('the scribe on that day'), which confirms p2 as the scribe.

title: Kulavṛtti
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: ≈ 1632 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: || ādyakhaṃṇḍasaṃpūrṇṇaḥ || || śubham astu sarvvadā || || saṃvat 752 thvadaṃ śrī 3 bhavānīśaṃkarapritina śrīkālidāsena saṃcaya yāṅā | umeśāprītaye tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ | anena puṇyayogena tayor anter ayo ʼstute || || (fol. 169v9–11)
purpose: for the pleasure of Bhavānīśaṅkara (Umeśa); merit (puṇyayoga)
notes: The era is not named. NS is assumed because the script is Newari and the colophon is in Newari (NS 752 ≈ 1632 CE). The text says Kālidāsa compiled (saṃcaya yāṅā / saṃcita) the tantra in NS 752 ('thvadaṃ' = 'this year'). This may record when the compilation was made, so the manuscript could be his own or an autograph copy. However, the colophon does not explicitly call him the scribe or commissioner. The catalogue gives Pūrṇānaṃdanātha as scribe, but that name does not appear in this colophon; perhaps it comes from elsewhere in the manuscript. The final pāda 'tayor anter ayo ʼstute' is corrupt; perhaps 'tayor antar ... astu te'. Bhavānīśaṅkara and Umeśa are deities and are not counted as persons.
review: Kālidāsa: roles changed from commissioner+owner to author (compiler). 'saṃcaya yāṅā' and 'tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ' mean he compiled the work. They are not commissioning or ownership formulas. Confidence lowered to medium.
Evidence extended to include 'tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ'.
Purpose rephrased in English.

title: Cikitsāmṛta
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: śrīsarvavidyānidhāna kavīndrācārya sa………. ci[[ki]]tsāmṛtapustakam || rāmāya namaḥ || || (cikīrśīte) (!) karmaṇicakrapāṇe ‥‥‥ tāneva sāhāya sampat || pāṃcālajāyā paṭalaṃvittāne (!) madhye samaṃ yaṃ na tu nīnavedmā (!) || || | (fol.134v3–5)
notes: The quoted passage is an ownership note in the standard form used by the library of the Benares scholar Kavīndrācārya Sarasvatī (fl. c. 1600–1675): 'sarvavidyānidhāna kavīndrācārya sa[rasvatīnām] … pustakam'. The name breaks off after 'sa…', so the restoration to Sarasvatī is a guess, though a very likely one. The ownership note means the copy existed before c. 1675, but no date is given. The verse that follows ('cikīrṣite karmaṇi cakrapāṇe…') is a corrupt stanza and contains no persons. The catalogue fields 'Scribe: milhaṇa' and 'Place of Copying: ḍhillikānagara' do not appear in the quoted text. They very probably come from the author's own colophon: Milhaṇa composed the Cikitsāmṛta at Ḍhillikā (Delhi) in the 13th century (traditionally VS 1281 ≈ 1224 CE). If so, Milhaṇa is the author, not the scribe of this copy, and Delhi is where the text was composed, not where this copy was made. Neither has been added here as a person or place connected with the copy; this should be checked against the full catalogue entry.

title: Nāḍīparīkṣā
subject: Āyurveda
date_raw: Saṃvat 1773 jeṣṭhamāse dinagatā 29 vāra 1 thithau 2 nakṣatra 20 sudī saptamyāṃ sanaiścare likhitaṃ
date_note: = Wednesday 27 May 1716, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti samrāḍagnicit sūryadāsātmaja rāmacaṃdra somayāji kṛtaṃ sāḍyādi (!) parīkṣyāprakaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ || samvat 1773 varṣe jeṣṭamāse (!) dinagatā 29 vāre 1 tithau 2 nakṣatre 2 sudī saptamyāṃ sanaiścarai (!) liṣitaṃ sāḍyādi (!) parīkṣāprakaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ || yādṛsī pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādrisi pustakaṃ mayā yadi suddham asuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo nadīyateḥ (!) || || śrīsarasvatyai namaḥ || || śubha || || || || || || || || || ( fol.23r2-4)
notes: The scribe (Gṛhapati Jaisī), the king (prithipati sāha) and the place ('dharmmānadī taṭagrāme gorṣeśvarasthāne') are in the catalogue fields but not in the colophon quoted from fol. 23r2–4. They probably come from a part of the manuscript the cataloguer did not quote, so p3 and p4 are kept at low confidence. The catalogue's identification of the king as Pṛthvīvīravikrama Śāha (r. 1881–1911) is wrong. VS 1773 = 1716 CE, which falls in the reign of Pṛthvīpati Śāha of Gorkha (r. c. 1669–1716). 'Saṃvat' is read as VS because the copy comes from the Gorkha/Śāha milieu. The numbers 'dinagatā 29', 'vāre 1', 'tithau 2' and 'nakṣatre 2' don't fit the named day 'sudī saptamyāṃ śanaiścare' (śukla saptamī, Saturday). They may be counts of elapsed days or ghaṭīs; their meaning is unclear. The catalogue gives the nakṣatra as 20, the colophon as 2. In 'samrāḍagnicit-sūryadāsātmaja' the titles samrāṭ/agnicit grammatically belong to Sūryadāsa, but they may be meant for the author Rāmacandra. 'sāḍyādi' is a corruption of 'nāḍyādi'.

title: Madana[pāla]vinodanighaṇṭu
subject: Āyurveda
date_note: = Monday 13 Apr 1699, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīmadanapā[la]viracite madanavinode nighaṃṭau praśastivargaś caturdaśaḥ | | samāptaś cāyaṃ nighaṃṭuḥ | | dṛṅnetracārvāha śake madhauśitau pakṣe maheśasyatithau kaver dine nārānidhisvasya vilokanārthaṃ saṃprālikhatturṇam imaṃ nighaṃṭuṃ | yathāpratilikhitaṃ sadbhiḥ saṃśodhanīyaṃ | śubhamastu satatam | | ❁ | |śivaprasādāc chubham astu | trikaṭuka ajamodāsaiṃdhavaṃ jirake he samadhāraṇādhṛtānām aṣṭamohiṃgughāgaḥ ||(fol. 39r1-3)
purpose: svavilokanārtham (copied by the scribe for his own study)
notes: The chronogram 'dṛṅnetracārvāha' is corrupt. Dṛk = 2 and netra = 2. The rest ('cārvāha') cannot be resolved with confidence; read right to left, the year ends in ..22. The cataloguer's Śāke 1621 is marked with a query and does not fit a reading of dṛk = 2 as the units digit. ŚS 1622 (CE c. 1700) is equally possible, and ce_approx 1699 is only approximate. Maheśa's tithi is taken as caturdaśī (Śiva's tithi), as the cataloguer does. Kavi = Śukra, so the weekday is Friday. The scribe's name 'Nārānidhi' may be a corrupt form, for example of Nārāyaṇa or Nārāṇidhi. The Āyurvedic recipe (trikaṭuka...) after the colophon is a later addition and names no persons. The author Madanapāla is the king of Kāṣṭhā who composed the text, not a reigning king at the time of copying.

title: Rugviniścaya
subject: Āyurveda
date_note: = Wednesday 11 Jan 1792, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmādhavakaraviracitarugviniścayaḥ saṃgrahaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ || ||… saṃvat 1848 mīṭī (!) māgha vadī 2 vāra budhavāra || || kāśyāṃ madhye || || śrīrāmacaṃdrāya namaḥ || śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ || śrīgopālo jayati || śrīhanumataye || śrīlakṣmī najīāya(!)namaḥ || ❁ ❁ ❁ śrī śrī rājārāmacaṃdrāya nama (!) || || (fol. 92v6-93r1)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Kṛṣṇadāsa, but that name is not in the quoted colophon. It may be in the part left out at the ellipsis '…'. Because it can't be checked, Kṛṣṇadāsa is not added as a person. The era is not named. VS is assumed because the copy was made in Kāśī and because of the year range. The CE year is given as 1792, not 1791 (VS−57), because Māgha of VS 1848 (counting the year from Caitra) falls in early 1792. 'mīṭī' is Nepali miti, meaning 'date'. 'śrīlakṣmī najīāya(!)' is probably a corruption of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa. That name, and Rāmacandra, Kṛṣṇa, Gopāla, Hanumat and 'rājārāmacaṃdra', are deities in the closing invocations, not people.
review: ce_approx changed from 1791 to 1792. VS 1848 began in Caitra 1791, so Māgha vadī 2 of that year falls in January or February 1792. The simple VS−57 formula gives 1791.

title: Śāraṅgadharasaṃhitā
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrīśārṅgadharacikitsā samāpta(!)|| śrībhavānīśaṃkarābhyāṃ namaḥ || śubham astu || 6 || śrīkalyāṇam astu || mohanajibhahālajamiṭhālahena svārthaṃ paropakārārthaṃ śārṅadharākhyaṃ pustakaṃ yal likhitaṃ tat śrīmatkāśyāṃ kṣayasavatsare pauṣamāsi śuklapakṣe trītiyāyāṃ(!) samāptaṃ || || śubhaṃ bhavatu || śrīsadāśivārpaṇam astu (fol.155r6-11)
notes: The scribe's name is a single instrumental compound (-ena) and is probably corrupt or a vernacular (Hindi/Gujarati/Marwari) name. One possible segmentation is Mohanajī + bhahā(?) + lālaja (born of Lāla?) + Miṭhālā(la), with miṭhālahena perhaps an error for miṭhālālena. This would make the scribe one Mīṭhālāla, possibly identified through Mohanajī or Lāla(jī), but the segmentation is uncertain, so the full string is kept as the name. The year is given only as the Jovian saṃvatsara Kṣaya, without a numbered era. Under southern reckoning, Pauṣa of a Kṣaya year falls around Dec–Jan 1866/67, 1926/27, and so on (1986/87 is too late for this collection), so ce_approx is left empty. The book was copied at Kāśī, not in Nepal. Both svārthaṃ and paropakārārthaṃ are stated, so the scribe is treated as both scribe and owner.

colophon: || śrī śāke 1629 māse 7 tithau 30 vāsare 3 dinagatā 13 litaṃ (12\u2 2 1 dha 4ī) rmmaṇāḥ || tailādrakṣe jalādrakṣedrakṣe[t] śītalabandhanāt || mūrkhahaste nadātavyaṃ rvaṃ(!) vadati pustakāt(!) || bhagnapṛṣṭī(!) kaṭī grīvā vadhū(!) dṛṣṭiradhomukhaṃ || kaṣṭēna likhitaṃ graṃthaṃ yatnenaḥ paripālayet || śubhaṃ || || rāma rāmeti rāmeti rame rāme manorame || sahastra(!) nāmatā tulyaṃ rāmanāma varānaṇe (!) || || (fol.117v5-118r2)
notes: The scribe's name is garbled in the catalogue: 'litaṃ (12\u2 2 1 dha 4ī) rmmaṇāḥ'. 'litaṃ' is probably 'li[khi]taṃ' and 'rmmaṇāḥ' is the end of '-śarmaṇā', an instrumental with a stray visarga. So the scribe was a brahmin whose name contains something like 'dha' and 'ī'. The name itself cannot be recovered. 'dinagatā 13' may mean day 13 of a solar month, which would make month 7 = Tulā. It may instead mean 13 ghaṭikās elapsed. Month numbering is therefore ambiguous. ŚS 1629 = 1707 CE. This matches the catalogue field, but the date has not been checked against an ephemeris. The verses after the date ('tailād rakṣe…', 'bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭīgrīvā…', 'rāma rāmeti…') are stock scribal verses. They name no persons.

colophon: iti śrīsiddhanāgārjunaviracite kakṣapuṭe atyāhāra saṃgopāṃga nāma viṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ || || || (1) samvat 17(8)1 nesa 905 kārtikamāse śuklapakṣe dvādaśī ravīvāsare (!) anunakṣatre sumūharte (!) ne(2)pāladeśe bhavānīśaṃkara bhaṭena likhītaṃ (!) || śubhamastu yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā (!) tādṛśaṃ likhi(3)taṃ mayā yadi śubham 0aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate || 1 || śubhaṃ bhavatu || || ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ || ||…(fol. 47r16–47v3)
notes: The colophon gives two eras. The NS date is primary: NS 905 Kārtika śukla 12 = c. Oct/Nov 1784 CE. The other figure, 'samvat 17(8)1', doesn't fit. As VS it gives c. 1724 CE, and as ŚS it gives c. 1859 CE. The equivalents of NS 905 would be VS 1841 or ŚS 1706. The catalogue's 'SS 1721' (= c. 1799 CE) also conflicts with NS 905. Either the samvat figure is corrupt or the cataloguer misread it. The nakṣatra 'anunakṣatre' may stand for Anurādhā, but the moon would hardly be in Anurādhā on Kārtika śukla 12 (more likely Revatī/Aśvinī), so the reading is doubtful. 'bhaṭena' stands for bhaṭṭena, so bhaṭṭa is taken as a brahmin surname or title. The scribe's formulaic 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā…' verse adds no persons.

title: Jvaratimirabhāskara
subject: Āyurveda
date_note: = Thursday 6 Feb 1766, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti kāyasthacuṃḍakṛte, jvaratimirabhāskare jvaropadravacikitsā(3)paripūrṇṇatā nāma ṣoḍaśo dhyāyaḥ || || samāpto yaṃ jvaratimirabhāskaro nā(4)ma graṃthaḥ || || rasāṣṭavasbhir llakṣye, yāte nepālahāyane || māghe māsy aśite pakṣe, dvādaśyāṅ guruvāsa(5)re || jvarastimirahaṃsākhyaṃ, (!) raṃmyāsyākhyena (!) dhīmatāḥ (!) || vyalekhīdaṃ hitārthāya, sutārthaṃ jagatā (!) mudā || || (158r1) atha nepālabhākhā || samvat 886 māghakṛṣṇayā dvādasi,(!) bṛhaspatīvāra thva kuhnu vaidya bhinakhvāra(2)na, thva jvarastimirabhāskara (!) nāma grantha coya sidhakādina, thvaverasa, gorakhārina, kiṃdosa, segu(3)sa, hnuti sathā nātayāo edeśa sagheraya, yāṅāḍo dukhaviyāo tao juro || || śubha || || (fol. 157v2-158r3)
purpose: hitārthāya, sutārthaṃ jagatāṃ mudā: for the benefit (of the world) and for his son's sake (reading uncertain)
notes:
The chronogram rasa (6), aṣṭa (8), vasu (8), read right to left, gives NS 886. This matches 'samvat 886' in the Newari part. Māgha kṛṣṇa of NS 886 falls in early 1766 CE. The weekday was not checked by calculation.

The Sanskrit verse names the scribe 'ramyāsya' (corrupt 'raṃmyāsyākhyena dhīmatāḥ'). This is a Sanskrit rendering of the Newari name Bhinakhvāra: bhina = good/beautiful, khvāra = face. The '-na' in 'bhinakhvārana' is the Newari ergative ending.

The Newari note says the copy was finished at a time of hardship: the Gorkhalis set up posts at Kindol (kiṃdosa) and Segu (segusa, probably the Svayambhū area) and surrounded the country. This fits the Gorkha siege of the Kathmandu Valley in 1766.

The catalogue gives Yoginīpattana as the place and Rājamalla as the king. Neither appears in the quoted colophon, so both are left empty here. Also, in NS 886 Kathmandu was ruled by Jayaprakāśa Malla, so the catalogue's king field is doubtful.

'sutārthaṃ' could mean 'for his son'. No son is named, and no owner is stated.
review: Author's name normalized from 'Cuṃḍa' to 'Cuṇḍa' (the anusvāra before ḍ stands for ṇ).
Bhinakhvāra's evidence now also cites the Sanskrit verse 'raṃmyāsyākhyena (!) dhīmatāḥ (!) || vyalekhīdaṃ'.
Purpose rewritten in normalized form, with a note that the reading is uncertain.
Notes expanded: chronogram checked, Newari passage explained, catalogue place and king fields flagged as not supported by the colophon.
Date and the rest of the first reading confirmed.

title: Nakulacikitsā
subject: Aśvāyurveda
date_note: = Saturday 22 Oct 1689, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti nakula cikitsite aśvaśālā kathanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || śāke 1553 tathā saṃvat 1688 pravarttamāne śrāvaṇakṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ 11 jīvavāsare śālihotrasya pustakaṃ samāptaṃ || || ādarśa doṣānmati vibhramādvā tvarā viśeṣāllikhanasya vegāt | tanmārjjayitvā pariśodhayaṃtī kṣamaṃ tu saṃtaḥ khalu lekhakasya ||| śubhaṃ || || oṃ || rāmāya namaḥ || || || śrī śrī sumati jayajitāmitramalladevasana thva pustaka dayakā, bhāgirāma paramānayāvelasa, saṃvat 810 kārtika śudi 9 (fol.27r1-7)
notes: The colophon has two dates. (1) An inherited date, probably from the exemplar: śāke 1553 tathā saṃvat 1688, Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 11, jīvavāsara (Thursday). Śaka 1553 + 78 = 1631 and VS 1688 − 57 = 1631, so the two eras agree (July/Aug 1631 CE). (2) The date of this copy: NS 810 Kārtika śukla 9, about Oct/Nov 1689 CE. That falls within Jitāmitra Malla's reign at Bhaktapur (1673–1696). 'śālihotrasya pustakaṃ' names the text tradition (Śālihotra, the hippiatric author), not a person connected with this copy. The catalogue lists Bhāgīrāma as scribe, but 'bhāgirāma paramānayāvelasa' only dates the copy to 'the time when Bhāgīrāma was pramāṇa/pradhāna (minister)'. Bhāgīrāma is known as a pradhāna of Bhaktapur under Jitāmitra Malla. The scribe is not named. The place of copying is not stated, though Bhaktapur is likely from the king.
review: p1: name changed to the standard regnal stem 'Jitāmitramalladeva'. 'sumati jaya' is part of the royal style, so it moves to titles. Roles king + commissioner kept: 'thva pustaka dayakā' means 'had this book made'.

p2 Bhāgīrāma: the vague role 'other' is removed and only 'minister' is kept. 'paramāna' is read as pramāṇa/pradhāna, an office title. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's 'Scribe' field is wrong. Confidence raised to high because the Newari is clear.

The relation p2→p1 has been changed from under_reign_of to servant_of. That is a judgment call; he is a minister of the reigning king.

title: Aśvavaidyakaśāstra
subject: Aśvāyurveda
date_note: = Thursday 20 Feb 1687, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: mahāsāmanta śrījayadatta kṛtam aśvavaidyakaśāstraḥ samāptaḥ || (!) yādṛśaṃ pustaṃ dṛstvā (!) tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mama | (!) yadi suddhamasuddhaṃ (!) vā mama doṣo nadīyateḥ (!) || || jayadattanāma pustakaṃ śrī śrīhemantamalla varmanā svakarena likhitam idaṃ saṃpūrṃ || || samvat 807 phālguṇa māse śuklapakṣe navamyāṃ thithau rohinī (!) nakṣatre viskambhayoge vṛhaspativāsare thva kuhnu saṃpūrṇa yāṅādi juroṃ || śrī śrī śrī revantasuprasaṃnostu || śubham astu || (fol.48v1–4)
notes: The era is not named in the colophon ('samvat 807'), but the Newari script and Newari text make Nepal Saṃvat certain. Phālguna of NS 807 falls in about February–March 1687 CE. In the colophon the scribe's name is 'śrī śrīhemantamalla varmanā', which the catalogue gives as 'Hemanatalāla varmmā'. I follow the colophon text and read the name as Hemantamalla, with varman as a surname or title. The name could also be split as Hemanta Malla Varmā, so confidence is medium. 'jayadattanāma pustakaṃ' means the book is called after its author Jayadatta; it does not name an owner. The Newari line 'thva kuhnu saṃpūrṇa yāṅādi juroṃ' says the copy was completed on that day. Revanta, named in the closing invocation, is a deity and is left out. Rohiṇī on śukla navamī of Phālguna is a little early for that tithi (Mṛgaśiras or Ārdrā would be more usual), so the nakṣatra may be slightly off. I have not checked it by calculation.

Nakṣatra spelling normalized to Rohiṇī, yoga to Viṣkambha
Notes expanded: explains the varman title, the CE reckoning for Phālguna, the Newari completion formula, and why the Revanta invocation is excluded

title: Nakulacikitsā
subject: Aśvāyurveda
date_note: = Thursday 27 Jan 1678, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year read as current
colophon: iti nakulacikitsite aśvaśālākathanaṃ nāma śoḍaśo ʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || (fol.89v1–2) śrī śrīhemantamallanatha[[va]]tā nimirttina (!) dayakā || kayaṃgalana pitāṃ viya mate va || mahādullaṃbha vastu || samvat 799 māghamāsa śukla pakṣa śrīpañcamyāṃ tithau revatī nakṣetre gurudine || śubham astu sarvvadā || (fol.89v5–7)
purpose: for his own sake (thavatā nimittina); sons are told not to give it away
notes: The Newari reads: 'śrī śrī Hemantamalla-na thava-tā nimittina dayakā' = 'made by Hemantamalla for his own sake'. 'nimirttina (!)' stands for nimittina. The cataloguer's [[va]] is an inserted akṣara, giving thavatā. 'dayakā' (made, had made) usually marks the person who had a copy produced, so commissioner + owner is the more likely reading. The catalogue calls him the scribe, though, and dayakā alone does not rule that out. 'kayaṃgalana pitāṃ viya mate va || mahādullaṃbha vastu' = '[my] sons must not give it out(side); [it is] a very rare object'. The double śrī suggests a royal or noble person, but he is not called king, and no Malla ruler of that name reigned in NS 799 (Pārthivendra in Kathmandu, Śrīnivāsa in Patan, Jitāmitra in Bhaktapur). He may have been a prince or a member of the nobility. Date: NS 799 + 880 = 1678/79; Māgha śukla 5 (Vasanta/Śrīpañcamī) falls in Jan/Feb 1679 CE. Revatī as the nakṣatra is astronomically plausible for that tithi; the weekday has not been checked.

title: Śālihotra
subject: Aśvāyurveda
date_note: = Friday 28 Jun 1686, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || ❖ saṃvat 806 āṣāḍhaśukla saptamī śukravāra thva kuhnu, sohnemhavantā dvija śrīdevaśaṃkaraṇa (!), thva ṣaḍaṃśāstra (!) coya dhunakā dina joro śubham || revantāya namonamaḥ || || ○ || || saṃºº 902 phālguṇa śukla caturthī thva kuhnu śrīlakṣmīpati ju oṃ rāyā agnihotra mākasa śrīlakṣṃīśvarī agnihotrī sativana; thvana hṅāsati oṃ sivamadū(!) notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Bhavāniśaṃkara, but the colophon reads 'dvija śrīdevaśaṃkaraṇa (!)', i.e. Devaśaṃkara in the Newari agentive. The cataloguer's (!) may mean that the name is doubtful. 'sohnemhavantā' before 'dvija' is unclear. It could be a place or epithet, or a misreading. 'ṣaḍaṃśāstra (!)' is probably a corruption, perhaps of ṣaḍaṅga-śāstra or a name for the Śālihotra text. A second, later note dated NS 902 (≈ CE 1782), Phālguna śukla 4, records an event involving Lakṣmīpati, apparently his death. It also records that Lakṣmīśvarī, the agnihotrī who kept the agnihotra, became sati; 'thvana hṅāsati ... sivamadū' perhaps means 'five days after this ... died'. This note says nothing about the copying, and these persons may be later owners or their family. The NS 806 weekday has not been verified.

title: Karaṭikautuka
subject: Gajāyurveda
date_note: = Sunday 1 Dec 1591, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: || iti śrīkāyastha balabhadrātmajagopāladāsaviracite karaṭikautuke nakhataḥ sādhyā ʼsādhyanakhottamalakṣaṇa dvijamukhajātilakṣaṇāraṇyadantisādhukaraṇa hastivāhana hastisaṃkīrṇajātidaṃtidoṣakharaśītalīkaraṇa jalodgārajāṭharanāḍīsvaraviśeṣalakṣaṇa viṣacikitsā hasticakragajapraśaṃsā gajalūtākavacādikas tṛtīya ullāsaḥ | | samāpto ʼyaṃ karaṭikautukanāmā graṃthaḥ || || abde nāmgayugāṃgaśītakiraṇe 1648 taiṣetithau pakṣatau 1 kṛṣṇāyā minavāsare mṛgaśiraḥ sādhyollasat kaulave saṃpūrṇaṃ kṛtavān ayaṃ gajahitāyājñām avāpyāvanī pālādeḥ karikautukaṃ balisuto gopālanāmā ʼvanau || 1 || na sthāyi caṃcalaṃ varṣma tanujānām iha kṣitau cirasthāyyakṣaraṃ jñātvā ʼkarot karaṭikautukam || 2 || nindantu durjanāḥ sarve stutiṃ kurvaṃtu sajjanāḥ samam evāṃjaliṃ tebhyo badhvā ʼkāri dvipākṣaram || 3 || śubham || likhitaṃ jagannāthena śrīmad raṇabahādūrasenārthaṃ | śubhaṃ | (fol.54r1–9)
notes: The only date in the colophon is in the author's verse (saṃpūrṇaṃ kṛtavān ... gopālanāmā). The chronogram nāga 8, yuga 4, aṅga 6, śītakiraṇa 1, read right to left, gives 1648, which matches the numerals. So 1648 is when Gopāladāsa finished composing the text, not when this copy was made. The catalogue's 'Date of Copying: SAM 1648' is therefore probably wrong, and this copy is undated and must be later than 1648. No era is named: VS 1648 would be about 1591 CE and ŚS 1648 about 1726 CE, so ce_approx is left empty. 'kṛṣṇāyā minavāsare' is read as 'kṛṣṇāyām inavāsare' (Sunday). 'balisuto' in the verse is taken as a short form of Balabhadra's son. The king whose permission the author obtained (ājñām avāpyāvanīpālāt) is not named. Raṇabahādūrasena, for whom Jagannātha copied the manuscript, is presumably a Sena ruler; the catalogue gives 'King: Raṇabahādura'. The colophon gives him no royal title, so he is recorded as beneficiary only. He may also have commissioned the copy, but the colophon does not say so.

title: Vājalakṣaṇa

notes: The era is given explicitly as Śaka (śrīśakābde 1729), so the date is ŚS 1729 = 1807 CE (April–May, with the sun in Aries). The catalogue's 'SAM 1729' is misleading: read as Vikrama it would give 1672 CE. Chronogram: 'navadalananagacaṃdrais' = nava (9), dala(na) (2; probably a corruption of nayana = 2), naga (7), candra (1); read right to left this gives 1729, which matches the numeral. 'kriya' is the zodiac name for Aries (Meṣa). The text calls itself 'vājahotra', but the catalogue title is Vājalakṣaṇa. The name could also be read as two words, Śiva Nṛsiṃha.
review: No substantive changes. Notes now explain the chronogram (nava 9, dala/nayana 2, naga 7, candra 1; read right to left as 1729) and that 'dinakara kriyasaṃsthe' gives a solar month (sun in Aries), not a lunar month name.

title: Agnipurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 14 Nov 1645, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: pūrṇimānta months
colophon: || || ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe purāṇamāhātmyaṃ triśatādhikaekonasaptatitamo dhyāyo āgneyapurāṇaṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || || 369 || || śrīkṛṣṇārppaṇam astu || || śreyo 'stu saṃvat 766 mārggakṛṣṇa 11 aiji 3 sacocakājuro śubhaṃ || || (fol. 297v3-4)
notes: The catalogue's scribe 'Sacocakā?' comes from 'sacocakājuro'. This is most likely a corrupt or misread Newari phrase, perhaps for '(sa) coyakā juro' ('was caused to be written' / 'had it copied'), and not a personal name, so no scribe can be identified. The era is not stated: 'saṃvat 766' with a Newari phrase and Newari script means Nepāla Saṃvat. 'aiji 3' is probably a weekday notation (3 = Tuesday), but the meaning of 'aiji' is unclear. title: Viṣṇupurāṇa and Vaiṣṇavākūṭacandrikāṭīkā
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Monday 18 Oct 1790, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: [Mūla] iti śrīviṣṇupurāṇe pārāśarasaṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭheṃ ʼśe ʼṣṭamodhyāyaḥ || || 8 || samāptaṃ cedaṃ śrīviṣṇupurāṇaṃ śubham || (fol.409r7) [Ṭīkā] iti śrīratnagarbhabhaṭṭācāryaracitāyāṃ śrīmadvaiṣṇavākūṭacandrikāyāṃ ṣaṣṭheṃśe ʼṣṭamodhyāyaḥ || || varṣe śailasaripatībharajanīkāṃtair mite tīkṣṇagau kanyārāśim upāgate ʼmaladale some vivasvattithau || svasti śrīyuvabhūpater likhitavān viṣṇoḥ purāṇaṃbahā- dūrasyā ʼvanidevajaḥ śivanidhir nāmājñayā prabhoḥ || 1 || yuvarājavareṇa ropiteyaṃ janatāyāṃ karuṇakaṭākṣasekaiḥ || karuṇāvaruṇālayena tūrṇaṃ tarūṇām apy adhunā vidhīyatām || 2 || || ❁ || || || || ❁ || || || || ❁ || || || || || || || || || || (fol.409r8-11)
purpose: copied by order of the yuvabhūpati Bahādur
notes: The chronogram reads śaila 7, saritpati 4, ibha 8, rajanīkānta 1; read right to left, this gives 1847. The colophon does not name an era. VS is inferred because the date (1790 CE) fits the Gorkhā court of Bahādur. Śaka 1847 (1925 CE) would not fit. Tīkṣṇagu (the Sun) in Kanyā, the bright fortnight (amaladala) and Monday (soma) point to amānta Āśvina śukla. 'Vivasvattithi' is ambiguous. As a number-word, vivasvat = 12 (dvādaśī). As the tithi ruled by Sūrya, it would be 7 (saptamī). A rough mean-lunation calculation puts the new moon at about 8 Sept 1790 and the Kanyā saṅkrānti at about 13 Sept. On that basis Monday 20 Sept 1790 falls on or near śukla 12, while saptamī (14–15 Sept) falls on a Tuesday or Wednesday. So 12 is preferred, but this is not verified with exact tables. Who 'yuvabhūpati Bahādur' is remains uncertain. It is most likely the regent Bahādur Śāha (Pṛthvīnārāyaṇ's son, regent 1785–94). However, 'yuvabhūpati' could also mean the young king Raṇa Bahādur Śāha, who was about 15 in 1790. The catalogue is wrong to call Avanideva the scribe and Śivanidhi the donor. The text says Śivanidhi, son of Avanideva (avanidevajaḥ), copied the book by order of the prince. Verse 2 is a benedictory verse to the yuvarāja. The compound 'purāṇaṃbahādūrasyā' is a word-division artefact: purāṇaṃ + bahādūrasya.

colophon: iti śrīskaṃdapurāṇe brahmottarakhaṃḍe purāṇaśravaṇamahimā nāma dvāviṃśo dhyāyaḥ || 22 || || adṛṣṭa ... khalu lekhakasya || 1 || saṃvat 1775 varṣe bhādrapadamāse śuklapakṣe paurṇimāsyāṃ kavi(!)vāsare likhitam idaṃ pustaka bhavatyāṃ(!) dvivedinā kānhajīkena vā someśvareṇa || śrīr astu || lekhaṣapāṭhakau śubhaṃ bhaviṣīyāstāṃ || (fol. 69v4–9)
notes: The text reads 'dvivedinā kānhajīkena vā someśvareṇa'. 'someśvareṇa' is in the instrumental case like the scribe's name. That allows three readings: (a) a second name for the scribe ('Kānhajī alias Someśvara'); (b) a corrupt place reference such as 'vā(stavyena) someśvare', meaning 'resident of Someśvara', which is what the catalogue's place field suggests; (c) a second scribe, which is least likely. I recorded one scribe and gave Someśvara as a possible residence or place. The word 'bhavatyāṃ(!)' is corrupt and unclear. 'Kavi' is a standard name for Śukra, so the weekday is Friday. I did not check that weekday against VS 1775 Bhādrapada pūrṇimā (about August/September 1718 CE). The date is in Vikrama saṃvat, which fits a Devanagari manuscript from outside Nepal; the name 'Kānhajī' and the Gujarati/Rajasthani title 'dvivedī' point the same way.
review: p1 name normalised to Kānhajī: the -ka in 'kānhajīkena' is a suffix added to the name, and the catalogue gives Kānhajī. Confidence lowered to medium.

Removed p2 'Someśvara' as a separate scribe. 'vā someśvareṇa' most likely gives the scribe's place (the catalogue treats it as the place of copying) or another name for him. It is unlikely to be a second scribe. The doubt is recorded in notes and under place.
Place: entered 'someśvareṇa' as the possible place of copying (the catalogue gives Someśvara). Left the modern identification empty.
Weekday: kavi- is a name of Śukra (Venus), so kavivāsara means Friday. The (!) is probably unnecessary.
Purpose stays empty; the closing blessing on scribe and reader names no one.

title: Nepālavaṃśāvalī
subject: Itihāsa
date_note: ≈ 1910 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: yo vasāvari naka vahila atha nanivasnyā (!) ranavirasiṃha vānā inakā putra. harṣa bahādūraḥ ina ikā manasuvāle yo vaṃsāvari vanāyāḥ yo vaṃsāvari leṣanyāḥ pīvahālako pātravaṃsubābu manirājale yo vaṃsāvari lekhidiyā yo vaṃsāvari kasaile lobhanagarnū nepāli saṃvat 1030 miti+++++++siddha bhayo - - suubha (!) - (fol. 71v8–11)
purpose: made at the wish of Harṣabahādura
notes: The colophon is in Nepali. The month and day after 'miti' are lost. NS 1030 corresponds to 1909/10 CE, which agrees with the catalogue's 'SAM 1030'. 'vānā' is probably Bānā/Bare, the Newar Buddhist caste name. 'ina ikā manasuvāle' (read inikā, honorific 'by their wish') most likely refers to Harṣabahādura, though father and son together may be meant. 'pātravaṃsubābu' is obscure; it could be a surname or epithet, or a reference to Manirāja's father. Naka Bahila (Nakabahil) and Pīvahāla (Pim Bahal) are both localities in Patan. No place of copying is stated explicitly, but the scribe lived at Pīvahāla. The colophon ends with an imprecation against coveting the book ('kasaile lobha nagarnū').
review: p1 name normalized to Raṇavīrasiṃha (retroflex ṇ; long ī as in standard form), as_written kept
p1/p2 residence normalized to 'Naka Bahila (atha nani)', i.e. Nakabahil, Patan; residence for p2 marked as inferred from father
p2 evidence corrected to the actual colophon wording 'ina ikā manasuvāle yo vaṃsāvari vanāyāḥ'
p3 confidence lowered to medium: 'pātravaṃsubābu' is unclear (surname/epithet, or possibly '[son of] Pātra Vaṃśu bābu')
Date: NS 1030 = c. 1909/10 CE; ce_approx kept as 1910
Notes expanded (imprecation, caste reading of vānā, ambiguity of commissioner)

date_note: = Wednesday 20 Feb 1822, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: śrīśāke saṃmvat (!) 1743 || saṃmvat (!) 1878 || nipālasaṃmvat (!) 941 mti hāgruna || sivarātri (7) khunu saṃpūnūna julā suja || likhitaṃ bhājumana vaide || (unu) torako || robhagalyā maṃcce māhāryāpa ||| (8)subhaṃ || ❁ | ❁ || ❁ || jadi sudhorasudho vā. mama dokha na diaite (!) || ❁ || (fol. 72v6-8)
notes: The colophon gives three eras, and all three agree: ŚS 1743 (+78), VS 1878 (−57) and NS 941 (+880) each give 1821 CE. Phālguna Śivarātri falls around February–March 1821. 'saṃpūnūna julā' is Newari for 'was completed'. The phrase '(unu) torako || robhagalyā maṃcce māhāryāpa' is obscure. It may contain a locality (a ṭola?) or a further statement about the scribe or the copy, but no person or place can be read from it with confidence. The closing line 'jadi sudhorasudho vā. mama dokha na diaite' is a Nepali scribal formula meaning 'whether correct or incorrect, do not blame me'. 'vaide' is read as the caste name Vaidya. The catalogue fields (scribe Bhājumana Vaidya, ŚS 1743) agree with this reading.
review: Date: added implied pakṣa 'kṛṣṇa' and glossed the tithi as caturdaśī (Śivarātri); the colophon itself names only the festival
Notes: confirmed that the three eras agree on 1821 CE; glossed 'saṃpūnūna julā' and the scribe's closing formula; kept the obscure phrase unresolved

title: Amarakośa vyākhyā dīpikākhyā
subject: Kośa
date_note: ≈ 1805 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrī dāṇIṇātya śiromaṇībhūta citta pāvana śrī mukuṃda bhaṭṭātmajaḥ śrī viśvanāthabhaṭṭāṃ ghrilaghavidhyena śrī manmahārādhirājapārvata viṣayādhipa śrī trivikramasena pramvāśritena pāṃḍe ityupanāmaka viracitāyāmamaradīpikāyāṃ mamarasiṃhakṛta nāmaliṃgānuśāsana paṃjikāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ kāṇḍaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ śubham śrī śāke 1727 māse 6 likhitamidaṃ pustakaṃ rupanārāyaṇātmaja revatīramaṇa śarmaṇā śubham gokhuragrāme (fol. 97v10-98r4 )
notes: Corrupt readings: 'dāṇIṇātya' = dākṣiṇātya; 'viśvanāthabhaṭṭāṃ ghrilaghavidhyena' = viśvanāthabhaṭṭāṅghrilabdhavidyena ('who gained learning at the feet of Viśvanātha Bhaṭṭa'); 'manmahārādhirāja' = śrīmanmahārājādhirāja; 'pramvāśritena' probably = prabhvāśritena ('dependent on [his] lord'). The commentator of the Amaradīpikā is named only by his surname Pāṇḍe. He is described as a Cittapāvana (Chitpavan) brahmin of the South, son of Mukunda Bhaṭṭa and pupil of Viśvanātha Bhaṭṭa. Strictly, the Cittapāvana epithet qualifies the father inside the compound, and the commentator is assumed to share it. Trivikramasena, overlord of Parvata, was the commentator's patron. His role is recorded as 'other', not reigning king of this copy, although the catalogue field lists him as King. The colophon does not show whether he was still ruling in ŚS 1727 (c. 1805 CE). The scribe Revatīramaṇa, son of Rūpanārāyaṇa, copied the manuscript at Gokhuragrāma, which is not identified.
review: p4 Trivikramasena: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He is the patron of the commentator ('prabhvāśritena', read as prabhu-āśritena), not a ruler shown to be reigning when this copy was made in ŚS 1727. The catalogue field 'King' likely carries over the composition-time patron.
Relation p1→p4 changed from under_reign_of to servant_of (the commentator was a dependant of the king).
p6 Revatīramaṇa: removed residence 'Gokhuragrāma'. The colophon gives it only as the place of copying.
p1 confidence lowered to low: 'Pāṇḍe' is only the surname (upanāmaka), and the personal name is not given.
Notes rewritten: corrupt readings explained and typo corrected.

title: Amarakośa ( 1-3 kāṇḍa )
subject: Kośa
date_note: = Saturday 10 May 1664, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: liṃgādi saṃgraha varggaḥ || || ityamarasiṃhakṛtau nāmaliṃgānuśāsane | sāmānyakāṇḍa stṛtīyaḥ sāṃgaeva samarthitaḥ || || samvat 784 vaiśākhaśuklaḥ paurṇṇamāsī vudhahasta likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina || śrī 3 bhavānī śaṃkara prītirastu || śubhaṃbhavatu sarvvadā || namaḥ || (fol. 73v4-6 )
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Vudhahasta ?'. The most likely reading of 'vudhahasta likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina' is budha(vāra), hasta-likhita, saṃpūrṇa-dina: 'Wednesday, the day the handwritten copy was completed'. Hasta as nakṣatra is ruled out because a Vaiśākha pūrṇimā cannot fall in Hasta. A less likely reading is 'written by the hand of Vudha/Budha', which would make Budha the scribe; because of that doubt no scribe is recorded. The era is not named but is assumed to be NS (the script is Newari): 784 + 880 = c. 1664 CE (April/May). The weekday has not been checked against the calendar. Bhavānī-Śaṅkara is a deity and is not recorded as a person.
review: Removed 'hasta' as nakṣatra: at a Vaiśākha full moon the moon stands near Viśākhā/Anurādhā, so Hasta (two asterisms before Citrā) is astronomically impossible here. 'vudha' is taken as Budhavāra, and 'hasta likhiti' is read as hastalikhita ('written by hand').
Date as_written now includes 'likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina'.
Purpose reworded as a devotional dedication.
Notes expanded with the Vudha-as-scribe alternative.

title: Trikāṇḍaśeṣa
subject: Kośa
date_note: = Wednesday 16 Apr 1806, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīpuruṣottamadevaviracitas trikāṃḍaśeṣābhidhānakośagraṃthaḥ samaptaḥ (!) || śrīraviḥ prīyatāṃ || nabhasi bahu(37v1)lapakṣe vāsare sūryasūno (!) sarajvananatithau (!) śrīviśvanāthopakaṃṭho (!) || likhitam idam apūrvaṃ kośakāṃḍatriśeṣaṃ muninamivaryyāḥ svāmināmtaḥ sute(2)na || 1 || likhita iha mahārtho yas trikāṃḍyāstuśeṣo (!) || saṃvat 1863 vaiśākhamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe 13 rāma rāma rāma śrīrāma rāmaḥ (fol. 37r10-37v2)
notes: The scribe is not named. He calls himself the son of someone whose name ends in -svāmin: 'muninamivaryyāḥ svāmināmtaḥ' probably stands for something like 'munivarya-svāmi-nāmnaḥ'. The father's name, read here as Munivaryasvāmin, is corrupt and uncertain. The verse gives a date of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa), dark fortnight, Saturday, with a corrupt tithi word 'sarajvana'. This is probably a corrupt tithi name, or possibly a chronogram, and cannot be resolved. The prose date is saṃvat 1863 Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 13, so the two dates give different months. They may mark different stages of the work, or one of them may be copied over from the exemplar. The era is taken as Vikrama, since this is a Devanagari manuscript and the place is Vārāṇasī (VS 1863 ≈ 1806 CE); the era itself is not stated. 'śrīviśvanāthopakaṇṭhe' means near the Viśvanātha temple, i.e. Vārāṇasī. 'śrīraviḥ prīyatām' is an invocation of the god, not a person.
review: Scribe: 'Svāmin' is not the scribe's name. The text says the copy was written 'svāmināmtaḥ (= °svāmināmnaḥ?) sutena', i.e. by the son of a man called …svāmin. title: Nepālamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
date_note: = Wednesday 8 Oct 1952, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti skandapurā(4)ṇe himavatkhaṇḍe nepāla[[māhā]]tmye triṃśodhyāyaḥ || || śākābde siṃdhubājīdharaṇi ca dharayute, (!) kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣe, paṃcamyāṃ sādhyajoge, (!) ruru(5)śira ca ravau saṃcitaṃ dharmaheto (!) | vyākhyārthaṃ devidāsa dvijakulasumaṇeḥ pūjyapujāṃ prayatnā,l lekho 'yaṃ parśurāmo hariharakathāṃ pustakaṃ santayo(6)gyaṃ || || yatrāste śaṃkaro devo, vāgmatī yatra nimnagā | naipālasaṃbhavaṃvāṇīṃ sthāpitaṃ girijālaye || || || bhavānyai (!) prītir astu (fol. 92r3–6)
purpose: dharmahetoḥ; for Devīdāsa's exposition (vyākhyārtham); deposited (sthāpitam) in the Girijālaya by the Vāgmatī
notes: The chronogram is corrupt (dharaṇi ca dharayute). The most likely reading is sindhu(4)-vājī(7)-dharaṇidhara(8)-dharā(1), which reads right to left as ŚS 1874 = 1952 CE and matches the catalogue. If dharaṇi and dharā are each taken as 1, the year would be ŚS 1174 (1252 CE), which is implausible. The catalogue's bracketed alternative, NS 874 (1754 CE), conflicts with the explicit 'śākābde', so ŚS is kept. A 1952 copy in Newari script is late but possible. The date details (Kārttika kṛṣṇa 5 with the moon in Mṛgaśiras) fit an amānta month. Devīdāsa is described with the epithet 'dvijakulasumaṇi' (jewel of the brahmin family). He is not explicitly the commissioner. The final verse records that the book was installed in the Girijālaya (a Pārvatī shrine where Śaṅkara resides and the Vāgmatī flows, probably in the Paśupati area). This is where the book was deposited, not necessarily where it was copied, and the shrine is unidentified. bhavānyai (!) prītir astu is the closing benediction.

colophon: || iti śrīskandapurāṇe himvatkhaṇḍe nepālamāhātmye triṃśodhyāyaḥ || || nepāle smi(4)n rudravasubhi (!) vaiśāṣakṛṣṇapakṣe aṣṭamyāyāṃ (!) tithau śatavṛṣanakṣetre (!) vaidhatiyoge (!) āditavāsare (!) vṛṣarāsiko savitari kumbharāsiko candramasi, śrī 2 bhūpālendramallasya sāmrājye, śrīke(5)śavacandrakṛta pārāvatamahāvihārāvasthita, (ṅataḍholake,) mārgapūrvabhāge, gṛhavāsinā, śrīsūryyacandrabhiunā (!) likhitaiṣā pustīti || || yādṛśaṃ...(6) guṇirjjanai || || ❁ || || || śubham astu || || || ❖ || śrīśrīśrīpaśupatiprītir astu śubha || || ❁ || ❖ || (fol. 89r3–6)
notes: The year is given as a chronogram in Nepāla (= NS) era: 'rudravasubhiḥ'. Read right to left it gives vasu = 8, then rudra = 11, so NS 811 (≈ 1691 CE). This agrees with the catalogue and falls within Bhūpālendra Malla's reign in Kathmandu (c. 1687–1700). The Moon in Kumbha fits Śatabhiṣā nakṣatra. The scribe's 'bhiunā' is a corrupt or vernacular form of bhikṣuṇā. 'gṛhavāsinā' marks him as a married (householder) monk living at Keśavacandrakṛta Pārāvata Mahāvihāra, i.e. Itum Bāhā in Kathmandu. 'ṅataḍhola' is a local Newari place name of uncertain identification. The closing benediction 'śrīśrīśrīpaśupatiprītir astu' is a blessing, not a purpose of copying. The 'yādṛśaṃ...' verse is the usual formula asking forgiveness for scribal errors.

The catalogue reads the digits in direct order as 794(!), i.e. 1674 CE. Scribes sometimes did write chronograms in direct order. A 1377 copy of the Skandapurāṇa Nepālamāhātmya would be unusually early, which makes the 794 reading worth taking seriously. Checking whether Bhādrapada śukla 2 fell on a Sunday in NS 497 or in NS 794 should decide it. The text is 'nepāla mahimā', i.e. the Nepālamāhātmya. 'likhet' is an optative used with past meaning.

Notes expanded: the direct-order reading 794 (1674 CE) is flagged as a real possibility, given the catalogue's reading and the generally late dating of the Nepālamāhātmya; the weekday could settle it.

title: Rudrākṣamāhātmya
subject: Māhātymya

(fol. 8r3) iti śrītaṃtraciṃtāmaṇau rudrākṣamāhātmyaṃ || (fol. 8r5) rudrākṣasya ca lakṣaṇaṃ suphaladaṃ māhātmyam evaṃ śubhaṃ rudreṇoktam idaṃ prasastam aśubhaṃ tat tasya yā devatā || tat sarvaṃ suvi(7)cāryya nīlakavinā gairīya bhāṣānvitaṃ rājendrādimavikramāya vibhave bhavatyārpitaṃ pustakaṃ || || || || (fol. 8r6–7)
purpose: offered with devotion (bhaktyārpitam?) to King Rājendravikrama
notes: The colophon has no date. If the king is Rājendra Vikrama Śāha of Nepal, the manuscript would date from about 1816–1847 CE. 'rājendrādimavikramāya' is garbled; it probably stands for Rājendra(-ādima?)vikrama, and the catalogue reads Rājendravikrama Śāha. 'bhavatyārpitaṃ' is probably an error for 'bhaktyārpitaṃ' (offered with devotion). 'gairīya bhāṣā' presumably means the hill language, i.e. Nepali (Gorkhālī/Parbatiyā). 'prasastam' should read 'praśastam'. Nīlakavi made the Nepali bhāṣāṭīkā on the Rudrākṣamāhātmya, which comes from the Tantracintāmaṇi, and presented it to the king. VS is inferred: it fits the north Indian context, and VS 1938 Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 8 (pūrṇimānta), i.e. Janmāṣṭamī, falls around 18 Aug 1881, which was a Thursday, matching guruvāsara. The colophon gives Vilāsapura only as the scribe's residence, not explicitly as the place of copying. colophon: iti śrī[[bhaviṣyottarapurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇa arjuna samvāde]] anaṃtavratakathā samāptaḥ (!) śubham astu samvat 1762 samaināma āśvinavadi aṣṭamī idaṃ stotraṃ jaikṛṣṇa brāhmaṇa chitupuragrāmavāsinaṃ (!) rāma rāma (fol. 9r4–6)
notes: The phrase 'idaṃ stotraṃ jaikṛṣṇa brāhmaṇa chitupuragrāmavāsinaṃ (!)' has no verb such as likhitam. It reads most naturally as a statement of ownership ('this stotra [belongs to] Jaikṛṣṇa, a brahmin living in Chitupuragrāma'). The scribe role rests only on the catalogue. 'Jaikṛṣṇa' is probably a vernacular form of Jayakṛṣṇa. 'samaināma' is most likely a vernacular form of 'samaye/samaya nāma'. 'samvat 1762' is taken as Vikrama (NS 1762 is impossible). Āśvina vadi 8 in VS 1762 falls in roughly September–October 1705 CE. Chitupuragrāma is given as his place of residence and is not explicitly the place of copying, although the catalogue lists it as the place of copying. The catalogue spells the names 'Jaikṛṇa Brāhāmaṇa' and 'Chitupurgrāma'; these are typos for the colophon's jaikṛṣṇa brāhmaṇa and chitupuragrāma.
review: Jaikṛṣṇa: confidence lowered from high to medium. The colophon has no verb of writing. 'idaṃ stotraṃ [X]' most naturally marks ownership. The scribe role is kept only because the catalogue gives it.
Place of copying cleared. The colophon gives Chitupuragrāma only as Jaikṛṣṇa's place of residence ('-vāsin'), not as the place where the copy was made. It stays under the person's residence.
Pakṣa written as 'vadi (kṛṣṇa)'. Notes added on 'samaināma', the possible Jayakṛṣṇa name form, and the misspelled catalogue fields.

subject: Kathā
date_note: = Thursday 4 Jan 1607, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrī(itihāsasamucyaye bahulāvratakathāyāṃ samāptā śubham astu) samvat 1663 samaye pauṣasudi saptamī gurau likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ candrabhānunā ❁ (dvaipāyanasyedaṃ) (fol.5v1–2) iti śrī (itihāsasamucyaye bahulāvratakathāyāṃ samāptā) śubham astu || || samvat 1664 samaye māghavadi daśamī śanivāsare likhitamidaṃ pustakaṃ candrabhānunā (|| pūrrajñasyedaṃ || ) (exp.12:1–3)
notes: The colophon ends twice. Fol. 5v is dated samvat 1663 Pauṣa sudi 7, Thursday (gurau), and carries the ownership mark 'dvaipāyanasyedaṃ'. Exp. 12 is dated samvat 1664 Māgha vadi 10, Saturday (śanivāsare), and carries the ownership mark 'pūrrajñasyedaṃ'. Both colophons name Candrabhānu as scribe. The second date is about a year later (VS 1664 Māgha falls around January 1608). This suggests the reel holds two copies of the Bahulākathā by the same scribe, each with a different owner, rather than one manuscript. The era is not stated. It is taken as Vikrama because the script is Devanagari, the scribe is not Newar, and the date formula is North Indian. VS 1663 Pauṣa corresponds to December 1606 or January 1607. I did not check the weekdays. 'pūrrajña' is evidently corrupt; Pūrṇajña is a possible reading. The ownership marks are in brackets and may be later additions, so no link between the scribe and the owners is recorded.

Lowered confidence for Pūrrajña to low, because the name is evidently corrupt.

title: Madālasopakhyāna[satīka]
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Thursday 25 Dec 1721, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti bhāśvatīkaraṇe śatānaṃdaviracite parilekhādhikyaro ʼṣṭamaḥ samāptaḥ || śrīgaṃgāsāgarārppaṇam astu || śake 1643 pauṣe māse śukle 7 gurau (drugulyāṃ) śrīgoviṃdajotirvidā likhitaṃ svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || atra gauḍagraṃthe siddhāṃtarahasye deśāṃtaraṃ jojanaṃ (!) || 205 śrīrāghavaśarmaṇā likhitam asti tenātrāsmābhir likhitaṃ deśāyo 205 deśāṃtaṃraṃ [[155]] (!) 2135 prabhā 5/10 yadvā 5/8 ----- /// (fol. 6r7-11)
purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for the scribe's own use and for others)
notes: The catalogue lists Rāghava Śarmā as the scribe, which is wrong. The colophon names Govinda Jyotirvid as the scribe of this copy. Rāghava Śarman is cited for a deśāntara value of 205 yojanas in the Gauḍa work Siddhāntarahasya ('śrīrāghavaśarmaṇā likhitam asti tenātrāsmābhir likhitaṃ'). He is probably Rāghavānanda Śarman, the Bengali author of the Siddhāntarahasya, so he is the source of a cited figure, not someone involved in making this copy. 'svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca' could imply Govinda also owned the copy, but because it is for others as well, owner was not added. 'śrīgaṃgāsāgarārppaṇam astu' ('may it be offered to Gaṅgāsāgara') is ambiguous: it could refer to the pilgrimage site or deity, or to a person named Gaṅgāsāgara. No person was recorded for it. The place 'drugulyāṃ' was put in parentheses by the cataloguer, so the reading is uncertain, and it cannot be identified. CE: Pauṣa śukla 7 of ŚS 1643 falls around late Dec 1721 or early Jan 1722, and the weekday has not been checked. The numbers after the colophon (deśāntara 2135, prabhā 5/10 or 5/8) are the scribe's astronomical notes.

p2: title normalized to 'jyotirvid' (written 'jotirvidā')
date: weekday given as Thursday (gurau); ce_approx given as 1721 (Pauṣa ŚS 1643 falls in Dec 1721 to Jan 1722)
notes: added the ambiguity of 'śrīgaṃgāsāgarārppaṇam astu', the uncertain place reading and the svārtha/parārtha ownership question

colophon: iti jaiminibhārataṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || || sumatiśrījitāmitra,malladevo mahīpatiḥ || yudhiṣṭhirasya yajñasya nṛtyārambhaṃ karoti hi || śrīsūryavaṃśaśatapatrasahasraraśmir nnamrībhavan nṛpatikairavakānanenduḥ | bhaktāpure jayati bhūpaśirastharatna- bhābhir vvicitrapadapaṅkaśrīnakhenduḥ1 || || jitāmitramallaṃ, gopālaṃ gopālaḥ | jitāmitramallaḥ saputraṃ punātu || || ≪in a later hand:≫ samvat 810 pauṣasudi 3 pyākhana ṛ tayā dina || samvat 809 caitrasudi 13 ghaṃtijyā ārambha yāṅā dina || || samvat 809 śrāvaṇa śudi 1 ghaṃtijyā, dhuna dina || || (fol. 37v)
notes: The dates were added in a later hand and appear to record the production of the play rather than the copying of the manuscript. In chronological order: NS 809 Caitra śukla 13 (c. Mar/Apr 1689), the ghaṃtijyā was begun (ārambha); NS 809 Śrāvaṇa śukla 1 (c. Jul/Aug 1689), the ghaṃtijyā was finished (dhuna); NS 810 Pauṣa śukla 3 (c. Dec 1689/Jan 1690), the day of the pyākhana (dance-drama performance). 'ghaṃtijyā' is unclear; it may mean rehearsal or preparatory work for the play. The phrase 'pyākhana ṛ tayā' looks corrupt. No explicit copying date is given. Jitāmitra Malla (r. c. 1673–1696, Bhaktapur) is praised as the king. His authorship of the play is inferred from 'nṛtyārambhaṃ karoti' and from the usual attribution of the Jaiminibhārata nāṭaka to him; the colophon does not state it outright. 'gopāla' in the closing benediction is the deity (Kṛṣṇa). The catalogue lists Ugra Malla and Bhūpatīndra Malla, but they are not named here; they are only implied by 'saputraṃ' (with his son(s)). 'bhaktāpure' occurs in the praise verse, so Bhaktapur as the place of copying is plausible but not explicitly stated.

title: Ākhyātacandrikā
subject: Vyākaraṇa
colophon: ity ākhyātacandrikā samāptā || || vītyāśugābdābdaśake śucer dale ʼṣṭamyāṃ bhṛgau dvandvabhage bhage tv idam | nepāladeśe nijadarśanārtha〈〈ṃ〉〉m alīlikhac chrīdvijalālaśarmmā || 1 || (fol. 14v14-15)
notes:
Role: 'alīlikhat' is strictly the causative aorist of likh ('caused to be written'), so Dvijalāla might have commissioned the copy rather than written it. Nepalese colophons, however, often use alīlikhat simply for 'wrote'. Together with nijadarśanārtham and the catalogue's Scribe field, this makes scribe + owner the more likely reading. Commissioner remains possible.

Chronogram: 'vīty-āśuga-abda-abda-śake' is unresolved. vīti (horse) = 7 and āśuga (arrow) = 5, but 'abda' (cloud? or simply 'year') has no secure numerical value. If the second 'abda' just means 'year', only three digit-words remain, which is too few for a Śaka year. The era is taken as ŚS from 'śake', but 'śaka' can also mean 'era' in general. If the year were ŚS 1757 the date would be about CE 1835, but this is speculative, so ce_approx is left empty.

Pakṣa: 'dale' does not name the pakṣa. Śukla is inferred from the astronomy: Āṣāḍha aṣṭamī with the sun in Mithuna and the moon in Pūrvaphalgunī fits the bright fortnight. 'Śuci' may also denote Jyeṣṭha in some usage.

The 〈〈ṃ〉〉 in nijadarśanārtha〈〈ṃ〉〉m is the cataloguer's mark of a redundant anusvāra.
review: p1 roles changed from commissioner+owner to scribe+owner. 'alīlikhat' is formally a causative aorist, but Nepalese scribes routinely use it for their own copying. 'nijadarśanārtham' with himself as subject and the catalogue's 'Scribe' field both point to self-copying. Confidence lowered to medium.

date.month normalised to Śuci (= Āṣāḍha); era kept as ŚS but flagged as uncertain; chronogram discussed in notes; ce_approx left empty.

title: Dānakelikaumudī
subject: Nāṭaka (Bhāṇikā)
colophon: dānakelikaumudī nāma bhāṇikā samāptā grathitā sumanaḥsukhadā yasya nideśena bhāṇikāsrag iyaṃ || tasya mama priyasuhṛdaḥ kaṃṭhataṭīkṣaṇam alaṃkurutāṃ || naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā || gate manuśate śāke caṃdrasvararamanvite (!) || atha bhāṇikālakṣaṇaṃ || bhāṇikā ślākṣṇa(!)nepathyā mukhanirbbahaṇānvitā || kaiśikī bhāratīvṛttiyutaikāṃkavinirmmitā|| etc. (fol. 33v)
notes: The colophon gives nothing about the copy itself: no scribe, commissioner, owner, copying date or copying place. All of it is the author's own closing text. It says the bhāṇikā was written at the command of an unnamed dear friend ('yasya nideśena ... tasya mama priyasuhṛdaḥ'). It was composed while living at Nandīśvara ('naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā'), the hill at Nandgaon in Braj. The composition date is 'gate manuśate śāke caṃdrasvara(sa)manvite' (the cataloguer marks 'ramanvite' as corrupt with (!)). This reads as Śaka 1471, i.e. about 1549 CE. The work is Rūpa Gosvāmin's Dānakelikaumudī, but he is not named here. After this comes a definition of the bhāṇikā genre ('atha bhāṇikālakṣaṇaṃ ...'), quoted only in part (etc.), so a scribal colophon may follow on fol. 33v without being quoted.
review: Date fields cleared (era 'none'): 'gate manuśate śāke candrasvara-samanvite' is the author's composition verse, not a copying date. Its reading is Śaka 1471 (manu 14 hundreds + candra 1, svara 7 read right to left = 71), about 1549 CE. That reading is correct and is kept in the notes.
Place cleared: Nandīśvara is where the work was composed ('naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā'), not where it was copied. It is moved to the notes.
Persons left empty. The author (Rūpa Gosvāmin) is not named in the colophon, and the 'priyasuhṛd' at whose command the work was written is anonymous.

The catalogue lists Rucipati as scribe and Bhairavasiṃha as king. However, Rucipati (Upādhyāya) wrote the commentary on Murāri's play under the Oinwāra king Bhairavasiṃha of Mithilā. Neither name appears in the quoted colophon, so neither is recorded here as scribe or reigning king. Rucipati was also not added as commentator, because he is not named in this colophon. The copy is undated.

title: Paśupatiprādurbhāvopākhyānanāṭaka
subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: ≈ 1711 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: itiśrī śrījayabhūpatīndramalladeva, mahārājādhirāja, viracitaṃ nalacaritanāma nāṭake (!) pañcamoṅka (!) || śubham astu || || śloka 1601 || samvat [ 808 . . .] śudi 2 roja 2 śrīśivarājopādhyāyale banāyāko pustakam idaṃ bhūyāt || ❁ || (fol. 4v10–12)
notes: The year is uncertain. The cataloguer put '808' in square brackets and it is followed by lacunae. The catalogue itself gives 'NS 808?', and the month is lost. NS 808 (1688 CE) is earlier than Bhūpatīndra Malla's reign in Bhaktapur (c. NS 816–842 / 1696–1722 CE), yet the colophon calls him mahārājādhirāja. So either the reading is wrong (e.g. 818 or 828) or the title was given to him retrospectively. Bhūpatīndra appears here only as the author of the play. The catalogue lists him as 'King', but the colophon does not say this copy was made in his reign. The scribe's name 'śivarājopādhyāya' can be split as Śiva + Rājopādhyāya (the usual Newar Brahmin title) or as Śivarāja + Upādhyāya. The catalogue's 'Śivamarājopādhyāya' might point to Śivarāma. 'banāyāko' (Nepali, 'made') most likely means he copied the book, but it could also mean he had it made. 'pustakam idaṃ bhūyāt' is a garbled Sanskrit ending.

p2 confidence lowered from high to medium: the name might be Śiva + Rājopādhyāya, or Śivarāja + Upādhyāya, and the catalogue gives 'Śivamarājopādhyāya' (perhaps a corrupt Śivarāma)

Lāḍanavalla is the patron/dedicatee of the original composition: Kalyāṇamalla wrote the Anaṅgaraṅga for the amusement (vinoda) of Lāḍ Khān Lodī. 'sthalaḥ' (for sthalam) is the colophon's own form.

title: Vṛttaratnākara
subject: Chandaḥśāstra
date_note: ≈ 1721 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti vṛttaratnākare ṣaṣṭhodhyāya || ❁ || (fol. 45v8) iti śrīmadvidvnmu(10)kuṭaratna śrīmadbhaṭṭarāmeśvarasūnunārāyaṇabhaṭṭaviracitāyāṃ vṛttaratnākaravyākhyāyāṃ prastārādhyāyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ || ❁ || gaṃthaś ca samāptaḥ (11) || ❁ || nīlalohitatanu svaraśailabhūmitavikramasamā sugatā surasāsuralikhitam idaṃ vṛttaratnākaranāmakaṃ chaṃdaḥ || śubham bhūyāt || śrī | (fol. 46r9–11)
notes: The chronogram is a bhūtasaṃkhyā: nīlalohita-tanu = 8 (Śiva's eight forms), svara = 7, śaila = 7, bhū = 1. Read right to left this gives Vikrama year 1778, about 1721 CE. The catalogue gives SAM 1878 (about 1821 CE). It may have read śaila as 8 or simply be wrong, so the catalogue date conflicts with the colophon. 'sugatā' is unclear: it may be corrupt for a month or pakṣa word, or simply mean 'elapsed'. 'surasāsuralikhitam' is corrupt. It might hide a scribe's name (e.g. Sura..., Sureśvara?), but that cannot be read with confidence, so no scribe is recorded. The colophon names the commentator Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa, son of Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa. Kedārabhaṭṭa, who wrote the root text, is not named.
review: Date: chronogram re-read. nīlalohita-tanu = 8 (Śiva's aṣṭamūrti), svara = 7, śaila = 7, bhū = 1. Read right to left this gives VS 1778, not 1878. ce_approx changed from 1821 to 1721.
Notes: recorded that the chronogram conflicts with the catalogue's SAM 1878, and that 'surasāsuralikhitam' may hide a scribe's name.
Persons and relations confirmed.

colophon: iti śrīmadbhārabdāvā(!)ṣṭhakṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu dinakarakṛte vṛttaratnākaraṃdarśaḥ samāptim aphāṇīt śrīmārṇastu saṃvat 1864 māse caitra sule(!) pakṣa 11 graṃthasamāvate subham astu pustakam idaṃ śrīkṛṣṇajośī || rāmanagara bālo (fol. 102r4-6)
notes: The commentary is the Vṛttaratnākarādarśa ('vṛttaratnākaraṃdarśaḥ'). The author's genealogy is corrupt: 'śrīmadbhārabdāvā(!)ṣṭha' = Bhāradvāja gotra? 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' most likely means 'son of [?de]vabhaṭṭa, the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The father's name is lost; it may be (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa, i.e. the Pāyaguṇḍe family (Bālakṛṣṇa → Mahādeva → Divākara/Dinakara), but this is unverified. 'samāptim aphāṇīt' is a corruption of 'agamat', and 'śrīmārṇastu' of 'śrīr astu'. The era is a bare 'saṃvat', taken as VS. 'rāmanagara bālo' (Hindi -vālā) marks Kṛṣṇa Jośī as being from Rāmanagara (possibly the one near Vārāṇasī). It is not explicitly the place of copying. The catalogue fields (scribe Padmanābhadvija; ŚS 1701 ≈ 1779 CE) do not match this colophon, which names no scribe and gives saṃvat 1864. These fields may belong to another colophon in the same MS or be a cataloguing error.

p2 name changed to stem 'Kṛṣṇa', with bhaṭṭa kept as a title.

Relation p1→p2 changed from son_of to grandson_of. 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' reads as 'son of [X]bhaṭṭa, who is the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The garbled 'do bha' probably hides the father's name, perhaps (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa.
p1 confidence lowered to medium. The name may be a corruption of Divākara, and the genealogy is garbled.
Place of copying cleared. Rāmanagara is stated only as the owner's residence ('rāmanagara bālo' = 'of Rāmanagara'). It is kept in p3's residence field.
Era basis explained in notes. The colophon has a bare 'saṃvat'; it is taken as VS, so 1864 = 1807 CE (Caitra śukla 11, spring 1807).

title: Vālmīkirāmāyaṇa āraṇyakāṇḍam saṭīka
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 10 Oct 1843, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ityārṣe rāmāyaṇe āraṇyekāṇḍe vālmīkīye paṃcasaptatimaḥ sargaḥ (fol. 236r6) iti śrī majjānakīramaṇa padapaṃkajaparicaraṇa parāyaṇa śivalāla pāṭhaka pādānuyāyi bhaṭṭadevarāma saṃgṛhīte śrīmadrāmāyaṇīya viṣamapadavyākhyāne svapāṭārthaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ saṭipaṇam lilekha kāśikāṃ madhye śrī rāmacaṃdra āleye 1 samvat 1900 kārttika vadi 2 (fol. 236r7-8)
purpose: svapāṭhārtham: for the (unnamed) scribe's own study
notes: The verb 'lilekha' has no expressed subject, so the scribe is not named in this colophon. Devarāma may have copied his own commentary with the text, but the wording does not show this. The catalogue's scribe, Rādhākṛṣṇa, is absent from the quoted colophon and may be named on another folio. Śivalāla Pāṭhaka is described as devoted to the feet of Jānakīramaṇa (Rāma). He is Devarāma's teacher ('pādānuyāyi'), so he is linked to the commentary, not to the act of copying. The commentary is the Rāmāyaṇīya Viṣamapadavyākhyāna. 'āleye' should be read 'ālaye': the copy was made at a Śrī Rāmacandra temple or house in Kāśī. The '1' before 'samvat' is probably a punctuation mark or a stray numeral. Saṃvat 1900 Kārttika vadi 2 is taken as VS, giving about October/November 1843 CE.
review: Purpose normalised to 'svapāṭhārtham: for the scribe's own study'. The scribe is not named in the colophon.

Notes expanded: the subject of 'lilekha' is unexpressed. Devarāma may be both compiler and copyist, but this is unproven. Rādhākṛṣṇa (from the catalogue) is not in the quoted text. Śivalāla is Devarāma's teacher, not the teacher of the scribe of this copy. Place = a Rāmacandra temple (ālaya) in Kāśī. The stray '1' before 'samvat' is noted.
