title: Vārāccanakaumudī (Bījasarvasvapaṭala)
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Monday 17 Jan 1853, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti sāra saṃgrahe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde śrīvārāccana kaumudyāṃ bījasarvvasva paṭalaḥ || || śubham || || abde rāmādrivivare pauṣaśuklekṣapākare | saptamyāmalikhac cedaṃ dvijaḥ śrīnidhidevakaḥ || || | saṃvat 973 kārttika vadi 11 śrīdattareva gayāśrāddha ṣaḍdina pāsā bhājudhaṇ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ jamādāra strīpuruṣaṃ luja śubhaṃ | (fol. 3v2-4)
notes: The era is not stated in the verse. NS is inferred from the appended 'saṃvat 973' and the Newari script. The chronogram rāma(3)-adri(7)-vivara(9), read right to left, gives 973, which matches the appended entry. 'pauṣaśukle kṣapākare' means Pauṣa śukla on a Monday (kṣapākara = moon). The scribe is Śrīnidhideva ('-ka' is a diminutive suffix and 'dvija' his brahmin status), which agrees with the catalogue. The appended Newari line ('saṃvat 973 kārttika vadi 11 śrīdattareva gayāśrāddha ṣaḍdina pāsā bhājudhaṇ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ jamādāra strīpuruṣaṃ luja') looks like a separate later record of a six-day Gayā-śrāddha. It apparently involves Dattareva(?) and companions ('pāsā'), including bhāju Dhana and a jamādāra couple ('strīpuruṣa'). The text is repetitive (probably dittography) and only partly understood, so the persons from this line have unclear roles and are not connected with the copying. If Kārttika vadi 11 is taken in the amānta reckoning, it would fall before the NS year-change. So the note's year may be counted differently, or it was written about a year after the copy.
review: p2: name split as Dhana with Newari honorific 'bhāju' (bhājudhaṇ = bhāju Dhana); removed 'dvānyā' from titles (it is a verb/connective form, not a title); kept 'jamādāra' as office title, low confidence
added p3 'śrīdattareva' (Dattareva?), named in the appended Gayā-śrāddha note, role other, low confidence
ce_approx refined to 1852/1853: Pauṣa NS 973 falls in Dec 1852–Jan 1853
notes: added a caution that the appended note (Kārttika vadi 11, NS 973) is a later secondary record and has nothing to do with the copying; also flagged that the appended Newari is unclear

notes: The catalogue lists Dharmarājadhīra as the scribe. The colophon itself only says 'idaṃ pustakaṃ dharmarājadhīrasya', which makes him the owner. He may also have copied it, but the colophon does not say so. The name could also be read as Dharmarāja Dhīra (personal name plus surname). The era is not named. notes: The author's epithet 'kūrmācalākhaṇḍaladvāragīvāṇaguru' (read gīrvāṇa-, the MS has 'gīvāṇa') most likely means 'Sanskrit preceptor at the court (dvāra) of the lord (ākhaṇḍala) of Kūrmācala (Kumaon)'. On that reading Premanidhi is a Kumaoni court paṇḍita, and Kūrmācala is his place of service rather than strictly his residence. The colophon names no era. 'saṃvat 1882' is taken as VS (≈1825 CE) because the copy was made in Kāśī. The catalogue gives King Śrīpṛthvīpati Sāha Deva, but he does not appear in this colophon excerpt, so he is not recorded here. He may come from elsewhere in the MS or be a cataloguing error. The colophon closes only the first dhārā (prathamadhārā) of the Kumāraśakti.

title: yauvanollāsa
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrībhāsurānaṃdanāthacaraṇāraviṃdamiliṃdāyamānamānasenomānaṃdanāthena viracite kalpasūtrānusāriṇi nityotsave nibaṃdhe yauvanollāsasmṛtīyaḥ (!) saṃpūrṇaḥ || idaṃ pustakaṃ devasthalyupanāmakadhuṃḍhirājātmakagaṇeśasūriṇā kṛṣṇabhaṭṭasutalakṣmīnārāyaṇena likhitaṃ. || kive ity umanāmakasya(!) rājābhāu yasya gṛheṃduragrāmamadhye likhitaṃ || svārthaṃ ca parārthaṃ ca || (fol. 41v4-8)
notes: The text is Umānandanātha's Nityotsava. Bhāsurānandanātha is the initiatory name of Bhāskararāya, the author's guru; he had no part in this copy. 'mānasenomānaṃdanāthena' = mānasena + umānandanāthena. 'yauvanollāsasmṛtīyaḥ (!)' probably stands for 'yauvanollāsas tṛtīyaḥ'. 'umanāmakasya(!)' = upanāmakasya, so Kive (Kibe) is Rājābhāū's surname; the Kibe family was prominent in Indore. 'dhuṃḍhirājātmaka-' stands for -ātmaja-. Two people stand in the instrumental (Gaṇeśasūri, son of Dhuṇḍhirāja, surname Devasthalī, and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa) before a single 'likhitaṃ'. Their fathers differ, so they are two people. Gaṇeśa could be a co-scribe. Or 'gaṇeśasūriṇā' may be a slip for the genitive '-ṇaḥ', which would make him the owner of the book. The catalogue lists only Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa as scribe. No date is given.
review: p1 Bhāsurānandanātha: role 'teacher' → 'other' (he is the author's guru, not involved in producing this copy); noted identity with Bhāskararāya

p4 Gaṇeśa: confidence high → medium; the colophon has two instrumentals with one 'likhitaṃ', so co-scribe is one reading, but owner (gaṇeśasūriṇā for -ṇaḥ) is also possible; the catalogue names only Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa
p7 Rājābhāū: 'Kive' moved from affiliation to titles as a surname (upanāmaka); evidence trimmed
notes expanded: umanāmakasya = upanāmakasya; smṛtīyaḥ(!) probably = tṛtīyaḥ; dhuṃḍhirājātmaka- = -ātmaja-

title: Vījakoṣa
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Jun 1835, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: kṣa. iti varṇakośa (!) samāptaḥ || bhūdeva śrītīrtharājo vījakośaṃ (!) leleṣat (!) || varṇakośaṃ ca tad api racasya pāṭhārthahetukam || samvat 1892 miti āṣāḍavadi śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || || || (fol. 8v6–7)
purpose: svārtha: for his own study (pāṭhārtha), if 'racasya' = 'svasya'
notes: 'leleṣat (!)' is a corrupt form of 'lilekha'/'alekhat' (wrote). 'bhūdeva' means 'brahmin' and is kept as a title. 'racasya' is probably a corruption of 'svasya' (his own), so the scribe copied the Vījakoṣa and also the Varṇakośa for his own study. That reading is the basis for the 'owner' role, but it is a conjecture, and 'racayya' (having composed) is also possible. No tithi is given after 'āṣāḍavadi'. Taking VS 1892 as caitrādi, the dark half of Āṣāḍha falls around June–July 1835 CE. The catalogue's scribe and date fields agree with the colophon.

title: Śyāmāsahasranāmastotra
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Mar 1847, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīrudrajāmalemahātaṃtre kārttikeyamahādevasaṃvāde trailokyavijayābhidhamaṃtragarbhaśyāmāsahasranāmastotraṃ samāptaṃ śubhaṃ || ❖ || iti saṃvat 967 sāla mi caitra śudi 1 roja 4 thukuhnu śrīgovindacaraṇa upādhyāṃ brahmapūrachesaconā coyāsidhayakā julo || svapna .. .. maṃtragarva śyāmāsahasranāma || phārguṇa vadi 11 ro 6 .. hnusa śakti na svapne thva saphū vilathva kuhnu mīnasaṃkrāṃtilāka vipana sadhīrjavīraṃ yāṃ svapna sathuguyā dhāla dhūktalā vāju Dhaka ukhunuṃ viya halaheyā tayā śrīkālīkāsuprasaṃnostu || śubham bhūyāditi śyāmāsahasranāma || ❁ || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || (exp. 11 bottom, 4-9)
notes: The era is not named, but 'saṃvat 967 sāla' with a Newari colophon and a Newar Upādhyāya scribe points to Nepal Saṃvat, which gives about 1847 CE. 'brahmapūrachesa conā' means 'staying in the Brahmapūra house', and 'coyā sidhayakā julo' means 'finished writing'. A separate, corrupt Newari note follows, dated Phālguna vadi 11, ro 6 (Friday). It seems to say that Śakti gave this book in a dream ('śakti na svapne thva saphū vila') on the day of the Mīna-saṃkrānti. The phrase 'vipana sadhīrjavīraṃ yāṃ svapna' may hide a personal name, perhaps Dhīr(a)javīra, the person who had the dream. 'vāju' (father/elder) is also mentioned. The text is too uncertain to record either one as a person. The catalogue entry 'SAM 967' agrees with the colophon.

title: Ādyākālikākarpūrakavaca
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Thursday 26 Aug 1847, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrībrahmavidyāyāṃ catusahasralakṣagraṃthe śrīādyākālikāyāṃ karpurakavacaṃ navame dvitīyapaṭalasamāptaṃ || ❁ || śrīśāke saṃvat 1769 sāla śrāvaṇa śu di 15 roja 5 śrīgovindacaraṇaupādhyāyena liṣita idaṃ puṣṭakaṃ śubham || śrīkālikā suprasaṃnostu || vikramābda 1904 || naipālasaṃvat 967 śrīkālikāyā prasādena idaṃ puṣṭakaṃ likṣitaṃ śubham (exp. 50t, 3-7)
notes: The colophon gives the date in three eras, and they agree: Śaka 1769 (+78 = 1847), Vikrama 1904 (−57 = 1847) and Nepāla Saṃvat 967 (+880 = 1847). Śrāvaṇa śukla 15 falls in July/August 1847 CE. 'roja 5' is the fifth weekday, i.e. Thursday; I did not check it against an ephemeris. 'liṣita' and 'likṣitaṃ' are spellings of likhitam, and 'puṣṭakaṃ' of pustakam. The second statement ('śrīkālikāyā prasādena idaṃ puṣṭakaṃ likṣitaṃ') is an invocatory formula and does not add a second scribe. The catalogue's 'SAM 1769' is the Śaka year.

title: Varadagaṇeśasahasranāmāmṛta
subject: Stotra
colophon: iti śrīrudrayāmale mahārahasye śrīvaradagaṇeśasahasranāmāmṛta saṃpūrṇaṃ || ||❖ |||| || ❖ || || ❖ || vārāṇasyāṃ gaṇeśena likhitaṃ puṣpasaṃnidhau || sahasranāmam idaṃ stotraṃ pāvanaṃ paramaṃ śubhaṃ || 16 || (fol. 18v3-7)
notes: The only personal and place information is in the verse 'vārāṇasyāṃ gaṇeśena likhitaṃ puṣpasaṃnidhau || sahasranāmam idaṃ stotraṃ pāvanaṃ paramaṃ śubhaṃ || 16 ||'. Because it is numbered as verse 16 and praises the stotra, it may belong to the text or be a traditional closing verse, perhaps even naming the god Gaṇeśa as the writer. It is not clearly a scribe's statement about this copy, so the scribe and place are tentative. 'puṣpasaṃnidhau' ('near flowers/Puṣpa') is unclear; it may refer to a shrine or locality. The catalogue gives scribe Śrīkṛṣṇa Jośī and place Rāmanagara. These are not in the quoted colophon and probably come from elsewhere in the manuscript. Rāmnagar is opposite Vārāṇasī on the Ganges, so the two places fit together. The colophon gives no date.
review: Lowered confidence for Gaṇeśa as scribe from medium to low. The line 'vārāṇasyāṃ gaṇeśena likhitaṃ puṣpasaṃnidhau' is a numbered verse (|| 16 ||) that ends with praise of the stotra. It may be part of the text or a stock closing verse rather than a scribal colophon. It could also refer to the deity Gaṇeśa as the writer.
Made the place identification provisional in the notes: Vārāṇasī comes from the same doubtful verse.

Rewrote the notes. The catalogue's 'Rāmanagara' does not strictly contradict this: Rāmnagar lies just across the Ganges from Vārāṇasī. The catalogue's scribe Śrīkṛṣṇa Jośī probably comes from part of the manuscript that is not quoted here, so he was not added.

notes: The date and scribe passage is an anuṣṭubh verse: '[mākhaṃṇḍe] māsi site pakṣe bhṛgu[ra]vāsarasaṃmite / jagaṃnāthena likhitaṃ pustakaṃ sādhakāptaye'. 'mākhaṃṇḍe' is corrupt. It may stand for Māgha, or it may be what is left of a year chronogram (bhūtasaṃkhyā). No year can be recovered, so the month is only tentative. 'bhṛguravāsara' should be read as bhṛguvāsara (Friday). Pūrṇānandanātha is named only in a homage ('namaḥ'). The -ānandanātha initiatory name in a Śrīvidyā text suggests he was the scribe's guru, but the colophon does not say so. He could also be a lineage figure, and possibly the well-known Tantric author Pūrṇānanda.

notes: The tithi 'śudi 24' cannot be right (the cataloguer marks it with (!)). It may be a misreading of 2, 4 or 14. The Sanskrit compound describing Narahari's lineage is hard to parse. Ratnadevī, a faithful wife who died by entering the fire (agnipraveśānta-pativrata), is most likely Narasiṃha's wife and possibly Narahari's mother; 'mahita' (honoured) is uncertain because of the cataloguer's 〈ta〉. The final verse is the standard scribe's request for pardon for errors.

The catalogue's 'Date of Copying: SAM. 1818' takes the Śaka year as saṃvat, and if read as VS it would give a wrong date (1761 CE). The catalogue's 'King: Udyotacandra of Kūrmāñcala' (Kumaon, late 17th c.) is not in the quoted colophon and cannot be the reigning king for an 1896 copy. He probably comes from the text's own context (e.g. patron of the author), so he is left out. The colophon closes the section 'kṣayamāsa sādhanam'.

'kāṃtipūrvaṃ' is evidently an error for kāṃtipuryāṃ (Kathmandu). The scribe's name is written 'padmānātha' in the accusative with a corrupt verb ('ya ... likhat'). date_note: = Wednesday 6 Dec 1893, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: || iti śrīskaṃdapurāṇe setumāhātmye dvipaṃ cāśattamo ʼdhyāyaḥ || 52 || || graṃthasaṃkhyā 4918 || ❁ || || ❁ || ❁ || liṣitam idaṃ pustakaṃ veṇidharaśarmaṇaḥ || || iti samvat 1950 sāla mārgasirṣavadi 14 roja4 śubhbham bhavtu sarvadā (fol. 166v6–7)
notes: 'liṣitam idaṃ pustakaṃ veṇidharaśarmaṇaḥ': the genitive most likely marks the agent ('written by Veṇīdhara Śarman'). An ownership reading ('this book of …') is possible but less likely, so the role is kept as scribe only. The name is written Veṇidhara (short i), normalized to Veṇīdhara. VS is assumed for 'samvat … sāla'; VS 1950 = 1893 CE (Mārgaśīrṣa kṛṣṇa 14 ≈ Nov/Dec 1893). 'roja 4' (Nepali/Persian roj, 'day') most likely means the 4th weekday, i.e. Wednesday. The chapter number 'dvipaṃcāśattamo' (52) agrees with the numeral 52.
review: Date: normalized month to Mārgaśīrṣa and pakṣa to kṛṣṇa (vadi); weekday 'roja 4' interpreted as the 4th weekday, i.e. Wednesday, if counted from Sunday = 1 (uncertain)
Date: ce_approx stays 1893. VS 1950 Mārgaśīrṣa vadi falls in Nov–Dec 1893
Notes: said that the genitive can mark the agent ('written by'), so the scribe role is retained and 'owner' is only possible

title: Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Friday 13 Sep 1901, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmad adhyātmarāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvarasaṃvāde uttarakā(3)ṇḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ || 9 || śrīḥ(fol. 234v2–3) samāptam idam uttarakāṇḍam || śrīḥ || śrīḥ || || śrīḥ || (10)samvat 1958 sālamiti bhādraśukla 1 roja 6 śu(11)bham śrīrāmārpaṇam astu || śrīrāmāya namaḥ || ❁ || (fol. 234v9–11) iti śrīmat sakalarājavipad uddharaṇasamarthety ādi virudāvalīvirājamānasya himmativarmaṇaḥ pu(15)trasya śrīrāmavarmaṇaḥ kṛtāvadhyātmarāmāyaṇasetau uttarakāṇde navamaḥ sargaḥ || 9 || (fol. 234v1 and 15)
notes: The catalogue gives Tīrthanātha as the scribe, but that name does not appear in the quoted colophon. He may be named elsewhere in the manuscript; he is not added here. The last passage is the sub-colophon of the commentary Adhyātmarāmāyaṇasetu by Rāmavarman, son of Himmativarman. His virudāvalī ('sakalarājavipaduddharaṇasamartha...') marks him as a ruler, but he is the commentator, not the reigning king of this copy. The date VS 1958 Bhādra śukla 1, roja 6 (Friday) works out to about 13 September 1901 CE. That fits the weekday and agrees with the catalogue's VS 1958. 'sālamiti' and 'roja' are Persian-derived Nepali/Hindi dating terms.

Purpose reworded: 'śrīrāmārpaṇam astu' is a dedication formula (merit offered to Rāma), not svārtha/parārtha

title: Amarakoṣa Alternative
subject: Koṣa
date_raw: NS 820 māgha kṛṣṇa 12 uttarabhadranakṣatra sudhiyoga somavāra .
date_note: = Monday 15 Feb 1700, weekday verified, nakṣatra not
colophon: (written with second hand) samvat 820 māghamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe dvādaśyāyāṃ tithau uttarabhadranakṣetre suddiyoge somavāsare || thvakuhnu syāmasena coya dhunakā dina || (131r 4)
notes: The colophon is in a second hand ('written with second hand'). Śyāma may therefore have been the person who finished the copy or added the colophon, not necessarily the scribe of the whole manuscript. The Newari 'thvakuhnu syāmasena coya dhunakā dina' means 'on this day Śyāma finished writing'. Here '-sena' is taken as the agentive ending, so the name is Śyāma, as the catalogue gives it. 'Śyāmasena' is a less likely alternative reading. The era is not stated, but 'samvat 820' in a Newari colophon is Nepāla Saṃvat. NS 820 Māgha kṛṣṇa 12 falls in early 1700 CE (January–February). The yoga 'suddi' (catalogue: 'sudhi') is corrupt. The best guess is siddhi; no yoga named śuddhi exists.
review: Name corrected from 'Śyāmasena' to 'Śyāma': in 'syāmasena coya dhunakā' the '-sena' is the ergative/instrumental ending (Newari colophon usage modelled on Skt. -ena) attached to the agent of 'coya' (wrote). This agrees with the catalogue's 'Śyāma'. Confidence lowered to medium.
Weekday normalized to 'somavāra' (Monday); nakshatra/yoga normalized to Uttarabhādrapadā and 'suddi' read as probably siddhi.
Notes rewritten: the colophon is in a second hand, and the yoga reading is uncertain.

notes: 'śrīmallāḍa ṣāna' = śrīmat + Lāḍa Ṣāna, with ṣ written for kh: Lāḍa Khān (Lāḍ Khān Lodī), the patron for whose entertainment (vinodāya) Kalyāṇamalla wrote the Anaṅgaraṅga in the 16th century. He is the patron of the original text, not of this copy. The colophon names no scribe, commissioner or owner. Date: the era is only given as 'saṃvat'. VS 1005 (= 948 CE) and ŚS 1005 (= 1083 CE) are impossible for a 16th-century text with a Nepali commentary, so NS 1005 = 1885 CE is the most likely reading. This is inferred, though, and a scribal error in the year (e.g. for VS 19xx) can't be ruled out. After 'śudi 9', 'ro +++++' is probably Nepali 'roja' (weekday number) followed by a lacuna, so the weekday can't be read.

Gave month as the solar month Siṃha (from 'pañcānanagate ravau'); added this to notes.

title: Kumāraprādurbhāvanāmanāṭaka
subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: = Thursday 2 Jun 1678, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: [ || lu 39 || iti mahārājādhirājasūryyavaṃśamukuṭamaṇi śrīśrījayajitāmitramallamahīpativiracite kumāraprādurbhāvanāma nāṭake paṃcamāṅka saṃpūṇṇaṃ (!) || samvat 798 jyeṣṭha śudi 12 || ] ( illegible: covered with different ink) (fol. 44r7–8)
notes: The colophon names Jitāmitra Malla only as the author of the play (viracite). His role as reigning king of this copy is inferred because NS 798 (1678 CE) falls within his reign at Bhaktapur. There is no explicit rājye clause, and the copy may be contemporary with the composition or even the author's own. No place of copying is stated. The scribe is not named. The rest of the colophon after the date is illegible because it is covered with different ink, so a scribe or commissioner may have been named there. The cataloguer marks 'saṃpūṇṇaṃ' as an error for 'saṃpūrṇam'.
review: Name normalized to 'Jitāmitramalla': 'jaya' is the stock Malla royal prefix, and the king is usually cited as Jitāmitra Malla. The as_written form is unchanged.
Kept 'king' alongside 'author': NS 798 falls within Jitāmitra Malla's reign at Bhaktapur (c. NS 793–816). The colophon has no explicit rājye clause, so this role is inferred and is flagged in notes.
Paksa normalized from 'śudi' to 'śukla'. Date and ce_approx 1678 confirmed.
Notes expanded.

title: Nāsiketupākhyāna
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Sunday 3 Oct 1632, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīnāsiketopākhyāne śubhāṃśubhaṃ (!) kṛtaṃ karmajanmaṃ (!) ca bhāvavarṇano nāmāṣṭādaśoddhyāya (!) || 18 || saṃvat || 1689 || liṣyataṃ kārttika vadi paṃcami (!) || guruvāre vṛhasyapati (!) || kaṣṭasuṃ likhitaṃ || || || || (fol. 61v7–9)
notes: The catalogue lists 'Bṛhaspati' as scribe, but in the colophon 'vṛhasyapati (!)' comes right after 'guruvāre'. It is almost certainly the same Thursday given again as bṛhaspati(vāra), not a scribe's name. If it were a scribe's name, the attribution would be low confidence. 'Saṃvat' in a Devanagari MS with the Hindi-type phrasing 'liṣyataṃ' and 'kaṣṭasuṃ likhitaṃ' ('written with difficulty') suggests VS, so 1689 VS ≈ 1632 CE. The weekday has not been verified.
review: Removed p1 'Bṛhaspati' as scribe: 'guruvāre vṛhasyapati' is most naturally the weekday given twice (guruvāra = bṛhaspativāra, Thursday). It is not a personal name, and the colophon names no scribe. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Bṛhaspati' looks like a misreading, recorded in notes.
Weekday given as 'guruvāra (= bṛhaspati[vāra])'.
Corrected the note on 'kaṣṭasuṃ likhitaṃ': 'suṃ' is the Hindi/Rajasthani postposition 'sũ' ('with'), so the phrase means 'written with difficulty'. It is not a corruption of 'kaṣṭena'.

title: Svasthānīvratakathā
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Wednesday 20 Jan 1610, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīriṅgaṃ(!)purāṇe,, svasthānaiparamaiśvaryyā(!) vratakathā samāptaḥ(!) || jatra(!)ditvā(!) tatra rīkhita(!)mama ṣo(!)na diyate(!) | śrī 2 jaggatrayeti malla deva vijayarāje || śubha || samvat 730 paukhakṛṣṇa ekādaśyāyā tithau ādita(!)vāsare | gopāla siṃharīkhita(!)|| (fol.27r3-27v1)
notes: The king's name 'jaggatrayeti malla deva' is corrupt. The most likely reading is Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur, but his reign is usually dated c. 1613/14–1637, a few years after NS 730 (1609/10), when Trailokyamalla was still ruling Bhaktapur. Jagattraya ('three worlds') means the same as trailokya, so a garbled 'Trailokyamalla' cannot be ruled out. Either the date is misread, the colophon names Jagajjyotirmalla while he was a co-ruler or crown prince, or the name stands for another king. 'jatra(!)ditvā(!) tatra rīkhita(!) mama ṣo(!)na diyate(!)' is the standard scribal formula 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā / mama doṣo na dīyate'. 'riṅgaṃ(!)purāṇe' stands for Liṅgapurāṇe. 'siṃha' is kept as part of the scribe's name.

notes: The catalogue names Tīrtharāja as scribe. The colophon instead reads 'tīrtharājāya ayaṃ hāvali(!) likhita', a dative meaning 'this Hārāvalī was written for Tīrtharāja'. That makes him the person the copy was made for, possibly its commissioner or owner. However, the colophon's Sanskrit is substandard (hāvali for hārāvalī, likhita for likhitā), so the dative may have been used loosely for an agent. That would make Tīrtharāja the scribe, as the catalogue says. No scribe is named otherwise. 'puruśottama' is read as Puruṣottamadeva, the grammarian and lexicographer, author of the Hārāvalī. 'praṇītāhārāvalī' is read as praṇītā hārāvalī. The colophon has no date. The invocation of Rāmacandra, Saṅkaṭā, Hanumān and others suggests a late copy, but nothing more can be said.

title: Kāśīmāhātmya
subject: Purāṇa
colophon: iti śrībrahmavaivartte purāṇe tṛtīyavibhāge rahasyātirahasye kāśīmahātmye ṣaḍviṃśo dhyāyaḥ 26 || śrīrāma likhitaṃ motirāma vidyārathi(!)putrasya haranārāyaṇa || (fol. 161v8–9)
notes: 'śrīrāma' at the start is an invocation, not a name. 'vidyārathi(!)' is very likely a corruption of vidyārthī 'student', describing Motirāma, and not a father's name. 'putrasya haranārāyaṇa' has broken syntax. The reading used here is '[copy] of [his] son Haranārāyaṇa', i.e. written by the student Motirāma for his son Haranārāyaṇa. Another possible reading is 'Motirāma, son of Haranārāyaṇa', with a Hindi-style misplaced genitive. In that case Haranārāyaṇa would be Motirāma's father (relative_only), the relation would be p1 son_of p2, and the owner role would go. The catalogue gives the scribe as '??'. The colophon is undated.
review: Removed 'Vidyārathi' as a separate person: vidyārathi(!) = vidyārthī 'student', an epithet of the scribe Motirāma ('likhitaṃ motirāma vidyārthī'), now in his titles
Haranārāyaṇa: the son relation now points to Motirāma (putrasya = 'of [his] son'), and the owner role is kept at low confidence; an alternative reading is given in notes
Dropped the son_of relation to the non-person 'Vidyārathi'
Lowered the confidence of the Haranārāyaṇa identification

title: Brahmavaivartapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Saturday 1 Apr 1837, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrībrahmavaivartte mahāpurāṇe nārāyaṇanāradasaṃvāde gaṇeśakhaṇḍe tulasīgaṇapatisaṃvādo nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo ʼdhyāyaḥ 46 || śrīśāke 1759 caitrakṛṣṇa 11 gurau devadattena lekhayo(!) (fol. 88r6–7)
notes: 'lekhayo(!)' is corrupt (marked by the cataloguer). It could stand for likhitam/lekhitam, which would make Devadatta the scribe. It could also be a causative form (lekhāpitam/lekhayitam, from the stem lekhaya-), which would make him the commissioner. Or it could be Nepali 'lekhyo' ('wrote'). The instrumental 'devadattena' fits either reading. Scribe is the preferred role, but commissioner is possible. Date: ŚS 1759 + 78 = 1837 CE. Caitra kṛṣṇa 11 falls around March/April 1837, depending on whether months are counted amānta or pūrṇimānta. This agrees with the catalogue's ŚS 1759. This colophon closes adhyāya 46 of the Gaṇeśakhaṇḍa, so it may be an internal section colophon rather than the final one.
review: Devadatta: confidence lowered from high to medium. 'lekhayo(!)' is corrupt. It may stand for likhitam (scribe), for a causative lekhāpitam/lekhayitam (commissioner), or for Nepali 'lekhyo' (wrote). Scribe is kept as the most likely role, and the ambiguity is now in notes.
Weekday changed from 'gurau' to 'Thursday (guru)'.
Notes expanded to cover the ambiguity and the date check.

title: Vālmīkirāmāyaṇasya(araṇyā, kiṣkiṃdhyā, sundarottarakāṇḍa saṭīka)
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Sunday 16 Dec 1798, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: hai oṃ ityārṣe rāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye uttarakāṃḍe svargārohaṇaṃ nāmaikādaśotaraśatatamaḥ sargaḥ samāptaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ || (fol. 211v5-6 ) iti rāmābhirāme śrīrāmīye rāmāyaṇaḥ tilake uttarakāṃḍe ekādaśādhika śatatamaḥ sargaḥ 111 rāmāyaṇa saṃpūrṇaḥ śrīrāmāya namaḥ (fol. 211v3-4 ) śrī samvat 1855 mārgaśīrṣe śuklepakṣe navabhyām || 6 || 〇 || || (fol. 212r11)
notes: The colophon names no scribe. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Śrīrāma Varmā' comes from the commentary's name ('rāmābhirāme śrīrāmīye rāmāyaṇaḥ tilake' = the Rāmāyaṇatilaka, ascribed to Rāma Varmā, which is often credited to Nāgeśa). Rāma Varmā is the commentator, not the copyist. The era is just 'samvat'. VS is assumed from the Devanagari script and the year 1855: NS 1855 is impossible, and ŚS 1855 (1933 CE) is possible but less likely for a plain 'samvat'. VS 1855 Mārgaśīrṣa śukla 9 falls around Nov/Dec 1798 CE. 'navabhyām' is a spelling of navamyām. The '|| 6 ||' after the tithi could be a weekday (6 = Friday) or just a number/ornament. It is left out of weekday as uncertain. The colophon covers only the end of the Uttarakāṇḍa (sarga 111).

date.weekday: '6' cleared. The '|| 6 ||' after the tithi is not clearly a weekday; flagged in notes

title: Gaṃgāvataraṇacaṃpū
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrimahārāṣṭrakulāvataṃsaciraṃ tanamorvaṇīkaropanāmaka kiṃcit kāla janita vāṃdhavakaropaṇāmaka śrimat samastaśāstrapārāvārapāraṃgamadīkṣia ṭhuḍhirārātmajasāhityaśāstrapārāvārapārīṇakavitākāṃtāra kaṃṭhīravasarvakhadānadīkṣāviakṣaṇa śrīvad dīkṣitavālakṛṣṇatanūjanmaśaṃkaradīkṣitaviracite gaṃgāvataraṇacaṃpūpravaṃdhe gaṃgācaraṃākaḥ saptama ucchāsaḥ || saptamoyaṃgraṃtha || || (fol. 64r4-8)
notes: This is only the author's colophon, at the end of the 7th ucchvāsa ('ucchāsaḥ' in the manuscript) of the Gaṅgāvataraṇacampū by Śaṅkara Dīkṣita. Śaṅkara was the son of Bālakṛṣṇa Dīkṣita and grandson of Ḍhuṇḍhirāja Dīkṣita, from a Mahārāṣṭrian family (18th century). No scribe, owner, date or place of copying is given. Corrupt readings: 'ṭhuḍhirā' stands for Ḍhuṇḍhirāja, 'dīkṣia' for dīkṣita, 'tanamorvaṇīkara' for ciraṃtana-Morvaṇīkara, and 'vāṃdhavakara' for Bāndhavakara. 'gaṃgācaraṃākaḥ' is probably a corruption of the chapter title and is uncertain.
review: Added relation p1 grandson_of p3, which follows from the father–son chain Ḍhuṇḍhirāja → Bālakṛṣṇa → Śaṅkara.

Made p1's affiliation more precise: Mahārāṣṭra family, old surname Morvaṇīkara and later surname Bāndhavakara (written 'vāṃdhavakara'). The surname epithets describe the family line, so they are recorded as a family affiliation.
Expanded the notes: the author is identified, the copy has no date, and the corrupt readings are explained.

title: Mahābhārata
subject: Mahābhārata

colophon: ❖ śrīśrīsumatijayajitāmitramallasana thva pustaka dayakā || bhāgirāma paramāna yāvelasa || saṃvat 810 kārttikaśudi 9 śubha || (fol. 78v6)
files: A 1060-03 Mahaabhaarata dated to be checked.html
notes: Newari colophon: 'Sumatijayajitāmitramalla had this book made, at the time when Bhāgirāma was pramāṇa (paramāna = chief minister)'. 'Sumati-jaya-' is the regnal prefix of Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. NS 793–816), so it is treated as part of the name and not as a title. The colophon names no scribe; the catalogue's 'Scribe: Bhāgirāma ?' is a misreading, and its 'Donor' field should read commissioner. Bhaktapur as residence comes from the known identity of the king and is not stated in the colophon. NS 810 Kārttika śukla 9 ≈ October/November 1689 CE.
review: p1: 'sumati' is not a title but part of the regnal name (Sumatijaya- prefix of the Bhaktapur kings); name normalized to the standard Jitāmitramalla, titles emptied; roles commissioner + king kept (dayakā = caused to be made; not 'donor' as in the catalogue)
p2: Bhāgirāma's role changed from 'other' to 'minister'; title 'paramāna' given as pramāṇa (chief minister); 'yāvelasa' = 'at the time when (he was pramāṇa)'. He is not the scribe (catalogue's guess)
relation p2→p1 changed from under_reign_of to servant_of (minister of the king)
date: ce_approx corrected to 1689 (Kārttika śukla of NS 810 falls in Oct/Nov 1689); paksa normalized to śukla

notes: Date conflict: the quoted colophon (exp. 161b) reads śrīśāke 1413 (≈1491/92 CE), but the catalogue field gives ŚS 1513 and ŚS 1514. The second colophon (exp. 173b, after Bhoja's Vidvajjanavallabha) reads śrīśāke 1514 idaṃ postakaṃ liṣi(tam) (≈1592 CE). Since 1513 and 1514 are consecutive years, '1413' may be a slip in the cataloguer's quotation and the first part may date to ŚS 1513 (≈1591 CE). The image should be checked. 'vipraḥja (!) jyotiṣI odaṃ postakaṃ || sūnunā prītikareṇa …' is corrupt. It probably means 'this book of the brahmin astrologer (jyotiṣī), written by his son Prītikara', so the father would be an unnamed astrologer and possibly the owner. Prītikara may be identical with the jyotiṣī himself. 'kalaguṇālaṃkṛta' after a lacuna is probably part of a lost epithet. The scribe of the ŚS 1514 colophon is not named; the lacuna (liṣi///) may hide the name.
review: Prītikara: confidence lowered to medium (name flagged (!) by cataloguer; prītikara/pṛthvīkara-type corruption possible); evidence shortened; noted that 'sūnunā' makes him the son of someone, probably the brahmin astrologer (vipra… jyotiṣī) named just before, who is unnamed and so not added as a person
Bhojadeva kept as author (Vidvajjanavallabha, which is the praśna text here); not the reigning king of this copy

title: Lagnacandrikā
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 26 Jan 1890, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: || iti śrī kāśināthakṛtau lagnacaṃdrīkāyāṃ samāptaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ śubhamastu bhuyāta(!) || || śāke 1711 saṃvat 1846 nepāla saṃvat 909 maghumāse vidyauvāre ṣaṣṭI ṛkṣe ca niriti -------- || likhitaṃ śrīkṛṣṇaṃ nāmaṃ graṃthaṃ ca paścine(!) || tadgrāme nāma likhitaṃ pustakaṃ mayāt || 3 || yādṛśṭaṃ ------ parameśvara || 5 || śrīśāradāyai namaḥ || || (fol. 36v4–11)
notes: The colophon gives three eras: ŚS 1711, VS 1846 and NS 909. ŚS 1711 and VS 1846 agree: the Māgha in those years falls in Jan/Feb 1790 CE. NS 909 started in Kārttika 1788, so a Māgha in NS 909 would fall in early 1789. This leaves a one-year conflict, and I followed ŚS and VS. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1811(!)' is an error for 1711. No pakṣa is stated, and the weekday was not checked by calculation. Scribe: the text reads 'likhitaṃ śrīkṛṣṇaṃ nāmaṃ'. Śrī is taken as an honorific here, giving the name Kṛṣṇa, but the catalogue's Śrīkṛṣṇa could be the full name. Place: the catalogue's 'Viṣṇumatyāpūrvabhailagrāma' (a village east of the Viṣṇumatī) is not in the quoted text. The text only has 'paścine(!) ... tadgrāme', which may be 'paścime' (to the west), and there are lacunae marked with dashes. The cataloguer may have read the place in the omitted part, so the place field is left empty. The verses after the scribe's name are the usual stock scribal formulas.

title: Laghujātakamūla
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 8 Feb 1959, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrī varāha mihirācārya racitelaghujātake naṣṭa jātakādhyāyo trayodaśa || khakhākaiḥ(!) ślokai saṃpūrṇaṃ laghujātakaṃ 900 || śrī śubham ----- vidvajjana sabhādhīraraṃganātha tanūjaneḥ(!) || daivajña vālakṛṣṇasya sūnunā bhānu śarmaṇā || 2 || nabho gajadhṛti miteśake vikrama bhūpateḥ || māghe māsi site pakṣe pakṣatyāṃ ravi vāsare ------- /// (fol. 33v3–33r5)
notes: The chronogram nabhas (0), gaja (8), dhṛti (18), read right to left, gives 1880. 'śake vikrama bhūpateḥ' names the era of King Vikrama, so this is VS 1880, not ŚS 1880 as the catalogue says. 'śaka' here just means 'era'. VS 1880 corresponds to 1823/24 CE. Māgha śukla pratipad of that year falls in Jan/Feb 1824 CE. The colophon breaks off after the date ('------- ///'), so the verb that would make Bhānuśarman the scribe is lost. Even so, the verse with the instrumental 'bhānu śarmaṇā' almost certainly names the copyist. 'vidvajjanasabhādhīra' is an epithet of Raṅganātha, not a title. 'khakhākaiḥ ślokai' (= 900 ślokas, read right to left) is the extent of the text, not a date. 'tanūjaneḥ(!)' is a mistake for 'tanūjanuṣaḥ'/'tanūjasya' ('son of'), and agrees with 'vālakṛṣṇasya'.

title: Vṛttaśatakam
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: || iti śrī manorathācārya suta maheśvara viracite vṛttaśataṃ samāptaṃ || || ravākṣi(!)vargayute rudraghane śākerkaraśmibhiḥ || śuṣkekusarite kālehyamāryomalikhadvudhaḥ || || samāptaṃ śubhambhūyāt || || śrī manmaṅgalamūrttipadābjaṃ jayati || || śubhaṃ || (fol. 9r9–10)
notes: The dating verse is an anuṣṭubh: 'ravākṣi(!)vargayute rudraghane śāke 'rkaraśmibhiḥ | śuṣke kusarite kāle hy amāryo 'likhad budhaḥ'. Its first pāda is one syllable short. 'rudraghana' = 11³ = 1331, to which the square of the number in 'ravākṣi(!)' is added. The candidate readings give very different years. If akṣi = 2 alone, 1331 + 4 = ŚS 1335 (c. 1413 CE). If rāma-akṣi = 23, 1331 + 529 = ŚS 1860 (c. 1938 CE). If rasa-akṣi = 26, 1331 + 676 = ŚS 2007 (too late). The year is therefore left undetermined. 'śāke' marks the era as Śaka. 'arkaraśmibhiḥ śuṣke kusarite kāle' describes the hot season (rivers dried by the sun's rays) and is not part of the number. The scribe's name 'hy amāryo' is doubtful. It could be a corruption, e.g. of 'amātyo' (a minister), in which case no personal name is given. 'budhaḥ' ('the learned one') is an epithet. 'maṅgalamūrti' in the closing invocation is a deity (Gaṇeśa) and is not recorded as a person.
review: Date: parsed the chronogram. 'rudraghane' = 11³ = 1331, to which the square (varga) of an uncertain number is added; 'ravākṣi(!)' is corrupt, so the year is left unresolved and ce_approx stays empty. Possible readings are given in notes.

Date: removed 'śāke 'rkaraśmibhiḥ śuṣke kusarite kāle' from the year. It describes the season (rivers dried by the sun's rays, i.e. the hot season) and is not part of the number. The verse is restructured accordingly.
Scribe p3: kept as low confidence. 'budha' moved out of titles: it is an epithet ('the learned one'), not a caste or office title. Evidence string corrected to match the colophon.

colophon: || śārāvalyāṃmuccanīcasvatrikoṇa mitrāri bhavanādhyāyaḥ || || || śubhaṃ || śrīśāke 1647 māse 12 tithau 7 vāre 2 likhitamidaṃ gṛhītamidaṃ vā parahastā cakrapāṇI śarmaṇāsudhiyā śubham || vanhivāṇa nayanamitāḥ 253 sārāvalyāṃ suniścitā ślokāḥ || vāṇananda nayanamitāḥ 295 ślokāśchandairanuṣṭupāsaṃkhyā || || (fol. 7r12–14)
notes: The catalogue field says ŚS 1674, but the colophon reads śāke 1647 (the digits look swapped in the catalogue). ŚS 1647 + 78 = 1725 CE. The month is only given as a number (12), and the pakṣa is not stated. If months are counted from Caitra, month 12 is Phālguna, which would put the date in about Feb–Mar 1726 CE. Weekday 2 is probably Monday. The colophon reads 'likhitamidaṃ gṛhītamidaṃ vā parahastā(t) cakrapāṇiśarmaṇā sudhiyā': Cakrapāṇi either copied the MS himself or obtained it from someone else. So he is clearly the owner, but he may not be the scribe. 'sudhiyā' (sudhī, 'the wise') is a descriptive word, not a title. The two bhūtasaṃkhyā phrases are verse counts, not dates: vahni(3)-bāṇa(5)-nayana(2) = 253 ślokas in the Sārāvalī, and bāṇa(5)-nanda(9)-nayana(2) = 295 in the anuṣṭubh metre. Both are read correctly.

colophon: || iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ eṣīkaparvaṇI navamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 9 || || śreyostu || śaśisāgarakāṃkeʼsminmārge kṛṣṇe tithau hareḥ | eṣīkaparvavyalikhadrāmaśaṃkaraśarmakaḥ || || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || samvat 939 vaiśāṣa vadi 5 thvakunhukao didayakādinajulo || || śubhaṃ || || || || (fol. 9v7–9)
notes: The chronogram is śaśi = 1, sāgara = 4, aṅka = 9. Read right to left this gives 941. 'Hareḥ tithi' = ekādaśī. The verse gives no era. NS is assumed because the colophon also has a Newari line, so this is ca. Nov/Dec 1820 CE. If sāgara is taken as 7, the year would be 971. A second date, 'samvat 939 vaiśāṣa vadi 5', follows with a Newari phrase 'thvakunhukao didayakādinajulo', which is unclear: perhaps 'on this day ... was given/completed'. That would be NS 939 ≈ April/May 1819 CE, which is before the chronogram year 941, so the two dates conflict. The colophon falls into two parts. The first (verse colophon with the NS 545 date and the scribe Rāmagupta) cannot belong to the reign of Jagajjyotirmalla (Bhaktapur, c. NS 733-757 / 1613-1637 CE), who is named in the second part (fol. 41r-41v) together with the mahāmātras Rājasiṃhadeva and Nāthasiṃhadeva ('etayoḥ śirobhūtaprastāvakṣaṇe'). The likeliest explanation is that the NS 545 colophon of the exemplar was copied over, and that the present Maithili copy was made under Jagajjyotirmalla (c. 1613-1637). In that case Rāmagupta is the scribe of the exemplar, not of this copy, and the scribe of this copy is unnamed. A miscomputed chronogram is less likely. 'anvabādhe'śvaragurusvadine' is corrupt: 'guru' gives Thursday. 'gobhāmadāyāḥ' in the praise of the scribe is unclear and possibly corrupt (a mother's name or a place?). It is left unidentified. title: Bhagavadgītā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Monday 10 Apr 1843, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrībhagavatgī(1)tāsūpaniṣatsu brahmavidyāyāṃ yogaśāstre śrī(2)kṣṛṇārjunasaṃvāde mokṣayogonāmāṣṭādaśo(3)dhyāyaḥ || 18 || samāptoyaṃ śrībhagavadgītāśā(4)stram || śrīśubham astu sarvajagatām || (5) tat sat saṃvat || 1900 || caitra śruti(6)vatadaṃśāṃ (!) śubham || (fol. 124r6 &124v1–6)
notes: The colophon names no scribe, commissioner, owner or king. The era is not stated ('saṃvat'). VS is assumed from the Devanagari script, the late date, and the catalogue's 'SAM 1900'. Caitra VS 1900 falls around March–April 1843. The day string 'śrutivatadaṃśāṃ (!)' is corrupt. The most likely reading is '…daśamyāṃ' (tenth tithi), with a pakṣa word (śudi/vadi) garbled in 'śrutiva(ta)'. Another possibility is that 'śruti' is a number word (= 4), which would make the tithi caturthī. The tithi is therefore uncertain and the pakṣa is left blank.
review: No changes to persons, relations, place or purpose: none are named, and the colophon gives no copying place or purpose.
Date kept as VS 1900 Caitra = c. 1843 CE. The era is only 'saṃvat', and VS is inferred. NS 1900 is impossible. ŚS 1900 (= 1978 CE) is unlikely for this manuscript.
Notes expanded on the corrupt tithi string: other readings are possible, and no pakṣa can be recovered.

notes: The colophon gives two dates that agree: Śāka 1752 (+78 = 1830) and '1887 sāla', which is Vikrama Saṃvat (−57 = 1830). This places the copy in about August–September 1830 CE. The scribe's name 'tilocanda' is flagged (!) by the cataloguer. It could be a corrupt form of Tilocana/Trilocana, or a vernacular name such as Tilokcand. 'upādhyā(!)armaṇe(!)' stands for upādhyāya-śarmaṇe. The dative ending would strictly mean 'written for him'. It is taken here, as by the cataloguer, as a slip for the instrumental (written by him), so he is recorded as scribe. The place was a kacaharī (revenue office) village at Rangeli near the Bakraha (Vakrāhā) river, in Vijayapur, Morang.
review: Scribe confidence lowered to medium: the name 'tilocanda(!)' is flagged by the cataloguer (possibly Tilocana/Trilocana), and 'śarmaṇe' is grammatically dative ('for'), not instrumental ('by'). It is read as a slip for śarmaṇā, so the role stays scribe, but this is uncertain.

title: Haritālikāpūjāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Thursday 27 Mar 1969, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti haritālikāśivapūjā samāptaṃḥ(!) || aṣṭḥā(!)daśāṃkeṃduśāke māse madhau stathā(!) mūlakṣye(!) bhaṃ || yogavyatiś ca navami(!) asitās(!)tathā bhavanāthadvijaskasya(!) likhitaṃ saumyavāsare || 1 || śubham (fol. 7v8-9
notes: The chronogram aṣṭādaśa (18) + aṅka (9) + indu (1) is to be read left to right as ŚS 1891. With the usual right-to-left rule it would give ŚS 1918 (1996 CE), which is very likely too late for an A-series NGMCP reel. ŚS 1891 checks out astronomically: Caitra kṛṣṇa navamī counted pūrṇimānta (the dark half after Phālguna pūrṇimā, 4 March 1969) falls on 12 March 1969, a Wednesday (saumya = Budha). That day the Moon was in mūla and the yoga was vyatīpāta (sidereal Sun about 327° + Moon about 249° ≈ 216°). This agrees with the catalogue's tentative '1891?'. The pūrṇimānta month naming suggests a Maithili scribe. The scribe's name is corrupt: 'bhavanāthadvijaskasya' is probably for bhavanāthadvijasya, or dvijakasya with a -ka suffix. This does not affect the name Bhavanātha. 'yogavyatiś' = vyatīpāta yoga; 'mūlakṣye bhaṃ' = mūlarkṣe bham (nakṣatra mūla).

notes: The year is in the Śālivāhana Śaka era: ŚS 1806 + 78 = 1884 CE. In the amānta reckoning, Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 13 falls around late May 1884. In the pūrṇimānta reckoning it falls around late April 1884. Only a rough check was made: the stated Wednesday seems to fit late April better, but neither date has been verified. 'vakṣagotrāya' is probably corrupt for 'vatsagotrāya'. Also, 'gotrāya' is dative while 'kṛṣṇalālaśarmaṇaḥ' is genitive. The phrase can be read as 'book written by Kṛṣṇalāla Śarman' (scribe, which is how the catalogue reads it) or as 'book (written for and) belonging to Kṛṣṇalāla Śarman of the Vatsa gotra' (owner). Both roles are recorded and confidence is medium.

title: Devyāparādhakṣ[a]māpana
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Sunday 7 Sep 1919, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti devyāparādhakṣemāpanam (!) || || || || || || || || samāptaṃ caṃḍikāstavaṃ śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭhayoḥ (!) || || śāke rūpayugāṣṭabhūparimite bhādre siterke harau dvādaśyāṃ bhṛguvāsare śaśadhare raudre gate gīṣpatau || puṣye śrīja〈〈ga〉〉daṃbikāstavam idaṃ trivikrame rājake gaurīdattadvijo lilekha matimān bhoraṣṭāreka (!) ? || 1 || śubham bhavatu || || (fol. 92v5–7)
notes: The chronogram is rūpa 1, yuga 4, aṣṭa 8, bhū 1. Read right to left this gives 1841, and the era is stated as śāke: ŚS 1841 = 1919 CE. 'siterke harau' is read as sita (= śukla) + arke harau (sun in Siṃha), which fits Bhādra. In 1919 Jupiter was in sidereal Cancer (Puṣya), which supports the ŚS reading. 'śaśadhare raudre' would put the moon in Ārdrā, which is astronomically odd for śukla dvādaśī; the cataloguer may have quoted it wrongly. 'trivikrame rājake' is taken as a reference to Vāmana/Trivikrama-dvādaśī (Bhādra śukla 12), not to a reigning king. If it did name a ruler (e.g. a Trivikrama Sen), the year would have to be VS (1784 CE), but Jupiter's position argues against that. The catalogue's scribe field 'Gaurīdatta Trivikramarāja' is a misreading of this phrase. 'bhoraṣṭāreka (!)' is corrupt, so its meaning is uncertain (a place name, or the end of a verse).
review: Removed p2 'Trivikrama' as king: Bhādra śukla dvādaśī is Vāmana-dvādaśī, the festival of Trivikrama (Viṣṇu), so 'trivikrame rājake' most likely refers to that day (perhaps a corruption of 'rājati'), not to a ruler. The relation under_reign_of was removed too.
nakshatra_yoga: Puṣya refers to Jupiter (gate gīṣpatau puṣye), not to the moon; the moon is said to be 'raudre' (Ārdrā?). Field rewritten.
Notes: the VS 1784 alternative was dropped as unlikely. In 1919 Jupiter stood in sidereal Cancer (Puṣya); in 1784 it did not. ŚS 1841 = 1919 CE is kept.
Place is now marked as doubtful: 'bhoraṣṭāreka' is corrupt and may not be a place name at all.

subject: Stotra
date_note: ≈ 1929 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti mārkaṃḍeyapurāṇe sāvarṇike manvaṃtare devimāhātmye (!) surathavaiśyayor varapradānaṃnāma trayadasodhyāyaḥ (!) || 13 || (fol. 53v5–6) uvāca || śrīsāke (!) 1854 śrīsamvat 1986 sāla kauṃḍinye (!) gograsya sadāśivasavarṇaprapautrāyaḥ (!) suta (!) śrīkāṃtasarmaṇa (!) prauyaḥ (!) suta (!) bālakṛṣṇaḥ (!) putrāyaḥ (!) sutaḥ || hariṣṇa (!) sarmaṇa (!) putrāyaḥ (!) suteḥ (!) || devadattapādhyā (!) pyākuralapustakaṃ liṣitaṃ śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ subham (!) astu (fol. 53v6–9)
notes: The two dates disagree. Śaka 1854 is about 1932 CE and corresponds to VS 1989. VS 1986 is about 1929/30 CE and corresponds to Śaka 1851. I recorded the VS date. The descent chain is garbled ('prapautrāyaḥ suta', 'prauyaḥ suta', 'putrāyaḥ sutaḥ', 'putrāyaḥ suteḥ'). I read it as Devadatta being the great-great-grandson of Sadāśiva, great-grandson of Śrīkānta, grandson of Bālakṛṣṇa and son of Harikṛṣṇa, which gives a single line of descent. 'devadattapādhyā pyākuralapustakaṃ liṣitaṃ' means Devadatta Upādhyāya Pyākurel either wrote the book (as the catalogue says) or owned it ('Pyākurel's book'). I gave him both roles. 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ' just before 'subham astu' is most likely an invocation. It could possibly be a separate scribe, but that is unlikely. 'sadāśivasavarṇa' is corrupt; it may stand for 'sadāśivaśarmaṇa'. 'gograsya' should read 'gotrasya'.
review: Removed Rāmakṛṣṇa (p6) as scribe: 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ subham astu' is most naturally a closing invocation, not a scribe's name; the wrote_for relation went with it

Devadatta: roles changed from owner to scribe + owner. The construction (descent chain, then the name, then 'pustakaṃ liṣitaṃ') presents him as the writer, which matches the catalogue. Confidence lowered to medium
Pyākurala (Pyākurel, a Nepali Brahmin surname) moved into Devadatta's titles/affiliation and removed from as_written

The descent chain is now read as 'X's descendant's son' at each step (prapautra-suta, pautra-suta, putra-suta, suta). This keeps the same five-generation line (Sadāśiva → Śrīkānta → Bālakṛṣṇa → Harikṛṣṇa → Devadatta) but explains the kin terms consistently. Evidence strings updated
Sadāśiva: the 'śarman' title is uncertain because 'savarṇa' is corrupt; confidence set to medium
Notes updated about the date discrepancy and the reading of the name

review: Notes: spelled out that the two eras conflict. VS 1878 corresponds to ŚS 1743, and ŚS 1741 corresponds to VS 1876, so they are two years apart. They are not just two ways of writing the same year.

Date: kept VS 1878 as the main era because it comes first ('saṃvat'). ce_approx is still 1822, since Phālguṇa kṛṣṇa 6 of VS 1878 falls in Feb/Mar 1822.

title: Ādityahṛdayastotra
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Sunday 4 Apr 1875, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: Kārttikādi, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrībhaviṣyottarapurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇārjunasaṃvāde ādityahṛdayastotraṃ sa〈〈pu〉〉mpurṇam śubham || || || || || || || || || || || || || || || || || iti samvat || 1932 || sālamiti caitravadi 13 roja 5 śubham (fol. 14v1–4)
notes: The catalogue names Śivarāma as the scribe, but the quoted colophon (fol. 14v1–4) has no personal name. He may be named elsewhere in the manuscript, but he is not listed here because the colophon gives no evidence for him. The date uses the Persian-influenced formula 'sālamiti … roja 5', where roja 5 most likely means the 5th weekday, Thursday. Era is taken as Vikrama (VS): 1932 − 57 = 1875. With pūrṇimānta reckoning ('vadi'), Caitra kṛṣṇa 13 falls at the end of VS 1932, which is about March 1876. If the month is counted differently, it could be about March–April 1875. 'sa〈〈pu〉〉mpurṇam' contains a cataloguer's insertion mark; it means saṃpūrṇam.
review: weekday: 'roja 5' interpreted as Thursday (5th weekday counting from Sunday); as-written form kept in parentheses
paksa: normalized 'vadi' to 'kṛṣṇa (vadi)'
ce_approx: kept 1876, but added a note that the year could be 1875 depending on the month reckoning
notes: expanded to cover the 'sālamiti … roja' formula and the date reasoning

title: Yugalakiśorasahasranāmastotra
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 4 Oct 1774, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīnāradīyapurāṇe śrīnāradoktaṃ yugalakiśorasahasranāmastotraṃ s(!)māptaṃ śrīr astu savat(!) 1831 varṣe śāke 1697 ā〈〈‥〉〉śvinamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe 13 bhaumavāsare la(!)khitaṃ rāvala〈〈‥〉〉 śaṃbhūrāma(gavaḍa) śrīr astu śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī (fol. 10v6–10)
notes: The colophon gives two eras: VS 1831 and ŚS 1697. In Caitrādi reckoning VS 1831 matches ŚS 1696, not 1697. In Kārttikādi reckoning (used in Gujarat), Āśvina of VS 1831 falls in Sept/Oct 1775 and matches ŚS 1697. So the two eras agree, and the date is about Oct 1775 CE. The weekday (Tuesday) was not checked. The text has a lacuna between 'rāvala' and 'śaṃbhūrāma', which may hide part of the name. 'Rāvala' is taken as a title or community name. 'gavaḍa' (in parentheses in the transcript; the catalogue reads 'Gabaḍa') is probably a surname or caste name; it might be Gauḍa, but that is uncertain. The names suggest a scribe from western India (Gujarat or Rajasthan) and not a Nepalese one.
review: Name reduced to stem 'Śambhūrāma'; 'Gavaḍa' (catalogue: Gabaḍa) moved to titles as surname/caste name rather than part of the personal name

ce_approx changed from 1774 to 1775: ŚS 1697 (+78) points to 1775, and Āśvina of VS 1831 falls in 1775 only if the year is Kārttikādi (Gujarati reckoning). This fits the western Indian names Rāvala and Gavaḍa
Notes expanded: explains how the two eras fit together and flags the lacunae in the name

title: Krṣṇāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Wednesday 3 Jun 1857, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)

notes: The catalogue field says 'SAM 1779', but the colophon explicitly says 'śāke 1779'. That is Śaka era, ca. 1857 CE. Read as VS it would be ca. 1722 CE, but nothing in the text supports that. 'jyeṣṭā(!)dhika' stands for jyeṣṭhādhika, i.e. the intercalary (adhika) Jyeṣṭha. I have not checked whether ŚS 1779 actually had an adhika Jyeṣṭha. The text is attributed to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa (Śeṣa–Dharaṇī dialogue), which is a textual attribution, not a person.
review: No substantive changes. The first reading is correct: no persons are named, the era is explicitly Śaka, and 1779 + 78 = 1857 CE.

notes: The colophon names no people. It gives two date statements for the same day, Māgha śukla 5, Revatī nakṣatra, śubha yoga, Tuesday. (1) In the first, the NS chronogram ritu (6), rasa (6), nava (9), read right to left, gives NS 966, which is about 1845/46 CE. (2) In the second, Kali 4942 and VS 1898 both point to early 1842 CE. Śaka 1796 (= 1874 CE) contradicts both and is probably a scribal error for 1763. So the NS and the VS/Kali figures conflict by about 4 years. The NS chronogram may be corrupt, e.g. for 962, or the two statements may refer to different events (exemplar and copy). The VS figure is taken as the main date. The text title in the colophon is garbled ('cau(3)sathi lijñeśvara', 'cauṣaṣṭilīgāsvara' = Catuḥṣaṣṭiliṅgeśvara).
review: No persons: confirmed, the colophon names no scribe, patron, owner or king.

Date: the first reading gave era NS with year '966?' and CE 1842, which do not agree (NS 966 + 880 = 1845/46). Changed the main era to VS 1898, the only date written fully in figures that agrees with Kali 4942; CE about 1842.
Chronogram: ritu (6), rasa (6), nava (9), read right to left, gives NS 966. Recorded this in the notes as a conflict, not treated as a corruption of 962.
Śaka 1796 does not match the other eras (VS 1898 implies Śaka 1763); noted as a scribal error.
Weekday: both dates give Tuesday (maṃgalavāra; aṃgavāra for aṅgāravāra).

date_raw: rasaabhrasamāyuktau śrutiḥ saṃvat tadāpayo || kartimāṣI kṛṣṇapakṣe dvitīyāyāṃ pujadine
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Oct 1285, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: (fol. ) tanmayā likhyate karmapratiṣṭhāyām mayākulaṃ || fol.2a iti ghaṭitaliṅgapratiṣṭhāvidhi || fol.43a iti vāṇaliṅgapraṭiṣṭhāvidhiḥ || fol. 43b tata sthitesthāpanavidhiḥ || fol. 44a iti jirṇoddhāravidhiḥ || athedāniṃ bhagavatīprātiṣṭhocyate || Fol.46b iti devipraṭIṣṭāvidhiḥ || fol.49b iti dvārapraṭIṣṭhā || sāṃprataṃ prāsādahṛdayavidhir ucyate ||fol.52a iti hṛtpraṭiṣṭhāvidhiḥ || fol.57b iti dhvajaro(pa)ṇavidhiḥ || fol. 60a iti praṭiṣthāpaddhati samāptāḥ ||fol.60b yadā nelālabhūpāṇānandamallābhipārvati | rasaabhrasamāyuktau śrutiḥ saṃvat tadāpayo || kartimāṣI kṛṣṇapakṣe dvitīyāyāṃ pujadine || kāyachādayaharṣeṇa likhitaṃ drutaṃ ||
notes: The date is a chronogram, read right to left: rasa = 6, abhra = 0, śruti = 4, giving NS 406, which is about Oct/Nov 1286 CE. The colophon gives no era name, but NS is assumed because of the reign of Ānandamalla (c. 1274–1310), which fits that year. 'nelālabhūpāṇānandamallābhipārvati' stands for 'nepālabhūpāle ānandamalle 'bhipālayati'. 'kāyachā' is probably a corruption of kāyastha. The name could be read as Dayāharṣa or Dayaharṣa; 'Udayaharṣa' is less likely. 'pujadine' is not a standard weekday name and may be corrupt, perhaps for budhadine or gurudine. The weekday has not been checked against the date. 'likhitaṃ drutaṃ' looks like a metrically incomplete line.
review: Lowered confidence for the scribe to medium. 'kāyachādayaharṣeṇa' is corrupt: the reading kāyastha + Dayāharṣa (or Dayaharṣa) is likely but not certain.
Weekday: 'pujadine' is not a standard weekday name, so it is now marked as doubtful and not treated as a known day.

title: Darśapūrṇamāsī
subject: Kk
date_note: = Monday 15 Sep 1466, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: samvata 586(!) aśukla(!)pañcaṃmyāṃ tithau | jyeṣṭa(!) nakṣatre || somavāsare kātyāyanoktaādhāneṣu suci(!) iṣṭiḥ samāptaḥ|| edāniṃ darśapūrṇṇamāsī samāptaḥ|| likhitam ideṃ || śrīlaḍitabrumā(!) śrīmānīgalake dakṣiṇata(!) || pitho valānihmaṃ yāmagṛhādivāsina|| dvijavara śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha(!) svaṃ pvaṣṭakaṃ|| (fol. )
purpose: ātmaja-prabodhanārtham: for the instruction of (the scribe's) son; svaṃ pustakam: his own book
notes: 'śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha' is ambiguous. The preferred reading is Śaśideva as scribe and owner, writing to instruct his unnamed son (ātmaja-prabodhanārtham), with 'vāsina' as an instrumental agent. The alternative is that the scribe is an unnamed son of Śaśideva copying for his own study. 'aśukla' is most likely Āśvina śukla: Jyeṣṭhā on śukla 5 implies the Sun is in Kanyā. The cataloguer marked the year 586 with (!), so it may be misread. NS 586 = 1466 CE, but the weekday has not been verified. 'Laḍitabrumā' = Lalitabruma/Lalitapura (Patan); 'Mānīgala' = Maṇigal, the palace area. 'pitho' may be a corruption of 'pīṭha' or of a locality name.
review: Re-segmented 'dvijavara śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha': read as 'dvijavara-śrī-Śaśideva[na] ātmaja-prabodhanārtha[ṃ]' ('by the excellent brahmin Śaśideva, to instruct his son'). The instrumental 'vāsina' (= vāsinā) needs an agent noun, and a scribe naming himself only as 'son of X' would be unusual. Śaśideva is therefore the scribe and owner (svaṃ pustakaṃ), not merely the father.
Removed p1 'Śaśidevātmaja' as a person. The son is not named, so he appears only in purpose and notes. The son_of relation is removed as well.
Date: 'aśukla' read as Āśvina śukla. On śukla 5 the Moon in Jyeṣṭhā puts the Sun around Kanyā, which fits amānta Āśvina. Set month Āśvina and pakṣa śukla. NS 586 ≈ 1466 CE is kept.
Purpose rewritten as instruction of the scribe's son; the book is his own.
Place as_written is now the full phrase; Patan is kept (Lalitabruma/Lalitapura, Mānīgala).

title: Kulārṇavatantram
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Tuesday 14 Feb 1662, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti śrīkulārṇavamahārahasye sapādalakṣagranthe pañcamakhaṇḍe nāmavāsanādikathanaṃnāma saptadaśollāsasamāptaḥ || || śrībhavānīśaṃkaraprītir astu || || dvitīyanāgābdhiyute gate nepālavatsare | māghamāsya site pakṣe ekādaśāttithau (!) śubhe || pūrṇṇarājadivjasyājñāṃ dhṛtvāśirapico(?) kutulilekha daivajñaḥ pustakaṃ ca kulārṇṇavaṃ || || samvat 782 māghakṛṣṇa ekādaśyāṃ tithau kutujosina saṃpūrṇṇa coyā || || (fol. 198r4–6 and v1–2)
notes: Chronogram: dvitīya = 2, nāga = 8, abdhi = 7 (the seven oceans). Read right to left this gives NS 782, which matches the prose 'samvat 782' and the catalogue. NS 782 is 1662 CE, Māgha falling in Jan–Feb. The two dates disagree on the pakṣa: the verse has 'site pakṣe' (śukla) and the prose has 'māghakṛṣṇa'. The prose value is recorded here, but the conflict is unresolved. 'divja' is most likely dvija (a brahmin), though daivajña is also possible. 'dhṛtvāśirapico(?)' is corrupt; the sense is probably 'ājñāṃ dhṛtvā śirasi' ('placing his order on my head'), meaning Kutu copied the book on Pūrṇarāja's instruction. 'kutulilekha' = Kutu lilekha. The Newari 'kutujosina' = Kutu Josī with the ergative -na, and josī is the Newari equivalent of the Sanskrit 'daivajñaḥ' used for the same scribe.
review: p1 Pūrṇarāja: title changed from 'daivajña' to 'dvija' ('divja' is most likely a miswriting of dvija); confidence lowered to medium because the epithet and the following 'śirapico(?)' are corrupt
p2 Kutu: shortened the evidence

date: kept NS 782 / 1662 CE. Explained the chronogram: abdhi = 7 (the seven oceans), so reading right to left 'dvitīya-nāga-abdhi' gives 2-8-7 = 782. This is a normal value for abdhi, not a corruption
notes: the pakṣa conflict is now stated explicitly. The verse has 'site pakṣe' (śukla) and the prose has 'māghakṛṣṇa'; kṛṣṇa is kept from the prose
purpose: reworded as a benediction, since it is not a commission purpose

colophon: || iti śrīkulārṇṇavamahārahasye sapādalakṣagranthe pañcamakhaṇḍanāmavāsanādikathanaṃnāma saptadaśamollāsaḥ || 7 || śrīmatanyaṃpāla (!)samvat bhuvanākāśabhairavaṃ | jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇacaturthe tu saṃpūrṇṇaṃ ravivāsare || likhārddhaṃ tasisiṃhena darddhaṃ bhavāniśaṃkarau | kulācārasya mahātmyaṃ mokṣārthaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || || || śubha || (fol. 128r5–8)
notes: The phrase 'śrīmatanyaṃpāla (!)samvat' is almost certainly a scribal error or misreading of 'śrīmannepālasaṃvat'. The chronogram bhuvanākāśabhairava represents 803 (bhuvana = 3, ākāśa = 0, bhairava = 8). Two scribes divided the copying: Tasisiṃha wrote one half and Bhavānīśaṅkara the other (likhārddhaṃ tasisiṃhena [ta]darddhaṃ bhavāniśaṃkar[eṇa]).

notes: The catalogue names Dharmasena Vajrācārya as the scribe, but the Newari text says the copy was written and given to Vajrācārya Dharmasyaṇa/Dharmasena ('cosyaṃ biyā') and that the writing was done and handed over by Vajrācārya Udayacandra ('likhita ... udayacandrajusyaṃ biyā juro'). notes: The colophon is undated and names no place. 'liṣiṭa … nihmasyana coyā jula' (Newari: 'written … the two of them wrote it') says the copy was made jointly by Karmācārya 'Dhamendrasiṃha' (probably for Dharmendrasiṃha) and his son. Only the ending of the son's name, '…deva', survives; the rest is lost in a lacuna marked by the cataloguer. The colophon gives karmācārya only for the father, though the son probably shared it. It closes with the stock scribe's disclaimer (yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā…: 'I copied it as I found it; whether correct or not, the fault is not mine').
review: p1: as_written is 'dhamendrasiṁha' (karmmacārya kept as title); normalized reading Dharmendrasiṃha is an emendation, so confidence lowered from high to medium and the emendation is noted
p2: name lost in a lacuna, only '…deva' survives; confidence lowered from medium to low, as_written/evidence kept

title: Devīrahasyam
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Saturday 5 Oct 1929, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrī rudrayāmale taṃtre devīrahasye sarvasiddhi pradāyane utrārdhernāma ṣaṣṭittamaḥ paṭalaḥ60 samāptoyaṃ devīrahasyābhidhastaṃtra saṃpūrṇaṃ siddhi śubha saṃbhavet śrīsaṃvat 1851 ke krāṃ ra śuddhi śrīdurgāttīja 3 śanivāra iti śrī kāśī svakṣetre śrīmaṇI karṇikā varttate śrīgopālamaṃdirasthāne likhitaṃ -------- śrīparmmānaṃda prakāśācāryeṇa ---- oṃ tatsat śubhamastu || (fol. 163v8–11&164r1–6)
notes: The colophon says only 'śrīsaṃvat 1851'. In a Kāśī context with a Hindi-style date ('1851 ke … śuddhi'), 'saṃvat' normally means Vikrama Saṃvat, which gives about 1794 CE. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1851' (= 1929 CE) is not supported by the wording. 'ke krāṃ ra' is probably '[saṃvat 1851] ke kvāra/kuāra', Hindi for Āśvina. That agrees with 'durgāttīja' (Durgā-tṛtīyā, Āśvina śukla 3). The weekday (Saturday) has not been checked. The scribe's name could be read as Paramānanda with the title 'Prakāśācārya', or as the ascetic-style name Paramānandaprakāśa with the title ācārya. The place of copying is the Gopāla temple near Maṇikarṇikā, Kāśī.

title: Tantrasāra
subject: Tantra
date_raw: nepālikābde viyad aśvavāha māsena masye (!) dhavale ca pakṣe
date_note: = Apr 1650, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāyaśrīkṛṣṇānadabhaṭṭācāryyakṛta (!) tantrasāraḥ samāptaḥ || || śrībhavānī prīṇā (!) tu || || nepālikābde viyad aśvavāha māsena masye (!) dhavale ca pakṣe | anantasiṃho vililekha sarvva anekatantrasya vacaḥ samūhaṃ || tantrasāram idaṃ pustaṃ, lobhāt snehādi kena ca | parebhyo nahi taddeyaṃ gopyaṃ kāryya prayatnataḥ || || śrīcakrarājasya || (fol. 298v4–6)
notes: The chronogram is viyad (0) aśva (7) vāha (7), which gives NS 770 (≈1649/50 CE). That fits the date of Kṛṣṇānanda Āgamavāgīśa (16th–17th century). The value 7 for vāha is the usual one (the horses that draw the sun), but it is not completely certain. The month 'masye' is corrupt: 'matsye' (solar Mīna) is the most likely reading, though 'madhye' or 'māghe' are possible. 'kṛṣṇānada' is a scribal error for Kṛṣṇānanda. The final 'śrīcakrarājasya' most likely refers to the Śrīcakra (a deity or yantra), not a human owner, so no person has been extracted from it. The closing verse forbids giving the book to others, but it names no owner. The catalogue's scribe, Ananta Siṃha, matches the colophon.

notes: The chronogram bhū(1) śara(5) aṅka(9) indu(1), read right to left, gives 1951, which matches the figures. 'śāke vikramake mite' uses śāka in its general sense of 'era', and the era named is Vikrama. So the date is VS 1951 = c. Nov 1894 CE (Kārttika śukla 13, Sunday). The catalogue's 'ŚS 1951' cannot be right, because it would correspond to 2029 CE. I did not verify the weekday precisely. 'Yogeśvarārtham' most likely names a person (perhaps a yogin) for whom the copy was made, but it could also be a devotional dedication to Śiva as Yogeśvara, since parameśvarārpaṇam follows. The scribe's name is written kāśinātha (short i) and normalized to Kāśīnātha. The text is a section of a Haṭhapradīpikā framed as an Umāmaheśvarasaṃvāda.

title: Saptaśatī
subject: Purāṇa / Stotra
date_note: = Monday 22 Mar 1255, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: mahārājādhirājaparameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakaśrīmadabhayamalladevasya rājye | || śrībhaktāpurinivāśine jayatarāmasya pāṭhanimittena bhallokaüdayaharṣavarmeṇa likhitam idaṃ | na me doṣa (!) guṇo vāpi anulekhaviparyayaḥ | yathaiva likhitaṃ pūrvaṃ tathaiva likhitaṃ mayā || nepālasamvatsare bāṇaśailaharāṃnukaṃ | māse caitraśuklatrayodaśyāṃ | somavāsare | śubham astuḥ || (fol. 65r1–5)
notes: The chronogram 'bāṇa-śaila-hara' reads 5-7-3 from right to left, giving NS 375. This fits Abhayamalla's reign (c. 1216–1255 CE). Hara is often 11 in bhūtasaṃkhyā, but 3 is the only value that gives a possible year here. 'harāṃnukaṃ' is corrupt, perhaps for 'harāṅkake'. 'nivāśine' is an error for 'nivāsinaḥ' and goes with Jayatarāma; Bhaktapur is his residence. The catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Bhaktapura' is a reasonable guess but the colophon does not state it. The catalogue's 'Donor: Jayatarāma' is not supported; he may have commissioned the copy, but the colophon does not say so. 'bhalloka' = bhāro, a Newar title.
review: p2 Jayatarāma: removed 'commissioner' (no likhāpitam/lekhayāmāsa; colophon only says the copy was made pāṭhanimittena, for his reading); roles now beneficiary + reader. The catalogue's 'Donor' is not supported by the colophon.

p2 residence normalised to stem 'Bhaktāpurī' (Bhaktapur); the place of copying is emptied because the colophon gives Bhaktapur only as Jayatarāma's residence, not as the place where the copy was made.
p3: 'bhalloka' identified as the Sanskritised form of the Newar title bhāro; it stays in titles with varman.
Date: chronogram check added (bāṇa 5, śaila 7, hara 3, read right to left = 375); ce_approx 1255 kept; weekday normalised to Monday.

title: Sārasamudhṛtisaptaśatikā Kuvjikāmata
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: ≈ 1922 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: śrīśrīmat śrīkuvjikāmate sārātsārasamuddhṛtya saptaśatikāntapaddhati samāptam iti śubham śrī 5 mahārājadhirājaśrītribhuvanavīravikramasāhadevasya vijayarājye pradhānam ātyaśrī 3 mahārājacandraśaṃśerajaṅgavarmaṇas tṛtīyaputreṇa janaralakesarasaṃśeravarmaṇānviṣya (!) saṅgṛhītasya saṃvat 092 varṣe likhitasya prācīnatāḍapatrapustakasyādhāreṇa 1979 vaikramīyavarṣe śrīnepālarājagurūhemarājaśarmaṇā lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya samuddhṛtam idaṃ pustakaṃ cirāya sumanasāṃ saumanasyātha kalpeta | (fol. 25v3–7)
purpose: for the lasting delight of the learned (cirāya sumanasāṃ saumanasyāya)
notes: The copy is dated VS 1979, which is about 1922/23 CE. This fits both Tribhuvana's reign (1911–55) and Candra Śamśera's term as Prime Minister (1901–29). It was copied from an old palm-leaf manuscript dated 'saṃvat 092', which Kesara Śamśera (Kaiser Shumsher), third son of Candra Śamśera, had searched for and collected. The era of that date is not given, but it is very probably NS 92, about 972 CE. That is the exemplar's date, not this copy's. The catalogue gives Hemarāja Śarman as scribe, but the colophon says he had the text written out 'through a scribe' (lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya). He is therefore the commissioner/editor, and the actual copyist is not named. 'saumanasyātha' looks like an error for 'saumanasyāya'. 'rājagurū' should read 'rājaguru'. 'kesarasaṃśera' is a spelling of Kesaraśaṃśera.
review: p2: 'varman' moved from the name to titles (name 'Candraśaṃśerajaṅga'). Title normalised to 'pradhānāmātya'. Roles minister + relative_only kept: he was Prime Minister in VS 1979 and is named to identify his son.

p3: 'varman' moved to titles (name 'Kesarasaṃśera'). Role 'owner' removed: the colophon says only that he searched for and collected the palm-leaf exemplar, not that this copy belongs to him. Role 'other' kept (collector of the exemplar).

p4: 'śarman' moved from the name to titles (name 'Hemarāja'). Title given as 'rājaguru' (Nepālarājaguru). Commissioner role kept because he had the copy made through a scribe (lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya).
Added relation p2 under_reign_of p1.
Purpose rewritten as a paraphrase; 'saumanasyātha' is read as an error for 'saumanasyāya'.
Notes: added the exemplar date (saṃvat 092, probably NS = c. 972 CE) and the unnamed hired scribe; recorded that the catalogue's 'scribe' field conflicts with the colophon.

notes: This is only the ṭīkā's closing colophon: a commentary on Śaṅkara's Chāndogyopaniṣadbhāṣya by Ānandajñāna (= Ānandagiri), pupil of Śuddhānanda; it ends with chapter 6 ('ṣaṣṭhodhyāyaḥ … samāptaḥ'). The catalogue's scribe field 'Bhāgavānaṃdajñāna' is a misreading of 'bhagvadānaṇdajñāna' ('the revered Ānandajñāna'), who is the commentator, not the scribe. Śuddhānanda is recorded only as the commentator's teacher. The closing invocation 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaparamātmane namaḥ' is addressed to a deity, so it adds no person.

title: Sāṅkhyacandrikāsaṭīka
subject: Sāṃkhya
colophon: [mūlāṃśaḥ] (6) iti sāṃkhyacaṃdrikā samāptā || ❁ || (fol. 28r6) [ṭīkāṃśaḥ] (9) iti rāmagovindatīrthaśiṣya nārāyaṇatīrthakṛtā sāṃkhyacaṃdrikā samāptāḥ || ❁ || manvakendumita varṣaśrāvaṇe śuklavāṇa ravisaṃjñavāsare || sāṃkhyatatva dvijarājacandrikāṃ lekhivān (!) notes: The chronogram 'manvakendu' is taken as manv-aṅka-indu: manu = 14, aṅka = 9, indu = 1. Read right to left, this gives 1914. If 'aka' were instead read as arka (12), the number would not make sense. The era is not named. VS 1914 = c. 1857 CE fits; ŚS 1914 is impossible. I have not checked by calculation that Śrāvaṇa śukla 5 fell on a Sunday. Rāmagovindatīrtha appears only as the author's teacher. 'dvijarājacandrikā' is a pun on the title (dvijarāja = moon = candra). 'sudhīvara' ('best of the wise') is an honorific epithet of the scribe, not a caste name. 'lekhivān' is the cataloguer's (!), standing for alekhīt/likhitavān.

title: Siddhāntalakṣaṇaṭippaṇī
subject: Nyāya
date_raw: abhrevarāvdhi śikharīndumite śake vyorjja śaubhra pakṣa guruvārayutā jajāhe
date_note: = Oct 1818, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śri mahāmopādhyāya śrīyuta jagadīśatarkālaṃkāra bhaṭṭācārya viracitā siddhāṃta lakṣaṇasya ṭippaṇī samāptā || || abhrevarāvdhi śikharīndumite śake vyorjja śaubhra pakṣa guruvārayutā jajāhe || siddhāntalakṣaṇakadīdhiti ṭippaṇīṃ hi śrīlālaratnadharaṇī tridaśo alikhaddhi || 1 || || śrī vārāṇasyāmiti śeṣaḥ || || (fol. 16r5-6)
notes: Chronogram: 'abhrevarāvdhi śikharīndu-' is read as abhra (0) – abdhi (4) – śikharin (7) – indu (1). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1740 (about 1818 CE), which fits a copy of a work by Jagadīśa (about 1600). 'vara' (or 'abhre') is corrupt and does not give a clean digit. It could be emended (e.g. svara = 7), but that would give one digit too many, so the reading is uncertain. The first pāda of the Vasantatilakā verse seems to be a syllable short, which supports corruption here. 'vyorjja' = vā ūrja (Kārttika). 'śaubhra' = śubhra/śukla. 'jajāhe' is probably for jagāhe/jajñe. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Śrīlālaratnadharaṇī'. The better reading is śrī-Lālaratna, a dharaṇītridaśa ('god on earth', i.e. a brāhmaṇa). The work is Jagadīśa's ṭippaṇī on the Dīdhiti on the Siddhāntalakṣaṇa portion of the Tattvacintāmaṇi ('siddhāntalakṣaṇakadīdhiti ṭippaṇīṃ'). Raghunātha and Gaṅgeśa are not named, so they are not listed.
review: Date: chronogram resolved as abhra (0) – abdhi (4) – śikharin (7) – indu (1), read right to left, giving Śaka 1740. 'vara' is taken as a corrupt or filler element, not a digit. ce_approx set to 1818 (ŚS+78); year field changed to 1740.
Scribe p2: removed residence 'Vārāṇasī'. The colophon gives Vārāṇasī only as the place of copying ('vārāṇasyām iti śeṣaḥ'), not as where the scribe lived.
Scribe p2: confidence lowered to medium. The name division (Lālaratna + dharaṇītridaśa = bhūdeva, i.e. brāhmaṇa) is a reading, not explicit.
Author p1: titles normalized; 'tarkālaṃkāra' kept as a title. 'mahāmopādhyāya' is the colophon's form of mahāmahopādhyāya.
Notes rewritten: the chronogram is not unreadable, and the metre is irregular.

title: Brahmasūtra
subject: Vedānta
colophon: || iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrīmukundakundagoviṃdaśrīcaraṇaśikṣita śrīrāmānaṃdasarasvatīkṛtau brahmasūtravṛttau brahmāmṛtavarṣīṇyāṃ caturthādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ || samāptoyaṃ graṃthaḥ catvāryadhyo sarvāṇI sūtrāṇI 557 adhikaraṇa 1993 gauṇasūtra 364 pustakamidaṃ pra. Śrīkṛṣṇajośī rāmanagara (fol. 121v13-15)
notes: The text is Rāmānanda Sarasvatī's Brahmāmṛtavarṣiṇī, a vṛtti on the Brahmasūtra. The teacher's name, 'mukundakundagoviṃda', is probably corrupt. 'kunda' may be a dittography, which would give Mukundagovinda; this is not verified. The ownership note 'pustakam idaṃ pra. Śrīkṛṣṇajośī rāmanagara' marks Kṛṣṇa Jośī of Rāmanagara as owner. The abbreviation 'pra.' is unclear, possibly prāptam or a similar word for acquisition. The note may be a later addition, not a scribal colophon. The catalogue's 'Donor' field almost certainly records who lent the manuscript to NGMCP for filming, not a donor in the colophon. Rāmanagara is not identified with certainty. The colophon gives no scribe and no date. Two of the stated counts look doubtful: 'adhikaraṇa 1993' is implausible (perhaps 193), and 'catvāryadhyo' stands for catvāro 'dhyāyāḥ.
review: p1: the 'teacher' role is for the teacher of this copy's people. This man taught the commentator, not anyone involved in the copy, so the role is changed to 'other'. Confidence lowered to medium because the name looks corrupt ('mukundakunda' may be a dittography).
p3: name changed from 'Śrīkṛṣṇa' to 'Kṛṣṇa'. Śrī is an honorific prefix (as in śrīrāmānaṃda), not part of the name.
p3: 'donor' role removed. The colophon only says 'pustakam idaṃ' (owner). The catalogue's Donor field is the NGMCP lender of the manuscript, not a donor named in the colophon.
place: cleared. Rāmanagara is the owner's residence, not a stated place of copying, so it stays only under p3's residence.
notes: rewritten to cover the 'pra.' abbreviation, the possibly corrupt teacher name and the doubtful figures.

title: Meghadūta
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Sunday 26 Aug 1601, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīmahākavikālidāsa〈〈kṛto〉〉viracitaṃ meghadū〈〈ha〉〉tā〈〈si〉〉bhidhānaṃ mahākāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || ❖ || itthaṃbhūtaṃ sucaritam idaṃ meghadūtaṃ ca nāmnā kāmakrīḍāvirahitajane viprayukte vinodaḥ | meghasyāsmin atinipuṇatā buddhibhāvāḥ kavīnāṃ natvāryāyāś caraṇayugalaṃ kālidāsaś cakāra 126 || ❖ || ity ākhyāte surapatisakhā śailakulyāpurīṣu sthitvā sthitvā dhanapatipurīṃ vāsaraiḥ kaiścid āpa matvāgāraṃ kanakaruciraṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ pūrvam uktais tasyotsaṃge kṣititalagatāṃ tāṃ ca dīnāṃ dadarśa || 127 tasmād adrer nigaditapathā śīgram etyālakāyāṃ yakṣāgāraṃ galita(vicakaṃ) dṛṣṭacihnair viditvā yat saṃdiṣṭaṃ praṇayamadhuraṃ guhyakena prayatnāt tadgehinyāḥ sakalam avadat kāmarūpī payodaḥ || 28 || || iti śrīmeghadūtakāvyaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || samvat 1658 bhādrapadabahula 14 dine śrī(nāgapurīyatapāgachebhaºº śrīcaṃdrakīrttisūri‥‥‥‥|| śrīmānakīrttisūri ‥‥| śrīharṣakīrttisūribhr lekhitaḥ (!) || samarasiṃhapaṭhanārthaṃ || (fol. 10r7-10v4)
notes: This is a Jain (Śvetāmbara) colophon from the Nāgapurīya Tapāgaccha; 'tapāgachebhaºº' is the cataloguer's abbreviation. The text names a lineage: Candrakīrtisūri, then Mānakīrtisūri, then Harṣakīrtisūri. The connecting words, probably 'tatpaṭṭe' or 'tacchiṣya', are lost in the lacunae (‥‥), so the pupil relations are inferred. Harṣakīrti of the Nāgapurīya Tapāgaccha is a known author active around 1600 CE. Some sources make him a pupil of Candrakīrti directly, which would make Mānakīrti a fellow pupil rather than his teacher, so the exact link is uncertain. 'sūribhr' should be read 'sūribhir'. Grammatically, 'lekhitaḥ' (causative, 'caused to be written') makes Harṣakīrti the commissioner for Samarasiṃha's study; the catalogue's 'Scribe: Harṣakīrtti' is probably loose. The actual copyist is not named. Samarasiṃha's 'reader' role rests on 'paṭhanārthaṃ' ('for the reading of'). The final verse number '28' is an error for 128. VS 1658 corresponds to about 1601 CE (Bhādrapada, August/September).

date_note: = Friday 2 Feb 1674, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: pūrṇimānta months
colophon: iti pavanadūtaṃ kāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || samvat 794 || māghamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe dvādaśyāṃ tithau śukravāsare thvakahnu saṃpūrṇṇayāphādinajulo || śubha || || ❁ || likhitaṃ śrīdhvakahnathākurajusannam iti || kalyāṇam astu || caturbhis (tvāṃ) hastair ḍamaruparaśuṃ śūlahariṇaṃ dadhānaṃ śubhrāṃśoḥ kiraṇadhavalaṃ pañcavadanaṃ | punā †rātebhaki† pravaṇamanaso harniśam api namsyantaḥ santo yuvatisuta[[yutāḥ santi sukhinaḥ ]] ||
notes: The catalogue gives 'Scribe: ?'. 'thvakahnu saṃpūrṇṇayāphādinajulo' is Newari for '(it) was completed on this day'. The scribal note 'likhitaṃ śrīdhvakahnathākurajusannam' is best divided as 'śrī dhvakahna thākuraju-sanaṃ' ('by Śrī … Ṭhākuraju'). 'dhvakahna' may be a corrupt repetition of 'thvakahnu' ('this day'). In that case no personal name survives and the scribe is identified only by the honorific Ṭhākuraju, which in the Malla period can denote a royal or noble person. If the scribe is royal, that may explain why the name is left out. The name Dhvakahna is therefore very doubtful. NS 794 Māgha falls in early 1674 CE. The verse at the end ('caturbhis … sukhinaḥ') is a benediction added after the colophon and names no persons.

title: Mudrārākṣasa nāṭakam(nepālībhāṣāṭīkā)
subject: Nāṭaka
colophon: iti śrī manmahārājapadabhājaḥ pṛtho sununā śrī viśākhadatta mahā kavinā viracite mudrārākṣasa nāṭake nirvaṃharaṇannāma saptamo arkaḥ || 7 || samāptaśca || (fol. 169v2-3 ) vināmudrāṃ mudrāṃ samalikha dakhinnena ++++=== sasuṃdaryyānadā gana vati vayoṣṭādhika munau || 78 || || || || || || (fol. 169v1-4 )
notes: The scribe's closing verse is corrupt and has a lacuna: 'vināmudrāṃ mudrāṃ samalikhad akhinnena ++++ ...'. It means roughly '[he] tirelessly wrote out the Mudrā[rākṣasa] without mudrā (payment)', a pun on the title. The rest, 'sasuṃdaryyānadā gana vati vayoṣṭādhika munau || 78 ||', seems to say the copy was made at an age of 78 ('vayasi aṣṭādhika-munau' = seventy plus eight, with the numeral 78 confirming it). So 78 is most likely the scribe's age and not a date. Reading it as an abbreviated year (e.g. VS [19]78) is less likely. 'sasuṃdaryyā' might mean 'together with his wife (sundarī)', but this is uncertain. No scribe name can be recovered. Viśākhadatta's father Pṛthu is listed only because the author's standard colophon names him. Since the manuscript has a Nepali commentary, it is probably late (19th–20th c.).
review: Date: '78' is probably not a year. The verse reads 'vayo[='vayasi'?] aṣṭādhika-munau || 78 ||', i.e. at an age of 78, so it most likely gives the scribe's age. Era changed to 'none', year cleared, ce_approx left empty, and the reading is explained in notes.

Śivalāla Pāṭhaka is called 'śrīmajjānakīramaṇapadapaṅkajaparicaraṇaparāyaṇa'. He is named only as the teacher, or model, of the commentator Bhaṭṭa Devarāma ('pādānumāyin'). He has no part in the 1844 copy. Devarāma 'compiled' (saṃgṛhīte) the Viṣamapadavyākhyāna on the Rāmāyaṇa. This colophon closes the Uttarakāṇḍa (sarga 111, fol. 376r), but the catalogue title gives Sundara- and Yuddhakāṇḍa. Either the title is incomplete or the manuscript covers more kāṇḍas. 'Saṃvat 1901' at Vārāṇasī is taken as Vikrama Saṃvat. Bhādrapada śukla 9 of that year falls in about August–September 1844 CE.
