title: Vaiśākhamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
date_note: = Wednesday 16 May 1668, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīpadmapurāṇe pātālakhaṇde vaiśākhamāhātmye yamabrāhamaṇasaṃvāde trayodaśodhyā(2)yaḥ samāptaḥ || 13 || śubhaṃ || || yāte bhujaṃgāṣṭaturaṃgamebde jyeṣṭhe site nāgatithau budhehni | patirggaṇānāṃtara(3)sā dvijo sau vaiśākhamāhātmyamidaṃ lilekha || samvat 788 jyeṣṭhaśukla paṃcamī budhavāra thva kuhnu balānihmayā (4)śrīgaṇapatina thva vaiśākhamāhātmya coya dhunakādina juro || thva velasa rājdhirāja śrī śrī śrīnivāsamallaprabhusana, (5) saptāṅkakaṃsabadhapyāṣaṃadayakaṃ, vokhata voyakaṃ huyakāvala, tavasamadāya, ju va juro || śubham || (fol. 99v1–5)
notes: The verse chronogram bhujaṅga (8), aṣṭa (8), turaṅgama (7), read right to left, gives 788. This matches 'samvat 788' in the Newari prose. nāgatithi = pañcamī (5), also matching the prose. NS 788 + 880 = 1668 CE. That falls within the reign of Śrīnivāsa Malla of Patan (c. 1661–1684), so a Patan setting is likely, but no place of copying is stated. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Gaṇeśa'. The colophon has Gaṇapati: 'patir gaṇānāṃ' in the verse and 'śrīgaṇapatina' in the prose. 'balānihmayā' = 'the one of Balāni'. This is taken as the scribe's residence or origin, but Balāni is unidentified. The final Newari sentence is garbled: 'saptāṅkakaṃsabadhapyāṣaṃadayakaṃ, vokhata voyakaṃ huyakāvala, tavasamadāya'. It seems to record a contemporary event: King Śrīnivāsa Malla staged a Kaṃsavadha dance-drama (pyākhaṃ), perhaps over seven days ('saptāṅka' might mean 'seven acts'). It does not name any further persons.
review: Place of copying set to empty: 'balānihmayā' ('the one of Balāni') describes the scribe's residence or origin, not where the copy was made. It is kept as p1's residence.

Notes expanded: nāgatithi = pañcamī matches the prose; Śrīnivāsa Malla of Patan reigned c. 1661–1684, which fits NS 788 = 1668 CE; the king's festival or Kaṃsavadha performance is described; Balāni is unidentified.

title: Kuvalayānanda
subject: Alaṇkāra
colophon: iti śrīmatpapramāṇajñatatsadbhāraḥ(!)ma mahātmaja vaidyanāthakṛtā laṃkāracaṃdra(!) kākhyā kuvalayānaṃda ṭīkā || 2 || śrīśubhaṃ || || lekhaka pāṭhakayo śubhaṃ bhavatu (fol.122v4-5 )
notes: This colophon belongs to the text, not to the copy. Vaidyanātha Tatsat wrote the Alaṅkāracandrikā ('laṃkāracaṃdra(!) kākhyā' = alaṅkāracandrikākhyā), a commentary on Appayya Dīkṣita's Kuvalayānanda. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Ṭīkākāra : Vaidyanātha' is wrong: he is the commentator, not the copyist. The father's name is corrupt in 'śrīmatpapramāṇajñatatsadbhāraḥ(!)ma mahātmaja'. It probably stands for śrīmat-pramāṇajña-tatsad-bhaṭṭa-rāma-mahātmaja ('great son of the learned Rāma Bhaṭṭa Tatsat'), but this reading is uncertain. The phrase 'lekhaka pāṭhakayo śubhaṃ bhavatu' is a standard blessing that names no scribe or reader. The copy gives no scribe, date or place.

This is a Marathi-style name: given name Lakṣmaṇa, father Śrīdhara (taken as father by convention, not stated outright), surname Nāmdeukara (perhaps Nāmdeukar/Nāndgāvkar). The place 'naṃdagāva' is a Nandgaon, most likely in Maharashtra, but several places have this name, so it is left unnormalized. This is a manuscript copied in Western India, not Nepal. The weekday matches: 10 Dec 1867 was a Tuesday (bhauma).

notes: The place string 'jaikaradāśaśadṛśraṇapuramadhye' is corrupt. It probably reads as the scribe's name (jaikaradāsa) followed by 'śāharaṇapuramadhye', i.e. Saharanpur, as the catalogue says. 'lālārāma kṛṣṇadāsa' can be read as Lālā Rāmakṛṣṇadāsa (lālā being an honorific), taken here, or as two persons, Lālārāma and Kṛṣṇadāsa. The author's name 'suṃjāditya' may be a corruption of Muñjāditya. 'māśotamāse' = māsottame; 'aśvana' = Āśvina. notes: 'pradhyumna śarmapa' is corrupt. It probably stands for 'pradyumnaśarmaṇaḥ' (for Pradyumnaśarman's study) or 'pradyumnaśarmaṇā' (written by Pradyumnaśarman). On either reading he is the person for whose study the copy was made. The colophon does not name the scribe separately. The catalogue lists him as the scribe, so he is taken here as scribe + owner (a copy made for his own study), at medium confidence. The two eras agree: VS 1905 − 57 = 1848 and ŚS 1770 + 78 = 1848, so the copy dates to about August/September 1848 CE. The weekday has not been checked against the tithi. The (!) after Śatānanda is the cataloguer's mark. Śatānanda is the known author of the Bhāsvatī, and Puruṣottamakṣetra is Puri. The title in the catalogue, 'Bhāśvatīkaraṇa', should read Bhāsvatīkaraṇa.

colophon: iti śrī vārāhapurāṇe śrīgītāmāhātmyeṃ sapta purṇa subham || || iti samvat 1938 sāla mīti jeṣṭha sudi 6 roja 6 || liṣīte pasupati guhyeśvari nikaṭe || cavivela gaṇeśā sase || cāvela grāme śrī amvaradhoja hilavāla liṣete || || śubham || || rāma || rāma || rāma || kṛṣṇa || kṛṣṇa || kṛṣṇa || kṛṣṇa || (fol. 4r2-6)
notes: The book was copied in Cāvela village (Chabahil, also spelled Cāvahil), near Paśupati and Guhyeśvarī. 'cavivela gaṇeśā sase' probably means 'beside the Cāvahil Gaṇeśa' (Chabahil Gaṇeśa temple). 'Hilavāla' is probably a family or clan name and is kept as a title. 'Amvaradhoja' is the Nepali form of Ambaradhvaja. The era is unspecified ('samvat … sāla'), but the Nepali phrasing ('sāla mīti', 'roja') points to Vikrama Saṃvat, which gives 1881 CE for VS 1938. The weekday was not checked against the tithi. The catalogue fields agree with this reading.

title: Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa and Adhyātmarāmāyaṇasetu
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Monday 26 Oct 1744, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmadadhyātma rāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde kiṣkiṃdhākāṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ 9 6 || (fol. 39r5-6) iti śrīmatsakala rājavipaduddharaṇa samarthetyādi virudāvalī virājamānasya himmati varmaṇa putrasya śrīsanma(!) varmaṇaḥ kṛtāvadhyātma rāmāyaṇa setau kiṣkiṃdhākāṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ 96 śubhamastu saṃvat śrī rāmāyaṇa ṭīkeyaṃ rāmavarmaṇakṛtāśubhā rāmārpaṇaṃ 6 || saṃvat 1801 mītīkātīka vaṃda 5 vāraśomā (fol. 39r2&8-9 )
notes: The catalogue's 'Scribe: Śrīrāma Varmā' is a mistake. Rāmavarman, son of Himmativarman, is the author of the Setu commentary ('ṭīkeyaṃ rāmavarmaṇakṛtā'), not the copyist. No scribe is named. 'śrīsanma(!)' is read as 'śrīrāma'. The figure '9 6' / '96' after 'navamaḥ sargaḥ' looks like a running sarga count. The date 'saṃvat 1801 (mītī) Kārttika vadi 5, Monday' comes straight after the commentary's closing verse. It may therefore date the commentary (or a copy reproduced with it) rather than this manuscript, so treat it as the copying date only with caution. Taking the era as VS gives 1744 CE (October/November). The weekday has not been verified.
review: Merged p2 'śrīsanma(!) varmaṇaḥ' into p3 Rāmavarman. 'sanma(!)' is almost certainly a misreading of 'rāma' (śrīrāmavarmaṇaḥ). The same colophon names the Setu's author as rāmavarmaṇa, so both refer to one commentator, son of Himmativarman. Confidence is now medium.
Moved the son_of relation to the merged person (Rāmavarman son_of Himmativarman).
Himmativarman: the titles field now holds the virudāvalī as an epithet. Role stays relative_only, and confidence is medium because the name could be a form of Himmat(a)varman.
Purpose rewritten as 'dedicated to Rāma (rāmārpaṇam)'.
Notes expanded: no scribe is named, and the date may belong to the commentary rather than to the copy.

title: Kārttikamāhātmya
subject: Māhātmya
colophon: iti śrīpadmapurāṇe kārtikamāhātmye ekonatriṃśodhyāyaḥ imāḥ kathā kārttikamāghayo/// śubhaphaṇabhṛmithautra śrīviṣṇututyartham idaṃ purāṇaṃ kuvuddhināśāya gṛhavrata nāma likhitaṃ pahaladaṃ puṃsājñānamuktayabhivāṃchatām jñādigrāmābhidhānaṃ śrīgajādharadvijanmanā || || 1 || śubham astu viṣṇoḥ prasādāt || (fol. 23v8-11)
purpose: For Viṣṇu's satisfaction (viṣṇututyartham = tuṣṭyartham) and to destroy bad thinking (kubuddhināśāya).
notes: The colophon is a corrupt verse. It probably reads: śrīviṣṇutuṣṭyartham idaṃ purāṇaṃ kubuddhināśāya ... likhitaṃ phaladaṃ puṃsāṃ jñānamuktyabhivāñchatām / jñādigrāmābhidhāne śrīgadādharadvijanmanā. 'Gajādhara' is most likely Gadādhara. The as-written form is kept. 'śubhaphaṇabhṛmithautra' follows the lacuna (///) and is corrupt. It contains phaṇabhṛt ('serpent', which can stand for 8 in a chronogram) and may hide a date such as a year name or a chronogram. However, no reading can be made with confidence, so no date is recorded. 'gṛhavrata nāma' is unclear. It could be a corrupt epithet, or part of the place or person description. It is not treated as a person. The place-name Jñādigrāma is not identified.
review: Name normalised to Gadādhara (Gajādhara is almost certainly a mistake for the common name Gadādhara; ja/da confusion). Confidence lowered to medium.
Title changed from 'dvijanman' to 'dvija (brahmin)'.
Place normalised to the village of Jñādi (jñādigrāmābhidhāne). Residence set to the same, but this is uncertain.
Purpose rephrased.
Notes expanded: the corrupt passage and the lacuna.

title: Nītisaṃgraha
subject: Nītiśāstra
date_note: = Sunday 1 Apr 1973, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti mahārājādhirājaśrījagajjotir malladevaviracito nītisaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ || || vāṇanavavasubhūmite śake caitrāsitatrayodaśyāṃ budhavāsare kāṣṭhamaṇḍape likhitaṃ dvijaśrīvinodena hariprīty artham (fol. 43r5)
notes: The chronogram vāṇa(5) nava(9) vasu(8) bhūmi(1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1895, which is about 1973 CE. That makes this a modern copy of a text ascribed to the Bhaktapur king Jagajjyotirmalla (r. c. 1613–1637). He appears only as the author ('viracito'), not as the reigning king. The weekday (budhavāsara) has not been checked against the tithi. The catalogue gives Dhanarāja as a scribe and Bhaktapura as the place of copying, but the quoted colophon names only Vinoda, writing at Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa (Kathmandu). Dhanarāja and Bhaktapura may come from another colophon or another part of the manuscript that was not quoted.

title: Muhūrttamārtaṇḍa

colophon: iti śrīmannārāyaṇaviracito muhūrtamārtaṇḍa samāptaḥ || 162 || sukhanipuruṣārthakṣmā 1493 rimitaśaka kāle jātamārtaṇḍe || Iti (!) śrīsvakṛtamuhūrtamārtaṇḍa vallabhāyāṃ vidhānasamāptim agamat || yādṛśaṃ…. …..na diyate. || ❁ || iti śrīśāke 1765 śrīsamvat 1600 kārtikaśukla 7 tithau vāre 1 taddine liṣitaṃ (!) valabhadrapādhyā luñiṃṭyāla leṣaka (!) śubhaṃ bhūyāt || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || lagnamānadinasūkta…..bhavaṃti bhogyadaṃ || 1 || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 25r9–25v6)
notes: The colophon gives two dates: śāke 1765 (= 1843 CE) and śrīsaṃvat 1600. As transcribed, 1600 cannot be VS: VS 1600 would be 1543 CE. The catalogue field gives VS 1900, which equals 1843 CE and matches the Śaka year. So '1600' is probably a misreading or scribal error for 1900 (Devanagari 6 and 9 look alike). The catalogue field 'ŚS 1756' does not match the colophon's 'śāke 1765' and is probably a transposition of the digits; this record follows the colophon. The weekday has not been checked against the tithi. Separately, the chronogram 'sukhanipuruṣārthakṣmā 1493 rimitaśaka' (meaning 'measured', i.e. parimita) gives the date the work was composed, Śaka 1493 (1571 CE), not the date of copying. That matches the known date of Nārāyaṇa's Muhūrtamārtaṇḍa. The colophon also refers to the author's own commentary (Mārtaṇḍavallabhā), so Nārāyaṇa is listed as both author and commentator. The concluding verses ('yādṛśaṃ …', 'lagnamāna…') are stock verses, not prosopographical.

notes: The verse colophon is metrically and grammatically corrupt. The year is given as a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram in the Vikrama era: 'pārāvāra' = 4, but '-ādyana-' is corrupt (perhaps adri = 7 or nanda = 9, with syllables lost), so the year cannot be fixed. 'arke' most likely means Sunday, though it could be arka = 12 as part of the number. 'kalāvihīne' is most likely the scribe's modesty formula ('lacking in skill'), matching 'kaṣṭena likhitam', and is not a tithi. I take 'durgāsomasutaḥ' to describe the scribe Lakṣmīnātha (dvija), but the verse does not say so outright. 'likhitaṃkṣarodvijoyaṃ' is corrupt (perhaps 'likhitam akṣaraṃ dvijo 'yam'). The colophon is that of Bhaṭṭotpala's commentary on the Bṛhajjātaka, adhyāya 25 (dreṣkāṇasvarūpa). The final verse 'aṃśakād jñāyate dravyaṃ ...' is a stray textual verse, not part of the colophon.

colophon: ityārṣe rāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye ʼdbhutottarakāḍe saptaviṃśatimaḥ sarggaḥ || || || || samāptoyaṃ adbhuto rāmāyaṇaṃ daivajña. kṛṣṇaviraliṣitaṃ || || saṃvat 973 jyeṣṭhamāse śuklapakṣe 14 tithau vāsare 2 thvakunhu yaladeśa dulitaṃ nhetanīyājosikṛṣṇavīrana coyājolo || śubham || (fol. 32v11–12)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Daivajña Kṛṣṇa'. The colophon names him in full as Kṛṣṇavīra: 'kṛṣṇaviraliṣitaṃ' = kṛṣṇavīra-likhitaṃ, and the Newari 'josi kṛṣṇavīrana coyā jolo' means 'written by Jośī Kṛṣṇavīra'. The era is not stated, but 'saṃvat 973' together with the Newari phrasing makes it Nepāla Saṃvat (NS 973 ≈ 1853 CE). 'yaladeśa' = Yala, i.e. Patan. 'dulitaṃ nhetanī(yā)' seems to be a locality or quarter in Patan, but the reading is uncertain. The colophon ends the 27th sarga (saptaviṃśatimaḥ) of the Adbhutottarakāṇḍa, while the catalogue title says 'Paṃcaviṃśatisarga' (25 sargas). Vālmīki is the traditional author, listed only as author.

colophon: thvatena bhīmasena pūjā vidhiḥ || || (4) ❖ samvat 871 āṣāḍha śudi 12 sidhayakāva vidyāpīthayā vidyācājya 〈〈 maṇiratnadhara〉〉 (5) yatā biyā thva saṃphula sunānaṃ lobha yātasā pañcamāhāpāta julo || || śubham astu || (exp. 11b3-5)
purpose: gift: given to Vidyācārya Maṇiratnadhara of Vidyāpīṭha (yātā biyā)
notes: Newari: 'sidhayakāva' = siddha yānāva ('having completed'); '... yatā (= yātā) biyā' = '(it was) given to ...'; 'thva saṃphula sunānaṃ lobha yātasā pañcamahāpātaka julo' = 'whoever covets this book incurs the five great sins'. The person giving the book (donor, perhaps also the scribe) is not named. The cataloguer puts the name in 〈〈 〉〉, which may mean it was inserted or rewritten, so the recipient's name could be a later addition. vidyācājya = Newari spelling of vidyācārya; a garbled vajrācārya is also possible. 'vidyāpītha' = Vidyāpīṭha, possibly a vihāra or tantric seat; I could not identify it for certain. The date may be the date of completing the copy or the date of the gift. NS 871 + 880 = 1751 CE.

Title normalized to 'vidyācārya' (as_written vidyācājya kept in evidence); Vidyāpīṭha kept as affiliation only, residence emptied (yā = genitive 'of', more likely an institution than a stated residence)

title: Saptamīvratakathā
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Friday 9 Oct 1383, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti saptamīvratakathā samāptāḥ (!) || kīṭalīḍhākṣarāṃ pustīṃ lipidoṣād durakṣaraḥ | asaṃpūrṇṇā samālokya maṇikākhyena pūritā || vahniśūnyaśare yāte nepālābdi vidhīyate | aśunyāś ca site pakṣe tithau kāma bhṛgudine || vīraśiṃhāvidhānena likhitañ ca suśraddhayā | saptamīvratarājeśaṃ dvijāya saṃprabodhitaṃ || śubham astu || ○ || (fol. 10v1–3)
notes: The year is a bhūtasaṃkhyā: vahni = 3, śūnya = 0, śara = 5, read right to left = NS 503. 'aśunyāś' is corrupt, probably for āśvinyāṃ (the month Āśvina). 'kāma' stands for the 13th tithi, as the catalogue also gives. The verse says the book was insect-eaten (kīṭalīḍhākṣarām), badly written, and incomplete, so the one named Maṇika completed it (pūritā). Maṇika may therefore have supplied the missing portions as a scribe, not only corrected them. 'vīraśiṃhāvidhānena' is probably corrupt for vīrasiṃhābhidhānena ('by the one named Vīrasiṃha'), so he is taken as the scribe, which agrees with the catalogue. Read literally as vidhāna ('by arrangement of'), it would make Vīrasiṃha the commissioner instead. It is unclear whether Maṇika's completion happened at the same time as Vīrasiṃha's copy or later. The last line, 'saptamīvratarājeśaṃ dvijāya saṃprabodhitaṃ', seems to say the vrata story was expounded to a brahmin. That refers to the text's content, not to this copy's purpose, and no beneficiary is named.

subject: Gītā/Purāṇa

colophon: iti śrīkṛṣṇārjunasaṃvāde gītāsāragitā samāpta || rāma rāma || samvata sāla 60 pradovisā || pusā māsa saṃpurṇa bhayā || ❁❁❁❁ || oṃ namo brahmaṇe(!)devāya nama (!) sāmipyasārūpyasālokyasāyāhya || (fol. 6v)
notes: The colophon names no human persons: no scribe, owner, commissioner or king. The date formula is in Nepali ('samvata sāla 60 ... pusā māsa saṃpurṇa bhayā' = 'completed in the month of Pauṣa, year [..]60'). The year '60' is probably an abbreviated year with the century left out. Nepali 'sāla' dating suggests Vikrama Saṃvat (e.g. VS 1960 = c. 1903 CE), but this cannot be confirmed, so the era is left unspecified and ce_approx is left empty. 'pradovisā' is obscure. It may be 'pra[viṣṭa]' (the solar day count used in Nepali dates) followed by a corrupt day numeral, possibly a misreading of 'bāisa' (22); this is uncertain. The final invocation is corrupt ('brahmaṇe(!)devāya ... sāyāhya' for sāyujya) and has no prosopographical content.

colophon: iti uḍḍīsa pārameśvara mahātanumahārṇave caturviṃśatiśārasaṃgrahae śārātsārasaṃgraha uḍḍiśo nāmaḥ(!) paṭala samāptam (abhūt) || ○ || ❁ || śreyostuḥ || samvat (139) kārttika śukla ----- (viśākha) nakṣatraḥ | āyodhānayogeḥ | ravivāre || śrīrājādhirāja parameśvara bhaṭṭārakasya nārāyana(!) śrī śrī jayajyoti mala(!)devānām rājye vijayarāje(!) likhitam idam uḍīsara śāstuṃ śrī ||(mānīsake śrī dakṣiṇe vihāre śrī yotho vihāra kūṭumbaja pradhānāṃga ----- śāstraśrī jayate ------- dvija baruttama śrī manokusośarmanasothe likhitedam śāstraṃ || yadi śuddham aśuddham vā lekhito nāsti dośitaḥ | yathāsāstra tathā likhitaṃ mama doṣo nadīyate || kaṣṭena (lakṣiṇam) ------ (x. 54a5-54b5 )
notes:
The year is read as NS 139 (= 1019 CE), but that is impossible under Jayajyotirmalla, who reigned c. NS 528–548 (1408–1428 CE). The first digit is probably a damaged 5, which gives NS 539 = 1419 CE. This is a conjecture. The tithi is lost in the lacuna. 'āyodhāna' yoga is probably a corruption of āyuṣmān.

On Vijayarāja: 'vijayarāje' could be 'vijayarājye' ('in the victorious reign'). But that would be redundant right after 'rājye', so I followed the catalogue and kept him as the scribe.

The passage in parentheses after '||' looks like a second colophon. It may be secondary, and it is lacunose. It seems to describe a pradhānāṅga of a family (kuṭumbaja) belonging to Yotho vihāra, the southern vihāra in 'Mānīsaka'. That place may be Maṇigalaka (Patan), but this is unconfirmed. The person's name is lost in the lacuna. The phrase may give that person's affiliation rather than the place of copying.

'manokusośarmanasothe' has two possible readings:
- '…śarmaṇaḥ sārthe/syārthe' ('for Manokuso-śarman'): he is the commissioner. This is the reading used in the record.
- '…śarmaṇā svahaste' ('by Manokuso-śarman with his own hand'): he would be a second scribe.

The name may be Manokusuma.
review: p3: removed the brahmin suffix śarman from the name and added it to titles. The name is now 'Manokuso' (perhaps Manokusuma). Confidence lowered to low because the second colophon is corrupt and lacunose.
p3: kept the commissioner role ('-sothe' read as '-sārthe'/'-syārthe'). Notes now give the alternative reading 'śarmaṇaḥ svahaste', which would make him the scribe.
p2: kept as scribe at low confidence. Notes say 'vijayarāje' may be a corruption of 'vijayarājye'; that is redundant after 'rājye', which favours the catalogue's personal name.
Date: year field changed to '139 (as read; perhaps 539)'. ce_approx marked as conjectural. Yoga 'āyodhāna' noted as probably a corruption of āyuṣmān.

Place: left the normalized field empty. Notes say the locative phrase may describe the affiliation of a person lost in the lacuna (a pradhānāṅga of a family of Yotho vihāra) rather than the place of copying. 'Mānīsaka' may be Maṇigalaka (Patan).

title: Kubjikāmata
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Monday 29 Jun 1080, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti kulālikāmnāye śrīkubjikāmate samastājñānāvabodhacaryyo nirddeśo (nāpaś ca) viṃśatiṣaṭ paṭalaḥ || iti caturvviṃśatisāhasre (sārātsāraṃtaraṃ) śrīkubjikāmnāyaṃ śrī(otiyonapīṭhavirnirggataḥ)paścaviṃśatimaḥ paṭalaḥ || ❁ || (sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike tadā āśāmāśe śukladaśaṃyāṃ tithim uttamaṃ viśākhaṛkṣaṃ nāme tu || || likhitaṃ sārasaṃgrahakubjikā) (fol. 200v1-4)
notes: The colophon names no persons: no scribe, patron, owner or king. The date verse is corrupt. 'sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike' most likely stands for 'śatadve vatsare pūrṇe pañcāśad ekādhike', meaning 'when 200 years were complete, plus fifty-one', i.e. year 251. The catalogue gives [NS] 200, which apparently ignores 'pañcāśad ekādhike'. The year should be checked against the manuscript image. The era is not written; NS is assumed from the Newari script and the Nepalese provenance. If the year is 251, NS 251 is about 1131 CE; if 200, about 1080 CE. 'āśāmāśe' = āṣāḍhamāse. Moon in Viśākhā on Āṣāḍha śukla 10 is astronomically plausible. The closing words 'likhitaṃ sārasaṃgrahakubjikā' give a title for the text ('Sārasaṃgraha-Kubjikā'), not a person.
review: Year reinterpreted: 'sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike' is most likely a corrupt 'śatadve vatsare pūrṇe pañcāśad ekādhike' = 200 + 51 = 251, not 200 as the catalogue says. ce_approx changed from 1080 to 1131 accordingly; marked uncertain.

Month normalised to Āṣāḍha; tithi to daśamī; nakṣatra to Viśākhā. Viśākhā on Āṣāḍha śukla 10 is astronomically plausible.

title: Kubjikāmatatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 13 Feb 1092, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti mahāmudrāpīṭhe śrīkubjikāmate paramarahasye guhyātiguhye aṣṭamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || ○ || samvat 212 phālguṇaśuklaaśvanī(!) nakṣatre śukradine śrīmandarathasya rāja (śrīhallapiṅgaviṣaye kāthadhuṭōllakāpicāsinā kulaputravajābhāvokasya pūjārthas puṇyārthinā paramarahasya) pustakam idaṃ khitam(!) iti || ○ ||śivam astu || (fol.39r2-5 )
purpose: pūjārtha, puṇyārtha (for Vajābhāvoka's worship and merit)
notes: 'rāja' probably stands for 'rājye' (under the reign of). No king named 'Mandaratha' is known in Nepal around NS 212 (1092 CE), when Harṣadeva or Śivadeva ruled. He may be a local ruler of the Hallapiṅga viṣaya, or the name may be corrupt (e.g. for 'śrīmad-…'). 'kāthadhuṭōllakāpicāsinā' is probably an error for 'kāthadhuṭollaka-vāsinā' (resident of Kāthadhuṭollaka). The colophon has an instrumental agent ('…vāsinā … puṇyārthinā … [li]khitam') alongside the genitive 'kulaputravajābhāvokasya pūjārtha[ṃ]'. There are two readings: (a) the genitive is a case error for the instrumental, so Vajābhāvoka is the scribe and wrote the copy for his own worship (adopted here); (b) the writer is unnamed and Vajābhāvoka is only the beneficiary. Nothing supports 'commissioner', since the verb is likhitam, not likhāpitam. 'khitam(!)' = likhitam. The name may be a corruption of 'Vajrābhāvoka' or similar. The tithi is not stated.
review: p2 roles: dropped 'commissioner' because the verb is 'likhitam' (written), not 'likhāpitam'. The instrumental agent ('…vāsinā … puṇyārthinā … likhitam') is the writer. Read Vajābhāvoka as that agent (genitive -kasya for instrumental -kena), giving roles scribe + beneficiary ('pūjārthaṃ'). Confidence lowered to low.
p2 residence normalised to 'Hallapiṅga viṣaya, Kāthadhuṭollaka' (kāpicāsinā read as -ka-vāsinā).
p1 confidence lowered to low: no king 'Mandaratha' is known for Nepal c. 1092 (Harṣadeva or Śivadeva). He may be a local ruler of Hallapiṅga, or the name may be corrupt.

notes rewritten.

title: Sāṃkhyakārikā, Sāṃkhyatattvakaumudī
subject: Sāṃkhya
date_note: = Monday 25 Apr 1825, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti śrīvāca(6)spatimiśraviracitā sāṃkhyatattvakaumudī samāptā || || arvābdhyadrīnduśake rādhāsitapakṣagauhasaume ʼhni || svārthaṃ kā(7)śyām alikhad yadolālalaratnākarākhyaḥ || 1 || || śubham astu || || || || || (fol. 27v5-7)
notes: The year is a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram: arvan (horse) 7, abdhi 4, adri 7, indu 1. Read right to left this gives Śaka 1747, which is ŚS+78 = 1825 CE. The colophon is a single Āryā verse. 'Gauha' (gau long) is metrically required and means 'belonging to Guha', i.e. ṣaṣṭhī. The scribe's name: the ms has 'yadolālala'. The metre (27 mātrās) works with either 'yadolālala' or the catalogue's 'yādolāla', so the name is probably Yādolāla/Yadulāla with a doubled 'la'. 'Ratnākara' is probably a family name or epithet, so I kept it in the name. A rough calendar check: if 1747 is the expired year, Vaiśākha śukla 6 falls around 22–24 April 1825, which does not give a Monday. If 1747 is the current year (= 1746 expired), it falls around 3 May 1824, which is a Monday and matches 'saume'. So the date could be 1824 rather than 1825. This was checked only with mean new moons and is unconfirmed.

date.tithi: 'gauha' is not a corruption. It is the vṛddhi derivative of Guha (the day sacred to Guha/Skanda = ṣaṣṭhī, 6). The Āryā metre needs the long 'gau'
date.weekday: 'saume' read as Monday (sauma < soma); Wednesday (saumya) is possible but less likely

The invocation 'śrīturajāpuryai namaḥ' addresses the goddess of Tuljāpur (Tulajā Bhavānī), which points to a Maharashtrian scribe. It does not name the place of copying. Date: Śaka 1787 = Krodhana in the southern 60-year cycle (Prabhava = Śaka 1789), so the year is consistent: 1865–66 CE. 'krodhanāvde' is a corrupt spelling of krodhanābde.
review: p1: confidence lowered from high to medium. 'koṭena' may stand for the Marathi family name Koṭe rather than a personal name Koṭa, and 'Aṇṇā/Aṇṇa' is given as an upanāman (by-name or call-name).
Notes: added the ambiguity of the name, the Tuljāpur invocation (a regional pointer, not a place of copying), and a check of the Jovian year.

notes: The author Aṣṭāvakra is a legendary sage, so he is left out of the persons list. The era is unmarked, but 'saṃvat 1887' with 'miti' and 'roja' is VS in Gorkhālī-period style, i.e. 1830 CE (Āśvina amāvāsyā, around October 1830). Roja 5 = Thursday. 'rāmadilamuṇyāśrame' is probably 'rāmadilapuṇyāśrame' (the catalogue field reads Rāmadilapuṇyāśrama). 'galkoṭadaśruśaile' is obscure (perhaps galkoṭadeśe ... śaile?). Galkot is in western Nepal (Baglung district).

title: Aṣṭavakragītā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Tuesday 22 Jul 1823, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: Kārttikādi, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: ity aṣṭāvakre saṃkhyākramāḥ || ekaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam || || (fol. 55r6) || iti śrī (aṣṭavakraviśveśvaraviracitāyāṣṭāvakrakālasaṃkramaṇāddivyākhyā)1 samāptaṃ || || || śrīśubhaṃ bhavatu || || śrīrastu || || samvat 1880 āṣāḍhaśukla purṇamāravaudine lī o. bhaṭa raṇachoḍajī śāmajī śrīgoḍajñātīya || śrījīrṇadurga nivāsi || || śubhamastu || || || (fol. 55r7-10)
notes: 'lī o.' probably abbreviates likhitam. Raṇachoḍajī Śāmajī follows the Gujarati pattern of personal name + father's name, both with the honorific -jī; Śāma may stand for Śyāma. The scribe was a Bhaṭṭa of the Śrīgauḍa jñāti living in Jīrṇadurga (Junagadh, Gujarat). The catalogue gives 'Jīrṇadurganivāsī' as the place of copying, but the colophon describes it as the scribe's residence; copying there is likely but not stated. The title passage '(aṣṭavakraviśveśvaraviracitāyāṣṭāvakrakālasaṃkramaṇāddivyākhyā)' is corrupt (the cataloguer flags it with note 1). Viśveśvara seems to be named as the author of a commentary or gloss (vyākhyā), but the reading is uncertain. Date check: in western India VS years start in Kārttika, so Āṣāḍha śukla 15 of VS 1880 falls on about 11 July 1824, a Sunday, matching the colophon. The Caitrādi reading (about 23 July 1823) would fall on a Wednesday.
review: p1 Viśveśvara: confidence lowered to medium; the title in parentheses is garbled, so his exact role (commentator or author of a gloss) is uncertain
p2: as_written widened to include the '-jī' honorific. The name stays Raṇachoḍa and the residence stays as given
p3 Śāma: residence removed. The colophon gives residence only for the scribe, so it should not be carried over to the father. The caste affiliation is kept because it is inherited

date: ce_approx changed from 1823 to 1824. In Gujarat (Junagadh) VS years start in Kārttika, so Āṣāḍha śukla 15 of VS 1880 falls in mid-1824. The full moon of about 11 July 1824 was a Sunday, which matches 'ravau dine'. The Caitrādi alternative, about 23 July 1823, was a Wednesday
date: tithi normalised to pūrṇimā and weekday to Sunday (ravau dine)
place: emptied. 'jīrṇadurga nivāsi' gives the scribe's residence, not the place of copying. Copying at Junagadh is likely but not stated (see notes)

title: Uttaragītā [ adhyāya 1-3 ]
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Monday 24 Jan 1707, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti uttaragītāyāṃ tṛtīyodhyāyaḥ || (fol. 25r7–8) iti śrīgauḍapādācāryaviracitāyāṃ uttaragītā ākhyātāyāṃ tṛtīyodhyāyaḥ samāptim agamat || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || samvat 1628 vyayasamvatsare māghavadya paṃcamī somavāra taddivase idaṃ uttargītā ākhyāṃ murarīna likhita sadānanda pustakamadaḥ śrīkṛṣṇa jośī || (fol. 25r5,8–10)
notes: The colophon says only 'samvat', which normally means VS. However, the samvatsara name Vyaya matches ŚS 1628 (1706/07 CE) and does not match VS 1628 (1571/72 CE), so I read the era as Śaka. The weekday has not been checked. 'pustakamadaḥ' = pustakam adaḥ, meaning 'this book is Sadānanda's'. 'śrīkṛṣṇa jośī' follows the ownership phrase with no syntax linking it, so his role is unclear. He could be a second owner, Sadānanda's father or family name (Sadānanda [son of] Kṛṣṇa Jośī), or someone who added a later note. Ascribing the Uttaragītā to Gauḍapāda is traditional. The catalogue gives the scribe's name as Murārī; the manuscript has 'murarīna', which I normalised to Murāri.
review: Era changed from VS to ŚS: the samvatsara name Vyaya fits ŚS 1628 = 1706/07 CE exactly (Vyaya, 20th Jovian year), whereas VS 1628 (1571/72 CE) would fall in Prajāpati/Aṅgiras. ce_approx changed from 1572 to 1707 (Māgha kṛṣṇa ≈ Jan/Feb 1707).
Removed the wrote_for relation Murāri→Sadānanda. The colophon only says Murāri wrote the copy and Sadānanda owns it; it does not say the copy was made for him, and the ownership note could be later.
Lowered Kṛṣṇa Jośī to low confidence and expanded the note on his unclear role.

title: Pañcīkaraṇavārttika
subject: Vedanta
date_raw: vasu vāṇavasu kṣoṇī mita varṣe nabhasyamuṃ
colophon: iti śrīparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrīmacchamkarabhagavatpādapūjyaśiṣya śrīmat sudeśvarācārya racitaṃ paṃcīkaraṇavārtikaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || vasu vāṇavasu kṣoṇī mita varṣe nabhasyamuṃ || tāropākhya maṇirāmaṣyaṣyāṃ(!) mamdevyalī | likhat || || śrīḥ || || śrīḥ || śrīḥ || śrīḥ ||
notes: The chronogram vasu (8), bāṇa (5), vasu (8), kṣoṇī (1), read right to left, gives 1858. No era is named. If it is VS, the year is about 1801 CE, which fits a Devanagari manuscript with the name Maṇirāma; if it is ŚS, it would be about 1936 CE. Nabhasya is Bhādrapada; 'nabhasy amum' means 'in Nabhasya, this [book]'. The dating line is an anuṣṭubh: 'vasubāṇavasukṣoṇī-mitavarṣe nabhasy amum | tāropākhyamaṇirāma-ṣyaṣyāṃ(?)maṃdevy alīlikhat'. The verb is alīlikhat, a causative aorist ('had written'), though it is often used loosely for 'wrote', so Maṇirāma may be the scribe rather than the commissioner. 'ṣyaṣyāṃ(!) maṃdevy' is corrupt (the cataloguer marked it with '!') and may hide a further word, such as a form of śiṣya or a female name ending in -devī, but no reliable name can be recovered from it. Śaṅkara is named only as the author's teacher. 'Sudeśvara' is a corruption of Sureśvara.
review: Removed 'Mamdevyalī' as scribe: the line is an anuṣṭubh half-verse ('tāropākhyamaṇirāma- / ṣyaṣyāṃ maṃdevy alīlikhat'), and '-lī likhat' is the verb alīlikhat, not part of a name
Maṇirāma: role changed from owner to commissioner (alīlikhat, a causative aorist: 'had [this] written'), noting he may be the scribe; 'tāropākhya' moved from titles to affiliation as the surname Tāro
Śaṅkara: role changed from teacher to other (he is the author's teacher, not connected with this copy); name normalised to Śaṅkara
Author name changed from Sudeśvarācārya to Sureśvara, with 'ācārya' as a title only; the corruption is noted
Removed the wrote_for relation, which depended on the false scribe
Notes rewritten with the metrical analysis and the uncertainty about the era

title: Pañcadaśī
subject: Vedanta
date_raw: aṅkenduddakadairmite śaka itepatyaudyutīnāṃdhane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhavale lekhīrajevāsare
colophon: iti śrīviudyāraṇyamunikṛtāyāṃ vedāntapañcadaśyāṃ pañcabhūtavivekonāmā dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sampūrṇam (fol. 13r10-11) iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrībhāratītīrthavidyāraṇyamunivaryaśiṣyeṇa śrīrāmakṛṣṇākhya viduṣā viracitā pañcabhūtavivekatāṭparyadīpikā samāptatāmaglobīt śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ || aṅkenduddakadairmite śaka itepatyaudyutīnāṃdhane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhavale lekhīrajevāsare vedāntāpi tṛtīyakādikamidaṃ satpañcasadaśyā śubhaṃ śrīkāśyāṃ śivaśarmaṇā prakaraṇaṃ saṅkhyāvatā śrīmatā 1 (fol. 13r12-14)
notes: The date is a śārdūlavikrīḍita verse. Pāda a: aṅkendu-[uu]-dair-mite śake ite patyau dyutīnāṃ dhane. 'duddaka-dair' (two short syllables plus one long) is corrupt, so the Śaka year can only be read as ?19 (units 9, tens 1, read right to left). ce_approx is left empty. Pāda b ends lekhi + [short–long] + vāsare. 'rajevāsare' is unmetrical as a weekday name; indujavāsare (Wednesday) fits the metre, but this is conjecture. 'raver vāsare' (Sunday) does not fit. Pāda c (vedāntāpi tṛtīyakādikam idaṃ sat-pañcadaśyāḥ śubhaṃ) suggests the scribe's verse belongs with prakaraṇa 3 onward, even though it follows the end of prakaraṇa 2 (with Rāmakṛṣṇa's Tātparyadīpikā). Other scribal errors: 'viudyāraṇya' = Vidyāraṇya; 'samāptatāmaglobīt' is corrupt (≈ samāptim agamat). The final '1' is probably a verse number. The catalogue's scribe (Śivaśarmā) and place (Kāśī) agree with the colophon.
review: p4: name 'Śivaśarman' → 'Śiva' with 'śarman' in titles, per the stem rule; residence 'Kāśī' removed, because Kāśī is only stated as the place of copying; epithet saṅkhyāvat ('learned') added to titles; evidence changed to the dated verse.

p2: as_written cut down to Bhāratītīrtha alone. The compound bhāratītīrtha-vidyāraṇya-munivarya-śiṣyeṇa is a dvandva naming two teachers of the commentator. 'munivarya' and the ascetic titles belong to both. The role 'teacher' becomes 'other', since this is the commentator's teacher, not anyone involved in this copy.
p1: Vidyāraṇya kept as author. Noted that he is also named as the commentator Rāmakṛṣṇa's teacher, which is why the pupil_of relation p3→p1 is kept.
p3: the title 'vidvas' kept as an epithet (viduṣā).

Weekday 'Sunday' rejected: the metre needs two syllables, short–long, before vāsare. The likely reading is (lekh)īndujavāsare, Mercury's day = Wednesday, but this is uncertain.

notes: The colophon reads 'saṃvat 1989', but the catalogue field has VS 1689. One of the two is a typo that can only be settled from the image. If 1989 is right, the date is c. 1932 CE; if 1689, c. 1632 CE. The era is not named. VS is assumed because the scribe lived in Rudraprayāga (Garhwal), where Vikrama saṃvat is normal. The tithi after 'vadi' is not given. 'kaṇvālaya rudraprayāga nivāsi' gives the scribe's residence, not explicitly the place of copying. 'Kaṇvālaya' may be a locality (cf. Kaṇvāśrama in Garhwal) or a house or āśrama name. 'nepāladdeśe…' is cut off by the cataloguer and its function is unclear: it may name a destination or owner, or begin a later note. It is not treated as the place of copying. The catalogue's 'Scribe' field wrongly includes 'āśvina vadi'.
review: Place: removed 'nepāladdeśe' / Nepal as place of copying. The fragment is cut off ('nepāladdeśe…'), probably opens a new clause and does not say the copy was made there. No place of copying is stated explicitly; the catalogue's Rudraprayāga is only the scribe's residence.
Date: kept VS 1989 = c. 1932 CE. The era is inferred from a bare 'saṃvat' (VS is the usual era in Garhwal). Added a note on the catalogue's VS 1689.
Notes: rewritten to reflect the above; residence given as Kaṇvālaya, Rudraprayāga.
Person p1 is unchanged (Naranātha, scribe, paṇḍita).

The abbreviation string 'haºº āºº svāºº maºº duºº bāºº kṣeºº kāºº miºº' before the date probably stands for a formula or a list (possibly mantra syllables). I did not read it as personal names. title: Bhagavadgītā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Saturday 4 Apr 1693, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrībhagavadgītāsūpaniṣatsu vrahmavidyāyāṃ yogaśāstre śrīkṛṣṇārjjunasaṃvāde śatasāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ śrīmahābhārate bhīṣmaparvvaṇi paramārthanirṇṇaya mokṣayogonāmāṣṭādaśodhyāyaḥ || || śubha || svasti || samvat 813 phālguṇakṛṣṇacaturddaśi utrabhadra (!) nakṣatre ēndrayoga śaniścala (!) vāsare thvakunhu || kāśyapagotra ipalāccha ṭolayā vāsudeva bhārona śrī 3 indrāyaṇīprītina śrī 3 paśupati skeduṃtājuro || śubham astu || (fol. 68v2–5)
purpose: offered to Śrī 3 Paśupati for the pleasure of Śrī 3 Indrāyaṇī (indrāyaṇīprītina)
notes: 'skeduṃtājuro' is probably a corruption, or a word-division error, for '(paśupati)sa deduṃtā juro', 'was offered/dedicated to Paśupati'. That makes Vāsudeva the donor. The colophon does not say he commissioned or wrote the copy. The catalogue calls him the scribe, but the colophon gives no scribe statement. He may have copied it himself, but this cannot be confirmed. 'bhārona' = Bhāro (caste/title) + Newari ergative -na. Ipalāccha ṭola (catalogue: Ipalāttha) is stated as his residence, not explicitly as the place of copying, and its identification is uncertain. NS 813 + 880 gives early 1693 CE: Phālguna kṛṣṇa 14 falls around February–March 1693. The weekday and nakṣatra were not checked by calculation.
review: p1 roles: removed 'commissioner' — no causative verb (likhāpitam/coyakā) in the colophon. 'skeduṃtājuro' is best read as Paśupati-s(a) deduṃtā juro, 'was offered to Paśupati', which supports only 'donor'.
Notes: replaced the 'caused to write' reading of skeduṃtājuro with the dedication reading. Also noted that the catalogue's 'scribe' attribution is not stated in the colophon.
Place of copying: emptied. Ipalāccha ṭola is given only as Vāsudeva's residence (ṭolayā), not as the place of copying.
Purpose: rephrased as a dedication to Paśupati for the pleasure of Indrāyaṇī.
Date: normalized weekday (Saturday), nakṣatra (Uttarabhādrapadā) and yoga (Aindra). Normalized tithi spelling. Refined ce_approx (Feb–Mar 1693).

title: Laṅkāvatārasūtra
subject: Bauddhasūtra
date_note: = Sunday 1 Feb 1789, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year read as current
colophon: āryyasaddharmalaṃṅkāvatāla nāma mahāyānasūtra sagāthakaṃ samāptam iti || ❁ || ❁ || ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā hetu teṣān tathāgataḥ | h avada teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evamvādi mahāśravaṇaṃ || ❁ || samvat 950 mti māghamāsya śuklapakṣe ṣaṣṭammītithau aśuṇinakṣatre, śubhayogya yathākarṇṇamahātre, ādityavāsare, makrarāsigate śavitre meṣarāsigate candraṃmasi || || dānapati hataṣāde onani, śrībhāju dhaṃsiju tasya bhāryyā vilalakṣmi putra jio dhaṃju tasya bhāryyā jñānalakṣmi putra munirāja, thuti sayāṃ maṅgalajuya māra śubhaṃ || || (fol. 222v)
purpose: Pious gift (dānapati) by Dhaṃsi and family; ends with Newari 'thuti sayāṃ maṅgala juya māra' = may all these (the named family) be blessed
notes: The catalogue gives the year as NS 910, but the quoted colophon reads 'samvat 950'. The colophon reading has been followed, though the catalogue figure may be the correct one. NS 950 + 880 = 1830. However, Māgha falls in January–February, so the actual date is probably early 1831 CE. Sun in Makara with Moon in Meṣa/Aśvinī on śukla 6 fits Māgha. 'hataṣāde onani' is unclear: perhaps a locality (tole) followed by a Newari locative or verb form. It is recorded as the donor's residence, not as the place of copying. 'bhāju' and '-ju' are Newari honorifics, so the stems are Dhaṃsi (also possible: Dhaṃsiju) and Jio Dhaṃ. The split of 'jio dhaṃju' is uncertain; it might be a single name, Jiodhaṃ. 'vilalakṣmi' might be a corruption of Vilāsalakṣmī. No scribe is named.

date_note: = Friday 17 Jun 1892, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti subhāṣitamahāratnāvadāna [[vasundharāvratakathā samāptā]] 〈〈samāptā 〉〉 śubham astu sarvajagatāṃ sarvadā || . || yo māyābhidhamātṛsundarakarṭibhi(tyā...) yatredaṃ sūtrarājendraṃ prāvartayet kalāvapi bhāṣed yaḥ śṛṇuyād yaś ca śrāvayet yaśca cārayet || eteṣāṃ tatra sarveṣāṃ saṃbuddhāḥ sakalāḥ sadā || kṛpā dṛṣṭyā samālokya kurvantu bhadram mā bhavaṃ || sarvāḥ pāramitā devyas teṣāṃ tatra sadāśivaṃ kurvantyo bodhisaṃbhāraṃ pūrayaṃtu jagaddhite || || anena saddharmarasāmṛtena sarvajñabhāsvadvadanodbhavena || kleśānalaprahvaritāturāsu prajāsu duḥkhapraśamostu nityam || || (śubha samvat 1012 miti jyaṣṭhakṛṣṇasaptami śukravāra ṣunusvālavāhalayā vajrācāryya tejaratna naṃtrelayā paṃditapiniguratnāvadānapustaka thamanaṃ guṇaprakāśayāya pā(!) nimirttinaṃ dakṣaṇā viyāo thao tadayantā thva teyā dharmmanaṃ anūttarapadalokajuyāya thva pustaka sunānaṃ lobhayāta sādvalaṅkipaṃ ca mahāpāpalāyajula thva pustakaguptayāya madu. calaṃyāya māla. jikāya. cṅayā yhupaparyyantadarasaṇtānaṃ caleyāya māla ) (fol.368r8-368v7 )
purpose: for spreading virtues (guṇaprakāśa) and, through this merit, attaining the unsurpassed state (anuttarapada)
notes: The colophon says only 'samvat', with no era named. The catalogue suggests VS with a query, but VS 1012 (about 955 CE) does not fit a Newari-language colophon of this kind. Nepal Samvat 1012 (1892 CE) is much more likely, though the weekday has not been checked. The catalogue calls Tejaratna the scribe. The Newari reads more like this: Tejaratna paid dakṣiṇā to (or through) paṇḍitas, who are not named, to have the Ratnāvadāna book made. The paṇḍitas may therefore be the actual copyists. Two readings are unclear: 'naṃtrelayā' and the prefix 'ṣunu-' in the vihāra name. The closing clause says the book must not be hidden, must be kept in circulation and copied for future generations, and curses anyone who covets it.
review: Removed role 'donor' from Tejaratna: he paid dakṣiṇā to the paṇḍitas for producing the copy, which makes him the commissioner. The colophon does not say he donated the book.
Residence given as written ('ṣunusvālavāhala'), with the reading flagged as uncertain.
Place of copying cleared: the vihāra is Tejaratna's residence, not a stated place of copying.
Purpose rephrased: spreading of virtues (guṇaprakāśa) and merit toward the unsurpassed state (anuttarapada).
Added notes on the unnamed paṇḍitas, who may have done the actual copying, and on the clause saying the book must not be hidden but kept in circulation.
Lowered confidence from high to medium because it is unclear whether Tejaratna was scribe or commissioner.

The colophon breaks off at fol. 96v5 with 'śtīmallabhūupaticaranakamaradhuridhusa…', read as śrī-[…]-malla-bhūpati-caraṇa-kamala-dhūli-dhūsarita(-śiras) 'whose head is grey with the dust of the lotus feet of King […] Malla'. In Newar colophons this formula usually comes right before the name of the scribe or donor, which is lost here. The king's personal name is missing or omitted ('śtī' = śrī), so he cannot be identified beyond 'Malla', which matches the catalogue's '… Malla'. There is no date, so the Malla period (roughly 13th–18th c.) is the only clue to dating. The title 'pūrvvaśrīvasundhārā' is corrupt for Vasundharā, and 'asoghoṣo nandimukho' is probably Nandimukhasughoṣa-avadāna.

notes: The only personal name is in the cataloguer's parenthetical '(bhupakamalla virita tapavana vimocano)'. This passage looks garbled or tentative. 'virita' probably stands for 'viracita' ('composed by'), so the person is an author or compiler, not the scribe. 'bhupakamalla' may be a corrupt form of a Malla king's name (for example Bhūpatīndramalla of Bhaktapur, 1696–1722), or 'bhūpa' may be a royal epithet. 'śrīmaṃmunīndra' (= śrīman munīndra) most likely refers to the Buddha, though it could also be read with the following name. 'tapavana vimocano' may be 'tapovanavimocana', part of the title. The colophon gives no scribe, date or place.
review: Confidence for Bhūpakamalla lowered from medium to low: the whole passage is in the cataloguer's parentheses and is garbled. The name and the authorship are uncertain.

Notes expanded with other possible readings: the name may be a Malla king (for example a corruption of Bhūpatīndramalla); 'tapavana vimocano' may be 'tapovanavimocana'; and 'munīndra' might belong with the following name rather than being an epithet of the Buddha.

colophon: iti ācāryakriyāsamuccayaḥ samāptaḥ || |||| kritir iyaṃ vyākhyāṇā (!) mahāmaṇḍalācāryyapaṇḍitāvavṛtaśrīmaṅkagadarppaṇasyeti || || ye dharmmāhetubrabhāvāhetu teṣān tathāgata (!) hyavadat teṣāñca yo nirodha evaṃ vādi mahāśramaṇaḥ || || granthapramāṇam asyānuṣṭupchandasā ṣaṭsahasrāṇi || 6000 || || bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭigrīva adhodṛṣṭir adhomukha kastena (!) likhitaṃ granthaṃ yatnena pratipālayet || || jalaṃ rakṣet tailaṃ rakṣed rakṣet sītalabandhanaṃ (!) || mūrkhahaste na dātavyaṃ naivaṃ vadati puṣṭakaṃ (!) || maṃgalaṃ lekhakānāṃ ca pāṭhakānāṃ ca maṃgalaṃ maṅgalaṃ sarvalokānāṃ bhumau bhūpatimaṃgalaṃ || saṃbhrāntacittena mayā kvacit kvacit yad bhūtam aśuddhaṃ tat paṇḍitaiḥ śodhanīyaḥ || svavaṃśe putrapautrādipaṭhanārthe likhitaṃ mayāḥ (!) || || śubha || samvat 988 āṣāḍhaśuklayā paṃcamī bṛhaspativāra ṣūnūsakaumūlabdeyā śrīvajrācāryyamukuṭānamdana thva kriyāsamuccaya sabhūlacoya siddhaya kāgudinajulaśubhaṃ || || (fol. 361r-361v)
purpose: svavaṃśe putrapautrādipaṭhanārthe (for reading by his own lineage: sons, grandsons, etc.)
notes: The author's name is corrupt. 'paṇḍitāvavṛtaśrīmaṅkagadarppaṇa' is taken as paṇḍita-avadhūta śrī Jagaddarpaṇa, the known author of the (Ācārya)Kriyāsamuccaya. In 'śrīvajrācāryyamukuṭānamdana', the final -na is the Newari ergative ending, so the name is Mukuṭānanda. 'sabhūla coya' probably means 'wrote it in full', and 'siddhaya kāgu dina' means 'the day of completion'. The phrase 'ṣūnūsakaumūlabdeyā' before the scribe's name is unclear. It may be a locality or residence (a genitive -yā), or a garbled date element; it has not been interpreted. The catalogue gives the scribe as Vajrācārya Dhanasāgara, which conflicts with the colophon (Mukuṭānanda). Dhanasāgara may come from another part of the manuscript, or the catalogue may be wrong. The date was not checked against an ephemeris: NS 988 = 1868 CE, Āṣāḍha śukla 5, Thursday.

title: Pratimāpratiṣṭhādaśakriyāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Wednesday 14 Oct 1772, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti pratiṣṭhādaśakriyāvidhi samāptaḥ || || śubhaḥ || (30v1) likhiteyaṃ sayava tolake (tarumura)mahāvihārāvasthita raraṃkṛtavihārasya dakṣanadi(2)sagṛhāntavya vajrācāryya śrīhemā〇krana likhyate || yathā dṛṣtaṃ tathā likhitaṃ lekha(3)ko nāsti doṣaṇaṃ | yadi śurddhaṃm aśu〇rddhaṃ〇 〇 vā sodhanīya mahabuddhaiḥ || samvat 892 (4) āśviṇakṛṣṇa tṛtīyā buddhavāra 〇 thvakuhnu sidhu juroḥ || śubhamaṅgalaṃ bhavantuḥ || (fol. 30r6-30v4 / exp. 63b-64t)
notes: The scribe's name is written 'śrīhemā〇krana'. '〇' is probably a string-hole space and not a lost character, and the final '-na' is likely the Newari ergative ending, so the name reads Hemākara (Hemākara-na likhyate). The place is unclear. 'sayava tolake' is a locality (tola) in Newari locative. '(tarumura)' is the cataloguer's uncertain reading of the mahāvihāra's name. 'raraṃkṛtavihāra' may be corrupt. 'dakṣanadisagṛha' means a house on the south side (dakṣiṇadiśā). The city is not identified. The year is in NS with no conflicting era. Thvakuhnu sidhu juro (Newari) means 'completed on this day'.
review: Notes expanded: final '-na' in 'hemā〇krana' read as Newari ergative suffix (Hemākara-na), supporting the reading Hemākara; '〇' is a string-hole/space mark, not a lost akṣara
Affiliation clarified: the scribe's house is on the south side of the Raraṃkṛtavihāra, which belongs to the (Tarumura) Mahāvihāra
Date checked: NS 892 + 880 gives 1772 CE for Āśvina; buddhavāra is Wednesday

title: Vasudhārādisaptadhāraṇī
subject: Bauddhadhāraṇī
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Feb 1790, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: ’’ āryagrahamātṛkānām adhāranīparisamāptā || ye dharmmāhetu prabhāvāhetu 〈〈vā〉〉 heṣāṃ tathāgatahevadatteṣā ca yā nirodha evaṃ vādimahāśravaṇaṃ || ❁ || samvat 910 phārguṇaśuklatṛtiyā buddhavāra kunhu ṅatabhucchayātor ādharadhana ‥‥ siṃyātacosyaṃ viyājuhā … (fol.31v1–5)
notes: The Newari clause after the date is damaged: 'ṅatabhucchayā tor ādharadhana ‥‥ siṃyā tacosyaṃ viyā juhā'. It probably names someone living in the Ṅatabhuccha tol, 'ādharadhana' and a name ending in -siṃ(ha), followed by 'viyā juhā' ('gave'). 'tacosyaṃ' may be a corruption of '(ta)coyā syaṃ' ('having written'), but this is uncertain. Because of the lacuna it is unclear whether these are two persons or one name (e.g. Ādharadhana[…]siṃha), and whether the person was the scribe, the donor or the recipient, so both are recorded with role 'other' and low confidence. Ṅata is probably Nyata (Nardevi area) in Kathmandu, but this is not certain. Date: Phālguna in NS 910 falls in Feb/Mar 1790 CE; the weekday was not checked. Catalogue date NS 910 agrees.

title: Ugratārānāmadhāraṇī
subject: Bauddhadhāraṇī
date_note: ≈ 1760 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: || āryya eka jaṭānāmadhālanī(!) || mahogratārānāmadhāraṇī parīsamāpta(!) ||❁ || liṣitai (!) śrī 3 āryyāvareokiteśvarasyaṃ(!) caranaśevaka(!) , vajrācāryyaśrīdhatnarājaṃ riṣāyitaṃ|| saṃ 880 || (fol.29r1–3)
notes: The name is written 'dhatnarāja'. That is not a recognisable name, so the most likely reading is Ratnarāja; Dhanarāja is also possible. The catalogue's 'Donor: Śrī 3 āryyāvareokiteśvara' is a misreading. Āryāvalokiteśvara is the deity, and the scribe calls himself his 'caraṇasevaka' (servant at the feet). This may point to a link with a Lokeśvara shrine, but none is named. The verbs 'liṣitai' (likhitam) and 'riṣāyitaṃ' (likhāyitam/likhāpitam) are both tied to the same person. Newar copyists often use the causative loosely to mean 'written', so he may only have been the scribe and not also the commissioner. NS 880 converts to about 1759/60 CE. No month or day is given. The catalogue gives no reigning king, and none is named in the colophon.
review: p1 name: normalized the corrupt 'Dhatnarāja' to the probable 'Ratnarāja'. The written form is kept in as_written, and the doubt is recorded in notes and confidence.
p1 roles: kept scribe + commissioner. The roles rest on liṣitai plus riṣāyitaṃ (= likhāyitaṃ), and notes explain why the causative may be used loosely here.
Notes: added that the catalogue's 'Donor' is a misreading, and that the NS 880 conversion gives 1759/60 CE.

title: Pañcarakṣā
subject: Bauddha Tantra
date_raw: samvat 825 kārttikamāse śukramakṣa, trayodasyāṃ, tithau,, revatīnakṣatre, harṣana pravajayoge … śuklavāsare, tulyarāsigate savītri, mīnarāsigate candramasi
date_note: = Friday 30 Oct 1705, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year + 1
colophon: iti tatra buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvanādevatānāṃ devatānubhāvena mahatī hyupaśānteti || mahārakṣā mahāmantrānusāriṇī mahāyānasūtraṃ rakṣākalpaṃ samāptaḥ(!) || ❁ || āryamahāpratisarā || āryamahāsāhasrapramarddanī || āryyamahāmāyūrī || āryyamahāśītavatī || āryamahāmantrānusāriṇī || etānipañcamahārakṣāsūtrāṇi parisamāptam iti || ❁ || ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā hetun teṣān tathāgato hyavadat teṣāñ ca yo nirodhaḥ evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ❁ || ... svastiśrīmatpaśupaticaranā(!)kamaladhūri(!)dhūsaritasiroruha, śrīmanmānyeśvaliṣṭa(!)devatābalara(!)bdhaprasādadedīpyamānamānonnataravikura(!)tiraka†haruma†rdhvajanepāleśvalamahārājādhirājarājarājendrasakara(!)rājacakrādhiśvala(!), śrīśrījayabhāṣkala(!)malla palamabhaṭṭārakadevānāṃ sadā samaravijayinām prabhṛthākulasya vijayarājye || ❁ || dānapati kāntipulamāhānagare, makhatvalabhe śrīśrīśrīratnakitīmahāvihāra... jayarājasya putrī, dhalamaṇilakṣmī [[tasyaputra vajrācāryaśrī jayapatidevena]], jājamānasya āyurārogyajaṇadhanasantāṇabṛdhī rastuḥ ||(!)... śreyo stu || samvat 825 kārttikamāse śukramakṣa, trayodasyāṃ, tithau,, revatīnakṣatre, harṣana pravajayoge jathākarṇṇamahātre(!) śuklavāsare, tulyarāsigate savītri, mīnarāsigate candramasi || etaddine likhita(!) sampūrṇnaṃm iti || ❁ || likhiteyaṃ śrīśuvarṇnapanātrimahānagare śrīhemavarṇṇamāhāvihālāvasthīta, ‥ ‥ ‥ rahamanidevena likhāpitaṃḥ(!) || ❁ || ... (fol. 154v1–157r)
purpose: For the long life, health, wealth and offspring of the yajamāna (the donor family)
notes: p5: 'likhāpitaṃ' would literally make this person the commissioner. But the sentence opens with 'likhiteyaṃ … avasthita', and the donor (dānapati) is named separately, so p5 is read here as the copyist, a resident of Hemavarṇa Mahāvihāra (Ha Bahā), Patan. The beginning of p5's name is lost: '…rahamaṇi' may be the end of a longer name such as Brahmamaṇi(?). p4 (Jayapati): the cataloguer marks his clause with [[ ]], probably a later or marginal insertion. The donor family lived in Kathmandu (Makhan Tol, Ratnakīrti Mahāvihāra), but the copy was written in Patan, so the catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Makhana Tola' seems to confuse the donor's residence with the place of copying. 'dhala-' is read as Newar l/r for 'dhara-' (perhaps Dharmamaṇilakṣmī?). Date check: NS 825 Kārttika = November 1704, which falls within Bhāskara Malla's reign (c. 1700–1714). This is consistent with the Sun in Tulā and the Moon in Mīna (Revatī).
review: p5: role changed from commissioner to scribe. The colophon says 'likhiteyaṃ … likhāpitaṃ', and the donor is named separately, so 'likhāpitaṃ' is most likely used loosely for the copyist here. Name given as '…rahamaṇi' without the -deva suffix, to match how Jayapati is treated.
p4 (Jayapati): 'beneficiary' removed. The blessing is for the yajamāna in general, and no one is named as beneficiary. Noted that he appears in the cataloguer's [[ ]] insertion.
p2 (Jayarāja): residence and affiliation emptied and confidence lowered to medium. The '...' lacuna separates the vihāra from his name, so they cannot safely be given to him.
p3: confidence lowered to medium because of the 'dhala' = dhara(?) reading. Residence and affiliation kept.
Place of copying changed to Suvarṇapraṇālī (Patan) only. Kāntipura/Makhatvala is the donor's residence, not where the copy was made, so the catalogue field 'Makhana Tola' is probably mistaken.
Date: weekday normalized to Friday (śuklavāsare = śukravāsare). Yoga given as harṣaṇa followed by vajra. ce_approx 1704 (November) confirmed.
Purpose restated briefly in English.

title: Bagalāsāṅkhyāyanatantra
subject: Śāktatantra
date_note: = Wednesday 2 Sep 1840, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīṣaḍvidyāgame śāṃkhyāyaṇataṃtre homavidhiviśeṣakathanam māma catustriṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāpta || || saṃvat 1897 sāla miti bhādraśudi 6 roja 4 śubham || || graṃthasaṃkhyā eka hajjāra asī siloka || || 1080 || (fol. 36r1–4)
notes: The colophon gives no era name, and the catalogue's '[ŚS]' is the cataloguer's addition. A weekday check supports VS. In VS 1897 (1840 CE), Bhādrapada śukla 6 fell on Wednesday, 2 Sept 1840: the new moon was on 28 Aug 1840 with the sun in Siṃha, and tithi 6 was current at sunrise on 2 Sept. That matches roja 4 = Wednesday. Under ŚS 1897 (1975 CE), the same tithi falls around Thursday, 11 Sept 1975, which does not match. So: VS 1897 = 2 Sept 1840 CE. The colophon names no scribe, owner or other person. 'graṃthasaṃkhyā … 1080' is the text's length in ślokas, not a date.
review: Normalized paksa 'śudi' → 'śukla' and weekday 'roja 4' → 'budhavāra (Wednesday; roja 4)'.
Set era to VS (was 'unspecified'): verified by computation, see notes.
Narrowed ce_approx to 1840 (2 Sept 1840).

title: Kālītattva
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 16 Nov 1685, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīrāghavabhaṭṭaviracite kālītattve rahasyādipratipādanavidhau ekaviṃśatimamaṃ tattvam || || śubha (!) || ṣaṣṭhadyogajasammite suraguror ghasre[ʼ]site pakṣake kālītatvam alekhayad vijavaraḥ śrīcakrarājaḥ sudhīḥ || māse kārttikike manohararasādevena saṃyatnataḥ pañcamyāṃ śubhayogamiśritabharaṇyāṃ tārakāyāṃ mudā || || || || || (fol. 77r7–9)
notes: The date is a verse chronogram in Śārdūlavikrīḍita: ṣaṣṭha (6), dyo/sky (0), gaja (8), read right to left = 806. No era is written. NS is inferred: it is a Nepalese manuscript, the catalogue gives 'SAM 806', and Rāghavabhaṭṭa is c. late 15th century, which rules out VS 806. NS 806 began in Kārttika 1685 CE, so Kārttika kṛṣṇa 5 of NS 806 falls in Oct/Nov 1685, not 1686. 'ghasre[ʼ]site' = ghasre + asite, i.e. the dark fortnight; 'suraguror ghasre' = Thursday. The date has not been verified. Bharaṇī is hard to reconcile with Kārttika kṛṣṇa pañcamī in either the amānta or pūrṇimānta reckoning; the nakṣatra or the pakṣa may be wrong. 'śubhayoga' may be the named yoga Śubha or a generic phrase. Names: 'vijavaraḥ' is a corruption of 'dvijavaraḥ'. Cakrarāja is the commissioner ('alekhayat'). The scribe is Manohara: 'manohararasādevena' = Manohara + rasādeva, and rasā-deva ('earth-god') is a synonym of bhūdeva, i.e. a brahmin. This agrees with the catalogue's 'Scribe: Manohara' and fits the metre.
review: Scribe: the first reading's 'Deva' is wrong. 'manohararasādevena' = manohara + rasādevena, and rasā-deva ('god of the earth') is a synonym of bhūdeva, i.e. a brahmin. So the scribe is Manohara, with 'rasādeva' (brahmin) as a title. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Manohara' is right. Confidence raised to high.
Author: 'bhaṭṭa' stripped from the name (name 'Rāghava', with bhaṭṭa kept in titles), following the rule on brahmin suffixes.
Cakrarāja: 'vijavaraḥ' marked as a corruption of 'dvijavaraḥ' (not marked by the cataloguer). 'sudhī' added as an epithet.

Date: chronogram confirmed (ṣaṣṭha 6, dyo 0, gaja 8, read right to left = 806). The era is not written and NS is inferred. ce_approx changed from 1686 to 1685, because NS 806 began in Kārttika 1685, so Kārttika kṛṣṇa of NS 806 falls in Oct/Nov 1685.
Yoga: 'śubhayoga' may be the named yoga Śubha or just 'an auspicious yoga'. This is now flagged as uncertain.
Notes rewritten: the rasādeva reading is explained, and the nakṣatra is flagged as a possible inconsistency.

title: Kālītantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 16 Nov 1685, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīrāghavabhaṭṭaviracite kālītattvarahasyādipratipādanavidhau ekaviṃśatimaṃ (!) tattvam || || ❁ || || śubhaṃ || ṣaṣṭhadyogajasammite suraguror ghasre[ʼ]site pakṣake kālītatvam alekhayad vijavaraḥ śrīcakrarājaḥ sudhīḥ || māse kārttikike manohararasādevena saṃyatnataḥ pañcamyāṃ śubhayogamiśritabharaṇyāṃ tārakāyāṃ mudā || || (fol. 94v5–7)
notes:
Chronogram 'ṣaṣ(ṭha)-dyo-gaja': ṣaṭ = 6, dyo (sky) = 0, gaja = 8. Read right to left this gives 806. The era is not named; it is taken as NS from the catalogue's 'SAM 806' and the Newari script. Kārttika of NS 806 falls in October–November 1685, or 1686 if the month is counted after the year's change.

Metre is Śārdūlavikrīḍita, and 'māse kārttikike manohararasādevena saṃyatnataḥ' scans correctly. So the extra syllable 'ra' is metrically needed. It may be a doubled 'ra' in the name: perhaps Manoharasa-/Manohara-deva, which would give 'Manoharadeva'. Alternatively it could be 'manohara-rasāt' plus a name 'Deva'. I follow the catalogue: Manohara.

'ghasre[ʼ]site': the dark fortnight (asita) depends on the cataloguer's avagraha. Read without it, as 'site', it would mean the bright fortnight (śukla). Neither a kṛṣṇa nor a śukla pañcamī in Kārttika fits the Bharaṇī nakṣatra well, so the date details may be faulty. Verify before converting.

Cakrarāja is called a dvija ('vijavaraḥ', missing its 'd'), so he is a brahmin. The text is given in the colophon as the 21st tattva of Rāghavabhaṭṭa's Kālītattvarahasya; the catalogue title is Kālītantra.
review: p1: name changed from 'Rāghavabhaṭṭa' to 'Rāghava'; 'bhaṭṭa' is kept only in titles.

p3: scribe's name changed from 'Deva' to 'Manohara', as in the catalogue. Splitting the word as 'manohara-rasād devena' (Deva, 'out of delight') is less likely than a personal name, and a scribe called just 'Deva' is implausible. Confidence stays medium.
p2: 'vijavaraḥ' recorded as an error for dvijavaraḥ. 'sudhīḥ' added as an epithet.

Date: 'ghasre[ʼ]site' parsed as ghasre + asite (dark fortnight, kṛṣṇa), which depends on the cataloguer's avagraha. The chronogram is confirmed as 6-0-8, read right to left = NS 806. ce_approx widened to 1685/86 because Kārttika falls at the turn of the NS year.
Notes: added the metrical check and a doubt about the nakṣatra, and removed the 'Deva' interpretation.

purpose: commissioned by Cakrarāja for himself (book is his)
notes: The date is given twice. (1) In prose: NS 806, Mārgaśira śukla 14, Sunday (ādityavāra), the day the copy was finished. This is about Nov/Dec 1685 CE. (2) In a verse with a Śaka chronogram, 'ṣaḍabhravāruṇair yute śake'. Read right to left: ṣaḍ = 6, abhra = 0, then vāruṇa (value unclear). The catalogue's reading ŚS 1606? would need vāruṇa = 16, which is not a standard bhūtasaṃkhyā value. ŚS 1606 Mārgaśira = Nov/Dec 1684 CE, one year earlier than NS 806; the matching Śaka year would be 1607. So the two eras conflict by one year, or the chronogram is misread. NS 806 is taken as primary. The catalogue lists Cakrarāja as scribe, but the colophon only has him commissioning the copy (lekhayāñcakāra, causative) and owning it ('śrīcakrarājyasya', a spelling of śrīcakrarājasya). The scribe is not named; he may have copied it himself, but the text does not say so. 'sudhīḥ' ('learned') is an epithet, not a title.
review: Notes expanded on the Śaka chronogram: 'ṣaḍabhravāruṇair' reads right to left as 6-0-(vāruṇa), and the catalogue's ŚS 1606 needs vāruṇa = 16, which is not a standard value. ŚS 1606 Mārgaśira is about Nov/Dec 1684, but NS 806 Mārgaśira is about Nov/Dec 1685, so the two eras are one year apart. This conflict is now flagged.
Noted the spelling 'śrīcakrarājyasya' for the genitive śrīcakrarājasya. Cakrarāja is kept as commissioner and owner. No scribe is named, so the catalogue's 'Scribe: Cakrarāja' is not supported.

title: Manthānabhairavatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_raw: nepālavatsaragatagrahavāṇanāme pauṣasya śuklatithisatrayodśī ca | aṣaṃ bhaveti, gurūdine
date_note: = Thursday 22 Jan 1739, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti śrīmanthānabhairavayajñe śatakoṭīpravistīrṇṇa ānvayena koṭyāvatāre śrīcaturviṃśati sāhastre tantrābhidhāne namaskāāśīrvvādavaiṣṇano (!) nāma trinavatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ || samāptaṃ śrīmadbhārakaṃ || yādṛśī pustakaṃdṛṣṭvā............................... ................................................parameśvarī || || nepālavatsaragatagrahavāṇanāme pauṣasya śuklatithisatrayodśī ca | aṣaṃ bhaveti, gurūdine sahamādayaṃti, saṃpūrṇṇalekhyam idam adbhutam ājñakhaṇdaṃ || || (fol. 249v3–6)
notes: The colophon names no persons: no scribe, commissioner, owner or king. The year is a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram in 'nepālavatsaragata-graha-vāṇa-nāme'. graha = 9 and vāṇa (bāṇa) = 5 are clear. 'nāme' is probably a corruption of 'nāga' (8). Read right to left, that gives NS 859, about 1738/39 CE; Pauṣa śukla falls around Dec 1738–Jan 1739. If 'nāme' is only 'nāmni' ('in the year named'), the year would be just '59', which is incomplete. The year and CE date are therefore tentative. 'aṣaṃ bhaveti' (perhaps a corrupt nakṣatra or yoga name, or 'akṣaṃ'?) and 'sahamādayaṃti' are unclear. 'ājñākhaṇḍa' names the section of the text that was completed; it is not a person. The scribe's stanza 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā...' is partly lost.

title: Merutantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_raw: śrīsamvat 1906 sāla miti. āṣāḍha śudi 8 roja 5
date_note: = Thursday 28 Jun 1849, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti śrīmahāmāyāmahākālānumate merutaṃntre (!) śīvapraṇīte kārttavīryyamantrakathanaṃ nāma paṃcaviṃśaḥ prakāśaḥ || 25 || || merau śīvapraṇīte smin merūṇā prakṛṭīkṛte || murebhūte ca tantrāṇāṃ mahīśmantranirṇayaḥ || || svasti śrīsamvat 1906 sāla miti. āṣāḍha śudi 8 roja 5 śubham || samāptam || idaṃ pustakaṃ śrīśrīśrīrājakumāraupendravikramasāhadevasya || vatāsadhairyyanārāyaṇena likhitā || ❁ || (fol. 560v4–7)
notes: The era is not named ('samvat ... sāla miti ... roja'), but the Nepali formula and the Śāha prince point to VS 1906, about 1849 CE. 'vatāsa' is unclear. It may be a family or office designation, or a corruption (perhaps of khavāsa, 'attendant'). The catalogue gives the scribe only as 'Nārāyana'. Upendravikrama Śāha was a son of King Rājendravikrama Śāha. Rājendra is not named in the colophon, so he is not recorded as a person. The reigning king in VS 1906 was Surendravikrama Śāha (from 1847), but he is not named either. The closing verse ('merau śivapraṇīte…') belongs to the text, not to the scribe.

title: Lalitārahasyasārabhāṣyam
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Thursday 2 May 1907, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti śrīmatpadavākyapramāṇapārāvārapārīṇa (!) dhuriṇā sarvataṃtraśrīmadgaṃbhīradīkṣiasūrisununā (!) bharatyupākhāne bhāskarayrāyeṇa bhāsurānaṃdanārthot (!) dīkṣānāma śālinā praṇītaṃ saubhāgyabhāskarākhyaṃ vrahmāṃṇdapurāṇīyaśrīlalitārhasyam sāhasraṃ bhāṣyaṃ samāptaṃ || || śubham || || śrīsaṃvat || 1027 caitrakṛṣṇaroja. 5..se śrī lalitāpuramahāvuddhavodhimadayasa vijyākalaśrīmarendranandanaṃ coyā sidhayakā jula śūbham || || (fol. 240r10–12, v1–3)
notes: The colophon is in Newari ('coyā sidhayakā jula' = written and completed), so the era is Nepāla Saṃvat: NS 1027 = c. 1907 CE. VS or ŚS 1027 would fall before Bhāskararāya (18th century), so neither is possible. 'roja. 5' is unclear: 'roja' (day) may mark 5 as the tithi or as a weekday number (5 = Thursday). Here 5 is taken as the tithi. The scribe's name 'śrīmarendranandanaṃ' is probably a slip for śrī-Narendranandana, as on the catalogue card. The word before it, 'vijyākala', is unclear: it may be a corrupt epithet or title, or part of the name. The place is the Mahābuddha (Mahābauddha) area/vihāra in Lalitpur (Patan), written 'mahāvuddhavodhimadaya-sa' with the locative -sa. Bhāskararāya is the author of the Saubhāgyabhāskara commentary on the Lalitāsahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa). The colophon gives his surname as Bhāratī (corrupt 'bharatyupākhāne') and his dīkṣā name as Bhāsurānandanātha (corrupt 'bhāsurānaṃdanārthot'). The text title is corrupt in the catalogue ('lalitārhasyam sāhasraṃ').
review: p1: name reduced to stem 'Gambhīra' (dīkṣita/sūri kept as titles); father of Bhāskararāya, conventionally called Gambhīrarāya Dīkṣita
p2: added surname 'Bhāratī' (bharatyupākhāne = bhāratyupākhyena) to titles; initiation name Bhāsurānandanātha recorded in notes
p3: residence moved out of the person record because the Mahābuddha phrase is given with locative -sa, so it is the place of copying; 'vijyākala' noted as an unclear word placed before the name
date: era NS confirmed (VS/ŚS 1027 would be before the 18th-century commentator), ce_approx 1907; ambiguity of 'roja. 5' noted
notes expanded

colophon: iti śrīśāradātilakaṭīkāyāṃ bhaṭṭarāghavaviracitāyāṃ satsampradāyakṛtavyākhyāyāṃ padārthādarśābhikhyāyāṃ paṃcaviśaśvaḥ(!) paṭalaḥ 25 || śubam astu || gopālāyai namaḥ || gaṃgā (!) saṃvat 1754 samaai nāma kuāramāse śuklapakṣe likhitaṃ kāśyāṃ madhye marṇīkarṇikāsamipe (!) || śrīviśveśvarāyai namaḥ śrīrāmāyai namaḥ gaṇapatayai namaḥ goviṃdāyai namaḥ gaṃgāyai namaḥ || nārāyai namahaḥ (!) śrīśaṃkarābhyo namahaḥ (!) || saṃvat 1754 samai nāma kārttikamāṃ(!)se kṣṇapche(!) lī(!)lkhitaṃ kāśyāmadhe(!) maṇikarṇikāsamīpe nāthurāmakāesthavā nījāmāvāda ke || || rāmayā (!) namaḥ gaṃgāya (!) namaḥ mahādevayāe (!) namaḥ manumānayāe (!) namaḥ || || (fol. 370v8–11, 371r1–2)
notes: The colophon gives two dates in saṃvat 1754: Kuāra (Āśvina) śuklapakṣa and Kārttika kṛṣṇapakṣa. In pūrṇimānta reckoning, which is normal at Kāśī, these are consecutive fortnights, so they probably mark the progress or completion of the copy. The catalogue reads the year as ŚS 1754. However, a plain 'saṃvat' in a North Indian (Kāśī) colophon is normally Vikrama, which gives VS 1754 ≈ 1697 CE; ŚS would give 1832 CE. 'samaai/samai nāma' is unclear; it may stand for samaya or a garbled saṃvatsara name. 'gaṃgā (!)' before the first saṃvat is probably part of the invocations rather than an era name. The scribe Nāthurāma Kāyastha is said to be 'of Nizāmābād' (nījāmāvāda ke). This is probably the Nizamabad near Azamgarh, UP, but the identification is not certain. The catalogue's 'Date of composition: SAM 1550' is the date of Rāghavabhaṭṭa's commentary (Padārthādarśa, c. VS 1550 ≈ 1493/94 CE) and is not stated in this colophon. The deity invocations (Gopāla, Viśveśvara, Rāma, Gaṇapati, Govinda, Gaṅgā, Nārāyaṇa, Śaṅkara, Mahādeva, 'manumāna' = Hanumān?) are not persons.
review: Kept both persons; only minor refinements.
p2 residence normalized to 'Nizāmābād' (nījāmāvāda ke), with the identification marked as probable; evidence shortened.
Date notes: the two dates are probably consecutive fortnights in pūrṇimānta reckoning (Āśvina śukla, then Kārttika kṛṣṇa), so CE 1697 (c. Sept.–Oct.). Added that 'samaai/samai nāma' is unclear.
Notes: the catalogue's composition date (SAM 1550) is the commentary's own date, not the copying date; 'gaṃgā saṃvat' is probably an invocation run together with the date.

title: Mādhavanidāna
subject: Āyurveda
date_note: = Wednesday 22 Nov 1797, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmādhavavīracitaṃ(!) mādhavanīdānam(!) samāpta(!) || śubham astu saṃvat 1854 budhavāra aghanaśuklapakṣe tīthau(!) caturthīyāṃ(!) lekhakacīraṃjīva(!) maganīrāma gīnātasārasuta aujhā śubham astu kalyāṇaṃ bhavatu śrīrāmacaṃdrāya namaḥ śrīhanumatebhyo(!) namaḥ || śrīgaṇādhapataye(!) namaḥ || (fol. 73r6-8)
notes: The colophon gives 'saṃvat' with no era. VS is assumed from the Devanagari script and the Ojhā surname. VS 1854 Mārgaśīrṣa = Nov/Dec 1797 CE, whether the year is reckoned from Caitra or Kārttika. A rough mean-moon check puts śukla 4 around Wed 22 / Thu 23 Nov 1797, so the weekday fits approximately; this was not computed exactly. 'Aghana' is the vernacular form of Agrahāyaṇa/Mārgaśīrṣa. 'cīraṃjīva' (= cirañjīva, 'long-lived') is an epithet for the scribe, not a title. 'aujhā' (Ojhā), the brahmin surname, comes after 'gīnātasārasuta', so it could belong to the father as well as the scribe. The father's name 'Gīnātasāra' is odd and probably corrupt. The catalogue reads the scribe's name as Maganīrāma Ojhā, which agrees with this reading. The author's name: 'mādhavavīracitaṃ' = mādhava-viracitaṃ.

p3: confidence lowered to low because the father's name is probably corrupt

title: Nānauṣadhakalpa
subject: (Tantra)Āyurveda
date_note: = Wednesday 11 Nov 1857, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīherambāecanavidhi saṃpūrśubhma (!) || |samvat 1914 sāla miti mārgavadi 11 roja 4 śubhma || || huṃ || (aṭala) || robhayānā kāladhālā paṃcamahāpāpa (!) thosaphu dhirjavīrasiṃha yāgu (exp.23.b:4-7)
notes: The phrase 'robhayānā kāladhālā paṃcamahāpāpa' is a Newari curse against theft. It reads as lobha yānā kāla dhāla(sā) pañcamahāpāpa(ka), 'if anyone takes [this book] out of greed, [may he incur] the five great sins'. So 'kāladhālā' is not a place of copying, and the catalogue's 'kāladhārā' is a misreading. 'thosaphu dhirjavīrasiṃha yāgu' means 'this book belongs to Dhirjavīrasiṃha'. He is the owner, and nothing in the colophon says he copied it, so the catalogue's 'Scribe' label is unsupported (he may be scribe-owner, but that cannot be shown). The name may stand for Dhīrajavīrasiṃha / Dhīra-Javīra Siṃha. The colophon's title is 'śrīherambāecanavidhi' (= Herambārcanavidhi), not Nānauṣadhakalpa, so this colophon may close a sub-text in a composite MS. '(aṭala)' after 'huṃ' is unclear (possibly a seal or a closing word). VS 1914 Mārgaśīrṣa ≈ Nov/Dec 1857 CE.
review: Place removed: 'kāladhālā' is not a toponym but part of the Newari curse formula 'robhayānā kāladhālā' = lobha yānā kāla dhāla(sā) 'if anyone takes [it] out of greed'; the catalogue's Place of Copying 'kāladhārā' and the normalization 'Kathmandu' are both wrong
Residence of Dhirjavīrasiṃha cleared (it came from the same misreading)
Weekday rendered as Wednesday (roja 4)
Notes rewritten: the curse formula is explained, owner-only role kept, colophon title Herambārcanavidhi noted

notes:
The copy is dated VS 1890 (c. 1833 CE). The following 'vṛṣe śākha 17 14' would be ŚS 1714 (c. 1792 CE). That conflicts with the VS year, which corresponds to ŚS 1755. 'vṛṣe' may be the name of the Jovian year (Vṛṣa) rather than part of the era. The Vikrama year is preferred here.

The verse 'śrīmad bhūpati vikramād gaṇanā khaṃ vahni sindhubhi sindubhir ... jyeṣṭha asi saptamī ... bhṛgau iyaṃ ṭīkā ... racī(tā) śrīnātha gosvāmibhiḥ' gives the date when the ṭīkā was COMPOSED (Jyeṣṭha, dark half, day 7, a Friday), not the copy date. The chronogram is uncertain. Read right to left, kha=0 and vahni=3 give a year ending in -30. The doubled 'sindhu' (4 or 7) looks like dittography, so a reading such as VS 1730 cannot be secured.

The commentator is 'harinātha' in the prose colophon but 'śrīnātha gosvāmibhiḥ' in the verse; this is probably 'śrī[hari]nātha'.

'cautastvaṃṭamārithe śarayure dhāryā bhiṣagbhiḥ' is garbled, roughly 'to be kept by physicians'. A place name (Sarayū?) is possible but uncertain.

'chaganajīvrane' is probably a corruption of Chaganajīvana (+ -ena/-sya). The book is said to be his ('paṇḍitasya ... pustakaṃ'). 'paṇḍita' could instead belong to Puruṣottama.

The final 'śrī mutharaśa (!)' is unclear: it may be Mathurā (the place) or a personal name. It is not recorded as either.
review: p4: name read as Chaganajīvana (a common Gujarati personal name, Chhaganjīvan) rather than 'Chaganajī'; role changed from commissioner to owner, since 'paṇḍitasya ... pustakaṃ' marks possession and nothing says he had it copied (no likhāpita). Confidence lowered to low.

notes: The catalogue gives ŚS 1789, but the colophon reads 'śrīśāke 1719' (= 1797 CE, Mārgaśīrṣa, so Nov./Dec. 1797). The 1719 reading fits the Gorkha occupation of Kumaon (1790–1815), when a Subbā (governor) Prabal Rāṇā would be plausible, so the catalogue figure is probably a misprint. 'Pravala' is probably Prabala/Prabal. 'Yogyeṣu likhitam' means 'written for (the use of)': it makes him the owner/beneficiary and probably the commissioner. The colophon does not support the catalogue's 'Donor'. Gaṃgāvālī = Gaṅgolī in Kumaon. The colophon gives it as the scribe's residence ('nivāsinā'), not explicitly as the place of copying. Paṃta = Pant, a Kumaoni brahmin surname. Vaṅgasena (son of Gadādhara) is the author of the text.

title: Nānāgranthasamuccayamaśvaśāstra
subject: Aśvāyurveda
date_note: = Wednesday 16 Jun 1593, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: samvat 713 jeṣṭha kṛṣṇa tṛtīyāyāṃ utrāṣāḍha (!) nakṣatra budhavāra thva kvahnu jayadatta nāma śāḍaṃyā śāstra coya dhuṃṅa dina juro || thva pustaka śrī śrī jayanārāyanāvatāra parameśvara paramabhaṭṭāraka rājādhirāja śrī śrī jagajjyotirmmalladeva prabhu ṭhākuras taṃ śrī jayantarājadevana coyā juro || e || śrī bhavānīśaṃkarābhyāṃ namaḥ || śubham astu || || [[❖śrī śrī sumati jayajitāmitramalladevasana thva ustaka dalavārayā kayaña gadāṅa guli dukā syaṃta yā juro || bhāgīrāma paramāna yā varasa || samvat 808 śrāvaṇa vadi 13 śubah ||]] (fol. 56v1–6)
notes:
The main colophon says that in NS 713 (c. 1593 CE), Jayantarājadeva copied Jayadatta's treatise on horses (Aśvaśāstra) for the lord Jagajjyotirmalla. The reading of 'prabhu ṭhākuras taṃ' is unclear: it could mean 'for the lord' or 'by the lord himself'. Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur reigned c. NS 734-757 (1614-1637 CE), so in NS 713 he could only have been a prince. Either the regnal titles were added later or the year is miscopied (perhaps 733?).

The bracketed later note is dated NS 808 Śrāvaṇa vadi 13 (c. 1688 CE). That date fits the reign of Jitāmitramalla of Bhaktapur (c. 1673-1696). The note records that the king acquired this book from the son of Dalavāra by paying a sum of money (gadāṅa; 'dukā syaṃta'). Bhāgīrāma acted as witness (paramāna = pramāṇa). 'varasa' is unclear. The catalogue lists Bhāgīrāma as the scribe, which is wrong. Dalavāra could also be an office title rather than a personal name.
review: p4: 'Sumati' is part of Jitāmitramalla's full regnal name, not a title. Name changed to Sumatijayajitāmitramalladeva and the title removed. Roles changed from king+owner to king+owner+other: he acquired the book in NS 808.
p5 Bhāgīrāma: 'paramāna yā' means 'acted as witness (pramāṇa)', not minister. Role changed to other, the 'paramāna' title removed, and confidence set to medium.
Removed p5 under_reign_of p4 and added p5 other->p4 (witness to the king's acquisition).
Added p6 Dalavāra (low confidence): the book was obtained from his son for money ('dalavārayā kayaña').
p2 Jagajjyotirmalla: commissioner confidence lowered to medium. NS 713 (1593) falls before his reign (c. NS 734-757), so the under_reign_of relation was removed. Kept wrote_for p3->p2.
p3 Jayantarājadeva confidence lowered to medium.

title: Devībhāgavatapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Friday 7 May 1529, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe ṣṭādaśasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyyāśikyāṃ dvādaśaskaṃdhe trayodaśo dhyāyaḥ || || samāptaś cāyaṃ skandhaḥ || lekhakapāṭhakayo śubham astu bhūpaṃ ca parjanyayuteṣu śāke śukrākhyamāsāsitapakṣake ravau śaṃbhos tithau vipravaro lilekha triśaktimāhātmyayutaṃ kathānakam || 1 || (fol. 22v3–5)
notes: 'Vipravaro lilekha' most likely means 'an excellent brahmin wrote [this]', which hides the scribe's name. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Vipravara' takes the epithet as a name, so it is doubtful. The chronogram 'bhūpaṃ ca parjanya-' appears corrupt; the catalogue reads it as bhū-pañca-parjanya. Parjanya is not a standard number word. If it stands for Indra (= 14), reading right to left gives ŚS 1451 = c. 1529 CE. That is only a guess, and other values for parjanya would change the year. Śukra is the old name for Jyeṣṭha. 'Śambhos tithi' is most probably caturdaśī (Śiva's tithi; kṛṣṇa 14 = Śivarātri), but ekādaśī (Rudra = 11) or aṣṭamī cannot be ruled out. The colophon ends Skandha 12, adhyāya 13, and includes a stock blessing for the writer and reader (lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ śubham astu).
review: Scribe 'vipravaro' kept, but confidence lowered to low: in the verse it most likely means 'an excellent brahmin' (vipra-vara), not a personal name; added 'vipra' (brahmin) as a title.

Tithi changed from ekādaśī to caturdaśī (probable). 'Śambhos tithi' names the tithi whose deity is Śiva, which is the 14th; kṛṣṇa caturdaśī is Śivarātri. Ekādaśī (Rudra = 11) and aṣṭamī are noted as alternatives.
Year: added a tentative reading of parjanya as Indra = 14, read right to left with bhū 1 and pañca 5 to give ŚS 1451 (≈1529 CE). It is marked as uncertain.
