title: Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Friday 3 May 1715, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe viṣṇurahasyopadeśo nāmāṣṭatriṃśo dhyāyaḥ || samāptaḥ || || 38 || || bālavahnivasucābde madhumāse kuhur 〈d〉 dine | śrībṛhannāradīyākhyaṃ paurāṇaṃ(!) vyāsanirmmitaṃ || harinārāyaṇo nāma daivajñakulabarddhanaḥ | likhitaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ śāstraṃ kṛṣṇaprīti (!) kṛtaṃ (!) mayā || || || śrī 3 nārāyaṇaprītir astu || ❖ samvat 1013 (jhi) kārttikavadi 11 maṅgalavāla thva kuhnu yaladeśa uku[[m]]vahāyā maheśavarānanda///- (fol. 184v4–6)
purpose: kṛṣṇaprīti (for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure); closing benediction: śrī 3 nārāyaṇaprītir astu
notes: The chronogram bāla(=bāṇa, 5)-vahni(3)-vasu(8), read right to left, gives 835. The era is not written; Nepal Saṃvat (NS) is assumed, giving NS 835 = c. 1715 CE (Caitra amāvāsyā). After the colophon comes a separate Newari note, 'samvat 1013 kārttikavadi 11 maṅgalavāla' (NS 1013 = c. 1892/93 CE, a Tuesday). It names Maheśvarānanda (written maheśavarānanda) of Ukubahāḥ, Patan, and breaks off ('///-') before saying what he did. The catalogue gives both scribes and both dates. Two readings are possible: (a) the NS 1013 note is a later owner's or reader's entry, or (b) Maheśvarānanda copied the manuscript in NS 1013 and carried over Harinārāyaṇa's NS 835 verse colophon from his exemplar. In case (b), Harinārāyaṇa would be the scribe of the exemplar, not of this copy. A look at the folio, its script and its hands is needed to decide. 'yaladeśa' belongs to the NS 1013 note, so it is not certain that this is where the NS 835 copy was made.
review: p3 Maheśvarānanda: affiliation normalised to Ukubahāḥ (Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra), residence Patan; confidence lowered to low because the note breaks off before his role is stated. The catalogue lists him as scribe, so he may be the actual copyist of NS 1013 (see notes).
p1 Vyāsa: confidence lowered to medium because this is the traditional authorship attribution.
date: era NS is inferred and not written with the chronogram; 'bāla' is read as bāṇa (5); the NS 1013 date is recorded in notes.
place: flagged as belonging to the NS 1013 note, which may or may not be where the copy was made.
purpose: expanded to give both the scribe's 'kṛṣṇaprīti' and the closing benediction 'nārāyaṇaprītir astu'.

title: Matsyapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 14 Oct 1890, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmatsyapurāṇe pāramasaṃhitāyāṃ anukramaṇikākhyaṃ matsyapurāṇaṃ samāptaṃ || 275 || liṣitaṃ tat tu kṣeyā(!) śrīvajrācāryye machindraviranāthanatho śāstra coyā julo || || samvat 1010 miti āśvinaśudi 1 roa 3 sasaṃpūrṇadhikādina julo || || maganāpuratamadhitolayā śrīupādhyāyahaladhāyānacoyā vaviyā julaḥ || yādṛśa ... doṣaka(!) || || śubhm || || (fol. 243v3–5)
notes: The colophon contains two Newari statements about writing. (1) 'śrīvajrācāryye machindraviranātha-na tho śāstra coyā julo' means 'Vajrācārya Machindravīranātha wrote this śāstra'. The verb is 'coyā' (wrote), not the causative 'coyakā', so he is the scribe, not the commissioner. (2) 'maganāpura tamadhi tola-yā śrī upādhyāya haladhāyāna coyā vaviyā julaḥ': 'haladhāyāna' is probably Haladhara-na (ergative), and 'vaviyā' is probably biyā ('gave' / 'wrote for someone'). The catalogue takes Haladhara as the scribe. If the ending is really -yāta, the sentence would mean the book was written and given TO Haladhara, making him the recipient or owner. So the relationship between the two men is unclear: they may be two scribes, or one may be the scribe and the other the recipient. The opening 'liṣitaṃ tat tu kṣeyā(!)' is corrupt. Maganāpura with Tamadhi ṭol is given as Haladhara's locality; it is not identified, and it is not stated as the place of copying. The era is read as NS: 1010 VS would be impossible for a Newari-language Devanagari colophon of this kind. That gives NS 1010 = c. 1890 CE. 'sasaṃpūrṇadhikādina' = the day of completion.
review: p1 Machindravīranātha: role changed from commissioner to scribe. Newari 'coyā' means 'wrote' (the causative would be 'coyakā'), and 'machindraviranātha-na tho śāstra coyā julo' means 'Machindravīranātha wrote this śāstra'. Confidence lowered to medium.

p2 Haladhara: kept as scribe, following the catalogue, but confidence lowered to medium. The phrase 'haladhāyāna coyā vaviyā' is corrupt, and Haladhara could instead be the person it was written for. Residence normalized to Tamadhi ṭol, Maganāpura.
Removed the wrote_for relation. The colophon gives no clear basis for saying p2 wrote for p1.
Date: pakṣa normalized to śukla and weekday to Tuesday (roa 3 = roja 3). NS 1010 = c. 1890 CE confirmed.
Place: kept, but the notes now say it is stated as Haladhara's locality, not explicitly as the place of copying.

notes: The colophon ends with the bare genitive 'gaurīdattasya', with no 'pustakam' and no 'likhitam'. 'jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇa(!)māyāṃ' probably stands for 'jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇāmāyāṃ', i.e. the new moon (amāvāsyā) of the dark fortnight of Jyeṣṭha. Śālivāhana-śaka 1715 + 78 gives about 1793 CE (roughly June). 'ṣaṣṭheśe(!)' stands for 'ṣaṣṭhe 'ṃśe'. The title also names a Vaiṣṇavākūṭacandrikāṭīkā, but the colophon quoted here covers only the Viṣṇupurāṇa.

notes: The colophon names no scribe, commissioner or owner. The era is not stated. It is read as VS because the copy is in Devanagari, the closing formula shows Hindi/Rajasthani features ('sukulapache', 'jagaranāthajī sahāi'), and NS 1825 is impossible. Mahīdhara composed the text in 1588 CE, which agrees with a VS date. The VS−57 rule gives 1768, but Māgha śukla 8 of VS 1825 falls in about January–February 1769. The weekday (Tuesday) has not been checked. 'ebhaenāma' is obscure; it may be a corrupt saṃvatsara name ('... nāma [saṃvatsare]'). 'śrīrāma', 'śrīkṛṣṇa' and 'śrījagaranāthajī' (Jagannātha) are invocations of deities, not persons.

Nepal Saṃvat is inferred from the Newari script and the Newari phrase 'kunhu dhunakā dina juro' ('on that day it was finished'), so NS 793 is about 1673 CE (Māgha kṛṣṇa 2, around January–February 1673). 'lekhakānāṃ trayāṇāṃ ... devānāṃ' sits inside a damaged stock benediction ('śubham astu sarvajagatāṃ ...'); it should not be read as naming three scribes. Gaṇapatiśarman is the author of the stotra, not a person involved in this copy. The colophon closes a Vāgvatīstotra (fol. 98v), while the catalogue title is Skandapurāṇa. The stotra may be an added text or a related Vāgvatī-māhātmya piece, so the date may apply only to this part of the codex.

title: Skandapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Wednesday 22 May 1686, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīskandapurāṇe ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ śrīpuruṣottamamātsya utkalakhaṇḍaṃ ekaṣaṣṭītamo dhyāyaḥ | || je(!)ṣṭhe kṛṣṇakuhusarohinīṃ budhe ṣadvinduvaśvaṃ kṛte | nepālīyamate smite vimaladhī śrībuddhisiṃhaḥ kṛti || cakre pūrṇṇam amuṃ svabhinnalipibhir bhaktyā jagatsvāmine || līlādāsa vayusmata(!)stutikathāmahātmyayustaṃ(!) mudā || || śubha || samvat 806 vaiśākhakṛṣṇa 15 amāvasyāṃ budhavāre rohina(!) nakṣatre gandhayoga kunhu, coyaṃ, vāravāhlācake(!), sidhayakāva śrīkālidāsa ujhājuyatā viyā puruṣottamapriti || (fol. 143v6–10)
purpose: For the pleasure of Puruṣottama (Jagannātha) ('bhaktyā jagatsvāmine'; 'puruṣottamapriti'). The finished copy was given to Kālidāsa Ujhā.
notes: The verse chronogram 'ṣaḍ-vindu-vasu' (6-0-8, read right to left) gives 806 'nepālīyamate', which matches the prose 'samvat 806' (NS). The verse names the month as Jyeṣṭha (pūrṇimānta), while the prose has Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa (amānta). These are the same new moon (kuhū), so the two do not conflict. 'ujhā' (Ojhā, Maithil brahmin surname/title) with honorific -ju and dative -yatā: Kālidāsa received the book. The giver is not named explicitly but is presumably the scribe. 'vāravāhlācake(!)' is corrupt and unclear; it could be a place or a verb phrase, so it is not used as the place of copying. 'līlādāsa vayusmata(!)stutikathāmahātmyayustaṃ(!)' is corrupt. Līlādāsa could be a personal name, but it is more likely part of a description of the text, so it is not entered as a person. 'jagatsvāmine' refers to the deity, not a person.

subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Thursday 26 Feb 1807, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīskandapurāṇe brahmottarakhaṇḍe purāṇaśravaṇe mahimānuvarṇanaṃ nāma dvāviṃśo dhyāyaḥ || 22 || śrīgaurīśaṃkarābhyāṃ namaḥ śrīumāmaheśvarābhyāṃ namaḥ ... || saṃvat 1863 sāla phālguna kṛṣṇapakṣacaturthītithi vṛhaspativāramā śrīsardāracaṃdravīrale śrīnagaramā mahānaṃdapaṇḍitamārphata brahmottarakhaṃḍaṃ purāna lekhāyā śubham (fol. 64r7–12)
notes: The colophon is in Nepali. It says Sardār Candravīra had the Brahmottarakhaṇḍa copied at Śrīnagara through (mārphata) Mahānanda Paṇḍita. Mahānanda may have been the actual copyist, or only the paṇḍita who arranged the copying. The text does not say which. Candravīra is probably Candravīra Kũvar, a Gorkhali sardār in Garhwal during the Gorkha occupation (1804–1815). That fits Śrīnagara = Srinagar in Garhwal, but the identification is not certain. The date is VS 1863 Phālguna kṛṣṇa 4, a Thursday, which is about Feb/Mar 1807 CE; the weekday was not checked against an ephemeris. The catalogue fields do not match the colophon. No Hariścandra appears in the quoted text; he may be named elsewhere in the manuscript. King Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha died in 1775, so he cannot be the reigning king; in 1807 the king was Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha, who is not named here.
review: p2 Mahānanda: 'scribe' role removed. 'mārphata' means 'through' or 'by the agency of', so he was the agent who got the copy made, not necessarily the copyist. Roles are now 'other'; confidence for scribe stays open (see notes).
Relation changed from 'p2 wrote_for p1' to 'p1 commissioned_from p2', because the copy was made through Mahānanda.
Identification of Candravīra with Candravīra Kũvar softened to 'probable' in notes.
Notes now say the catalogue's king (Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha, d. 1775) is anachronistic for VS 1863. The colophon also names no scribe Hariścandra.

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
date_note: = Monday 15 Aug 1718, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīitihāsasamuccaye paṃcapretopākhyāne paṃcatriṃśattamodhyāyaḥ || 35 || samāptoyaṃ graṃthaḥ || saṃvat 1775 varṣe māse bhādrapade kṛṣṇapakṣe caturthī caṃdravāsare avaṃtīnagaramadhye dvivedī kānhajītatputra (!) someśvara umābhyāṃ pitā putrābhyāṃ militvā liṣitoyaṃ (!) graṃthaḥ || svavācanārthaṃ paropakārārthaṃ vā || śrīrastu || || || || || śrīḥ || || || || || kṛṣṇo jayati || (fol. 93v5–8)
purpose: svavācanārtha (own reading) or paropakārārtha (for others' benefit)
notes: The phrase reads 'dvivedī Kānhajī tatputra Someśvara ubhābhyāṃ (written umābhyāṃ) pitāputrābhyāṃ militvā likhito (written liṣito) 'yaṃ granthaḥ': father and son copied the book together. The ending -jī in Kānhajī may be an honorific (stem Kānha), but it is kept because it works as the name in this western/central Indian usage. The colophon's 'dvivedī' stands before the father's name; giving it to the son as well is inferred from shared family status and the catalogue's 'Someśvara Dvivedī'. The catalogue names only Someśvara as scribe, but the colophon names both men. VS 1775 = c. 1718 CE (Bhādrapada, probably August–September 1718). Avaṃtīnagara = Ujjain. This is a non-Nepalese (Mālwā) manuscript.
review: Added 'owner' to both scribes: 'svavācanārthaṃ' means the copy was made for their own reading ('paropakārārthaṃ vā' = or for others' benefit).
Added the title 'dvivedī' to Someśvara as well. The family surname covers father and son, which matches the catalogue's 'Someśvara Dvivedī'.
Normalised the weekday 'caṃdravāsara' to 'Monday' and the tithi to 'kṛṣṇa 4'.
Changed the purpose field to a short normalised form.
Expanded the notes: the -jī ending, the ubhābhyāṃ correction and the word division.

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
date_note: = Monday 10 Apr 1679, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye nāradapuṇḍarīkasaṃvādo nāma dvātriṃśatitamoʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || lasannākanāthā layenopamāne, mahīmaṇḍāsmin pure bhaktasaṃjñe | nṛpe śāsati śrījitāmitra malle, kaniṣṭhogramalle virājatpratāpe || nepāle hāyanesmin grahanidhi turage caitramāse tamiśre, vaidhṛtyāṃ revatī divasakara śaśina saṃgame somavāre | devīprītyā sudhīmān śivahari dharaṇī daivatoyetihāsaṃ, vyāsoktaṃ pustakātryāṃ vitarāte śivasiṃhaḥsma daivajñe dhīraḥ || (fol. 161r2–5)
purpose: for the pleasure of the Goddess (devīprītyā)
notes: Chronogram graha (9), nidhi (9), turaga (7), read right to left, gives NS 799 = 1679 CE. This falls within Jitāmitramalla's reign at Bhaktapur (1673–1696), with his younger brother Ugramalla named beside him. The catalogue's 'NS 997' reads the chronogram left to right and is wrong. 'divasakara-śaśina-saṃgame' means the sun–moon conjunction, i.e. Caitra amāvāsyā. Revatī as the nakṣatra fits this, since the sun sits at the end of Mīna. The second verse is corrupt ('daivatoyetihāsaṃ', 'pustakātryāṃ' perhaps for pustakākhyaṃ/pustakārthaṃ, 'vitarāte' for vitarate, 'śivasiṃhaḥsma'). It has two nominative agents: Śivahari, a learned brahmin (dharaṇīdaivata), who 'gives' (vitarate) the Itihāsa spoken by Vyāsa, and Śivasiṃha, the daivajña. The verse does not say who wrote and who gave. Treating Śivahari as donor and Śivasiṃha as scribe follows the catalogue and the order of the verse, but it is not certain. Śivasiṃha could also be the donor/giver, with Śivahari as a person or exemplar source in another case.
review: p3 Śivahari: role changed from 'commissioner' to 'donor'. The verb is vitarate ('gives, bestows'), and no likhāpita or lekhayāmāsa appears. Confidence stays medium.
p4 Śivasiṃha: confidence lowered to medium. The verse has no explicit 'likhitam'. The scribe role rests on the catalogue and on his being named last as the daivajña.

Date confirmed: graha 9, nidhi 9, turaga 7, read right to left, gives NS 799 = 1679 CE. Caitra kṛṣṇa amāvāsyā, Revatī, Vaidhṛti and Monday all agree with each other. The catalogue's NS 997 is a misreading (read left to right).
Purpose clarified as 'for the pleasure of the Goddess (devīprītyā)'.
Notes expanded on the syntactic ambiguity of the second verse.

title: itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
date_note: = Thursday 23 Dec 1677, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye nāradapuṇḍarīkasaṃvādo nāma catvāriṃśatitamoʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 40 || || aṣṭāṃkasvarasaṃyāte mārggakṛṣṇe śubhetvadaḥ | caturddaśyāṃ gurorvvāre likhitāʼntakrśariḥ || || saṃpūrṇṇa (fol. 144v5–6)
notes: The chronogram is aṣṭa = 8, aṅka = 9, svara = 7. Read right to left, this gives 798. The colophon does not name the era. NS is inferred from the Newari script and from the plausibility of the date: NS 798 Mārgaśīrṣa falls in about Nov./Dec. 1677 CE. The weekday has not been checked against the date. 'śubhetvadaḥ' is corrupt, probably for something like śubhe 'hani. The scribe's name is corrupt. 'likhitāʼntakrśariḥ' probably stands for 'likhito 'nantakeśarī' (ananta- with the syllable 'na' lost, and krśari for keśarī). This matches the catalogue's reading, Anantakeśarī. The stem is given as Anantakeśarin.
review: Notes expanded: the era is not named and NS is inferred; the right-to-left reading of the chronogram is spelled out; the corrupt name segment is explained.

title: Viṣṇupurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Friday 6 Nov 1693, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīviṣṇupurāṇe ṣaṣṭhaṃśe ṣṭamo dhyāyaḥ ṣaṣṭhāṃśaś ca samāpta iti || śrīśrīśrīviṣṇuprītir astu || ... saṃ 814 kārttikaśukla 9 thvakunhu śrīśrīsumatijayajitāmitramalladevasanabhāgirāmapradhānāṅgayā velasathva viṣṇupurāṇamahāyatnanadayakā ana helāya yamateva ... yāya māla || || (fol. 177v1–3)
purpose: for the pleasure of Viṣṇu (viṣṇuprītir astu)
notes: The catalogue gives the date as SAM 818, but the quoted colophon reads 'saṃ 814' (NS 814 = 1693 CE). The year 814 fits the reign of Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur, who ruled until about NS 816 (1696). By NS 818 the king was Bhūpatīndra Malla, so 818 is probably a catalogue error. The catalogue also names the scribe as 'Bhāgīmāna Pradhāna', which looks like a garbled form of 'Bhāgirāma Pradhān(āṅga)'. In the colophon, Bhāgirāma appears only in a time phrase: 'pradhānāṅgayā velasa' means 'in the time of (minister) Bhāgirāma'. Nothing marks him as the scribe, and no scribe is named in the quoted text. The king is in the ergative case ('-sana') and is the agent of 'mahāyatnana dayakā' ('had it made with great effort'), so he is the commissioner. The phrase 'ana helāya yamateva ... yāya māla' is unclear and has a lacuna.

colophon: iti śrīmahābhārataśataāhasryā vaiyāsakyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ānuśāsanike parvaṇi bhīṣmaniryāṇaṃ || 155 || || samāptam idaṃm ānuśāsanikaṃ bhāratasya trayodaśaṃ parvaṇi || || 13 || śubhaṃ bhavatu || śrīr astu || samvat 1825 miti phā. va 6 (fol. 172v4–5)
notes: The era is not stated. 'samvat ... miti' in a Devanagari manuscript points to Vikrama Saṃvat, so 1825 VS gives about 1768 CE; Phālguna vadi 6 would most likely be in Feb/Mar 1769 CE. The catalogue field says SAM 1872 (about 1815 CE), which does not match the 1825 quoted from fol. 172v (Anuśāsanaparvan end). The 1872 date may come from another part of the multi-part reel B 260/2, or it may be a catalogue error. The colophon names no scribe, patron or other historical person. 'vaiyāsakyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ' is part of the title formula, so Vyāsa is not recorded as a person.
review: Era kept as VS, but the notes now say it is inferred: the colophon has only 'samvat' plus 'miti', which is the usual pattern for Vikrama dates in Devanagari manuscripts from Nepal.
ce_approx stays 1768 (1825−57). The notes add that Phālguna kṛṣṇa 6 of VS 1825 most likely falls in February/March 1769 CE.
Expanded the note on the catalogue's SAM 1872: it may belong to another part or another dated colophon of reel B 260/2, so it does not have to be a misreading.

Saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ dvisaptatitamo dhyāya (!) || 72 || || samāptaṃ śubham || || kāyaṇavāca………………….. doṣo na diyate (!) || svasti śrīśāke 1796 || śrīvikramādi 1931 śrīnepālī śrayos tu samvat 994 sālam iti naṣṭa āṣāḍhavadi 8 roja 3 mā liṣitaṃ śubham || likhāpaītvā (!) sakodeśe jalaṣu tola vāgvatuthikṣeyānhulakṣanārāṃyā (!) manasa dharmacitta utpattijuyā bhvate bhāṣasaphulatokātayā jula śubhaṃ (fol. 128v12–21)
purpose: merit: copy had made because a pious mind arose (dharmacitta utpatti juyā)
notes: The three eras agree: ŚS 1796 + 78 = VS 1931 − 57 = NS 994 + 880 = 1874 CE. The word 'naṣṭa' before āṣāḍhavadi is unclear. It may be a scribal word, or it may mark a kṣaya/irregular month; this has not been checked. The catalogue names Lakṣyanārāyaṇa as the scribe. However, likhāpaītvā (= likhāpayitvā, 'having caused to be written') together with 'dharmacitta utpattijuyā' suggests he was the patron who had the copy made. He may also have done the writing himself, but the colophon does not say so. His name is corrupt (lakṣanārāṃyā with Newari genitive -yā; possibly Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa). The 'nhu' before it and the string 'vāgvatuthikṣe' are unclear and may be part of a locality or a corrupt word, so they are not treated as an affiliation. The closing Newari phrase 'bhvate bhāṣasaphulatokātayā jula' is obscure.

subject: Kathā

colophon: pustakam etat stynārāyaṇasya śrīmajajagddhara (!) paṃtebhyo kurmāṃcalasthe[[bhyo]] kurmācalīya hutahut (!) [[te]]bhyo svahastena saṃpūrṇīkṛty smvt vedābhrāṅkabhūmimite pau[[ṣe]] māsi śukla[[pa]]kṣe trayodaśyāṃ somo samrpiteti śubham || (fol. 10r8–10)
purpose: gift: copy completed in the giver's own hand and presented (samarpitā) to Jagaddhara Paṃta of Kurmācala
notes:
The chronogram vedābhrāṅkabhūmi reads 4-0-9-1; read right to left this gives 1904. The colophon has only 'saṃvat', so the era is not stated. In Kumaon this almost certainly means VS, which gives Dec 1847 or Jan 1848 CE (Pauṣa śukla 13). The weekday (Monday) has not been verified.

Jagaddhara Paṃta (Pant, a Kumaoni brahmin family name), of Kurmācala, is named in the honorific plural dative as the person who received the book. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's Scribe field is a misreading. The person who completed the copy 'with his own hand' (svahastena saṃpūrṇīkṛtya) and gave it away is not named. 'kurmācalīya hutahut[te]bhyo' is corrupt. It is probably a further honorific description of Jagaddhara, for example something built on hutabhuj ('fire-priest' / agnihotrin). It could also be a second recipient, but this is uncertain. Kurmācala is Jagaddhara's residence; the colophon does not explicitly give it as the place of copying, although the copy was probably made there.
review: p1 Jagaddhara: role 'beneficiary' replaced by 'other' (recipient of the gift); 'owner' kept because the book was handed over to him. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's Scribe field is wrong.
Evidence shortened to the dative phrase plus samarpitā.
Place of copying emptied: the colophon gives Kurmācala only as Jagaddhara's residence ('kurmāṃcalasthebhyo'), not as the place where the copy was made.
Purpose changed from 'parārtha' to a specific gift statement.

notes: The era is not named, but NS is implied by the reign of Nṛpendramalla of Kathmandu (c. NS 794–800 / 1674–1680 CE). The chronogram navavivaravāha gives nava = 9, vivara = 9 (the nine openings of the body) and vāha = 7 (the horses of the sun). Read right to left, that is 799, so NS 799 ≈ 1679 CE. The catalogue's NS 709 is probably a misreading of the chronogram, since 709 would fall outside his reign. Nepāla is given as the scribe's residence (nepālādhirvāsinā, read nepālādhivāsinā); the place of copying is not stated separately. 'dijanmanā' should read dvijanmanā. 'naipāyikavāraṇapaṃcānana' should read naiyāyikavāraṇapañcānana, an epithet of the author Murāri. The weekday (Monday) has not been checked against the tithi.

title: Mālatīmādhava
subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: = Wednesday 3 Nov 1694, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmālatīmādhavaṃ nāma nāṭakaṃ sampūrṇam || || saṃvat 1616 mārgaśira vadi 1 dine budhavāsare śrīmad †vṛ(14) varatadagacchebha 0 † śrījinaharṣasūriguruṇāṃ saṃāne śrīmānakīrtimahopādhyānaṃ śiṣya paṃ. śrīdevakalaśamunipaṇḍitapravara (15) /// śiṣya vinayasāgaramunilibhir likhitaṃ || śrīdillīnagaramadhye || śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ (fol. 31v13–15)
notes: This is a Jain (Śvetāmbara, apparently Kharatara) colophon written in Delhi, not a Nepalese one. Era: 'saṃvat' in a western Jain colophon is normally Vikrama, so VS 1616 = 1559 CE. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1616 ?' is probably wrong, and the weekday has not been verified. The gaccha name is corrupt (†vṛ(14) varatadagacchebha 0†), and 'bṛhatkharataragaccha' is a conjecture. Caution: the best-known Kharatara pontiff called Jinaharṣasūri flourished c. VS 1856–1892 (I am recalling this, not checking a source). If that is the man meant, it would fit a date of VS 1916 better than 1616, so the numeral may have been misread. The point needs checking against the photographs. 'saṃāne' should read 'santāne' (lineage), and 'mahopādhyānaṃ' should read 'mahopādhyāyānāṃ'. The '///' before 'śiṣya' marks damage, so there may be intermediate pupils between Devakalaśa and Vinayasāgara. 'munilibhir' is probably a mistake for 'munibhir' or 'muninā'. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Sāgaramuni', but the colophon reads Vinayasāgara(muni).

p1: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. 'santāne' (written saṃāne) means 'in the lineage of', so he is the head of the lineage, not the direct teacher
p2→p1 relation changed from pupil_of to other (lineage, santāne)
p3: titles reduced to paṇḍita and muni (paṃ. = paṇḍita; paṇḍitapravara is an epithet)
p4: confidence lowered to medium and p4→p3 relation flagged, because the lacuna (///) before 'śiṣya' may hide one or more intermediate names

Notes expanded

Kṛṣṇa Jośī's confidence lowered to low: the closing note's function (owner, reader or later hand) is unclear.
Notes expanded: the obscure 'vāgaśītikhyāti', the cross-check of both eras, and 'heramba' as possibly a name rather than an invocation.

subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: = Sunday 23 Dec 1674, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti hastamuktāvalīsārasamudhṛtikāyāṃ śrīghanaśyāmaviracitāyāṃ samāptoyaṃ hastaprakaraṇaḥ || || śrīr astu || (1)vānanandaparvvatavarṣe(!) cāgrahāminikhau vihite ca | dvādaśī lalita mecakapakṣe,pūrṇṇatāṃ samanayet sadanantaḥ || || nepāla samvat 795 (2)agrahaṇa vadi dvādaśī ādityavāra, saṃpūrṇna coyādina || śubham || || (fol. 262v6–264r2) iti hastamuktḷāvalīsārasamuddhṛtāyām śrīghanaśyāmacviracitāyāṃ patrāṅkoyaṃ samāptaḥ || e || (fol. 269v6)
notes: The chronogram bāṇa-nanda-parvata (5-9-7, read right to left) gives 795, which matches NS 795 (about December 1674 CE). The chronogram verse is corrupt ('cāgrahāminikhau', 'lalita'), but it clearly refers to Agrahāyaṇa, the dark fortnight (mecakapakṣa) and the 12th tithi. 'sadanantaḥ' ('may the good Ananta bring it to completion') is a benediction to a deity, not a scribe's name, so the colophon names no scribe. The catalogue's king Jagajjyoti Malla is not mentioned in the colophon, and his reign (c. NS 733–757) is decades before NS 795. The attribution is probably a catalogue error, so no reigning king is recorded.
review: Removed p2 'Sadananta': in 'pūrṇṇatāṃ samanayet sadanantaḥ' the optative makes it a benediction ('may the good Ananta [Viṣṇu] bring it to completion'). It is a deity, not a scribe.
Verified the chronogram: bāṇa (5), nanda (9), parvata (7) read right to left give 795, which agrees with 'nepāla samvat 795'. mecakapakṣa means the dark fortnight and agrees with 'vadi'.
Expanded the notes: why the catalogue king is wrong, and that the date is consistent.

title: Nītisaṃgraha
subject: Nītiśāstra
date_note: = Sunday 21 Oct 1629, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti mahārājādhirāja śrīśrījagajjyotirmmalladevaviracito nītisaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ || || samvat 750 kārttikaśukla paṃcamyāṃ tithau, muraṇakṣatra (!) śubhajoga, āditya vārasa, dvija śrīdhanarāja devaṇa, likhitam saṃpūrṇṇaṃ, || śubhamastu || sadā sarvvadā, || idaṃ pustakaṃ svapāṭhārthaṃ likhitaṃ || nepālavatsare jāte vyomakhādahayāmite kārtikasya site pakṣe paṃcamyām ca tithau dine mūle vā śubhamyoje ca ravivāreṇa saṃyute vipraśrīdhanarājena likhyate nītisaṃgrahaḥ || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 44v3–45r1)
notes:
The prose date is NS 750 Kārttika śukla 5, a Sunday, with nakṣatra mūla. That corresponds to about Oct/Nov 1629 CE, because Kārttika śukla opens the NS year.

The verse chronogram 'vyomakhādahayāmite' seems corrupt. Reading vyoma = 0, kha = 0, haya = 7 from right to left gives 700, and '-āda-' has no clear numerical value. So it matches neither 750 nor the catalogue's '760'. The catalogue's '750 pauṣaśukla 15' also does not appear in the quoted colophon and may come from another part of the manuscript or be an error.

The scribe's name is 'dhanarāja devaṇa' in the prose and 'dhanarājena' in the verse. 'deva' may be part of the name (the catalogue gives Dhanarājadeva) or an honorific, followed by the Newari agentive -ṇa.

Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur, the author, ruled in about NS 734–757, so this copy was probably made during his reign. However, the colophon does not name him as the reigning king.
review: p1 Jagajjyotirmalladeva: removed role 'king'. He is named only as author of the Nītisaṃgraha ('-viracito'), and the colophon has no reign formula for this copy. NS 750 does fall within his Bhaktapur reign (c. NS 734–757), which is now recorded in notes.

p2: name changed from 'Dhanarājadeva' to 'Dhanarāja'. 'devaṇa' looks like deva + Newari agentive -ṇa, and the verse gives only 'vipraśrīdhanarājena'. The -deva form is kept as a possible variant in notes. Confidence lowered to medium for the name form; roles scribe + owner unchanged (svapāṭhārtham).
Date: ce_approx changed from 1630 to 1629. Kārttika śukla 5 falls at the very start of NS 750, about Oct/Nov 1629 CE.
Date: nakshatra written as mūla in standard form.
Notes rewritten: the chronogram 'vyomakhādahayāmite' as transmitted gives 0-0-7, read right to left = 700, which matches neither 750 nor the catalogue's 760. The prose figure 750 is preferred.

'paṃcasdaśakam' is a corrupt form of pañcadaśakam. The quoted colophon names no scribe, owner, king, date or place. The catalogue's King field (Jagajjyotimalla) is probably there because he is thought to have composed or patronised the songs (Jagajjyotimalla of Bhaktapur, who wrote Newari songs). subject: Rāmāyaṇa

date_note: = Monday 16 Jan 1775, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: || iti śrīmad adhyātmarāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde uttarakāṇḍe navamaḥ sargāḥ || 9 || || ❖ || || ❁ || || ❁ || uttarakāṃḍa samāptaṃ || adhyātmottara kāṇḍe ------------ tvārthataḥ || || śubham || graṃtha saṃkhyā 4200 (fol. 228v2-6 ) || iti śrīmatsakala rāja vipaduddharaṇa samarthetyādi virudāvalī virājamāna himmativarmaṇaḥ putrasya śrī rāma varmaṇa kṛtāvadhyātma rāmāyaṇe setau uttarakāṇḍe navamodhyāyaḥ || 9 || || samāptacāyamadhyāya rāmāyaṇa ṭīkā || || nepālena vanaṃ danaṃ damilite pauṣesite pūrṇimā nakṣatre ca punarvasu vudha dine yoge tathā eiṃdrake || śrī viprottamarājako haladharohyatyātma rāmāyaṇaḥ ṭīkā pustaka lekhitaṃ śubhadine śrīrāmasu prītaye || || śubham || || (fol. 228v1,7-8)
purpose: for the pleasure of Śrī Rāma (śrīrāmasuprītaye)
notes: The catalogue lists Śrīrāma Varmā as the scribe. The colophon shows he is the commentator: he wrote the Setu commentary and is the son of Himmativarman. He is not the copyist. Haladhara had the copy made ('lekhitaṃ', causative). It is possible he also wrote it himself, but the colophon does not say so. 'viprottamarājako' is unclear. It could be viprottama ('excellent brahmin') plus a word ending in -rājaka (a surname or place?), or a corruption. The year chronogram is corrupt. It might read 'nepāle bāṇa-nanda-danti-milite', i.e. 5, 9, 8 read right to left, giving NS 895 ≈ 1775 CE. This reading is tentative and has not been checked against the weekday or nakṣatra. A full moon in Pauṣa normally falls in Puṣya, not Punarvasu. 'adhyātmottara kāṇḍe ------------ tvārthataḥ' is a lacuna in the cataloguer's transcription.
review: Haladhara: removed 'scribe'. 'lekhitaṃ' (causative participle, 'caused to be written') supports only 'commissioner'. Confidence lowered to medium because 'viprottamarājako' is unclear. Title normalised to 'vipra' (with 'viprottama' kept as written).

Date: proposed reading of the corrupt chronogram 'vanaṃ danaṃ damilite' as bāṇa(5)-nanda(9)-danti(8) → NS 895, giving ce_approx 1775 (tentative; the year field shows it as a reading, not a certainty).
Purpose normalised to 'for the pleasure of Śrī Rāma (śrīrāmasuprītaye)'.
Notes updated: the earlier 'NS 99x' guess is replaced and the uncertainties are listed.

subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Sunday 24 Jul 1853, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmad adhyātmarāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde uttarakaṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ || 9 || rāmāyaṇa mahākāvyaṃ likhitaṃ pustakaṃ śubhaṃ śrāvaṇokṛṣṇapakṣevai pūrṇajātaṃ śubhapradaṃ || 1 || (fol. 62r6–8) iti śrīmatsakalarājyavipaduddharaṇa samarpyetyāde virudāvalī virājamānasya himativarmaṇaḥ putrasya śrīrāmavarmaṇaḥ kṛtāvadhyātmarāmāyaṇasetau uttarakaṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ || 9 || saṃvat || 18 9 ||(!) śāke || 17 || 75 || rattākṣanāma || ā. | tṛ. | (fol. 62r2–10)
notes: The colophon has two eras. The VS figure '18 9' is corrupt; it is probably VS 1910, which equals ŚS 1775 and 1853 CE, so the two eras agree. The saṃvatsara is 'rattākṣa' = Raktākṣa/Raktākṣī. In the southern 60-year cycle, Raktākṣī falls in ŚS 1786 (1864/65), not ŚS 1775, so either the year or the cycle name is doubtful. 'ā. tṛ.' is read as Ādityavāra and tṛtīyā, but this is uncertain: 'ā.' could also abbreviate a month. The month and fortnight (śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa) come from the verse after the mūla colophon. Rāmavarman, son of Himativarman (possibly Himmatavarman), wrote the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa-setu commentary. His birudāvalī suggests he was of royal or noble rank. He is not the reigning king of this copy. The catalogue's 'Scribe' field gives the ṭīkākāra. No scribe is named in the colophon.
review: Date: tithi/weekday from 'ā. | tṛ.' kept as tṛtīyā / Ādityavāra, but flagged as uncertain. 'ā.' could also abbreviate a month (Āṣāḍha/Āśvina).
Date: the month śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa comes from the verse after the mūla colophon ('śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapakṣe'), not from the dated line.
Notes: the corrupt 'saṃvat 18 9' is explained as probably VS 1910, which agrees with ŚS 1775 (= 1853 CE). The two eras do not conflict.
Notes: the Raktākṣa saṃvatsara does not obviously fit ŚS 1775 in the southern 60-year cycle (Raktākṣī falls in ŚS 1786 = 1864/65). This is flagged.
Notes: the catalogue's 'Scribe' field actually names the ṭīkākāra (Rāmavarman). No scribe is named. Himativarman may stand for Himmatavarman.

title: Kavikalpalatā
subject: *Sāhitya
date_note: = Tuesday 10 Oct 1662, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti kavikalpalatā samāptā || || śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ || || (3)❖ varṣe bhujebhaturage (dharaṇīja) vāre, ‥ ‥ stithāvi(ti ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ’ryamarthkṣe | śrī‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ 'sya ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ (4)‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ likhata śivahariḥ kavi[[ka]]lpavallīṃ || saṃvat 782 āśvinamāse (5) kṛṣṇapakṣe caturddaśyāṃ tithau aṃgā[[ra]] vāsare uttaraphālguṇinakṣatre brahmayoge sampūrṇ〈ṇ〉aṃ likhitaṃ (6) kavikalpalatāpustakaṃ †yaśalache† śrīśivaharivipreṇa svapāṭhārthaṃ || śubham astu sarvvadaiva || || (fol. 90r2–6)
notes: The chronogram 'bhujebhaturage' (bhuja = 2, ibha = 8, turaga = 7) confirms NS 782, and dharaṇījavāra matches aṅgāravāsara (Tuesday). The phrase '†yaśalache†' is likely a tole (locality) name where Śivahari resided or copied the text. A heavily damaged name preceded by 'śrī... sya' in line 3 may have referred to a reigning monarch or patron, but it is too broken to identify.

colophon: iti śri bhānudatta miśra viracitā rasamaṃjarī samāptā śrīrāmovijayate tarāma śubhaṃ (fol. 54r8 ) tāta śrī harivaṃśa bhaṭṭaika caraṇaśaraṇa gopāla bhṭṭakṛtā rasika raṃjanī ṭīkā samāptā śubhamastu leṣaka pāṭhayo(!) netrāṃkabhūpa pramite śāke māghe gurau dvikegatyā(!) śrīnagarabhye likhatsvayama 1693 śubhaṃ likhitā viṣṇu vallabhena śubham (fol. 54r8-10 )
notes: The chronogram 'netrāṅkabhūpa' read right to left gives bhūpa 16, aṅka 9, netra 2, i.e. Śaka 1692. The figure written in the colophon is 1693. The text says 'śāke', so the era is taken as ŚS, even though the catalogue just has 'Saṃ. 1693(!)'. If it were VS, the date would be 1636 CE. ŚS 1693 + 78 = 1771, but Māgha falls in January–February, so Māgha of Śaka 1693 is early 1772 CE. If the chronogram's 1692 is right, it is early 1771 CE. 'dvikegatyā(!)' is corrupt. It probably hides the 2nd tithi ('dvitīyāyāṃ'?), but this is uncertain, and the pakṣa is not stated. 'śrīnagarabhye' is probably 'śrīnagarākhye' or '-madhye'. Which Śrīnagara is meant (Garhwal, Kashmir, etc.) is not certain. 'leṣaka pāṭhayo(!)' is the stock blessing 'lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ śubham' and names no one. 'likhat svayam' just means the scribe wrote it himself.

Cleared purpose: 'likhat svayam' says the scribe wrote it himself, not that he wrote it for himself. No svārtha or owner role is stated.
Emptied place.normalized: 'Śrīnagara' could be Srinagar in Garhwal, Srinagar in Kashmir or another place, so the identification is not certain.
Lowered confidence for tithi 2 (read from corrupt 'dvikegatyā') and explained it in notes.
Expanded notes on the chronogram (1692) vs the figure (1693), the CE conversion for Māgha, and the 'leṣaka pāṭhayo' formula.

title: Kavikarpaṭīracanā

notes: 'śaṃkūdhara' is very likely a corruption of Śaṅkhadhara (kavirāja Śaṅkhadhara, author of the Laṭakamelaka, to whom the Kavikarpaṭī is attributed). The title is also corrupt: 'kavikarpaṭikaracanā' should be Kavikarpaṭīracanā. The scribe Rāmacandra is described as 'tāropākhya', meaning surnamed or called Tāra; the catalogue gives 'tārā'. 'mahāmati' is an epithet. The catalogue lists King Rājendravikrama Śāha (r. 1816–1847 CE), but he is not named in the quoted colophon, and the colophon has no date. If the catalogue is right, the manuscript would date to c. 1816–1847 CE. This is not verified from the colophon.
review: Author name normalized from the corrupt 'Śaṅkūdhara' to Śaṅkhadhara, the known author of the Kavikarpaṭī (and of the Laṭakamelaka); confidence lowered to medium; 'kavirāja' kept as title.
Noted that 'tāropākhya' means 'surnamed/called Tāra' and that 'mahāmati' is a laudatory epithet, not a title.

title: Daśakumāracarita

date_note: ≈ 1863 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti daśakumārakathābhāsāyāṃ viśrutacaritan nāma āryāvatīrya gorakṣavālī bhāsā aṣṭamochvāsaḥ saṃpūrṇam śrī śāke 1758 sāl 1893 māse 8 tithau balācaturdaśī maṃtrīpāṭḥārtham śubham (fol. 135r1–2)
purpose: maṃtrīpāṭḥārtham: for reading by a (unnamed) minister
notes: The colophon names no scribe, commissioner, owner or king. The copy was made for an unnamed minister to read ('maṃtrīpāṭḥārtham'). The text is a Gorkhali (Nepali) rendering ('gorakṣavālī bhāsā') of the Daśakumāracarita, and this is the end of the 8th ucchvāsa. Two eras are given and they agree: Śaka 1758 and VS ('sāl') 1893 both give CE 1836. The catalogue field 'ŚS 1785' does not match the colophon's 'śāke 1758' and is probably a digit transposition; its 'VS 1893' is correct. 'māse 8' probably means the 8th month counted from Vaiśākha, i.e. Mārgaśīrṣa/Mangsir. That is the month of Bālācaturdaśī (kṛṣṇa 14), which would put the date around late 1836 CE.
review: Persons/relations confirmed empty: the 'mantrī' for whose reading the copy was made is not named, so no person record.
Date confirmed: Śaka 1758 + 78 = 1836 and VS 1893 − 57 = 1836, so the two eras agree.
Notes: added that the catalogue field 'ŚS 1785' does not match the colophon's 'śāke 1758'. The catalogue figure is probably a digit transposition.
Notes: Bālācaturdaśī is kṛṣṇa caturdaśī of Mārgaśīrṣa (Mangsir), which fits 'māse 8' if the months are counted from Vaiśākha. The paksa field is left empty because the colophon does not state it.

date_note: = Wednesday 3 Nov 1677, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrikirātārjunīye mahākāvye bhāravikṛtau varapradāno nāmāṣṭādaśaḥ sargaḥ || || || || || śrīḥ || || śrīrāmacaṃdrāya namaḥ || || || śrīḥ || || śrīḥ || || saṃvatsaptadaśottaracatustriṃśattame varṣe prabhavanāmni saṃvatsare kārtike māsi sitepakṣe navamyāṃ budhavāsare vyāsa śrīmadhusūdanasūnūnā vyāsodaya kṛṣṇenālekhi kirātākhyaṃ pustakamadaḥ || || śrīḥ || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || || śrīviśveśovijatetarāṃ || || śrīḥ || || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ (fol. 91r1–5)
notes: The phrase 'saptadaśottaracatustriṃśattame' means 1734 (17 hundreds + 34). The catalogue's 'SAM (ŚS) 1754' looks like a misreading or typo. ŚS 1754 (1832 CE) would not be a Prabhava year in either cycle. 'Saṃvat' with Prabhava fits VS 1734 = 1677 CE: in the northern Bārhaspatya reckoning 1677 was Prabhava (the southern-cycle Prabhava was 1687). Kārttika śukla 9 falls on about 24 Oct 1677 Julian (= 3 Nov 1677 Gregorian), which was a Wednesday. That matches budhavāsara, and the moon was about 8 days past new moon. Scribe name: 'vyāsodaya kṛṣṇena' is read as Vyāsa Udayakṛṣṇa, son of Vyāsa Madhusūdana. The catalogue's 'Kṛṣṇavyāsa' takes only the second element, so 'udaya' might not be part of the name. 'sūnūnā' should be sūnunā. The invocation 'śrīviśveśo vijayatetarām' may point to a Vārāṇasī (Viśveśvara) milieu, but no place of copying is stated.
review: Lowered p3 (scribe) confidence from high to medium: 'vyāsodaya kṛṣṇena' could be read either as Vyāsa Udayakṛṣṇa or as Kṛṣṇa (the catalogue gives Kṛṣṇavyāsa). Udayakṛṣṇa is kept as the preferred reading.
Lowered p2 confidence to medium because the case form 'sūnūnā' is corrupt (for sūnunā).
Added a check of the samvatsara: Prabhava matches VS 1734 = 1677 CE in the northern (Bārhaspatya) reckoning.
Specified that 24 Oct 1677 is a Julian date (= 3 Nov 1677 Gregorian). Moon-phase and weekday checks agree with śukla 9 and Wednesday.

title: Meghadūta
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Sunday 26 Aug 1601, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti (8) śrīmahākavikāladāsakṛtīviracitaṃ(!) meghadūtā〈〈mi〉〉bhidhānaṃ mahākāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || ❁ || itthaṃbhūtaṃ sucarita(9)m idaṃ meghadūtaṃ ca nāmnā kāmakrīḍāvirahitajane viprayukte vinodaḥ | meghaś (!) cāsmin atinipuṇatā buddhibhāvaḥ ka(10)vīnāṃ natvāryāyāś caraṇayugalaṃ kālidāsaś cakāra 126 || ❁ || ity ākhyāte surapatisakhaḥ śailakulyāpurīṣu sthitvā (11) sthitvā dhanapatipurīṃ vāsaraiḥ kaiścid āpa matvāgāreṃ kanakaruciraṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ pūrvam ukataiḥ (!) tasyotsaṃge kṣititalagatāṃ tāṃ ca (11v1) dīnāṃ dadarśa || ❁ tasmād adrer nigaditapathā śīghram etyālakāyāṃ yakṣāgāraṃ galitavibhavaṃ dṛṣṭacihnair viditvā (2) yat saṃdiṣṭaṃ praṇayamadhuraṃ guhyakena prayatnāt tadgehinyāḥ sakalam avadat kāmarūpī payodaḥ || 28 || iti śrīmegha(3)dūtakāvyaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || saṃvat 1658 bhādrapadabahula14dine śrīnāga(purīyatapāgache bha,) śrīcaṃdrakīrtti(4)sūri(paddebha)śrīmān kīrttisūripahacchaiḥ śrīharṣakīrttisūrir (mallekhitaḥ) || samarasiṃhapaṭhanārthaṃ || (fol. 11r7-11v4)
notes: This is a Jain (Śvetāmbara) colophon from western India, not a Nepalese one: it names the Nāgapurīya Tapāgaccha. The era is therefore read as Vikrama, giving VS 1658 = c. 1601 CE. The lineage passage is garbled. Probable reading: 'śrīnāgapurīyatapāgacche bha° śrīcandrakīrtisūripaṭṭe bha° śrīmānakīrtisūri...', which would name a Mānakīrti between Candrakīrti and Harṣakīrti. On that reading, 'pahacchaiḥ' (unclear) may hide śiṣyaiḥ or a similar word, and Harṣakīrti could be the pupil of Mānakīrti rather than directly of Candrakīrti. Elsewhere Harṣakīrtisūri is known as a disciple of Candrakīrtisūri of this gaccha, so the pupil_of link to Candrakīrti is kept. '(mallekhitaḥ)' is the cataloguer's uncertain reading, probably for mayā likhitaḥ. 'Nāgapurīya' names the gaccha, not the place of copying.
review: p3 Harṣakīrti: removed 'commissioner'; '(mallekhitaḥ)' (prob. for mayā likhitaḥ / lekhitaḥ) marks him as the writer only, and nothing says he had the copy made.
Added p5 Mānakīrti (low confidence): read 'bha° śrīmān kīrttisūri' as bhaṭṭāraka Śrī-Mānakīrtisūri, named in the lineage after Candrakīrti's paṭṭa ('(paddebha)' = paṭṭe bha[ṭṭāraka]).
p2 Candrakīrti: titles expanded to include bhaṭṭāraka (abbreviated bha in the colophon).
Relation p3→p2 kept as pupil_of but the evidence is narrowed. Added a low-confidence 'other' relation p5→p2 (successor in the paṭṭa).
p4 Samarasiṃha: kept beneficiary + reader, since paṭhanārthaṃ explicitly states the copy is for his reading.
Purpose shortened. Notes rewritten to give the probable restoration of the lineage passage.

notes: The quoted text is the closing rubric of the work. It names Raṇajitmalla of Bhaktapur as the author and his father Bhūpatīndramalla. It names no scribe, patron or date for this copy. The catalogue gives the copying date as NS 886 (c. 1766 CE), but this date is not in the quoted colophon. The catalogue's King field, Bhūpatīndramalla, looks wrong. He ruled c. NS 816–842 (1696–1722 CE) and appears here only as the author's father. If NS 886 is right, the reigning king would be Raṇajitmalla himself (r. 1722–1769). He is not recorded as king of this copy because the colophon does not say so. The scribe wrote 'samāmāpti' (marked '!') for 'samāpti'.
review: Persons, roles, relations and the empty date are confirmed. Only the notes were expanded, to cover the catalogue's King field and the catalogue date.

title: Kautukacintāmaṇi
subject: Tantrā-yurveda
date_note: = Sunday 8 May 1808, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti śrīmahāerājādhirājapratāparūdradeva gajapatipādāravindaṣaṭpadāyammānasenasakalavidvajjanacaraṇa(9)sampāditaprajñāvibhavena caturacārarika (!) śvetanāgabhāyābhāṇḍāradhūrttakarttavividhavirūḍhavidhitena viśveśva(10)ramahāprasādisutena kadambeśvarāddhanyāsyānamahāprasādena sunṛtavādināviracite kautukacintāma(1) ṇīgraṃthe kautukanirūpanaṃ (!) nāma tṛtīyādīptiḥ samāptaṃ śubham astu || || śrīvikramādityasaṃvat 1865 sāla (2)vaiśāṣa śukla 13 ravivāsare liṣitaṃ kṛṣṇānanda sarmanaḥ (!) || kāṣṭhamaṃḍapasthāne || śubham || || || || (fol.59v8–11:60r1–2)
notes: The first part of the colophon (iti ... tṛtīyā dīptiḥ) is the author's own closing statement. It names Gajapati Pratāparudradeva of Orissa (16th century) as the author's patron. The work is often attributed to that king himself. Here it is written by a court servant, son of Viśveśvara. The servant calls himself 'sunṛtavādin' ('speaker of truth'), which is probably an epithet. The servant's name is corrupt. 'kadambeśvarāddhanyāsyāna' may hide a place or temple name ('Kadambeśvara') plus a name, so treat the name as uncertain. 'mahāprasādi/mahāprasāda' probably stands for mahāpātra. Pratāparudradeva is not the reigning king of this copy: the catalogue's King field takes him from the author's statement. The scribe's own colophon names no ruler. The copy was made by Kṛṣṇānanda Śarman at Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa (Kathmandu) in VS 1865 (c. 1808 CE), Vaiśākha śukla 13, on a Sunday. The weekday has not been checked.
review: p2 Pratāparudradeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He is the Gajapati of Orissa who sponsored the original work (the author calls himself a bee at his lotus feet). He is not the reigning king of this VS 1865 Kathmandu copy, so the catalogue's King field is misleading.
p1 Kṛṣṇānanda: residence cleared. Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa is given only as the place of copying.
p3 and p4: confidence lowered. 'mahāprasādi/mahāprasāda' is probably a corruption of the Orissan office title mahāpātra. The author's personal name is uncertain.
Weekday normalized to ravivāra (Sunday).
Notes expanded.

title: Golādeśa
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Wednesday 6 Sep 1826, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti dāmo(22)darīye golādeśe kālanirddeśo daśamaḥ || || nakhapurusūraghana 1748 śāke nabhasyeśajanya ho golādeśaṃ lālaratnākaro ʼlikha drameṭpure || 1 || || śrīśo ʼvatu lekhakaṃ paṭhantam || (fol. 20r21–22)
notes: The colophon gives the year 1748 in figures, Śaka era, which is 1826 CE (Bhādrapada falls in Aug–Sep 1826). The word-numeral chronogram 'nakhapurusūraghana' is corrupt or unusual and could not be checked digit by digit. 'nabhasyeśajanya ho' is read as 'on the day of Īśa's son (Gaṇeśa) in Nabhasya', which most likely means Bhādrapada śukla 4 (Gaṇeśa-caturthī). This is tentative. 'ʼlikha drameṭpure' should be divided as (a)likhad + rameṭpure, so the place is Rameṭpura. The name looks corrupt. The catalogue's suggestion of Umeśapura = Kāśī is speculative, so the place is left unnormalized. The scribe's name appears as 'lālaratnākara' and the catalogue gives 'Ratnākaralāla'. Lāla is probably a name suffix of the Kāyastha type, so the person may be catalogued as Ratnākaralāla. 'śrīśo ʼvatu lekhakaṃ paṭhantam' is a blessing formula and names no other person.
review: Scribe: name given as 'Ratnākara' with 'lāla' kept in titles, instead of 'Lālaratnākara' plus a duplicated title. The catalogue's 'Ratnākaralāla' is the same person with the parts reversed (lāla is put first in the verse).
Scribe: residence removed. Rameṭpura is where the copy was made, not a stated residence.
Date: tithi added as a tentative reading. 'īśajanya' (Gaṇeśa) probably points to Gaṇeśa-caturthī, Bhādrapada śukla 4. The chronogram could not be fully checked.
Notes: the sandhi of 'ʼlikha drameṭpure' is explained, and the Umeśapura/Kāśī idea is marked as the cataloguer's guess.

colophon: iti vācaspatīśiramasūnu lakṣmīdāsaviracite bhāskarīyasiddhāṃtaśiromaṇivyākhyāne gaṇitatattvaciṃtāmaṇau pātādhikāraḥ samāptaḥ || || samāptoyaṃ graṃthaḥ || saṃkhyā 7500 || || varṣe paṃcāgnivasv iṃdu mitaharidine kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣe vāre sūryasya sāṃghrir jayaharinagare gomatītīravāsī || jñātau śrīpārvatī yaḥ śukatanayavaraḥ śaṃkaro bhāskarīya ṭīkāṃ tattvākhya ciṃtāmaṇim iyam alikhat svārthaputrārthasiddhayai || 1 || śrīr astu || śubhāni bhavaṃtu sarvajatām || putakam idaṃ śrīkṛṣṇajośī rāmanagaravāle (fol. 175r10–14)
notes: The chronogram pañca(5)-agni(3)-vasu(8)-indu(1), read right to left, gives 1835. The colophon does not name the era. VS (= 1778 CE) comes from the catalogue and is plausible for a copy made on the Gomatī. If the era were ŚS, the date would be 1913 CE. The weekday has not been checked. 'vācaspatīśirama' is a corruption of Vācaspatimiśra, the father of the commentator Lakṣmīdāsa. 'sāṃghrir' after 'vāre sūryasya' is unclear: it may be a corruption, perhaps 'sāṃdhri'/'saṃdhyā'. I have not treated it as a name. 'jñātau śrīpārvatī yaḥ' = 'jñātau śrīpārvatīyaḥ' (of the Pārvatīya community). The scribe's unnamed son is a beneficiary. 'putakam idaṃ śrīkṛṣṇajośī rāmanagaravāle' (= pustakam) is an ownership note, probably later and in Hindi ('vāle'). The catalogue lists Kṛṣṇa Jośī as 'Donor', but the colophon only shows ownership.

p5 Kṛṣṇa: kept as owner; the colophon does not support the catalogue's 'donor'; noted that this is probably a later ownership entry

title: Narapatijayacaryāṭīkā
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Saturday 22 Oct 1689, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ❖ śrīśrīsumatijayajitāmitramalladevasana, thva pustaka dayakā || bhāgirāmaparamānayā velasa || samvat 810 kārttika sudi 9 || śubha || (fol. 145v6)
purpose: "Made at the order of King Jitāmitramalla"
notes: The colophon reads 'thva pustaka dayakā', meaning the king had this book made, so he is the commissioner. Bhāgirāma is named only to date the copy, as paramāna (minister) 'in whose time' it was made. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's 'Scribe: Bhāgīrāma' is a misreading, and the scribe is not named. The colophon spells the name Bhāgirāma (short i), while the catalogue has Bhāgīrāma. The place of copying is not stated. Sumatijayajitāmitramalla was king of Bhaktapur, so Bhaktapur is likely but has not been entered. NS 810 Kārttika śukla 9 is about Oct/Nov 1689 CE.
review: p2 Bhāgirāma: role changed from 'governor' to 'minister'. In Malla-period Newari colophons, paramāna/pramāna (= pradhāna/pramāṇa) is the chief minister or noble office. The phrase 'X-yā velasa' (in the time of X) is the usual formula for naming a minister.
Relation p2→p1 changed from under_reign_of to servant_of, since a minister serves the king.
ce_approx changed from 1690 to 1689. NS 810 begins in Kārttika 1689 CE, so Kārttika śukla 9 falls in about Oct/Nov 1689.
Notes expanded: the catalogue's 'Scribe: Bhāgīrāma' is wrong, and the scribe is not named. The place is not stated, though the king reigned at Bhaktapur.

title: Narapatijaycaryā
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: ≈ 1773 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: || iti narapatijayacaryayā vramhayāmalīyasvarodaya grahabhaktiḥ samāptaḥ || || yādṛśaṃ . . . . . . . . nadiyate || || śrīśākavāṇanidhi ṣaḍvidhugelileṣa śrīrājasūnu śivadeva . . . . . ja sudhimān || somena yukta śubhavāruṇabhenavabhyāṃ krodhisamvatsara svarodayapustakaṃ ca || || (fol. 66r3–5)
notes: The chronogram vāṇa (5), nidhi (9), ṣaḍ (6), vidhu (1) is read right to left, giving Śaka 1695, i.e. about 1773/74 CE. This matches the catalogue field. 'gelileṣa' is probably 'ge lilekha', with ṣa written for kha ('wrote'). The samvatsara is given as 'krodhi(n)'. In the southern 60-year cycle Śaka 1695 is Vijaya, and Krodhin falls in Śaka 1706 (1784/85 CE). This may be a mismatch, or the scribe used a different reckoning of the cycle. The colophon has lacunae in the scribal verse ('yādṛśaṃ ... ') and after 'śivadeva' ('. . . . . ja sudhimān'). 'rājasūnu' may mean 'prince' or may be part of a patronymic. The month and pakṣa are not stated. The final clause 'svarodayapustakaṃ ca' has no verb that survives.
review: Śivadeva confidence lowered from high to medium: a lacuna follows the name ('śivadeva . . . . . ja sudhimān'). The gap may have held more of the name, e.g. dvija, or a patronymic, and 'rājasūnu' could mean 'son of Rāja-…' as well as 'prince'.
Evidence string changed to the name phrase plus the verb reading.
Notes: added that the samvatsara name may not match the year, and recorded the lacunae.

title: Śakunāvalī
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Feb 1694, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti daprakaraṇaṃ caturthaḥ samāptaḥ || || ❖ ❖ || || śubhaṃ saṃvaṃt 1750 samaye phālguṇa śake (1) vadi 8 aṣṭamī budhavāsare revāgrāme || likhitaṃ chaṃdogakṛṣṇadīkṣite(2)na svārthaṃ paramārthaṃ ca || ❖ || śubham astu || śrīr astu || || bhavānī || (3) yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || yadi śuddhamaśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo (4) na dīyate || ❁ ❁ ||❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ (fol. 14v6–15r4)
purpose: svārthaṃ paramārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: Era conflict: the colophon gives the year 1750 explicitly as 'saṃvaṃt', which in a North Indian Devanagari colophon normally means Vikrama → c. 1694 CE (Phālguna VS 1750 ≈ Feb/Mar 1694). The word 'śake' follows the month with no number before the line break. It looks like an unfilled or broken Śaka slot (Phālguna śake might be meant as 'Phālguna in the Śaka year', i.e. Śaka 1615). The catalogue's 'ŚS 1750' (c. 1828 CE) looks like it applies the Śaka label to the saṃvat number. I have not checked the weekday (Wednesday, kṛṣṇa 8) against either year. Doing so would settle VS 1750 vs ŚS 1750. 'Chandoga' marks the scribe as a Sāmavedin. Revāgrāma is not identified (possibly a village on the Revā/Narmadā). The final verse 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā...' is a standard scribal formula. 'bhavānī' is an invocation, not a person.
review: Era set to VS: the colophon gives the year as 'saṃvaṃt 1750'. 'śake' has no number after it, so it is an unfilled or broken Śaka slot, not a second year. ce_approx = 1694. This conflicts with the catalogue's ŚS 1750 (c. 1828), which is recorded in notes.
Removed residence 'Revāgrāma' from p1. The colophon names Revāgrāma only as the place of copying, not where the scribe lives.
Moved 'chandoga' (Sāmavedin school designation) from titles to affiliation; 'dīkṣita' stays in titles.
Weekday normalised to 'budhavāsara (Wednesday)'; paksa given as 'kṛṣṇa (vadi)'.
Changed purpose to read 'for himself and for others'. Both phrases are kept in purpose.

notes: The two eras agree: VS 1900 − 57 = 1843 and ŚS 1765 + 78 = 1843. Pauṣa śukla 8 falls about late December 1843 CE. 'utprabhātīpayonāmaka (!)' is corrupt. It may be a garbled 'upretī-pada-nāmaka', meaning 'bearing the surname Upretī', which would make Durgādatta an Upretī Brahmin. This reading is tentative, so the name is not added to titles. 'idaṃ pustam' (for pustakam) begins an ownership statement but names no owner; possibly text is missing. The title in the colophon reads 'pallīpatanaśaraṭātohaṇa' (for -śaraṭārohaṇa, 'falling of the lizard and climbing of the chameleon'); the catalogue title is a corrupt form of this.

colophon: iti mihiraśrīvarāhaviracitāyāṃ vyakṣeśvamidhīyayātrāyāṃ paradrulaṃrgrala/// (!) (6) dhyāyaḥ /// || || (fol. *28v5–6) saṃvat 1561 sārṣe āṣāḍha vadi 10 śukravāsare || || śrīkaroenagare ṇṭhanagare darikhānadaṃ (!) bhujyamāne || || satpaṃḍita śrībahrorana ātmapāṭhanārthe pustaka liṣāpitaṃ (!) || kāyasṭha śrīvāstavya paṃḍi/// nīdharasutaḥ bhāgīrathī lekhi || || śubham astu || || ❁ || || ❁ || || ❁ || || ❁ || || || subham astu || mālūra kiṃ ... (fol. 27v1–4)
purpose: commissioned by Bahrorana for his own study (ātmapāṭhanārthe)
notes: The manuscript is North Indian, not Nepalese: it was copied by a Śrīvāstava Kāyastha under a Muslim governor. Because of this, plain 'saṃvat' is taken as VS (1561 − 57 = c. 1504 CE). 'sārṣe' is unclear; it is possibly a corruption, and it does not affect the era. 'darikhānadaṃ (!) bhujyamāne' most likely means 'while Daryā Khān was ruling/holding [the place]', i.e. a local Lodi-period governor, and the '-daṃ' is probably a corruption. The place reading 'śrīkaroenagare ṇṭhanagare' looks like a corrected dittography; the cataloguer reads it as Śrīkaṇṭhanagara. Śrīkaṇṭha is a traditional name for the Thanesar/Kurukṣetra region, but that identification is uncertain, so normalized is left empty. The father's name is damaged ('paṃḍi/// nīdhara'); it may be Dharaṇīdhara or similar. The catalogue's 'bhāgīrathī' is the scribe's personal name; 'Śrīvāstava' is his Kāyastha subcaste. The commissioner's name 'Bahrorana' is uncertain and may be corrupt.

p3: 'owner' added beside 'commissioner', since he had the copy made 'ātmapāṭhanārthe' (for his own reading)
p5: 'śrīvāstavya' also added to titles as the Kāyastha subcaste
date: month and pakṣa normalised (Āṣāḍha, kṛṣṇa/vadi); VS 1561 = c. 1504 CE confirmed

title: Bṛhajjātaka(caramādhyāyantam)
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Saturday 29 May 1824, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrī varāhamihirakṛtau vṛhajjātake caramādhyāyaḥ || || rasa nigamagahayendu śākakerke hyanaḍuhiśukrasitādirmeke jenhi || trinayana purilālaratna śarmmā likhadidamadhyayanāya bhūsurolam || 1 || || śubhamastu || || śrī viśveśvarāya namaḥ || || || (fol. 19v7-9)
purpose: adhyayanāya (for study, presumably the scribe's own)
notes: The chronogram, read right to left, is rasa 6, nigama 4, haya 7, indu 1, giving ŚS 1746 (about 1824 CE). 'gahaya' is a corruption of 'haya'. I take the corrupt date phrase as 'śākake 'rke hy anaḍuhi śukra-sitādime (?) jñe 'hni': the year in the Śaka era, the sun in Taurus, the month Śukra (= Jyeṣṭha), the first day of the bright fortnight, a Wednesday. The tithi and weekday readings are conjectural; I have not checked them against an ephemeris. Trinayanapurī ('city of the three-eyed one', i.e. Śiva) means Kāśī/Vārāṇasī, which fits the closing invocation to Viśveśvara. It could equally be the scribe's home rather than the place of copying. 'bhūsuro 'lam' marks Lālaratna as a brahmin. The catalogue's scribe field (Lālaratna Śarmā) agrees.
review: Lālaratna: roles changed from scribe+beneficiary to scribe+owner (he copied it 'adhyayanāya', for (his) study; no separate beneficiary)
Date: 'hy anaḍuhi' read as sun in Taurus (Vṛṣa); month 'śukra' = Jyeṣṭha; paksa normalised to śukla; tithi pratipad from 'sitādime' (tentative); weekday Wednesday from 'jñe 'hni' (written 'jenhi')
Purpose corrected: colophon has only 'adhyayanāya'; the 'bhūsurāṇām' in the first reading is not in the text ('bhūsuro 'lam' describes the scribe)
Notes expanded on the corrupt date phrase

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
date_raw: nobhranaya (!) munivarṣe māsasyaśrāvaṇastathā śitapakṣe tṛrodaśī (!) samāptaṃ kuca dinena
colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye puṇḍarīkopākhyānaṃ cāliśodhyāya samāptaṃ || || nobhranaya (!) munivarṣe māsasyaśrāvaṇastathā śitapakṣe tṛrodaśī (!) samāptaṃ kuca dinena || likhita śrīvāṣṭaka (!) kāyasta (!) hedayasiṃhena yadi śuddhaṃmaśuddhaṃmvā sodhanīyāmahatvudhai (!) || (fol. 115r2–4)
notes: The chronogram 'nobhranaya munivarṣe' is best read as nabho (0) + nayana (2) + muni (7). Read right to left, this gives 720. The colophon states no era. NS 720 (c. 1600 CE) is assumed because the manuscript is in Newari script; VS or ŚS 720 would be far too early. 'śrīvāṣṭaka' is a corruption of Śrīvāstavya/Śrīvāstava, a Kāyastha subcaste. 'kuca dina' stands for kujadina, i.e. Tuesday. The scribe's name 'Hedayasiṃha' (as in the catalogue) probably represents Hṛdayasiṃha. The tithi is śukla 13 (śitapakṣe = sitapakṣe). The weekday has not been verified against an ephemeris.
review: Chronogram resolved: 'nobhranaya' read as nabho- (nabhas = 0) + nayana (2), with muni (7); read right to left this gives 720, not the two alternatives the first reading offered
Era set to 'unspecified' because the colophon names no era; NS assumed on palaeographic and historical grounds, giving ce_approx c. 1600
Year field normalized to '720'
Title 'śrīvāstaka' normalized to Śrīvāstavya (the Kāyastha subcaste); note added that Hedayasiṃha probably stands for Hṛdayasiṃha

title: Āyāpraśna
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Saturday 12 Aug 1871, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti āyāpraśnaḥ saṃvat 1871 vṛṣasiṃhavṛścikaghaṭe vṛddhisthānaṃ gamāgamau na staḥ || na mṛtaṃ na cāpi naṣṭaṃ na rogaśāṃtir na cābhibhavaḥ || 1 || tadviparītaṃ tu carair dvisarīrai (!) miśri[[taṃ]] phalaṃ bhavati || lagnendor valtavyaṃ (!) subhāsadṛṣṭyā śobhanam ato [ʼ]nyataḥ || 2 || carasthīradviṣaḥ (!) meṣādyā rāśaya (!) || || iti āyāpraśnaḥ samāptam (!) || śāke 1793 bhādravadi 11 roja 7 śubhaṃ bhūyāt (fol. 9v7-10r6)
notes: The colophon names no persons. The final dating is Śaka 1793 Bhādra vadi 11, roja 7 (Saturday), which is 1871 CE. The 'saṃvat 1871' that comes earlier, inside the text, does not agree with this date if it is read as Vikrama: VS 1871 would be about 1814 CE, while Śaka 1793 is VS 1928. It agrees only if it is read as the Christian year 1871, which is unusual but possible in a late manuscript. Another possibility is that it belongs to an earlier exemplar, or is a stray marginal number that got copied into the text. The catalogue's 'SAM 1871' and 'ŚS 1793' therefore point to the same year only if SAM means CE. I took the Śaka date as authoritative.
review: weekday: 'roja 7' interpreted as Saturday (7th day counting from Sunday); kept the original wording in brackets

notes: added that 'saṃvat 1871' does not agree with Śaka 1793 if read as VS (VS 1871 = c. 1814 CE, whereas Śaka 1793 = VS 1928); it agrees only if read as the CE year. Also noted that it sits oddly inside the text and is placed before the verses, not in the final colophon

title: MuhūrttacintāmaṇI(ṭīkā piyuṣadhārā)
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_raw: śakepuṇa(!) bhrarasemāse ca māghasite || titherekādaśī scavye
colophon: iti śrī vidvadvaivajñayuk(!) murālekāranīkaṃ ṣjyoti(!)vidatputra(!) goviṃda jyotirvīdvaracitājyaṃ(!) muhūrttaciṃtāmaṇI ṭīkāyāṃ pīyūṣadhārābhidhāyāṃ śubhāśubhaprakaraṇaṃ samāptimagāt || || śubhamastu || || śrīḥ || || śakepuṇa(!) bhrarasemāse ca māghasite || titherekādaśī scavye likhitāṃ yugajmavataiḥ || 1 || śubhaṃ || ❖ || (fol. 49r6-8)
notes: The colophon is badly corrupt. The commentator Govinda of the Pīyūṣadhārā (composed ŚS 1525 = 1603 CE) is the son of Nīlakaṇṭha jyotirvid and nephew of Rāma Daivajña, author of the Muhūrtacintāmaṇi. So 'murālekāranīkaṃ ṣjyoti(!)vidatputra' probably garbles '...nīlakaṇṭhajyotirvitputra', not Murāri. The Śaka chronogram 'puṇa(!) bhrarase' may stand for pūrṇa(0)-abhra(0)-rasa(6), which gives 600 when read right to left. A thousands digit seems to be missing; it may be ŚS 1600 = 1678 CE, but this is unverified. The copy must postdate 1603 CE. 'scavye' probably stands for 'saumye' (Wednesday). 'likhitāṃ yugajmavataiḥ' may hide the scribe's name or may be a further corrupt chronogram/phrase. The text author Rāma is not named in the colophon.
review: Commentator's father: the standard Pīyūṣadhārā colophon calls Govinda the son of Nīlakaṇṭha jyotirvid (grandson of Ananta). The garbled 'murālekāranīkaṃ ṣjyoti(!)vidatputra(!)' most likely hides '...nīlakaṇṭhajyotirvitputra'. p2 is re-identified from Murāri to Nīlakaṇṭha, with low confidence; the 'daivajña' title is dropped as unsupported.

Date: 'puṇabhrarase' is not a valid year form. The chronogram probably reads pūrṇa(0)-abhra(0)-rasa(6), giving 600 when read right to left, so a digit is probably missing. The year is left uncertain and ce_approx stays empty.
Weekday: 'scavye' is probably a corruption of 'saumye' (Wednesday).
Scribe name 'yugajmavataiḥ' kept as low-confidence. The given name is now the form as written, not a reconstructed stem.
Notes rewritten to match.

title: Muhūrttadarpaṇa
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Monday 19 Mar 1866, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: || iti muhurttadarppaṇem ukaṃpa(!) phalaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam(!) śubham || || śrī samvat 1923 sālamiti caitra śudi 4 roja 2 etat dine idaṃ pustakaṃ likhitaṃ samāptam || || lekhaka śrī mahāvuddhopāśala(!) śrī jitānaṃdena || || śrī gurave namaḥ || ❁ || (fol. 43v6-8)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Śrījinānanda, but the colophon reads 'śrī jitānaṃdena' (Jitānanda). Jinānanda is possible if the cataloguer misread it. 'mahāvuddhopāśala(!)' is most likely a corruption of 'mahābuddhopāsaka', a lay Buddhist epithet. The catalogue gives the era as ŚS, but ŚS 1923 would be 2001 CE, which is impossible. The 'samvat … sālamiti … roja' formula is the usual Vikrama Samvat style of 19th-century Nepal, so the era is VS 1923. If the year began with Caitra, the date is about March–April 1866. If it was counted from Vaiśākha, as is usual in Nepal, Caitra śukla 4 falls in March 1867. 'roja 2' means Monday.

title: Horāsaukhya
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 22 Apr 1582, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: Kārttikādi, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: || iti śrīmanmahārājādhirājaśrīṭoḍaramallaviracite śrīṭoḍarānaṃde jyotiḥśāstre horāsaukhyaṃ saṃpūrṇam iti || || śubhaṃ bhavatu || kalyāṇam astu lleṣakapāṭhakayoḥ || || saṃvat 1639 varṣe viśākha śudi 30 anaṃtarapratipadāyāṃ śukre praohitarāmātmajena devadattena alīliṣat (!) || || sampūrṇa śubhaṃ bhavatuḥ(!) || ||śrīṭoḍarānandajaya (!)|| || ❁ || śrīkṛṣṇa || || śrīḥ || || || rāma || || rāma || rāma || rāma || (fol. 102r4–8)
notes: The catalogue's King field ('Ṭoḍarānanda Malla') is wrong. Ṭoḍaramalla (Rājā Todar Mal, d. 1589) is named as author or patron of the Ṭoḍarānanda, of which the Horāsaukhya is a part, and 'Ṭoḍarānanda' is the work's title. He is not the reigning king of this copy, and no reigning ruler is named. 'saṃvat 1639' in this Devanagari, North Indian setting is taken as Vikrama, giving 1582 CE; this also fits Todar Mal's lifetime. The tithi is irregular: a bright fortnight normally ends at 15, so 'śudi 30' plus 'the following pratipad' may be a slip for vadi 30 (amāvāsyā), or it may mean the full moon followed by pratipad. 'praohita' is read as purohita. 'alīliṣat' stands for alīlikhat ('wrote / caused to be written'). The catalogue gives Devadatta as scribe, and that is accepted here. 'lleṣakapāṭhakayoḥ' (for lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ) is a standard blessing on scribe and reader, not a named person.
review: p2 (Rāma): confidence lowered to medium because 'praohita' is a corrupt spelling, read as purohita (a title, not part of the name).

p3 (Devadatta): kept as scribe only, confidence set to medium. 'alīliṣat' stands for alīlikhat. That form is formally causative, but here it goes with the instrumental 'devadattena' and is loosely used to mean 'wrote'. There is no separate commissioner, so no commissioner role was added.
Date: month normalised to Vaiśākha and pakṣa to śukla. The odd 'śudi 30 anaṃtarapratipadāyāṃ' is flagged in the notes. VS and 1582 CE are confirmed.
Notes: corrected the catalogue's King field. Ṭoḍaramalla is the author or patron of the text, not the reigning king of this copy, and 'Ṭoḍarānanda' is the title of the work.

title: Meghamālā
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Friday 3 Apr 1587, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: amānta months, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: śāka 1 kuśa2 kroṃca3 śālmalī 4 na cet 5 puṣkara 6 jaṃbūdvī 7 || śrīkṛṣṇāparṇam astu || || śubhaṃ bhavatu || || kalyāṇaṃ || (7) || saṃvat 1644 varṣe | śāke 1509 pravarttamāne | ṣaṣṭyābdamadhye manmathanāmasaṃvatsare | | mālapakakṣetre || mudgala(vā)ta(8)sāha śrīakabararājye | ūcanudasamīpe sonakachagṛāme | śrīsādhu pūrṇimā gache | bhaya śrīsādhu suṃdarasūri tatpa(9)hebhaya śrījayasāgarasūribhir meghamālāgaṃtha likhitam asti || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt sarvvadā || prathamavaiśāṣavadi 11 ravi(9)vāsare liṣitaṃ || || maṃgalaṃ lekhikāṇāṃ tu | pāṭhakāṇāṃ tu maṃgalaṃ | maṃgalaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ | bhaūmau bhūpatimaṃgalaṃ || || śri || (fol. 36v5–9)
notes: VS 1644 and ŚS 1509 agree: both give 1587 CE. The text also names the year as 'manmathanāmasaṃvatsara' in the 60-year cycle. In the standard southern reckoning, 1587/88 is Sarvajit, not Manmatha. The name may follow a northern Bārhaspatya reckoning or may be an error; this has not been verified. 'prathamavaiśāṣa' means the first (intercalary) Vaiśākha. 'vadi' means the dark fortnight (pūrṇimānta reckoning). 'mālapakakṣetre' probably stands for Mālavakṣetre (Malwa). 'ūcanuda' is unidentified. 'sonakacha' may be Sonkatch near Dewas (Madhya Pradesh), but this is uncertain. 'bhaya' is probably the abbreviation 'bha°' for bhaṭṭāraka. 'tatpahe' stands for tatpaṭṭe: Jayasāgara succeeded Sundara(sūri) on the paṭṭa, which may not mean a direct teacher–pupil link. The name could also be read Sādhusundara, but 'śrīsādhu' more likely repeats the gaccha name. 'meghamālāgaṃtha' stands for meghamālāgrantha. The opening list (śāka, kuśa, krauñca, śālmali, ...) names dvīpas from the text and contains no persons.
review: Names given without the Jain title sūri: Jayasāgarasūri → Jayasāgara and Sundarasūri → Sundara, with 'sūri' moved to titles.
Read 'bhaya' as an abbreviation of bhaṭṭāraka and added it to the titles of p2 and p3.
Changed the affiliation from Pūrṇimāgaccha to Sādhupūrṇimāgaccha, a known branch: 'śrīsādhu pūrṇimā gache' is the gaccha name, so 'sādhu' is not a title of Sundara. Removed 'sādhu' from p2's titles.
Changed Akbar's title reading to 'mudgalapātasāha' (Mughal pādśāh); the 'vā' is the cataloguer's doubtful reading.
Moved 'manmatha' out of nakshatra_yoga: it is the name of the 60-year (Jovian) year, not a nakṣatra or yoga. It is now recorded in notes.
Cleared place.normalized: identifying Sonakacha with Sonkatch is plausible but not certain.
The pupil_of relation is kept but annotated: tatpaṭṭe means successor on the pontifical seat (paṭṭa), not necessarily a direct pupil.

notes: The colophon gives no scribe, patron or place. The date formula 'mahārājādhirāja cakravartti śrīvikramāditya-sat (= saṃvat) 1861' names the Vikrama era, not a reigning king. title: Sūryapakṣaśaraṇakaraṇam
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: ≈ 1608 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: śrīsūryapakṣaśaraṇe karaṇetijña sudaivajñacittaharaṇebhinavaprakāre || daivajñaviṣṇuracite khacarāgamesminyāta sphuṭa prakaraṇaṃ paripūrṇamāsīt || ❖ || śāko nakhāgnīṣubhuvaḥ samaughaḥ sūryā hatau saugatamāsamīhaḥ || (fol. 10v10–11r2)
notes: 1) The date verse probably belongs to the text, not to this copy. Viṣṇu Daivajña's Sūryapakṣaśaraṇa karaṇa is known to use Śaka 1530 (c. 1608 CE) as its epoch. This verse comes right after the text's own closing verse, so it most likely gives the composition/epoch year. If so, Śaka 1530 is only the earliest possible date (terminus post quem) for the copy, and the catalogue's 'Date of Copying: ŚS 1530' may be wrong. 2) The chronogram does not work out exactly. Reading 'nakhāgnīṣubhuvaḥ' right to left with nakha = 20 gives bhū 1, iṣu 5, agni 3, nakha 20, which is more than four digits. 1530 only works if nakha is taken as 0 (or the compound is read loosely). 1530 does agree with the known epoch of the work. 3) 'samaughaḥ sūryā hatau saugatamāsamīhaḥ' is corrupt or obscure. It does not clearly give a month, so no month is recorded. 4) The catalogue names the scribe as Rudradevadvija (probably Rudradeva, titled dvija), but no scribe appears in the quoted colophon. That name must come from somewhere else in the manuscript and could not be checked here.

Added a caveat in notes: the Śaka 1530 verse is probably the author's epoch (the date of the text's composition), not the date this copy was made.
Added a note on the chronogram reading (nakha = 20 does not fit four digits).
Kept Viṣṇu (daivajña) as author, Śaka 1530 = c. 1608 CE, and the remark about the scribe Rudradeva.

notes: The colophon gives NS 406 (Mārgaśīrṣa → c. Nov/Dec 1285 CE), which fits the reign of Anantamalla (c. 1274–1310). The catalogue's 'VS 1980' (1923 CE) conflicts with this. notes: The colophon gives only 'śaṃvat 1696' with no era name. VS is assumed, following the usual convention for an unqualified saṃvat in Devanagari manuscripts, which gives about 1639 CE. If it were ŚS, the date would be about 1774 CE. The month is damaged: mā(‥) could be Māgha or Mārgaśīrṣa. The scribe's name and caste are written run together as 'paramānaṃdkāstha', read here as Paramānanda kāyastha (the cataloguer reads 'Pramānanda kāyastha ?'). The catalogue's 'King: Kamari Datta Sen ?' does not appear anywhere in the quoted colophon, so no king is recorded. It may come from another part of the manuscript, or it may be a mistake. The verse 'jā(!)dṛśaṃ pustakaṃ kṛṣṭvā(!) ...' is the standard scribe's disclaimer (yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā) and says nothing about who owned or commissioned the copy.

title: Mahābhārata
subject: Mahābhārata
date_note: = Apr 1766, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ svargārohaṇakaṃ parvasamāptaṃ || śrīśāke 1688 vāre 7 māse 12 śrīrājapustakaṃ likhita rāmabhadradvuja rāmakṛṣṇa (fol. 9v6–7)
purpose: royal copy (śrīrājapustakaṃ), made for the king or the royal library
notes: 'rāmabhadradvuja' is corrupt. It most likely stands for 'rāmabhadradvija', meaning the brahmin Rāmabhadra, which is how the catalogue reads it too. It could also hide a kinship word such as '-tanuja' or '-ātmaja'. In that case the phrase would mean 'Rāmakṛṣṇa, son of Rāmabhadra', and Rāmakṛṣṇa alone would be the scribe. The relation between the two men is therefore left unrecorded. 'śrīrājapustakaṃ' marks the book as royal property, but no king is named. In ŚS 1688 (1766–67 CE) the Kathmandu Valley was being conquered by the Gorkhā ruler Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha, but nothing in the colophon says which court is meant. If 'month 12' is counted from Caitra it is Phālguna, which falls in early 1767 CE. If it is counted from Mārgaśīrṣa it is Kārttika, which falls in 1766 CE.

title: Matasāra
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Friday 25 Apr 1197, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmatasāre saptādaśamaḥ(!)paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || ❁ || maṅgalamahāśrīḥ || || yāte sapty uḍupānale bhṛgudine nepālasamvatsare māse mādhavaśuklake raṣatithau ṛkṣe ca tiṣye śubhe | divyaṃ śrīmatasāraśrīmatam idam bhogāpavarggapradaṃ bhaktyā hastalikhāyitaṃ śivapada(!) prāptuṃ jasa brahmaṇā || || rājādhirājaparameśvaraśrīpaśupatipādāmbujānugrahīt | śrīmallakṣīkāmadevasya vijayarājye || paṇḍitācāryaśrīśrī vaccharūdrācāryakṛtvā || śrījayabrahmasya(!) pustakaṃ | lekhakapipraśrījayabrahmaśarmmeṇa(!) likhāyitaṃ || svaprārthahetoḥ parāparaphalaprāptayetiśreyaḥ || ❁ || samvat 317 vaiśākaśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ | śukravāre | puṣyanakṣatre || likhidam(!) idaṃ | śubham astu || udakānalacaurebhyoḥ(!) mūṣikaśca tathaiva ca | rakṣitavyaṃ prayatnena mayā kaṣṭena likhitaṃ || maṅgalamahāśrīḥ || graṃthasahasra 2 || || (fol.145r4-145v5)
notes: The verse date and the prose date agree. In the chronogram, sapti (7), uḍupa (1) and anala (3), read right to left, give NS 317. The verse also gives mādhava = Vaiśākha, rasa (written raṣa) = 6, bhṛgudina = Friday and tiṣya = Puṣya. NS 317 is about 1197 CE, so the king must be Lakṣmīkāmadeva II of the late 12th century, not Lakṣmīkāmadeva I of the 11th century. 'lakṣī' is an error for lakṣmī. 'jasa brahmaṇā' in the verse is probably a corruption of jayabrahmaṇā. 'lekhakapipra' stands for lekhaka-vipra. Both 'hastalikhāyitaṃ' and 'likhāyitaṃ' are causatives. Here they probably just mean 'written', because Jayabrahman calls himself lekhaka and the copy is for his own use. A commissioner role cannot be ruled out entirely, though. 'paṇḍitācāryaśrīśrī vaccharūdrācāryakṛtvā' is unclear: it may name a teacher, a reviser or the person who arranged the copy, and the name may be Vatsarudra. I have not checked the weekday against an ephemeris.

title: Bhāgavata(daśamaskanda)
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Monday 14 Feb 1724, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: … haribhaktir astu śubhaṃ || sambat 844 māghakṛṣṇāpaṃcamī citrānakṣatra bhājudevanathavatāro cakāvatayā || (ṅākṣa 1036 vida) || (fol. 203v4-5)
notes: The Newari passage is corrupt. 'cakāvatayā' is most likely coyakā(va) tayā, 'had it written and kept'. That would make the named person the commissioner rather than the scribe; no scribe is named. 'bhājudevanathavatāro' is read here as bhāju (an honorific) + Devanātha (written 'devanatha'). The remainder, 'vatāro', is unclear. It could be a corruption, a genitive/ergative ending, or 'va tāro' ('and Tāro'), which would mean a second co-commissioner named Tāro/Tāra. The name, the title 'bhāju' and the role are therefore only medium confidence. The bracketed '(ṅākṣa 1036 vida)' appears to be a separate, later note: NS 1036 is about 1916 CE, and 'vida' may be Newari biyā, 'given'. It may record a later transfer of the manuscript and does not date this copy. The date itself, NS 844 Māgha kṛṣṇa 5, falls in about Jan–Feb 1724 CE.
review: Kept Devanātha as commissioner (medium); expanded the notes on how 'bhājudevanathavatāro' might be split, including a possible second name ('va tāro' = 'and Tāro').
Narrowed ce_approx: Māgha of NS 844 falls in about Jan–Feb 1724 CE.
Added a note on the bracketed '(ṅākṣa 1036 vida)', probably a later note (NS 1036 ≈ 1916 CE) that does not date this copy.

colophon: iti gauḍadeśīya raghunāthasārvabhaumaviracito vyavasthārṇavaḥ samāptaṃ saṃpūrṇam śrīśāke || 1700 || || śrīsaṃvat || 18 || 35 ||| miti dutīā āṣānhavaditerasī || †ke prasataka puraṇa bhaye ena somaradeṣyā somaralīṣyā ||† (fol. 71r3-5)
notes:
The colophon gives two dates, Śaka 1700 and Vikrama Saṃvat 1835. They agree: both are 1778 CE, and the catalogue fields match. 'dutīā āṣānha' probably means the second Āṣāḍha, which would make it an intercalary month. This has not been checked against an ephemeris.

The closing note is vernacular and corrupt: †ke prasataka puraṇa bhaye ena somaradeṣyā somaralīṣyā†. A likely reading is '[yah] pustaka pūraṇa bhaye; Somara dekhyā, Somara likhyā' ('the book was completed; Somara saw/checked it, Somara wrote it'). On that reading Somara is the scribe, and possibly also the checker of the copy. The name may also be Somāru, or the text may be a garbled 'somavāra' (Monday), so confidence is low.

'Gauḍadeśīya' describes the author Raghunātha Sārvabhauma, not the scribe.

title: Mukundavijaya
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Thursday 3 Aug 1780, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: svasti śrīnepālasamvatsaragate 900 śrāvaṇaśulkatṛtīyāyāṃ tīthau (!) uttarabhadraṇakṣatre (!) dhṛtiyoge śukravāsare ttaddine (!) sampūrṇam iti || śubham astu || || || śrīdivākarāya rastu (!) || || ❖ kṛttikānva viśākhānva bhaumavāreṇasaṃyutaṃ taddine ghaṭitaṃ śastraṃ saṃgrāme jayadāyakaṃ || iti sva[[rodaye]] || (fol. 38v6-8)
notes: 'śrīdivākarāya rastu (!)' is probably 'śrīdivākarāyāstu', a dative blessing meaning '[may it] be for Divākara'. That would fit a human owner or beneficiary named Divākara. It could also be a garbled invocation to the Sun god (Divākara), possibly a corruption of '...namo 'stu'. If it is the deity, delete p1, which is why its confidence is low. The colophon names no scribe or place. After the completion formula the copy adds a Svarodaya verse about weapons made on a Tuesday with Kṛttikā or Viśākhā; the cataloguer supplied '[[rodaye]]'. That verse's nakṣatras and weekday are not part of the copying date. 'ttaddine' is a corruption of 'taddine'. The colophon agrees with the catalogue date (NS 900).
review: No substantive changes. Persons, date, era and ce_approx (NS 900 + 880 = 1780; Śrāvaṇa of NS 900 falls in mid-1780) are correct.
Notes expanded: the uncertainty about Divākara is explained in more detail, and the nakṣatra and weekday terms in the appended verse are marked as not part of the copying date.
