title: Dīkṣāpaddhati
subject: Tāntrika Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāya rāmajīvanatarkālaṃkārabhaṭṭācāryyātmajaśrīvāgīśvarabhaṭṭācāryyaviracitāyāṃ dīkṣāpaddhatyāṃ paṃcamapaṭalaḥ || || †turārke† sitapakṣe vai tṛtīyāyāṃ śanau sudhīḥ śrīnārāyaṇaśarmāhaṃ vyalikhad īśvarechayā || 1 || samāptam || || śubham || (fol. 56r6-8, exp. 42b)
notes: The cataloguer marks '†turārke†' as corrupt. The probable reading is 'tulārke' ('when the sun is in Tulā'), which would give the solar month Tulā, roughly October–November. The colophon gives no year and no era, so the copy cannot be dated from it. The scribal verse mixes persons: 'nārāyaṇaśarmāhaṃ' is first person, but 'vyalikhad' is third person (as is 'sudhīḥ'); it is a metrical, ungrammatical verse, and the scribe is still clearly Nārāyaṇa. The colophon names the author as Vāgīśvara Bhaṭṭācārya, son of Mahāmahopādhyāya Rāmajīvana Tarkālaṃkāra Bhaṭṭācārya. The Bhaṭṭācārya title probably points to a Bengali scholarly family. The catalogue's scribe field (Nārāyaṇa Śarmā) agrees with the colophon.
review: p3: name changed from 'Nārāyaṇa Śarman' to 'Nārāyaṇa'. 'śarman' is a brahmin suffix, so it stays only in titles.
purpose: emptied. 'īśvarechayā' (by the will of God) is a pious formula, not a statement of purpose (svārtha/parārtha etc.).
notes: added remarks on the grammar of the scribal verse and on the tulārke reading.

notes: The colophon names Jayaccandradeva (Jayacandra, the Gāhaḍavāla king) as the reigning king in Vārāṇasī. The era is not named, but VS fits his reign (c. 1170–1194 CE), so VS 1239 ≈ 1182 CE. 'tatchāsanika' = tacchāsanika, 'his (the king's) officer/appointee'. 'rāuta' is a rank title (from rājaputra). 'surahi' is read as Sura plus the vernacular instrumental ending -hi, the agent of 'likhāpitam'; the name Surahi is less likely. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Sura Rāuta' is wrong: Sura had the copy made for himself (commissioner/owner). The actual scribe is not named; 'lekhaka' appears only in the closing benediction. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris.
review: p2 name normalized from 'Surahi' to 'Sura': '-hi' is the vernacular (Apabhraṃśa/Old Hindi) instrumental/agentive ending governing 'likhāpitam'. This agrees with the catalogue's 'Sura Rāuta'. Confidence lowered to medium.
Added a servant_of relation from p2 to p1. 'tacchāsanika' (written tatchāsanika) means 'his officer, one under his command', and 'tat' refers back to Jayacandradeva.
Title 'tacchāsanika' is kept as written. Notes now explain it and record that the scribe is not named.
Weekday normalized to 'budha'.

title: Pūrvāmnāyanityakarmadevārcanavidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Friday 17 Aug 1714, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīpūrvvāmnāyanityakarmmadevārccanavi(4)dhi samāptaṃ || || saṃvat 834 śrāvana śuklasaptamīkuhnu saṃpurṇṇa yā(5)ṅā juro || liṣiti vidyāpiyā karmmācarya, lakṣmīdharana saṃpurṇṇa yāṅā ju(6)ro || || saṃvat 832 vakādharaṃ dāṅāyā hlāṣa || || || (7) yā diṣṭi | puṣṭakaṃ dṛsṭā, tā dṛṣṭi likṣitaṃ mayā, jadi śuddhaṃ maśurddhaṃ vā liṣā(8)ko dāṣa(!) nāṣṭidaṃ || || yadakṣala pabhṛṣṭaṃ māṭrāhinaṃ tathaiva ca ta(33b1)t sarvva kṣammatā māta kṣamaśva parameśvarī || || iśvarī prītrīrastu || || (exp. 34t3-34b1)
notes: The Karmācārya Lakṣmīdhara finished copying this manuscript on Śrāvaṇa śukla 7, NS 834 (c. 1714 CE). His residence or affiliation 'vidyāpiyā' is unclear. It is a Newari genitive ('of Vidyāpī-') and could be a place, a lineage, or something corrupt. A separate line reads 'saṃvat 832 vakādharaṃ dāṅāyā hlāṣa', dated NS 832 (c. 1712 CE). It probably records something done by or with a person Vakādhara (perhaps Bakādhara). This could be the start of the copying, the handover of the exemplar, or a gift. The wording is obscure, so both the name and the role are uncertain. The two years 832 and 834 are both Nepāla Saṃvat and do not conflict. The colophon ends with the usual scribal verses ('yādṛṣṭaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā…', 'yad akṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ…').
review: Purpose: 'iśvarī prītrīrastu' is a closing benediction (īśvarī prītir astu, 'may the Goddess be pleased'). It does not say who the copy was made for. Recorded it as a benediction and gave a normalised form.
Lakṣmīdhara's residence 'vidyāpiyā' kept, but the notes now flag it as uncertain. It is a Newari genitive ('of Vidyāpī-') and could be a place, a lineage or a corruption.
Notes expanded on the NS 832 entry. Also noted that the 832/834 years are not two conflicting eras.

title: Pratimālakṣaṇasamuccaya
subject: vāstuśāstra
date_note: = Friday 25 Feb 1684, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: saṃ 804 phālguṇa śikla pakṣe navamyāntithau śukravāra thvakuhnu coya dhunakāvaṃ lānihma vāsinā śrītri(30r6)vikrameśādaṭa puṣṭakam iti || ||(7) gaṃgāya dhyana rudra jāmale || devīñcattrar.. joṃ gaṃgā trinetrāṃ mukta ṭo..lāṃ | padma daryyaṇahastāñcavaradā bhaya hastakāṃ || (30v1) divya vastra vṛtāṃ kāntāṃ sarvvābharaṇa bhūṣitāṃ || praṃcaṇḍa vadanāṃ dhyāyachi cotsaṃge ca comatāṃ || || gajuli(2)yā cosa luna thva yāvate thvani rañjana mūrtti || pustaka, padma, vara, abhaya, padmāsana || thvate juro || (3)
notes: 'śrītrivikrameśādaṭa' is corrupt. It most likely reads Trivikrama(-īśa/-datta?) plus the Newari dative -ṭa (= -yāta), meaning 'the book for Trivikrama...'. If so, he is the recipient/owner and the scribe is unnamed. 'lānihma vāsinā' is obscure: it could be '(the) resident of Lāni' or a Newari verb phrase. It is not taken as the place of copying. Everything after 'iti || ||' is a later addition: a Gaṅgā dhyāna 'from the Rudrayāmala' and Newari iconographic notes. These do not name anyone connected with this copy. 'śikla' = śukla.
review: p1: the final -ṭa in 'śrītrivikrameśādaṭa' is most likely the Newari dative ending ('for/to'). The book is therefore for Trivikrama..., not written by him. Roles changed from scribe+owner to owner. The scribe is not named.
p1 name: best reading is 'Trivikrama' (stem uncertain: perhaps Trivikrameśa or Trivikramadatta). Confidence lowered to low.
Residence/place: 'lānihma vāsinā' is unclear. It may be a Newari verb form ('handed over'?) and not a toponym. Removed 'Lānihma' as residence and as place of copying; explained in notes.
Purpose set to: book for Trivikrama (dative).
Date confirmed: NS 804 phālguṇa śukla 9, Friday, about 1684 CE (Feb/Mar).

notes: The catalogue conflates the names and surroundings into 'Viṣṇukailāśānandarāja upādhyāya'. The meter and sandhi reveal three individuals: Viṣṇu (viṣṇuś ca), Kailāśa (kailāśa[ḥ]), and Ānandaśarman (ānandaśarmmā), described as 'abhiṣekakāmā[ḥ]' (plural). 'Dolāgiri campakavṛkṣamūle' refers to the famous champak tree shrine of Viṣṇu at Dolādri/Dolāgiri (Changu Narayan); Garuḍadhvaja, Lakṣmīpati, and Trivikrama are epithets of the deity Viṣṇu worshipped there.

title: Śīghrabodha
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: doubtful: Saturday 19 Dec 907 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
date_doubtful: doubtful: Saturday 19 Dec 907 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
colophon: iti śrīkāśināthakṛtau śīghrabodhāyaḥ (!) prakaranaṃ samāpta (!) || || || 591 || || || ||❖ samvat. 28 pauṣaśukla 12 roja 7 vāla || || thva saphūlasidha yakā dina juro || || dai iba bhe || keśavasiṃhana juro || || || || śubha || (fol. 40v)
notes: The catalogue gives NS 591 (= 1471 CE), probably from the bare number '591' right after the text's closing words. That number has no 'samvat' and could instead be a grantha/verse count. The full date with tithi and weekday is 'samvat 28 pauṣa śukla 12, Saturday', which seems to have the century left out (e.g. NS 728 = 1608 CE or NS 828 = 1708 CE). The Persian loan 'roja' (day) and the Newari wording suggest the later Malla period rather than 1471, so ce_approx is left empty. If 591 is the year, the copy dates to 1471 CE. A weekday check of Pauṣa śu. 12 against NS 591 and 728/828 could settle this. 'thva saphū lasidha yakā dina juro' = 'this is the day the book was completed'. 'dai iba bhe' is unclear (perhaps corrupt; maybe a title like daivajña, or a place or a relative). Keśavasiṃha is taken as the scribe on the strength of the instrumental 'keśavasiṃhana juro', as the catalogue also has it.
review: Weekday normalised: 'roja 7 vāla' = 7th day, i.e. Saturday (roja = day); recorded as '7 (Saturday)' rather than 'roja 7'.
as_written for Kāśīnātha trimmed to the form as it appears (kāśinātha-), without śrī; stem normalised to Kāśīnātha.
Scribe confidence lowered to medium because the instrumental keśavasiṃhana stands next to the unclear 'dai iba bhe' and the clause only says the book was completed by him.
Date: the dated clause is still read as NS (century omitted) 28. The notes now explain the conflict with the catalogue's NS 591 (= 1471 CE) and give possible ce values.

notes: The scribe's name, 'Jayarūndrasiṃha', is probably a corrupt spelling of Jayarudrasiṃha. The catalogue gives a chronogram: durggā(9) aginī(3) vasu(8). Read right to left this gives 839, which matches the colophon's Saṃbat 839, so NS 839 = 1718 CE (kārttika). The catalogue also gives a bracketed second date, 'saṃvat 831', with the same month, pakṣa, tithi, nakṣatra, yoga and weekday. This conflicts with 839. It may come from a second colophon or be a misreading; 831 would be 1710/11 CE. The quoted colophon does not name the king (Mahīndrasiṃha) or the place (Kathmandu); they appear only in the catalogue fields, so they are not listed as persons or place. The date fits the reign of Mahīndrasiṃha (Mahīndra Siṃha Malla) of Kathmandu, c. 1714–1722.
review: Scribe's confidence lowered from high to medium: 'Jayarūndrasiṃha' looks like a corrupt spelling, probably of Jayarudrasiṃha. The as-written form is kept as the stem.

notes: The scribe's name reads rūparājena(!), but the catalogue gives Purarāja. Which reading is right is uncertain; Rūparāja is the one taken from the quoted text. The catalogue marks the year as 'NS 622 ?'. The bracketed passages '(ju)saraḥ (nīyanośi)' and '(rīsvāttarjña)' are garbled. The first may hide a word spelling out the year. The second may hide the weekday or nakṣatra (perhaps a corrupt '...vāsare'), but neither can be read safely. 'kṛteḥ' may stand for kṛttikā nakṣatra. Because Kārttika opens the NS year, Kārttika kṛṣṇa 13 of NS 622 is about Oct/Nov 1501 CE, not 1502.
review: Lowered p2 (Rūparāja) confidence to medium: the cataloguer marks the name with (!) and gives the scribe as Purarāja.
ce_approx changed from 1502 to 1501: Kārttika is the first month of the Nepāla Saṃvat year, so Kārttika kṛṣṇa of NS 622 falls in about October/November 1501.
nakshatra_yoga now says that kṛteḥ may be a corrupt kṛttikā; the garbled parts of the date are recorded in notes.

(fol. 46r1–7)
purpose: copied by order of Rājaguru Hemarāja Paṇḍita
notes:
This is a modern transcript (VS 1986, about 1929 CE). Hemarāja is almost certainly the well-known Rājaguru Hemarāja Śarmā (Paṇḍita).

The transcript was taken ('uddhṛtya') from an old palm-leaf manuscript written in Bhujimol script ('bhujavalākṣara'). It reproduces that exemplar's colophon: 'aśītyadhikasaṃyāte samvatsaraśatatraye' = year 380, Caitra śukla 5, a Friday, in the reign of Jayabhīma(deva). The exemplar's date names no era, but it is presumably NS 380 (about 1260 CE). That fits Jayabhīmadeva's reign, roughly NS 378–391.

For this reason Jayabhīmadeva has role 'other' rather than reigning king of this copy, so the catalogue's King field refers to the exemplar. 'vilikyā' stands for vilikhya. 'lekhayutāt' is unclear and may stand for lekhayuktāt.
review: p1 Jayabhīmadeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He reigned when the palm-leaf exemplar was copied in (NS) 380, about 1260 CE, not when this copy was made in VS 1986 (1929 CE).
p3: name changed from 'Pūrṇaprasāda Śarman' to stem form 'Pūrṇaprasāda'; śarman stays in titles only.
Date: paksa filled as śukla, which pūrṇimā implies.
Purpose: shortened to a plain description.

Notes: the exemplar's date was left without a stated era; it is now given as an inferred NS 380 with a check against Jayabhīmadeva's reign. Added notes on the exemplar's script and the corrupt word 'vilikyā'.

title: Kūlārṇava
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Aug 1791, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīkulārṇave mahārahasye īśvarapārvatīsaṃvāde dūtīsapādalakṣagranthe paṃcamakhaṇḍe dūtīyāgārccanaṃ nāmāṣṭādaśollāsaḥ || 18 || || śubhaṃ bhavatu sarvadā || || [after the sub colophon of the 17th chapter, on the exp.70 is given:] iti śrīkulārṇave mahārahasye sarvvasāre sapādalakṣagranthe tattvasāre paṃcamakhaṇḍe gurunāmāditattvapadārthannāmaḥ samāptaḥ || saṃvat 1713 bhādraṅṛṣṇatṛtīyāṃ(!) budha (!) revatyāṃ daivajña〈〈‥ ‥〉〉varmaṇā likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || yādṛśī pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā... kṣamyatāṃ parameśvari | ... manu || tīrthe maṃtre tathā deve daivajñe āiṣadhe tathā| yādṛśī bhāvanā yasya siddhir bhavati tādṛśī |\ bhāvena cuṃbite- (!) 1yuādśī bhāvanā yasya īśvarapārvatīsaṃvāde sapādalakṣagranthe tatvasāre paṃcamakhaṃḍe || gurunāmāditatvapadārthannāma saptadaśollāsaḥ samāptaḥ || saṃvat 1713 bhādrakṛṣṇatṛtīyāṃ vudharevatyāṃ daivajñavarmmaṇalikhitaṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || (fol. 62r5–6)
notes:
Scribe: the name is given twice. On exp. 70 it reads 'daivajña〈〈‥ ‥〉〉varmaṇā', with a marked lacuna or insertion between daivajña and varmaṇā. On fol. 62r it reads 'daivajñavarmmaṇalikhitaṃ'. The full name may therefore be '…varman', with only the ending surviving. 'Daivajña' is taken as a title (astrologer). The catalogue's 'Varmmaṇa' is an inflected form.

Era: the colophon says only 'saṃvat'. The catalogue gives ŚS 1713, which would be 1791 CE. A rough mean-lunation check (amānta Bhādrapada, kṛṣṇa 3) gives these results:
- VS 1713: kṛṣṇa 3 falls on about 6 Sept 1656, a Wednesday, with the Moon in about Revatī. This agrees with 'budha revatyāṃ'.
- ŚS 1713: kṛṣṇa 3 falls on about 15–16 Sept 1791 (Thursday/Friday), with the Moon near the Revatī/Aśvinī boundary. This fits less well.
VS 1713 (c. 1656 CE) is therefore preferred, but this has not been checked with an exact pañcāṅga.

Text: the same dated colophon closes the 17th ullāsa (gurunāmāditattvapadārtha), apparently in two copies. The 18th-ullāsa colophon has no date. The passage '...bhāvena cuṃbite- (!) 1yuādśī bhāvanā yasya...' is corrupt in the catalogue quotation.
review: Scribe evidence now uses the fuller form 'daivajña〈〈‥ ‥〉〉varmaṇā likhitaṃ'. Confidence lowered to low because the marked lacuna may hide the first part of the name (…varman).

Date: added a rough check of the weekday and nakṣatra. VS 1713 (6 Sept 1656 CE, a Wednesday, Moon in Revatī) fits better than the catalogue's ŚS 1713 (c. 15–16 Sept 1791, Thursday/Friday). ce_approx set to 1656 while the era stays 'unspecified'.
Notes expanded: the catalogue's ŚS attribution is questioned, the two colophon copies are listed, and the corrupt passage is flagged.

subject: Śaivatantra

colophon: iti śrīnāgabhaṭṭaviracite tripurāsārasamuccaye daśamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ | saṃvat 800 caitraśu ºº praºº || gaṇarāja || (fol. 32v8)
notes: The era is not stated. 'saṃvat 800' in a Newari-script manuscript is taken as NS, which agrees with the catalogue field. The date is heavily abbreviated: 'praºº' probably stands for pratipadā, but it is uncertain. 'gaṇarāja', written alone between daṇḍas after the date, is most likely the scribe's signature or an owner's name, which is common at that position in Newari colophons. notes: This manuscript is a paper transcript made in Kathmandu in VS 1991 (1934/35 CE). Pūrṇaprasāda copied it on the order of Rājaguru Hemarāja from a palm-leaf manuscript collected by General Keśara (Kaiser Shumsher Rana); the colophon calls that source largely corrupt ('prāyaśo .śuddha'). The transcript reproduces the source's own colophon ('ityantalekhayutāt'). In that colophon, Jayadeva(varmā) of Lalitapattana (Māniglaka), attached to Dakṣiṇāvihāra and Yothāvihāra, says he wrote it with his own hand for his own purpose ('svārthahetunā svahastena'). He did so on Māgha kṛṣṇa 2, under Uttaraphālgunī, in yoga Mūla, on a Sunday, in the reign of Yuvarāja Jagajjyotirmalla. Because of this, Jayadeva and the king are recorded with role 'other', not as scribe and king of this copy. The year of the source is a problem. The quoted colophon reads 'samvat 439' (1319 CE), but the catalogue gives NS 539 (1419 CE). 539 fits Jyotirmalla, son of Jayasthitimalla, who ruled about 1408–1428. 439 fits no known Jagajjyotirmalla. So 539 is probably correct and the '439' in the quotation is probably a typo; it needs checking on the reel. Several readings are uncertain: '†śrīmāniglake†' is marked corrupt by the cataloguer; 'āddhavanāyakamūrtyaṅgapradhānāṅgapātra' is an unclear string of office titles; and 'śrīdaºº.kaºº' is an abbreviated title of Keśara.
review: p1 Jayadeva: his role changed from 'scribe' to 'other'. He wrote the palm-leaf exemplar in NS 439/539, not this 1934 copy. Name stripped to 'Jayadeva' with 'varmā' moved to titles. Affiliation split into the two vihāras.
p2 Jagajjyotirmalladeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He was reigning when the exemplar was copied, not when this VS 1991 transcript was made.
p3 Keśara (General Kaiser Shumsher): role changed from 'owner' to 'other'. He collected the exemplar, not this copy. Name stripped to 'Keśara' with 'varmā' moved to titles.
p4 Hemarāja: 'śarmā' moved from the name to titles.
p5 Pūrṇaprasāda: 'śarmā' moved from the name to titles.
Added a relation from p5 to p3 (copied from the exemplar in p3's collection).
Notes: added the exemplar's full date and flagged the NS 439 vs NS 539 problem. 539 fits Jyotirmalla's reign; 439 does not.
Purpose: 'śubhāya bhavatu' is now labelled as a benediction. Jayadeva's 'svārthahetunā' (for his own purpose) applies to the exemplar, not this copy.

title: Nīlatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: ≈ 1776 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrīlīlataṃtre (!) sarvataṃtrottamottame bhairavapārvatīsaṃvāde paṃcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ 15 || 01 | samāptaś cā(2)yaṃ graṃthaḥ || 〇 || śubham astu samvat 1833 śrīyut sītārāmabhaṭṭasya pustakam idaṃ || ślokasaṃkhyā 1000 || (‥) 27 śāke 1698 śubhaṃ bhūyāt (fol. 33r1–2)
notes: The two eras agree: VS 1833 − 57 = 1776 and Śaka 1698 + 78 = 1776, so the year is about 1776/77 CE. '(‥) 27' comes after a lacuna. It is probably a day number (for example a solar day, gate) with the month name lost, and is not a tithi. The colophon names Sītārāma Bhaṭṭa only as owner ('sītārāmabhaṭṭasya pustakam idaṃ'). The catalogue's 'Scribe' and 'Donor' entries for him are not supported by the text, although he may also have been the scribe. The text title is written 'līlataṃtre (!)' for Nīlatantra.
review: Removed '27' from tithi: it follows a lacuna '(‥) 27', and 27 cannot be a tithi (a tithi number never exceeds 15, or 30 in continuous count). It is more likely a solar day (gate/miti) or an unrelated figure. Recorded in notes instead.
Widened date.as_written to the full date-bearing passage.
Expanded notes: VS 1833 and Śaka 1698 agree (both 1776/77 CE). The catalogue's scribe and donor roles are not supported by the colophon.

title: Tantracintāmaṇi
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Sunday 29 Mar 1857, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: || iti śrītantracintāmaṇau mātṛkāvarṇṇadhyā(6)nadaśavidyādinānāmantrabhedamuktyūpāya(!) antyeṣṭinirṇayanāmā (!) catvāriṃśattamaḥ prakāśaḥ samāptaḥ || śubhaḥ (!) || amarasiṃhāksaraṃ śubhaṃ || (7)saṃvat 977 śālamiti caitraśudi 4 roja 3 saṃni saṃsthiti coyā ...(8)svarggavāsa lāyu śubham (fol. 433v5–8)
notes: The date uses the Persian-style formula 'śālamiti … roja 3' (year-date … weekday 3 = Tuesday). Caitra śukla 4 of NS 977 falls in March/April 1857 CE. The date is followed by a lacunose Newari note, 'saṃni saṃsthiti coyā ... svarggavāsa lāyu'. It appears to record that someone died (went to heaven) on this date, but the name is lost in the lacuna. So the date may be the date of that death note rather than the date of copying. The catalogue gives the date of copying as NS 977, which suggests the cataloguer took this as the copying date. The catalogue's king, Bhūpālendra(malla), is not in the quoted colophon. He reigned in Bhaktapur c. 1687–1696 CE, which does not fit 1857 CE, so the catalogue field is probably wrong or comes from elsewhere in the manuscript.

purpose: sattvahetoḥ (for the benefit of beings): this is in the later line about consecration and donation, not in the copying colophon
notes: The year is written in words: 'śate sāṣṭakaviṃśayute' = 100 + 28 = 128. The colophon does not name the era. Bendall takes it as Nepal Saṃvat, which gives 128 + 880 = A.D. 1008, matching his conversion. The text says 'dvirājyaka': a joint rule of Nirbhaya and Rudradeva. 'शुक्लपञ्चे' is probably 'शुक्लपक्षे' (compare 'नचचरस्य' = नक्षत्रस्य), so the day of the month is not given. The phrase 'राज्ये परि... कवितवौरि संघे' is corrupt. The vihāra name 'श्रील्लुम्बिहार' is uncertain: it is marked (?) by Bendall and could not be identified. No scribe or donor is named in the part that can be read. The later line in fresher ink ('प्रणम्य प्रतिष्ठापनञ्चैवमस्या ... कारयन् सत्त्वहेतोः') records a later consecration of the book with gifts and feasts for monks. It mentions a 'वराचार्य' but gives no personal name.

colophon: यदत्र पुण्यं तन्नवलाचार्योपाध्यायमाता नेपालेश्वर श्रीमन्महा- राज हिन्दुपति बात्साह श्रीश्रीश्री रण बहादूर साह बहादूर समसेर (?) जंग देवानां सदा समरविजयिनां विजयराज्ये । युतीन्दुनन्द युत हायने स्मिन्तयावदाते (?) तिशिरामचन्द्रे तिथ्याडुवायां (?) बुधवासरे च सुरे च कुम्भशशिकर्कदेशे (sic) । दानपति कान्तिपूरे महानगरे कमिलाच्छितोल धालसिका नामगृहाधिवासित पुण्यात्मानुराधेन (?) बालमुकुन्द सहोदर- भाह भाजुधंपुत्र जयप्रतापसिं पिता महिजयलक्ष्मिता रत्न- वति दारा जगलक्ष्मी एते सहानुमतेन श्री ३ सुवर्णप्रभास° पुस्तकम जम्बूनन्देन चूर्णेन लिखापथिला प्रतिष्ठापितमभूत । अस्य देशभखा ।
purpose: merit (यदत्र पुण्यं); the dānapati and his family had the book written in gold and consecrated
notes:
The text comes from Bendall 1883 (Cambridge Add. 875). He warns that the gold-on-black readings are unreliable.

**Date.** The chronogram युतीन्दुनन्द is read right to left as 4-1-9 = 914, which agrees with Bendall's N.S. 914 = A.D. 1794. This falls within the reign of Raṇa Bahādura Śāha (1777–1799). The month is not stated. The sun in Kumbha (कुम्भ) points to about Phālguna. 'अवदाते' probably means the bright fortnight. 'रामचन्द्रे' may encode tithi 13. All three are uncertain.

**Family list.** The donor passage is corrupt. I take Bālamukunda as the dānapati, with brother Bhājudhaṃ ('भाजु' may be a Newari honorific), son Jayapratāpasiṃha, pitāmahī Jayalakṣmī ('पिता महि' = pitāmahī), mother Ratnavatī ('ता' = [mā]tā) and wife Jagalakṣmī. 'एते सहानुमतेन' makes them joint sponsors. An alternative reading, used by the first reader, makes Jayapratāpasiṃha the son of Bhājudhaṃ. 'पुण्यात्मानुराधेन (?)' is unclear and may hide another name.

**Scribe.** The scribe is not named. Bendall mentions invocations on the scribe's Ācārya parents, and 'नवलाचार्योपाध्यायमाता' may contain a personal name (Navala?), but this is too uncertain to record as a person.
review: Main dānapati/commissioner changed from Jayapratāpasiṃha to Bālamukunda. He is named first after the residence formula and the list then gives his relatives (brother, son, grandmother, mother, wife), all joined by 'एते सहानुमतेन'.

Jayapratāpasiṃha is now read as Bālamukunda's son ('पुत्र'), not as the son of Bhājudhaṃ. Bhājudhaṃ is read as Bālamukunda's brother ('सहोदर-भाह' ≈ sahodara bhrātā), with 'bhāju' perhaps the Newari honorific.
Kinship terms are now tied to Bālamukunda: pitāmahī Jayalakṣmī, mātā Ratnavatī and dārā Jagalakṣmī.
King's name normalized to IAST stem 'Raṇa Bahādura Śāha', with titles given in IAST. Shah kings do not take a -deva regnal name; 'devānāṃ' is an honorific plural.
Titles are now given in IAST instead of Devanāgarī. Inappropriate 'relative_only'+'commissioner' mixing removed.
Date: the paksa is now marked as an inference from 'अवदाते'. A possible tithi 13 (rāma=3, candra=1, read right to left) is recorded as uncertain. Notes added on the sun in Kumbha / moon in Karka.
Notes added on the unnamed scribe and the possible name 'Navala' in 'नवलाचार्योपाध्यायमाता'.

colophon: इति उष्णीषादिमणिशिखरान्तस्थानसप्तकेषु निरावरणी- कृतस्त्रचस्य....क्रियाषट्कविशुद्ध्या (?) दाचवारिशतश्लोका प्रत्य- वेक्षणं ज्ञानव्याख्या ॥ ‖ इति दादशाङ्गनिरीधदादशभूमिप्रतिलम्बविशुद्ध्या समता- ज्ञानगाथास्तुर्विश्रतिः ॥ 44b. ‖ इति निरावरणपञ्चदशकलाविशुद्ध्या सर्वतथागतसमाधि- गतकार्यकारणलक्षणकृत्यानुष्ठानज्ञानगाथाव्याख्या ॥ 49b. ‖ इति पञ्चतथागतज्ञानस्तुतिगाथाः पञ्च 50b. ‖ इत्यमृतकणिका नाम श्रीनामसंगीतिटिप्पनी परिसमाप्ता ॥ 52b.
notes: The genitive 'vīrasiṃhanāmadheyasya' is used where an instrumental is syntactically required with 'samavasthitena' and 'vyākhyānārthakāṅkṣiṇā', indicating Vīrasiṃha copied and/or studied the text together with his pupil Ratnacandra. The text mentions having come from Panarīnagara (śrīmatpanarīnagarītaḥ samāgatā?). Bendall identifies the place as Navakoṣṭha (Nuwakot) and notes Ratnajyoti was likely a local ruler.

colophon: श्रीगणेशाय नमः । अविर्लमदजलनिवहंभ्रमरकुलानिक- सेविकपोलं ।

colophon: इति स्कण्डपुराने<sup>(sic)</sup> शनिश्चस्वस्तीत्र समाप्तः। इति धा- रणीसंग्रहः संचित्रः परिसमाप्तः। ये धर्मा°। देयधर्मीऽयं प्रवरमहायानयायिनः...etc. अत्रिलीकर-स्त्री पूर्णावती द्वयो प्रमुखादिसगणपरिवाराणां यत्युष्ण° etc.।...नेपालेश्वर...श्रीशज- यमहीन्द्रसिंहमल्लदेव† परमभट्टारकदेवानां .. विजयराज्ये। ‖ सम्बत् ८३६ भाद्रवपदमास शुक्लपक्षे... etc. ‖ लिखितं। लेखकस्य काष्ठमण्डप महानगले तलमूर महा- विहारे खण्डचूकमहापुष्करिण्यां पूर्वदिशस्थित वज्रदेव्या- चरणाम्बुज श्रेवित महापात्रकुलश्रीवज्राचार्य श्रीपतिदेवेन लिखितसम्पुर्णं करोमि। यथा दृष्टं...। भग्नपृष्ठ...
notes: Bendall reads the date in his English header as N.S. 839 (A.D. 1719), but prints सम्बत् ८३६ in the Devanāgarī colophon text. N.S. 839 corresponds to 1719 CE, while N.S. 836 would be 1716 CE. Pārāvarta-mahāvihāra is Itum-bāhā in Kathmandu.

title: NĀMA-SAṄGĪTĪ and STOTRAS
colophon: इति श्री अनन्तनागराजाविरचितं श्रीलोकनाथतोचं समाप्त। ‖ इ° श्रीमच्छ्रीमदार्थ्यावलोकितेश्वरभट्टारकस्य जमराजा- स्तवतोचं परिसमाप्त। ‖ इ° श्रीमदार्थ्याव° कस्य त्रिष्णुनारायनतोचं समाप्त। ‖ इ° अ° कस्य चर्युतिया (?) विरचितस्तवतोचं परिसमाप्त। ‖ इ° अ° कस्य रूपस्तवतोचं परिसमाप्त।
notes: Bendall quotes no scribal colophon or date. He assigns the manuscript to the 18th century with a query, on the evidence of the script alone. The excerpts are only the subscriptions of the stotras. The Lokanātha stotra is attributed to Anantanāgarāja, a mythical nāga king, so he is not listed as a person. One stavatotra is attributed to 'चर्युतिया'. Bendall marks this reading (?), so it is probably corrupt and may not be a personal name at all. It is kept as an author with low confidence.
review: No substantive changes; notes expanded slightly (Anantanāgarāja excluded as a mythical nāga king, the 'Caryutiyā' reading is uncertain)

title: UTPĀTA-LAKSHAṄA-[LOKEṢVARA-BHĀSHITAM]
colophon: इति उत्यातलक्षणलोकेश्वरभाषितं तारा प्रच्छति समाप्तः । लिखितं यदिति तोल काथ बहालया श्रीवज्राचार्य कुलवजनं लिखापितादिनकुल गुरुभं ॥
notes: The colophon is in corrupt Newari: 'likhitaṃ yaditi tola kātha bahālayā śrīvajrācārya kulavaja-naṃ likhāpita dina kula gurubhaṃ'. I take कुलवजनं as Kulavajra plus the ergative -na, the agent of likhāpita ('caused to be written'). That makes him the commissioner. It is also possible that he copied the text himself, since the colophon begins with likhitaṃ. 'dina kula gurubhaṃ' is unclear. It may say the day of writing, perhaps a Thursday (guru), with the weekday garbled. It may also contain 'kulaguru' (family priest). I do not record it as a person. 'Kātha Bahāl' could be Kāṭhe Bahāl and 'Yadi tol' could be Yaṭkhā tol, both in Kathmandu, but neither identification is certain. The number ३३५ at the end is probably a verse or grantha count, not a date. There is no date: Bendall classes the manuscript only as 'modern'.
review: p1: name read as Kulavajra (कुलवजनं = Kulavaja[ra] + Newari ergative -na); role changed from scribe to commissioner, because the ergative agent goes with लिखापित 'caused to be written'; the initial लिखितं does not name a separate scribe
p1: Kāṭha Bahāl kept as affiliation and Yadi tol as residence, transliterated to IAST
p2 'Ādinakula' removed: दिनकुल गुरुभं most likely continues the Newari sentence (dina 'day' … guru, possibly the weekday Thursday, guruvāra), not a personal name
wrote_for relation removed (no separate scribe or commissioner pair can be established)
place transliterated to IAST

title: STOTRAS
date_note: ≈ 1785 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: इति सारदातवतोचं स°
notes: Bendall does not quote the vernacular (Newari) colophon. He only paraphrases it: 'written in the year given above by Ṣrīvajrācārya Bhājudhanamṛcay-āviyā (?) at Kāntipur (Kathmandu).' He marks the name as doubtful. The ending '-mṛcay-āviyā' is very likely a misreading of Newari '-na coyāviyā' (ergative -na + coyā biyā, 'written by'). review: Name re-read as 'Bhājudhana'. The rest of Bendall's '-mṛcay-āviyā' is probably a misreading of the Newari ergative plus verb 'na coyāviyā' ('written by'), not part of the name. Confidence stays low.
Residence removed: Kāntipur is given as the place of writing, not as the scribe's residence.
Notes expanded with the reasoning for the name.

title: RĀMĀṆKA-NĀṢIKĀ by DHARMAGUPTA, and fragment
date_note: ≈ 1360 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: श्रीधर्मगुप्तः कृती। पित्रा पुत्रकृपापरेण निपुणं शास्त्रान्वयं शिचित् एताम्भावरसीञ्चलां स कृतवान् रामाङ्गितान्नाटिकां। श्रेयो ऽस्तु। सम्वत् ४८० शुक्लिकदशम्यां रवि वासो। तेनैव धर्म- गुप्तेन श्रीमता रामदासिना। बालवागीश्वरेणैयं लिखिता रा- माङ्गनाटिका॥ शुभमस्तु सर्वदा॥
notes: Bendall describes the manuscript as the author's own copy (autograph). Dharmagupta, called Bālavāgīśvara and son of Rāmadāsa, both wrote and copied the Rāmāṅka-nāṭikā. The catalogue heading 'RĀMĀṆKA-NĀṢIKĀ' is an OCR garbling of Rāmāṅka-nāṭikā; the text itself also writes रामाङ्ग-. The era is not named in the text (just 'सम्वत् ४८०'); Bendall reads it as N.S. 480 = A.D. 1360 (480+880). No month is named: 'शुक्लिकदशम्यां' is corrupt, perhaps 'शुक्ल-दशम्यां' with the month dropped, or a garbling of a month name. Bendall calls Rāmadāsa 'a magistrate of Nepal', rendering नेपालावनपालमण्डलगुरुः. The prologue mentions Lalitāpura (Patan) as the place where the play is produced. That makes copying in Patan likely, but it is not stated as the place of copying.
review: Place: cleared. Lalitāpura (ललितापुरम्) is named in the prologue as the place where the play is staged or produced. It is not given as the place of copying, so it is now only mentioned in notes.
Notes expanded: the catalogue title is garbled by OCR, the month is missing, and the era is assumed.
Persons, relations and date confirmed, with evidence strings tightened.

title: ASHTASAHASRIKĀ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ
date_note: = Sunday 7 Oct 1263, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: देयधर्मी ऽयं प्रवरमहायानयायिनः परमोपाश्रिक-श्रीरा- मपासिडख (?) यदत्रपुण्यं... etc. ।
purpose: deyadharma (pious gift) by the donor; merit-transfer formula (yad atra puṇyaṃ ...)
notes: The year is written in letter-numerals, one digit per sign: ci = 3, a doubtful middle sign, and phrā = 4. Bendall reads the middle sign as 8 (ह/ङ) rather than 5 (ट), "on chronological grounds" because the colophon names king Abhayamalla, which gives N.S. 384 = A.D. 1264. ce_approx follows Bendall. However, the modern chronology (Petech) places Abhayamalla's reign at about N.S. 336–375 (A.D. 1216–1255). On that chronology, N.S. 354 (A.D. 1234) would fit the reign better, and 384 would fall after it. The date therefore needs checking. The donor's name is corrupt and Bendall marks it (?). The reading Rāmapāsiḍakha is mechanical; the first element is probably Rāma-. The title written परमोपाश्रिक is taken as paramopāsaka (lay devotee). No scribe is named. Bendall prints the beginning of the colophon only in part ("etc."), so the 1883 transliteration has been converted.
review: Date as_written now includes the year letter-numerals (चि-ह(?)-फ्रा) and the date words; tithi normalized to dvitīyā (दतीयाया = dvitīyāyāṃ); weekday normalized to Sunday (ādityavāra).
Donor titles normalized: paramopāsaka (written परमोपाश्रिक); the Mahāyāna epithet is kept as an epithet.
Purpose expanded to deyadharma with a merit-transfer formula.
Notes: added the conflict between N.S. 384 and the modern chronology of Abhayamalla's reign, and the corrupt donor name.

title: PAṄCARAKSHĀ
date_note: ≈ 1682 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: **एवं मया श्रुतम्यकस्मिंसमय भगवानः राजगृहे विहरति...**
notes: The date and the king's name are on the last leaf only. This leaf is on different paper and in a slightly later hand. Bendall takes it to be a fresh copy of a damaged original leaf, so N.S. 802 (A.D. 1682) is probably the date of the original manuscript and was recopied onto the supply leaf. Bendall's physical description dates the hand to the 18th century, which does not quite fit 1682; the supply leaf itself is undated. Bendall prints the year as ८°२ and reads it as 802. 'खस्सुसंस्वत्' is a garbled form of the era word (saṃvat). The royal name 'प्रथितुन्द्रमल्लदेव' is a corrupt form of Pārthivendramalladeva, king of Kathmandu, who reigned c. N.S. 800–807 (1680–1687). The year 802 falls in his reign. 'मयूरच्छत्र-खड्गशीर्षिकामनाथं (?)' and 'याकूरधर्माचक्रविजयराज्ये' are corrupt epithets and reign formulas. No scribe, donor or place is named. The two cover leaves from a Tantric Sūtra are unrelated to this copy.

title: A collection of DHĀRANĪS, etc
date_note: ≈ 1677 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: श्रीयो ऽसु संवत् ७८७ (month, nakshatra, day etc.) ... एतद्दिने लिखितं... काष्टमण्डपनगरे... श्रीरत्नवज्रिण (?)...।
notes: The two figures for the year do not agree. Bendall's physical description gives 'N. S. 797 (A.D. 1677)', but his Devanāgarī excerpt of the colophon prints 'संवत् ७८७' (NS 787 = 1667 CE). One of them is probably a misprint, and I can't tell which. I followed the colophon as printed (787 / 1667); if the heading is right, the year is NS 797 = 1677 CE. Bendall leaves out the month, nakṣatra and day. 'श्रीयो ऽसु' is probably a garbled 'श्रेयो ऽस्तु'. Bendall puts a query (?) after the scribe's name. 'रत्नवज्रिण' probably stands for the instrumental Ratnavajriṇā, after 'likhitaṃ'. I took the stem as Ratnavajrin; Ratnavajra is also possible. 'Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa-nagara' is Kathmandu.
review: Kept all extracted content; expanded notes on the conflicting year (797 vs 787) and on the probable instrumental form of the scribe's name

title: AMARA-KOṢA
date_raw: श्रीमन्नेपालिकसम्बन्धरे। सम्बत ५०० मार्गः शुद्ध श्रीपञ्चम्या तिथौ रैवतिनक्षत्रे साध्ययोगे सोमवासरे
date_note: = Tuesday 15 Nov 1379, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: नेपालाभुवमण्डलेश्वर प्रभूपते...। देवश्रीजयार्जुनो (*sic*) हि... परे लोकात्मम् (? 1. त०) भूपति।
purpose: for the study (adhyayanārtham) of Mahāpātra …tyaguṇamasiṃha and Mahāpātra Raghusiṃhadeva
notes: The year in the colophon ('सम्बत ५००') is in the retouched, modern-ink passage, so it is not reliable. NS 500 Mārgaśīrṣa = late 1379 CE. Bendall dates the manuscript from the note on the back of the leaf, which is probably in a contemporary hand: 'abdhi-vindu-viṣaye' = NS 504, Māgha kṛṣṇa 5 = A.D. 1384. That note also names King Jayārjunadeva (reigned c. 1361–1382). This conflicts with Bendall's 1384, since by 1384 Jayasthiti was ruling according to Add. 1395. Erasures in the colophon make the names hard to read. 'puṣā nāma maḍāpātra' may be a personal name (Puṣā) followed by the title mahāpātra, or a corruption; reading Puṣā as commissioner and resident of Lalitapur is conjectural. 'त्यगुणम सिंह' is preceded by an erasure, so the name is incomplete. The plural '-devānām' suggests more than one beneficiary.
review: Commissioner reassigned: the subject of 'likhāpitaḥ' is most plausibly the person resident in Lalitapur introduced by '…sitaḥ puṣā nāma', so Puṣā is now the commissioner (low confidence). Tyaguṇamasiṃha is now a beneficiary, as the genitive plural '-devānām adhyayanārthaṃ' covers more than one person.
'mahāpātra' is now treated as a title that comes before each name ('maḍāpātra śrī … tyaguṇama siṃha', 'mahāpātra śrīRaghusiṃhadeva').
Lalitāpurī residence moved from the scribe Jasacandra to the commissioner. The colophon does not say where the scribe lived.
Relations rebuilt: the commissioner commissioned the copy from the scribe; the scribe wrote it for the commissioner; both mahāpātras are linked to the commissioner as beneficiaries ('other').
King Jayārjunadeva's epithets reduced to titles. The reign relation is kept at medium confidence because the king is named only in the note on the back of the leaf.
Notes expanded to cover the retouched date: the colophon has 500, the note on the back has 504.

title: ḌAMBŪKĀVADĀNA
date_note: = Wednesday 15 Oct 1427, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: सम्भूकावदाननिदानकथा समाप्तः॥ स° ५४७ अष्टुनि कृष्ण १° लिखित श्री डंखाचोकवज्राचार्य श्री पंडजसः (?)
notes: Bendall marks the scribe's name with a query ('पंडजसः (?)'). The reading Paṇḍajasa is uncertain. It may be corrupt, for example for Paṇḍita Jasa(rāja), Padmajasa or a similar name. Ḍaṃkhācoka (डंखाचोक) is probably a locality or quadrangle (cuka/coka) in the Kathmandu Valley that the vajrācārya scribe belonged to. It is recorded as his residence, not as the stated place of copying. The month 'अष्टुनि' is likely a misreading or corruption of Āśvina. The tithi '१°' is taken as 10, but the ° could also be Bendall's abbreviation mark (compare 'स°'), in which case the tithi would be 1. NS 547 + 880 = 1427 CE, which agrees with Bendall's date. If the month is Āśvina, the date falls in about September/October 1427.
review: Place of copying cleared: डंखाचोक is given only as the scribe's residence or affiliation in a 'written by' phrase. It is not stated as the place of copying, so it is kept under the person's residence.
Notes expanded: the tithi reading '१°' is ambiguous, and the month and name readings are doubtful.

title: RATNAGUṆA-SAṄCAYA
date_note: ≈ 1830 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: रिषितेयं (i.e. लिखि<sup>०</sup>) काय-वाहारया श्रीवजवाक्ष्य पद्या- कलिासंहिन।
notes: Bendall says the MS is 'barbarously incorrect'. He does not quote the date line in Devanāgarī; he gives only 'N. s. 950 (A.D. 1830)'. NS 950 = 1829/30 CE. रिषितेयं = likhiteyam. श्रीवजवाक्ष्य is probably a garbled śrī-vajrācāryeṇa/-sya, so the title vajrācārya is conjectural. पद्याकलिासंहिन is most likely Padmākarasiṃhena; Padmākalisiṃha is also possible. काय-वाहारया looks like a Newari genitive, 'of Kāya-bahāra/bahāl'. This is a vihāra name that cannot be identified for certain (perhaps Kwā Bahā). It is taken as the scribe's affiliation, not as the stated place of copying. The leaves carry a second numbering (71–96), so the MS was probably part of a larger series.
review: Scribe's name normalised from 'Padmākalisimha' to the likelier reading 'Padmākarasiṃha' (पद्याकलिासंहिन read as Padmākarasiṃhena, instrumental). Confidence lowered to low.
Kāya-bahāra kept as the scribe's affiliation and residence. It was removed from 'place', because the colophon does not say the copy was made there.
Notes expanded: the vajrācārya reading is conjectural, and the year is about 1829/30.

colophon: ॐ अदया ऽद्वैधीकारा ॥ आर्यश्री शतसहस्राः (*sic*) प्रश्नं अष्ट- चिंशत्तमः परिव० । Then follows the date (see above) । श्री चन्द्र- न्तदेवः रत्नविलासदेवाकुलां विलासदेव-रत्नचूडामणिस्तथा । एते सहानुमतेन स्वस्वहस्तौ लिखिता श्रीमत्प्रज्ञापारमिता चय- षत (?) संपूर्णैति ॥

Month, tithi and weekday are not available. The name string 'श्री चन्द्रन्तदेवः रत्नविलासदेवाकुलां विलासदेव-रत्नचूडामणिस्तथा' is corrupt. The number of scribes, between three and five, is uncertain. The -deva endings are personal names, not regnal names. No king is named. title: ĀTASĀHASRĪ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ, Part 1
date_note: = Thursday 1 May 1806, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: आर्यशतसाहस्र्या भगवत्याः प्रज्ञापारमितायाः प्रथमखण्डं समाप्तमिति ॥ ये धर्मा० । गुरुभं etc. । समत् ५२७ वैशाषमास्य गुरुकूपचे चतुर्दश्यांतिथौ चिन्तानचत्रे वजयोगे यथाकर्ममही- न्तक (?) – बृहस्पति – वार – शकुह – श्रीरचभगवतिः प्रथमख- ण्डप्रज्ञापारमितापुस्तक चौपधुनकादिनजरो । ० । लिखित श्री- मानदेवसंस्कारितचक्रमहाविहाराधिष्ठितः श्रीवज्राचार्य ज्ञा- जणग्लन (?) संपूर्णमिति ।
notes: The date fields conflict. Bendall's header reads 'N. s. 926 (A.D. 1806)', but the Devanāgarī colophon as transcribed reads 'समत् ५२७', i.e. NS 527 = c. 1407 CE. The Devanāgarī comes from OCR and is heavily garbled (च for क्ष throughout, e.g. भिचु, नचत्र), and OCR can confuse ५ and ९, or ६ and ७. So the transcribed figure is not fully reliable either. NS 527 is preferred here because a palm-leaf manuscript of 494 leaves fits the early 15th century much better than 1806. This should still be checked against the printed catalogue or the manuscript. 'गुरुकूपचे' is taken as an OCR corruption of 'शुक्लपक्षे'. 'चिन्ता' = Citrā; 'वज' = Vajra yoga. The phrases 'यथाकर्ममहीन्तक (?) … शकुह – श्रीरचभगवतिः … चौपधुनकादिनजरो' (Newari, apparently 'the writing was completed …') are unclear and contain no secure personal name. Bendall himself marks the scribe's name 'ज्ञाजणग्लन' (?) as doubtful; it may be a garbled Newar name. The title header 'ĀTASĀHASRĪ' is an OCR error for ŚATASĀHASRĪ (the colophon reads शतसाहस्र्या).
review: Place: removed the modern identification (Cuka Bāhā / Kathmandu). Which vihāra 'Mānadeva-saṃskārita Cakra Mahāvihāra' refers to today is not certain, and the colophon names it as the scribe's vihāra, not explicitly as the place of copying.
Date: read the OCR-garbled 'गुरुकूपचे' as 'शुक्लपक्षे' and recorded this. Kept NS 527 = 1407 CE, but the notes now explain the conflict with Bendall's header (NS 926 = 1806) and why 527 is preferred.
Nakshatra spelling normalized to citrā.
Notes expanded: OCR problems, unclear Newari phrases, the title OCR error (ĀTASĀHASRĪ for ŚATASĀHASRĪ).

title: ASHTASĀHASRIKĀ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ
date_note: = Thursday 31 Mar 1015, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: पञ्चचिंसाधिके ऽब्दे शततमप्रशते\* चैत्रमासे हिमाभा । ‖ विख्याते ऽस्मिन् दशम्यान्दनिंजरिपुगुरौ (?°दनुज°) वासरे संप्रशस्ते ॥ ‖ राज्ञि श्रीभोजदेवे ऽष्यमितगुणगणाल[श्च]† श्रीरुद्रदेवे । ‖ श्रीलक्ष्मीकामदेवैररिजग[-त]कुलिसैरर्द्धराज्ये ऽपभुक्ते ॥
purpose: Merit of the redemption transferred to his mother, father and all beings (second colophon)
notes: Main colophon (verse): the year is NS 135 = 1015 CE, as Bendall gives it. Caitra, daśamī. 'danujaripuguru' means Bṛhaspati, i.e. Thursday. Śukla pakṣa is inferred from 'himābhā' ('moon-bright') and is tentative. The colophon was written during the joint rule of Bhojadeva and Rudradeva, with Lakṣmīkāmadeva holding half the kingdom. The scribe Sujatabhadra (probably Sujātabhadra) copied it in the Śrī-Lhaṃ-vihāra of Nepālamaṇḍala. 'तपसीरखुसागरे' is corrupt; 'खुधीः' is probably सुधीः. Second colophon, added in a later hooked hand: dvitīye śatasya gatavati + pañcāsatā navamāñcitena = NS 259 (= c. 1139 CE), Kārtika (probably śukla) 5, under Mānadeva. In it someone redeemed the book from a faithless person ([śra]ddhāhīna-jana). The name 'कर्तुणपूर्वण वज्रिण' is taken as karuṇāpūrveṇa vajriṇā = Karuṇāvajra; this reading is uncertain. Only the original date is entered in the date fields.

title: SĀDHANA-SAMUCCAYA
date_note: = Thursday 14 Jan 1216, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: The colophon runs thus: सवत् [३३६] (see above) पौषकृष्णा- ष्टम्यां षट्हसतिवासरे वैशाखनक्षत्रे राजाधिराजपरमेश्वर श्रीमदरिमल्ल दे [वस्य विजराज्ये (*sic*) लिखितमिदं साधनसमुच्चयं नाम पुस्तकं]

He suggests they may originally have been 2s, and says that, according to Prof. Adams, the weekday and month do not tally for 336, so the restoration is probably wrong. NS 336 would fall within Arimalla's reign (c. NS 320–336), so ce_approx 1215/16 stands only provisionally. 'षट्हसतिवासरे' is presumably a printing or scribal error for बृहस्पतिवासरे (Thursday). 'विजराज्ये' (sic) stands for vijayarājye. The bracketed words 'वस्य विजराज्ये ... पुस्तकं' were rewritten by a second hand. Ānandajīvabhadra is known only from the cover note (ārādhana in NS 458 = 1338 CE at the Ārinaka-vihāra). He is a later user, not part of the original production. The relation entry for him is a placeholder and can be dropped. Kumudākara and Ratnākaragupta are authors of individual sādhanas named in the index and are not included as persons of this copy.

purpose: The book was given to Hṛvadeva as wages (jyālā biyā) for his writing a Kriyāsaṃgraha for King Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur
notes: Bendall printed the date only in his description (NS 753 = AD 1633) and replaced the colophon's date line with 'date v. supra', so the year cannot be checked against the colophon. Bendall says the manuscript was written at Bhatgāon under Jagajjyotir Malla, but the colophon does not support this. Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur appears only as the king for whom Hṛvadeva wrote a Kriyāsaṃgraha. The Kāraṇḍavyūha copy itself is placed in Lalitapurī (ररितापुरि, i.e. Patan) during the joint reign (ubhayarājye) of Siddhinarasiṃhamalla and his son Śrīnivāsamalla. A joint reign with Śrīnivāsa as early as 1633 is unusually early and is worth checking. Jagajjyotirmalla (r. c. 1614–1637) fits 1633. The Newari is heavily corrupt: वीलसिंह probably stands for Vīrasiṃha; हृवदेवजयात is read as Hṛvadeva-jū-yāta ('to Hṛvadeva'), and the true name may be different. थचुक वाहार is the name of a vihāra and has not been identified. Other corrupt spellings: सिद्धिनलसिंह = Siddhinarasiṃha, श्रीशनिदास्सल्ल = Śrīnivāsamalla, गुरुद्धवावतार = garuḍadhvajāvatāra. The colophon does not say who paid the wages (perhaps the king), so no donor is assigned.

p2 Hṛvadeva: stem without the Newari honorific + dative -jū-yāta ('Hṛvadevajayāta' = Hṛvadeva-jū-yāta, 'to Hṛvadeva'); role beneficiary dropped, kept owner (book given to him) and added 'other' (he wrote a Kriyāsaṃgraha for the Bhaktapur king); confidence low because the name is corrupt
p3 Jagajjyotirmalla: role changed from king to other; he is king of Bhaktapur, named only because the Kriyāsaṃgraha was written for him, while this copy was made in Lalitapur under the Patan kings

title: ASHTASAHASRIKĀ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ
script: Kuṭila or early Devanāgarī hand as modified in the XIIth cent. A.D
date_note: = Sunday 18 Jul 1165, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: संवत् २८५ आवण गुरुत्ताष्टम्यामादित्यदिने। श्रीमदानन्ददेवस्य विजयराज्ये ॥ लिखितेदं (?) श्रीमस्वक्रयां (?) वन्ताण्डुल्लके (?) श्रीधर्मचक्रमहाविहाराधिवासिन शाक्यभिद्युमञ्जुश्रियेणेति ॥ श्रीधानपिङ्गविषयाधिवासिन बुद्धौभावे (?) नामधेयस्य यदत्र पुण्यं तद्भवत्वाचार्यध्यायमातापितृपर्वङ्गमङ्गला सकलसत्त्वराशेरनुत्तरज्ञानावाप्त्यादिति ॥
purpose: Merit transfer: the merit goes to the person from Dhānapiṅga-viṣaya, to be shared with teachers and parents and given to all beings for supreme knowledge (यदत्र पुण्यं तद्भवत्वाचार्य...सकलसत्त्वराशेरनुत्तरज्ञानावाप्तये).
notes: This is Bendall's catalogue (1883), and his Devanāgarī shows OCR or typographical corruption. Bendall also says the latter part of the colophon is partly obliterated. 'आवण' is read as श्रावण. 'गुरुत्ताष्टम्याम्' is probably शुक्लाष्टम्याम्, so the pakṣa is inferred. 'शाक्यभिद्यु' stands for शाक्यभिक्षु. 'श्रीमस्वक्रयां (?)' cannot be read. 'वन्ताण्डुल्लके (?)' looks like a locality name but is uncertain. Date: NS 285 + 880 = 1165 CE, which agrees with Bendall's 'A.D. 1165'; the weekday (Sunday) has not been verified. The king is Ānandadeva, as Bendall says. The third person's name is very doubtful: Bendall gives 'बुद्धौभावे (?)', which could be a corruption of something like Buddhabhāva or Buddhadeva. The person resides in Dhānapiṅga-viṣaya. The colophon assigns this person the merit, which suggests they were the donor or commissioner, but the colophon does not state that role.
review: p2 (Mañjuśrī): affiliation normalized to Dharmacakra-mahāvihāra. Bendall gives this as the scribe's residence, so it is also entered as residence. The place 'वन्ताण्डुल्लके (?)' is too doubtful to stand alone as residence.

p3: name reading lowered to low confidence (Buddhabhāva?). Roles changed from commissioner+donor to beneficiary: the colophon only assigns him the merit ('नामधेयस्य यदत्र पुण्यं'). It has no likhāpita or deyadharma.
Removed the p2→p3 wrote_for relation because the colophon gives no explicit commissioning.
Purpose rewritten to follow the colophon wording. The first reading had added words ('kṛtvā', 'upādhyāya') that are not in the text.
Place: as_written shortened to the actual locative. Normalized left empty.
Notes expanded: the OCR/typographical corruptions are explained and the date is checked.

title: GUHYĀVALĪ-VIVṚITI by GHANADEVĀ
date_raw: dated in the 37th year of Govinda-Pāla (A.D. 1198, cf. No. I)
date_note: ≈ 1198 CE, Bendall's own conversion (no era-dated colophon to recalculate)
colophon: गोविन्दपालदेवानां सं ३७ आमण(*sic*)दिने ११ लिखितमिदं पुस्तकं काशीगयाकरेणति ॥
notes: The year is the 37th of Govindapāla. Bendall converts it to A.D. 1198, which fits the usual reckoning of this era from c. 1161. The same scribe copied the other works in Add. 1699 over three successive years (1198–1200) in Bengali script. The month 'āmaṇa' is marked (sic) by Bendall and is corrupt; the intended month is uncertain. 'dine 11' is probably a day of the month rather than a lunar tithi. Bendall's English general note gives the scribe as 'Kācṛīgayākara'. This is almost certainly an OCR corruption of 'Kāçīgayākara' (= Kāśīgayākara), which matches the Devanāgarī 'काशीगयाकरेणति' (= -kareṇeti). Ghanadeva calls himself 'bhikṣu' in the opening verses and 'paṇḍita sthavira' in the colophon. Daṇḍīpāda, whose method (krama) the vivṛti follows, is the author of the root text, not a person connected with this copy, so he is left out.
review: p2 Govindapāladeva: removed 'deva' from titles (kept as part of the regnal name).
p1 Ghanadeva: evidence also covers 'भिक्षुश्रीघनदेवेन विवृतिः क्रियते' for the bhikṣu title. Kept roles author/commentator because he wrote the vivṛti on Daṇḍīpāda's work.
Date: month normalised to IAST 'āmaṇa (sic)'. Day 11 entered in the tithi field as 'dine 11'.
Notes: 'Kācṛīgayākara' in Bendall's English is explained as an OCR mangling of 'Kāçīgayākara' (= Kāśīgayākara), so the two do not conflict. Added a note on the regnal reckoning.
Shortened the evidence for under_reign_of.

title: YOGARATNA-MĀLĀ, a commentary on the HEVAJRA by KRISHṆA or KĀHNA
date_note: ≈ 1200 CE, Bendall's own conversion (no era-dated colophon to recalculate)
colophon: ॐ वज्रपद्मयोरधिष्ठानं येनाधिष्ठ्यते (*sic*) । योगरत्नमालायां क्वा हेवज्रपञ्चिकायाम् । यत्पुण्यमाचितं तेन निष्क्रेशः स्याद- खिलो जनः ॥ श्रीहेवज्रपञ्चिका योगरत्नमाला समाप्ता ॥ ॥ कृतिरियं पण्डिताचार्यश्रीकाङ्कपादानामिति ॥ परमेश्वरेत्या- दि राजावली पूर्ववत् । श्रीमद्गोविन्दपालदेवानां सं ३६ भा- द्रदिने १४ लिखितमिदं पुस्तकं काशीगयाकरेणिति ॥

Scribe's name is read as 'Kācṛīgayākara' in Bendall's English note, but the colophon reads 'Kāśīgayākara'. The author/commentator Kāhṇa / Kṛṣṇa is named as Kāṅkapāda in the final colophon.

title: PAṄCA-RAKSHĀ
date_note: = Friday 4 Jun 1389, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: °पञ्चरत्नामहायानसूत्राणि समाप्तेति। ये धर्मा°। देय- धर्मो ऽयं प्रवरमहायानयाचिन श्रीललितक्रमाया श्रीमाणिग- लके\* श्रीवच्चविहाराधिवांत-शाक्यपुत्र परसीगत-संध श्रीमले- चजजकस्य ॥ यदत्रपुण्यं etc.... ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तमिति ॥ श्री- योऽस्तु सम्वत ५०६ ज्येष्ठशुक्ल दशम्याया तिथौ शुक्रवासरे राजाधिराजश्री२ जयस्थितिराजमखराजेशुभः (*sic*) ॥
purpose: deyadharma (pious gift) of the donor, merit formula yad atra puṇyaṃ
notes: The transcribed Devanāgarī prints ५०६, but Bendall's description gives N.s. 509 = A.D. 1389. I followed Bendall and took ५०६ as a probable OCR confusion of ९ with ६. Bendall notes that the date and the king's name are in a different, apparently contemporary hand. There is another date inside the cover, probably of a recitation, but it is nearly obliterated. 'मखराजे' stands for 'मल्लराज्ये'. The donor's name 'मलेचजजक' is corrupt, either in the manuscript or in the OCR. 'परसीगत-संध' probably stands for 'paramasaugata-saṃgha'/'paramasaugata'. 'प्रवरमहायानयाचिन' stands for 'pravaramahāyānayāyin'. 'वच्चविहार' may stand for Vatsavihāra; the name is uncertain.
review: Date year changed from 506 to 509 (ce 1386 → 1389): Bendall's description states N.s. 509 (A.D. 1389). The '५०६' in the transcription is probably an OCR misreading of ५०९, since ६ and ९ are easily confused. 509 also falls within Jayasthitimalla's reign.
Donor name confidence lowered to low (corrupt). Added the title paramasaugata, the probable reading of 'परसीगत'. Separated affiliation (vihāra) from residence.
Purpose reworded as a pious gift (deyadharma) for merit, in place of the quoted formula.
Place: kept the normalization to Patan (Lalitakrama = Lalitapattana; Māṇigala = the Patan palace quarter). The vihāra name was removed from the place string.

title: VAJRĀVALĪ by ABHAYĀKARAGUPTA
date_note: = Saturday 3 Sep 1429, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: **महापन्दिता** (*sic*) **अभयाकरगुप्त-विरचिता वज्रावली नाम मण्डलोपायिका समाप्तः । ये धर्मं । सं ५४७ भाद्रपद शुक्लः पञ्चम्याया** (*sic*) **तित्यौ विश्राषणचत्रे शणिचर वासरे राजं जयजन्मलदेवस्य विजयराज्ये लिखित श्री माणिकलकेः उत्रविहारे श्रीहर्षवर्णमहाविहारावस्थितमिचु श्रीजिवयीभट्टेण स्वहस्तेन लिखितं । जथा दृष्टं etc. ॥**
notes: The Devanāgarī transcript reads सं ५४७, but Bendall's description gives N.S. 549 (A.D. 1429). The OCR probably confused ९ with ७, so 549 is followed here. The king's name 'जयजन्मलदेवस्य' is corrupt. It is read as Jayayakṣamalladeva because he reigned in NS 549, after Jayajyotirmalla, who died c. 1428. If the year were really 547, the king would be Jayajyotirmalla. Either way the identification is uncertain. Bendall names the scribe 'Jivayibhadra' in his English note, and the transcript's 'भट्टेण' is taken as a corruption of 'भद्रेण'. 'मिचु' = भिक्षु. 'विश्राषणचत्रे' = विशाखानक्षत्रे. 'माणिकलकेः' = Māṇigala, i.e. Patan. 'उत्रविहारे' and 'हर्षवर्णमहाविहार' are probably corrupt. They might stand for Rudravarṇa-mahāvihāra (Uku Bahal, Patan), but this is uncertain.
review: Year: Bendall reads N.S. 549 (A.D. 1429). The OCR '५४७' is most likely a misreading of ५४९, so year 549 and ce_approx 1429 are used, with the discrepancy noted.

King: the name was read as Jayayakṣamalladeva, with medium confidence. 'जयजन्मलदेवस्य' is corrupt, and in NS 549 Yakṣamalla was reigning, not Jyotirmalla, who died c. 1428. The title 'rājan' was dropped.
Scribe: the name was corrected to Jivayibhadra, following Bendall's English note. 'भट्टेण' is an OCR corruption of 'भद्रेण'.
Nakshatra: 'विश्राषणचत्रे' is normalised to Viśākhā (विशाखानक्षत्रे).
Affiliation: the vihāra name is flagged as uncertain in the notes.
Relation evidence shortened.

title: KHAḌGA-PŪJĀVIDHI
date_raw: dated N. s. 381, middle figure doubtful (A. D. 1261)
date_note: = Tuesday 4 Oct 1261, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: खड्गपूजाविधि समाप्तः । समाप्तः ३८१ (?) अश्विनि [? द]शम्यां तिथौ अञ्जार (?) दिने लिखितमिति । राजादिराजप्रमेश्चर (sic) श्री [?] ह मालदेवकारित । शके वैहारश्रीभिचु देव- मना लिखित ।
notes: Bendall reads the date as N.S. 381, with the middle figure doubtful (A.D. 1261). The colophon does not name the era, but N.S. is implied. Bendall's conversion is kept for ce_approx. The king's name is damaged: 'श्री [?] ह मालदेव'. One possible reading is Jayasīhamalladeva, who reigned about N.S. 391–394 (1271–1274 CE). If so, the doubtful middle figure could be 9, giving N.S. 391 (1271 CE). In 1261 the reigning king was Jayabhīmadeva, and his name does not fit '…ha malladeva'. This is unresolved. 'कारित' is taken to mean that the king commissioned the copy, but it could be only a formula of royal patronage. अञ्जार is probably aṅgāra (Tuesday). The scribe's name and his vihāra ('शके वैहारश्रीभिचु', perhaps Śākya-vihāra śrī-bhikṣu, or a corrupt 'śākyabhikṣu') are corrupt. The name could also be read Devamaṇi or Devamati.
review: King's name: confidence lowered to low; noted possible reading Jayasīhamalladeva (NS 391–394), which would fit if Bendall's doubtful middle figure is 9 rather than 8
Scribe's name normalized to the stem 'Devamana' (देवमना read as a nominative); confidence lowered to low
Scribe's affiliation given as a corrupt vihāra name (perhaps Śākya-vihāra) rather than 'Śake-vaihāra'; place of copying left empty because the colophon does not say where the copy was made
Added an under_reign_of relation from the scribe to the king
Notes expanded: the date and the king may not match, and several readings are uncertain

title: ÇAMBARA-PAÑJIKĀ
script: writing similar to that of No. I
colophon: स्ववरा (*sic*) पञ्चिकेयं समाप्तं। सर्वज्ञमित्रपादानां य (?) गुरु परंपरा .... ता। समादि सर्वसत्त्वराम् निस्सामसत्त्व (?)।
notes: This is part IX of Bendall's composite entry Add. 1706: 7 palm leaves of a Śambara-pañjikā, a manual of Śambara worship. The ending is corrupt ('स्ववरा (sic) पञ्चिकेयं समाप्तं' presumably stands for शम्बरपञ्जिकेयं). The verse after it names the guru lineage (गुरुपरंपरा) of Sarvajñamitra. He may be the author of the manual or only the head of the teaching lineage it comes from; his link to this copy is uncertain. He is possibly the Kashmiri Sarvajñamitra, author of the Sragdharāstotra, but that is not certain. No scribe, donor, owner, king, date or place of copying is given. Bendall gives no date for this part; he says only that the writing is similar to that of No. I.
review: Sarvajñamitra: dropped role 'teacher' (no teacher–pupil link to the scribe or owner of this copy is stated; he is named as the head of a guru lineage in the text's closing verse). Kept 'author' at low confidence.
Removed 'pāda' from titles: it is an honorific plural (-pādānām), not a caste or office title.
Purpose cleared: 'समादि सर्वसत्त्वराम्...' is a corrupt part of the work's closing verse, not a statement of why this copy was made.
Notes expanded: no scribe, donor, date or place is given.

notes:
The inscription is badly damaged.

Line 2: '. . . devasuta radevo' keeps only the endings of two names. Reading them as [Vṛṣa]devasuta [Śaṅka]radeva is a conjecture. It rests on Rajavamsi's reading 'śaṅkara-iti' in line 6 and on the known genealogy (Vṛṣadeva → Śaṅkaradeva → Dharmadeva → Mānadeva). Mānadeva is traditionally credited with founding the Mānavihāra, so the inscription may come from his reign or later. However, no reigning king, donor or recipient survives by name: 'rājā' appears only in line 13 and 'narendra' only in line 2.

Line 27, 'sāgraṃ śataṃ varṣāṇām', is part of the eulogy ('more than a hundred years'), not a date formula. No date survives.

p2: 'devasuta' gives only the end of the father's name. Read as [Vṛṣa]deva (Vṛṣadeva), low confidence.
p1 roles: changed from king/donor to relative_only. Śaṅkaradeva appears in a genealogical eulogy as an ancestor. The donor and reigning king are not preserved by name.
Removed 'narendra' as a title of p1. It stands separately in a broken context and may refer to someone else.

Her name is in the instrumental, so she probably petitioned for the grant or carried out the work, but the editor calls the grant 'in favour of' her. review: Jayasundarī: roles changed from beneficiary+relative_only to recipient. The editor describes the grant as made in her favour, and she acts in the inscription, so relative_only does not apply. Her name stands in the instrumental, so she was probably also the petitioner; this is now in the notes.
Ravigupta: as_written now gives Regmi's reading 'mahāpratihāra-ravi[guptaḥ]', with a note that the main text breaks off before the name.

It confirms their koṭṭa with full koṭṭa rights and exemption from cāṭas and bhaṭas, adds land exchanged near the Dakṣiṇa-rājakula and the Puṇḍi-rājakula, grants rights over charcoal, cakra and pine wood, and defines the boundaries. title: Saṃvat 187, Lalitpur, Su-bahāla
subject: inscription
date_note: = Friday 13 Jan 764, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon:
1. Oṃ saṃvat 187
māghaśukladivā 5 puṇyādhāre jareṃ śrīpaṃkeśa-
purpose: Fragment; probably records a pious act (perhaps an endowment) for the liṅga Paṃkeśa. The text breaks off.
notes: Only line 1 survives, and it breaks off. The editor says only 'mentioned śrī-Paṃkeśa' (DV 175). Paṃkeśa looks like the name of a Śiva liṅga (founder's name + īśa, as in Licchavi usage), so it is not listed as a person. The founder (Paṃka?) is not named outright. 'jareṃ' is unclear, possibly corrupt or the start of a lost word. 'puṇyādhāre' is read as 'on an auspicious occasion'. The year is in the Licchavi saṃvat, left unconverted as instructed.
review: Removed Paṃkeśa from persons. A Licchavi name ending in -īśa/-eśa (Paṃka + īśa) is almost certainly a Śiva liṅga named after its founder, so it is a deity, not a person; the founder's name may be Paṃka, but the text does not say so.

Changed purpose from 'water conduit' to 'fragmentary; probably concerns the liṅga Paṃkeśa'. Puṇyādhāre most likely means 'on an auspicious occasion', not a reservoir, and nothing in the text points to a water conduit.
place.as_written now gives the full find-spot: 'Lalitpur, Su-bahāla'.
Date: as_written now keeps the full wording 'saṃvat 187 māghaśukladivā 5'.

notes: Lines 1–9 are worn away and lines 10–18 are almost unreadable, so the issuing king is lost. The roughly 9–10 lines after line 73, which would have held the dūtaka and the date, are also illegible. The date is lost entirely. The verse is an anuṣṭubh, but R.'s first pāda has only 7 syllables, so R.'s text is probably corrupt there too. The name is therefore uncertain and should not be relied on. The editor reports that no date is visible. Concordance: DV 181; Gn LXXXVI; HJ 158; R. 153. The site lies at the eastern edge of Patan.

title: Viṣṇupādukā hill
subject: inscription
colophon:
1. devyāḥ
karttavyatābuddhyā śrīpādai . . . grajaḥ śailastambhakriyārambhe kedumbāṭo
niyojitaḥ
notes: This is a fragmentary, undated inscription (DV 8) on a column near a water conduit on Viṣṇupādukā hill. Kedumbāṭa was appointed (niyojitaḥ) to start the work on the stone pillar, apparently by royal order (śrīpādaiḥ). The king is not named. The queen (devyāḥ, 'for the queen' or 'of the goddess') is not named either. The lacuna 'śrīpādai . . . grajaḥ' may hide a word ending in -agrajaḥ ('elder brother'). If so, someone named in the lost text is described as an elder brother, possibly Kedumbāṭa himself, but this cannot be checked. 'Kedumbāṭa' is taken as a personal name, but it is not certain.
review: Kedumbāṭa: confidence lowered from high to medium, because the text is a fragment and the word could be a title or designation rather than a personal name. His role is kept as official, since he was appointed (niyojitaḥ) to the work.
